the rapporteur. - madam president! - i have to go. we will be voting today on the final report on the activities of the committee on petitions in 2014. i have been involved in the work of the committee on petitions since 2004, so i have followed its work for over a decade and have seen how the results of its work directly or indirectly affect eu legislation. at the legal level, citizens' complaints to the committee on petitions are a test of the implementation of community law in the member states. the number of petitions is still high, which shows that we are still facing a lack of proper enforcement or poor implementation of the law. the number of petitions, on the other hand, also shows that european union citizens are becoming more aware and aware that they can effectively assert their rights in the european parliament. in 2013, after a year-on-year increase in the number of petitions, we recorded a peak in the number of complaints received. the commission also found that the union industry's sales volume and market share developed over the period considered as follows: the statistics show that 2714 petitions were received by the european parliament during the period under review, which is 6% less than in 2013. in addition, 1877 petitions were closed in 2014, an increase of almost 10% compared to 2013. however, the time taken to process petitions is still not satisfactory. we must strive to ensure that each petition has the opportunity to be examined as quickly as possible, while at the same time addressing the issue in an effective and efficient manner. i hope that with the use of advanced information technology, our contacts with citizens will be more efficient and problems will be solved more quickly. the new web portal launched in november 2014 has already streamlined the previous web-based system. citizens can submit petitions electronically through the new portal, have all the necessary information on parliament's powers, register, file a petition, download supporting documents, obtain information on the status of their petition, and receive automatically generated email notifications on changes to the status of a petition. complainants are increasingly using the internet. 80% of the petitions received in 2014 were sent by email. the commission also found that the union industry's sales volume and market share developed over the period considered as follows: i would like to thank all the members who have contributed to this report. thanks to your involvement, we have been able to produce a fuller report, better reflecting the specific activities of the committee on petitions, and i would now like to hear your views.
madam president, i would like to stress the significance of the annual report on the activities of our committee. it does not only give the full view of what has been done in 2014, but it also represents a possible change for the future in the way we handle the petitions in our committee. the proper treatment of eu citizens who exercise their right to petition is very important: it influences trust in the petitions committee, and it also gives a certain credibility to eu institutions. i support the idea that petitions are the major instrument for our citizens to be more effectively involved in the democratic process of the eu and at eu level. in this regard, i believe that the epp plenary amendments are crucial to this report, because they clearly indicate the obligation to comply with the administrative procedure. this is very important, because we tend to fail to realise that the administrative procedure is very important in our work. these rules are guiding principles in the whole lifecycle of the petition, and this makes the whole mechanism more focused on real results. whatever we do, we have to make sure that we don’t give false hopes to the petitioners. we have to handle the petitions in a more transparent way, we have to make sure that citizens are properly addressed and that their issues are properly addressed in our committee, and we have to reduce the likelihood of politicisation of our agenda. there is still a lot to be done in in our committee, but i am certain that we can win this battle to find a proper definition of the admissibility of petitions. we have to find a good way to explain to petitioners why their petition is inadmissible, and also why their petition needs to be closed at times.
madam president! the committee on petitions exercises the right of citizens of the european union to have recourse to the european parliament in their difficult, everyday matters, as guaranteed by the treaties, provided that they fall within the scope of the european union's activities. the work of the committee on petitions can help to remove obstacles to the implementation of eu law. these tasks and objectives mean that the process of improving the functioning of the committee on petitions is ongoing. the members of the epp group shall be actively involved in this process. the rapporteur has not taken account of one of the amendments proposed by our group, which is to encourage member states to legislate for the establishment of committees on petitions in national parliaments. this issue was discussed in 2015 with the members of the committee on petitions. not all member states' parliaments have such committees in their structures and such a solution would significantly affect the effectiveness of the committee on petitions' cooperation with national parliaments. this would allow the national parliaments to be consulted on matters not falling within the union's remit. another amendment that was not included concerns childcare. after all, not only married parents but also couples living apart from each other have custody of their children. failure to do so can have serious consequences in child custody disputes. an important amendment concerns the length of the petition procedure. as a member of the working group on petitions for children, i object to the artificial maintenance of petitions that we lack competence to deal with. such a state of affairs only increases the delusional hopes of a positive outcome. so i invite you to receive it. the omission of these important amendments makes the report of the committee on petitions' work for 2014 less comprehensive.
member of the commission.– madam president, i would like to express my thanks to ms geringer de oedenberg for her very interesting report. i would also like to take this opportunity to thank those members who have intervened in this morning’s debate for their comments, which i have very carefully noted. the right to petition is a cornerstone of eu citizenship and a fundamental right under the treaty. demonstrating to europe’s citizens that we take their concerns seriously into consideration will serve to strengthen their trust in the european institutions. the commission repeats its commitment to work in close cooperation with the parliament and committee on petitions to ensure the effective and efficient handling of petitions.
the rapporteur. - madam president! - i have to go. as lead rapporteur, i am very pleased to have had the opportunity to produce a report with a group of highly engaged and creative people. it was a fruitful work, which not only shows the current state of the work of the committee, but above all gives guidelines for how to guide its activities in the future. the report aims to further improve the work on petitions. if some of us are critical of some of the conclusions of the report, that is good news. it's a signal of what areas we still have to work on. there is undoubtedly still a lot to do, but each step brings us closer to achieving better results and thus to acting more effectively for our citizens. i would like to thank commissioner avramopoulos for the detailed explanations he has given in connection with my report. the report was a collaborative effort. i would like to thank all the counter-rapporteurs whose suggestions, comments and hints have been very valuable to me, namely the following members: marina albiol, heinz becker, beatriz becerra, eleonora evi, professor notis marias, julia reda. i would also like to thank all the coordinators and advisers, the staff of the committee secretariat involved in the report, including soledad cabezón, vivienne byrne, nicolaidzie khier-koskina, karolina lecocq perez and my personal assistant karolina kocberskaya. i think that despite many initial differences, we were able to come together to produce a solid report with guidelines for the future work of the committee on petitions.
in writing. ‒ stabilisation and association agreements are part of the stabilisation and association process with the eu, which has the western balkan countries at its centre. the eu-kosovo stabilisation and association agreement was signed on 27 october. it is one of the key documents in the stabilisation and association process. it sets out rights and responsibilities and provides a strong incentive for the implementation and institutionalisation of reforms. the stabilisation and association agreement will create opportunities for investment, growth and business development, while strengthening good governance through the application of european standards and harmonisation with eu law, including in the framework of the establishment of a free trade area. i welcomed the recent signing of the stabilisation and association agreement between the european union and kosovo. the agreement is the first step towards european integration for the country. i hope that this agreement with the eu will help stabilise the situation in kosovo and help bring peace between the different ethnic groups and ensure prosperity in the country. with that in mind, i voted to accept the document.
in writing. ‒ as rapporteur for the opinion of the committee on international trade for the committee on foreign affairs on the stabilisation and association agreement between the european union and kosovo, i am very pleased that the european parliament has given its consent to this agreement, which aims to significantly deepen economic and trade relations between the partners. the stabilisation and association agreement is an opportunity for economic development in kosovo, the poorest country in europe. the agreement contained both incentives and commitments to carry out the necessary reforms and create the conditions for new investment and jobs. i hope that the authorities in pristina will use this opportunity to improve the situation of the people of kosovo, where about 40% of the population lives in extreme poverty and unemployment is as high as 30%. it is the only way to try to stop the mass exodus of people from the country that we have seen over the last dozen months.
in writing. ‒ georgia, moldova and ukraine are the three eastern partnership (eap) countries that have signed and ratified association agreements and deep and comprehensive free trade agreements with the eu. all three countries are now implementing their reform plans with varying success and depending on the circumstances. unfortunately, they also face the occupation of parts of their territories in conflicts in which russia plays a key role. in georgia, there are concerns about the independence of the judiciary, repression of political opposition and media freedom (initiated by the government's attempt to take over a television station). moldova is grappling with a deep political crisis that has almost brought reforms to a standstill and could threaten the country's european course. ukraine is engaged in an armed conflict in the east with separatists actively supported by russia. i have always sought to support the european aspirations of the eastern partnership countries and i welcome the progress made by these countries since the signing of the aa and dcfta. i also fully support the territorial integrity of all three states. however, there are still some problems with regard to the above areas which have not allowed me to vote for the adoption of the document. i hope that in the future (near future) all three countries will be free from the aforementioned ailments for the benefit of their people.
in writing. ‒ i fully support the resolution on the association agreements and deep and comprehensive free trade areas with georgia, moldova and ukraine. the efforts made in recent years by the associate countries to adapt their legislation and procedures are of great importance for their future, as they are deepening the process of integration with the eu in economic, legal, social and political terms. however, the geopolitical situation makes maintaining a pro-european stance increasingly challenging; in moldova in particular, the political and economic crisis has deepened and the state has been brought to the brink of bankruptcy. in this context, visa liberalisation between the eu and the eastern partnership countries is one of those concrete benefits that help convince citizens of the good balance of pro-european choice. visa-free travel facilitates contacts and helps to gain experience and develop the infrastructure, communication and business essential for the proper implementation of the association agreements.
in writing. ‒ association agreements and deeper trade agreements are important instruments to support the comprehensive development of european countries outside the european union. political and economic agreements are also a strong impetus for the necessary reforms so that in the long term these countries too can become full members of the community. in a resolution on the evaluation of the implementation of the trade and association agreements with ukraine, georgia and moldova, the european parliament called on the european commission to continue to support the countries in the implementation of the agreements, both technically and financially. he also called for the results of structural and social reforms in the abovementioned countries to be presented. however, it is also important to pay attention to the external aspect of these agreements, and in particular to russia's actions towards the former eastern bloc countries that have entered into closer cooperation with the european union. ukraine, for example, has had a trade agreement with the community since the beginning of the year. russia, convinced that the deal would hurt its interests, decided to impose tariffs and embargoes on ukrainian products, which would have a very negative impact on the weakened ukrainian economy. the other two countries, georgia and moldova, may also be in a similar situation. it is therefore important that the eu focuses its action on a holistic approach to trade and association agreements, without ignoring the geopolitical implications.
our common defence policy should be expressed above all in a common, united position within the atlantic alliance, to which three quarters of our countries belong. of course, it should also be reflected in the mobilization of the atlantic alliance to take greater care of our security. what is stopping us, as three-quarters of nato, from being more concerned about the security of estonia or latvia? if we really want to ensure our common security, it is time to guarantee it by mobilizing the alliance to which we belong, not by declaring on paper or falling into a kind of defensive schizophrenia, where we behave as if we were outside the european union - and before we joined it, or before it was created - and belonged to an alliance that effectively guaranteed our freedom and security.
in writing. ‒ at the meeting of defence ministers in the foreign affairs council on 17 november 2015, france invoked the mutual defence clause for the first time in history to ask other countries for support against the islamic state in syria and iraq and in other missions following the november terrorist attacks in paris. the french president pointed out that france was relying on article 42 (7) and not on the so-called solidarity clause, namely article 222 of the treaty on european union. while the latter opens the way for greater eu involvement, the former operates in an intergovernmental formula, allowing paris to play a greater role. france could also have invoked article 42 (7) to obtain derogations from eu treaty requirements both in specific cases and in general with regard to the budgetary savings imposed by the eu. in view of the lack of coherence between action and law, in the light of the above, and the discussion of two points related to article 42 (7) at the sede meeting on 1 december 2015, it appeared that there was no reason to use this article to promote a greater role for the eu in the field of security and defence. in view of the above, i abstained.
in writing. ‒ poland stands in solidarity with france and declared at the meeting of the defence ministers all assistance to france following the terrorist attacks in paris in accordance with article 42 (7) teu. however, this article only talks about bilateral cooperation and calls for the coordination of security policies by the member states within nato, which remains the foundation of their common defence. i therefore believe that the use of article 42 (7) to strengthen the eu's role in security and defence is contrary to the spirit and the letter of that article. however, in the interest of showing solidarity with france following the terrorist attacks, i abstained.
in writing. ‒ following the november attacks in paris, france decided to invoke the mutual defence clause under article 42 of the treaty on the functioning of the european union to obtain assistance from other eu member states in the fight against the perpetrators of this tragedy. the unanimous support given by the eu member states to paris is crucial to the effectiveness of these efforts, particularly in the area of the exchange of intelligence on the movement of arms, explosives and the movements of terrorism suspects. this exceptional situation can certainly serve as a pretext for creating a more effective platform for cooperation also in the field of border management and police and other law enforcement activities. france's request for assistance in the fight against the so-called islamic state should provide an impetus for closer cooperation on european security and defence and for the high representative for foreign affairs and security policy to develop practical solutions to ensure an effective collective response to similar situations in the future.
in the last two years alone, slovaks, slovenes, croats have been speaking out in national referendums in defense of the natural order of the family, against the political vindication of the homosexual movement being forced upon them. of course, similar provisions are found in the constitutions of hungary and poland or in the ordinary laws of lithuania. and yet today, once again, the european parliament voted to support these reclassifications. instead of representing the position of our countries in the united nations, or even respecting the positions taken by some of our societies in national referendums, the european parliament wants the european union to change us. all of this shows that the biggest threat to democracy in europe today is the policies of the current eu authorities.
in writing. ‒ while the draft resolution made many valid recommendations on eu priorities at unhcr sessions, i voted against the resolution as a whole because i disagree with its basic assumptions on, among other things, eu policy towards the use of the death penalty globally, affirmation of lgbti rights, attempts to extend the use of full reproductive health services and increased pressure on eu member states on migration. it is also unacceptable that the text of the resolution does not expressly mention human rights violations in russia, iran and china.
in writing. ‒ this year's european parliament resolution on the european union's priorities for the un human rights council addresses many important human rights issues in the world, such as the abolition of the death penalty, religious freedom, civil and political rights, the fight against terrorism, and the migration and refugee crisis. although the compromise text of the resolution was negotiated in the final vote, i could not support it because of the wording of a paragraph dealing with a very complex issue, the middle east peace process.
in writing. ‒ the european parliament is firmly of the view that respect for civil and political rights is a hallmark of a democratic, tolerant and pluralistic society. as chair of the ep delegation for relations with belarus, i am committed to speaking out about violations of human rights and democratic values in belarus in the widest possible forum. i am therefore glad that this resolution also refers to the situation in belarus. the european community was relieved to hear of the release of political prisoners in belarus in august 2015. we look forward to their full rehabilitation and restoration of their civil rights. we, along with international observers, watched the presidential elections in october 2015. unfortunately, there are a number of irregularities. free, universal and equal elections should be a fundamental right of all citizens. therefore, we expect the upcoming parliamentary elections to be held in accordance with international standards, which will result in the presence of opposition parties in the belarusian parliament. i would also point out that belarus is the only country in europe that applies the death penalty. parliament consistently expresses its opposition to the use of the death penalty, torture, inhuman and degrading treatment and punishment, and stresses that the abolition of the death penalty contributes to the strengthening of human dignity. i therefore call on the belarusian authorities to agree to a moratorium on the use of the death penalty, which will be the first step towards its total abolition.
in writing. ‒ the committee on petitions is an important tool for citizens to participate more fully in the democratic process at eu level, and it promotes debate and informs and supports citizens about their rights. the aim of the committee on petitions is to provide citizens with direct contact with the institutions and to ensure that they find someone in the institutions who will listen to their specific problems. after hearing the report, i have decided to vote in favour of the document.
in writing. ‒ the report contains a number of good provisions against forced adoption of children (including jugendamt). polish citizens living abroad also face this problem. unfortunately, the report also mentions that all countries should be members of the charter of fundamental rights, of which poland is not a member and does not intend to be. i was not able to vote for the report, so i abstained.
in writing. ‒ the right to petition the european parliament is a fundamental right of every citizen of the european union, and importantly, it is also a right of businesses, organisations and associations established in the european union. the work of the european parliament's committee on petitions is of great importance as it allows civil society to bring to the attention of parliament any cases of violation of their rights by a member state, local authorities or european union institutions. the number of petitions also shows that eu law is still not being properly implemented or respected in many places, which is important information for the european commission, which is the guardian of the eu treaties.

member of the commission.– mr president, i would like to thank mr lange for giving me the possibility to discuss this issue in depth with the honourable members. i am happy to update parliament on where we are on this file. let me start by stressing that the question is not whether china is a market economy or not. it is not – at least not in the way we understand the term. the question is whether the eu should change the method it must follow to calculate dumping in eu anti-dumping investigations. the debate is, as chairman lange said, about the expiry of the 15—year transitional period following china’s accession to the wto and about the application of certain anti-dumping methodologies and the implications for our jobs and our industry. anti—dumping actually only affects 1.38% of all our imports from china, but it can provide essential relief to individual companies or sectors suffering from unfair trading practices, dumping or subsidies. we are, in fact, analysing the three options that that mr lange referred to. first, not to change eu legislation. china obviously expects the eu to apply the wto protocol and change its methodology, as of 11 december this year. not doing so might have an impact on our trade and investment relations, in addition to potential legal challenges. this situation could have a cost for eu business, including in employment terms. these effects are, of course, very difficult, if not impossible, to estimate in advance. we can only speculate. there is a risk that this option would put the eu in breach of wto obligations, with possible economic effects. there are, indeed, different interpretations of section 15 of china’s accession protocol, but there are solid interpretations saying that at least some of the provisions will expire. the second alternative would be to remove china from the list of non—market-economy countries in our legislation without further conditions. this would be economically damaging to many eu industries and politically unrealistic. a preliminary estimation of the effects of this option has been circulated to you in an information note. third, to remove china from the list of market economy countries while, at the same time, introducing mitigating measures by strengthening the eu trade defence instrument to reflect the full extent of the numerous distortions that still exist in the chinese economy, thereby maintaining an effective anti-dumping instrument. we are of course aware that all these options have economic and social impacts and need to be properly assessed. no matter what path we choose, the commission remains committed to maintaining a strong anti-dumping instrument to protect our industry from unfair trade while respecting international obligations. the legal advice we have received indicates that the current method of dumping calculations need to be changed on the date of expiry of the transitional period. even under an alternative interpretation, there is a broad understanding that this so—called analogue country approach, as provided for in our current legislation, cannot be used as such anymore. so these are the basic options. they are all very technically complex and have effects. we are indeed carrying out a deep impact assessment. the paper you received is just a preliminary first assessment. the commitment is, of course, to keep you fully informed. we submitted this paper to you with preliminary findings, and this is part of the transparency we need to have with you. another issue is cooperation with other stakeholders. the commission is in regular contact with our main stakeholders, particularly eu industry, and they have all shared opinions with the commission. regarding the preliminary findings on the impact on eu industry and employment, we have based the study on robust methodology and existing data from the ongoing 52 cases that we have with china for the moment. this study estimates the following potential negative employment effects of changing from the current non-market economy methodology to the normal anti-dumping. they are estimates, and with each scenario it follows that we have made no mitigating measures. so this is the worst-case scenario. in the sectors covered by anti-dumping measures now, we estimate that between 34 000 and 77 000 jobs could be lost. in the longer run, if we look at other sectors that could also be affected, the study points at between 73 000 and 188 000 jobs. if you take into account the possible effects on downstream and upstream industries, we are talking about between 63 000 and 210 000 jobs. this is a lot, and it is important, but it is much lower than suggested by some other studies by, for instance, the washington-based economic policy institute. and, again, these estimations are made without any mitigating factors, so you should bear that in mind. we need to take these risks seriously into account, and this reminds us of the importance of the issue. regarding one of the other questions on coordination with other countries, we are indeed in contact with other partners on this. yet we must bear in mind that all wto members have to abide by their legal commitments and consider appropriate actions. some of our main trading partners do not have to amend their laws. we have to amend our laws, and that takes some time. some countries can make a decision in five minutes, so that makes us a little different from other partners such as the usa, for instance. so we are in a unique situation in that we are the only country that explicitly lists china as a non-market economy for anti-dumping. so should we choose to change our anti-dumping methodology – and we are not there yet, we are assessing all the alternatives, as i said – this would then require a change of legislation. in that legislation, you would of course be full co—legislators. it would be a proposal from the commission to the council and to parliament, so you would have a full say in that process. but we are not there yet, and this is a way to update you on where we are. i am happy to continue this debate to see if there are any remaining questions. thank you again for putting this on the agenda.

madam president! there is no doubt that the phenomenon of unregistered work in the broad sense must be counteracted and even combated. but it would be best if we could create a system where it doesn't pay for the operators to create these kinds of bad practices. the eu platform should therefore also be an impetus for the development of a concrete strategy and the allocation of eu money, measures for the radical reduction of labour costs, i.e. tax breaks, subsidy programmes, employer vouchers, facilitation of labour market regulations, the creation of financial incentives for friendly employment and the strict enforcement of labour law and culture, including a campaign to raise public awareness of the great harm of undeclared work. and that's what i'm calling for.
the platform envisaged in this report can only help to reduce the phenomenon of undeclared work if it actually helps, through the exchange of information and experience, to identify the real, numerous and diverse causes of this phenomenon, and does not attempt to impose a single approach and action on the member states. excessive taxes and other mandatory financial burdens, and sometimes lower wages, are often cited as reasons for remaining in the grey area. but it can also be the lack of legal employment, the high cost of certain services in some countries, and the high wages. the development of the grey area is also contributed by rigid legislation, a justified lack of confidence in the social security system, especially pension schemes, which have been used by some governments in recent times to temporarily supplement the budget and a general lack of interest in law. it is also necessary to look at the actual acceptance of unregistered work among employers and employees. it is primarily the responsibility of the member states to tackle these problems.
madam president, commissioner, i have to ask you to stop. unregistered work is costly economically and socially: it distorts the market, it deprives workers of their rights. that's why this platform is so necessary, but it would be a bad thing if its activities were focused solely on control. many employers and employees take or offer unpaid work out of desperation, poverty, poor regulation, or too much taxation. i therefore call for the various tools to combat undeclared work to focus on transparency of legislation, tax facilitation, reduction of burdens on employers and the preparation and streamlining of legislation on temporary, additional and seasonal work. better regulations are particularly needed in the domestic work market, which is dominated by women and is very difficult to control because it would disturb the peace of the home. there are good examples of how to solve this dilemma: we have a well-functioning voucher system in belgium, in france. and that's why we should go in that direction. i'm not going to let you down. the domestic work market will grow rapidly because of europe's ageing population, because of the increased retirement age, because of the longer presence of women in the labour market, because of the capitalist pension system. that's why it's so important to prepare the regulations for this market. in summary, clear rules, ease for businesses, and then control.
the issue of undeclared work and shadow employment affects all member states, and although they have the greatest competence in preventing and discouraging it, i am convinced that action at european union level is equally desirable and can bring good results. unregistered work has a negative impact on member states' budgets and administrations. however, it should not be forgotten that this is primarily a social problem, with a negative impact on the professional, social and family life of many millions of our citizens. the complex nature of the problem of undeclared work means that only cooperation between partners at all levels can contribute to its solution. i think the platform's responsibilities have been well defined. it has been given specific tasks, while respecting the principle of subsidiarity. i am also pleased that the social partners have been included and recognised as members. i hope that the platform will be a place for real cooperation between partners and will be able to develop common strategies for law enforcement.
mr president, commissioner, i have to ask you to stop this. the harmful phenomenon of tax avoidance by firms using aggressive instruments is draining budget revenues in the member states of the european union and is a source of unfair competition between firms. i agree that attempts to solve this problem by individual countries are not working. i therefore welcome the commission's proposal to radically reduce the scale of this phenomenon by adopting a legislative package comprising a draft directive against tax avoidance and a draft amendment to the directive on administrative cooperation. the commission is proposing six specific instruments to curb aggressive planning. these include limiting the tax deductibility of financial costs, eliminating double taxation, controlling foreign branches set up to transfer profits and controlling the transfer of assets abroad, and prohibiting the tax deduction of certain intra-corporate flows. these lines of action deserve support, especially as they are consistent with the g20 and oecd guidelines developed under the beps programme. however, i would like to make it clear that they must be compatible with the treaties, and in particular with the principles of subsidiarity and proportionality. in particular, there can be no question of harmonising tax rates. the measures adopted must not in any way affect the sovereign right of the member states to determine the level of taxation. they should also not unduly restrict the freedom of action of undertakings and impose additional administrative burdens on them.

in writing. ‒ having examined the commission proposal for regulation no 562/2006, it should be noted that this is an important amendment aimed at giving the eu another power that has previously belonged to individual community countries, namely the protection of its own borders. this can be indirectly inferred from the change in the wording of recital 19, which is worded as follows: as the objective of regulation (ec) no 562/2006 and subsequent acts amending it, namely to establish rules applicable to the movement of persons across borders, could not be sufficiently achieved by the member states and could be better achieved at union level, the union could adopt measures in accordance with the principle of subsidiarity as set out in article 5 of the treaty on european union. in accordance with the principle of proportionality, as set out in that article, that regulation and the subsequent acts amending it did not go beyond what was necessary to achieve that objective. the new provision in recital 19 of the regulation seems to be a further step in the implementation of the idea of establishing a common border guard to protect the eu's borders, which is intended to stem, among other things, the wave of illegal immigration into the community countries. the new entity is intended to replace the current frontex agency based in warsaw. france and germany have been advocating the creation of a common eu border guard for years. i do not agree with the amendment which provides for the eu to be given control over the protection of its borders in the long term, which in practice means giving the eu a considerable degree of sovereignty over the member states.
in writing. ‒ i support the draft regulation on the movement of persons across borders in the european union. however, it should be stressed that this document does not introduce any new substantive solutions, but only unifies the provisions concerning the so-called schengen area, which have been frequently amended in recent years. the functioning of the schengen area is one of the pillars of the european union. these rules allow eu citizens to move freely within europe. border controls carried out by one union state shall be carried out in the interest of all member states. this imposes a specific obligation on the eu country issuing the travel document. border checks should therefore always be carried out in a professional manner and with respect for the persons checked. the unification of the text will undoubtedly make it easier for the border services of the european union countries to work.
in writing. ‒ emissions of heavy metals and persistent organic pollutants affect human health and the environment around us. effective emission control requires international cooperation. both protocols list best available techniques for reducing emissions and reporting requirements, national emission limits and emission limits for different types of projects. the 1979 heavy metals protocol aims to reduce and control anthropogenic emissions of lead, cadmium and mercury to reduce respiratory and cardiovascular diseases, as well as biodiversity and agricultural production losses due to heavy metals. the second protocol aims to reduce and eliminate the discharge and emission of persistent organic pollutants, which include chemicals such as ddt and pollutants such as dioxins. the 2012 amendments to the metals protocol introduce stricter limits for dust emissions from certain stationary sources of emissions, as well as flexible provisions to allow for the entry into force of these amendments. the amendments to the second protocol, established in 2009, add new substances and supplement the provisions on existing substances. current eu legislation is in line with these amendments. since the ratification of the amendments by the eu will be a step towards their entry into force and will encourage other states parties to the united nations economic commission for europe (unece) to sign them, i voted in favour of the resolution.
in writing. ‒ amendments to the 1998 protocol to the 1979 convention on long-range transboundary air pollution on heavy metals, persistent organic pollutants. pollution by heavy metals is one of the most important threats to human health and the environment. respiratory and cardiovascular diseases are common in europe today, and recent scientific research has confirmed a significant link between the levels of heavy metals in the food we eat and the air we breathe and mortality from cancers, which are fast becoming the next civilized disease of our time. the same factors are causing huge losses in agricultural production and biodiversity. i am therefore convinced that raising the limits for emissions of heavy metals and persistent organic pollutants into the atmosphere, as well as updating the list of harmful metals, will significantly improve the quality of the environment and allow for the reconstruction and development of agriculture, thus positively affecting the health and lives of europeans.
in writing. ‒ emissions of heavy metals and persistent organic pollutants affect human health and the environment. these substances do not respect national borders and therefore international cooperation is required to control their emissions effectively. the two 1998 protocols list the best available techniques (bat) for emission reductions and their reporting requirements, national emission limits and emission limits for specific types of projects. in other words, they set up the tools to enable emissions reductions and to track progress. the heavy metals protocol aims to reduce and control anthropogenic emissions of lead, cadmium and mercury to reduce respiratory and cardiovascular diseases, as well as biodiversity and agricultural production losses due to heavy metals. i supported the report because of the importance of the record for the health of the citizens.
in writing. ‒ the convention on long-range transboundary air pollution aims to protect the environment and human life. research shows that air pollutants can travel thousands of miles before they reach the earth, and international action is needed to address these issues. the 1979 convention was the first legally binding international instrument in this field. it has established a framework to control and reduce the harm to human health and the environment caused by transboundary air pollution. however, almost 40 years after its signature, it is necessary to adapt to changes in both the economy and, above all, the environment. the latest amendment to the 1998 protocol, agreed in 2012, is the first to cover both a number of pollutants and their multiple effects, and to include specific national emission ceilings and reduction commitments for different types of pollutants. these actions should contribute to enhancing the protection of health and the environment.

in writing. ‒ the report concerns the proposed approval of the cooperation agreement between eurojust and ukraine to enhance judicial cooperation in the fight against serious crime, in particular organised crime and terrorism. the draft agreement contains provisions on operational cooperation between eurojust and ukraine, such as the secondment of a liaison officer to eurojust by ukraine and the exchange of information, including personal data. in accordance with article 26a (2) of the council decision of 28 february 2002 setting up eurojust, as last amended by council decision 2009/426/jha of 16 december 2008, it is for the council, acting by a qualified majority, to approve agreements concluded by eurojust with third countries or international organisations. i support the conclusion of this cooperation agreement with ukraine as it will support and strengthen the fight against serious crime and contribute to improving judicial cooperation, in particular in the area of organised crime and terrorism.

mr. chairman, please! i voted in favour of the creation of a european platform to improve cooperation on the prevention of undeclared work. available data show that on average 8% and in some countries up to 20% of europeans receive undeclared wages for their work. another 10% or more work without the necessary contracts. this shows that gray area work is still too common in europe. many people are unaware of the long-term consequences of such a practice. low official salaries and illegal employment not only mean lower revenues for the state budget and local government units, but above all, drastically reduce the amount of old age pension and cause lack of health care. the prevalence of this phenomenon may lead to a higher number of elderly people living in poverty in the union in the future. we must not forget that the problems of illegal employment or wages are varied, often depending on local specificities. specific actions to combat grey areas must therefore be undertaken at the lowest possible level and adapted to local requirements.
in writing. ‒ the european commission's proposal aims to create a platform that will facilitate the exchange of best practice and information and develop a common approach to undeclared work. i support the creation of such a platform, which i believe facilitates cross-border cooperation and knowledge exchange between law enforcement agencies. i voted for the party.
in writing. ‒ the problem of unregistered work is a very complex one. the very definition of this issue presents some difficulties, as it may concern both profit-making activities which have not been declared to the competent authorities and self-employment which has been declared but does not actually exist (i.e. the declared activity is not carried on). the avoidance of proper registration is usually the result of a desire to avoid taxation. to counter this phenomenon, the eu's legislative institutions are proposing the creation of a european platform to facilitate cooperation in the prevention of undeclared work. the platform is primarily intended to collect and exchange reliable information, joint planning and implementation of procedures. active action is necessary, especially given that the level of undeclared work in the member states is not decreasing and that therefore many citizens are still strongly motivated to practice and disseminate this practice. the proactive policy mentioned by the rapporteur seems to be the right approach, aimed at reaching out to those europeans who are moving in the so-called grey area and encouraging them to register their activities or change industries. understanding the problem, identifying the reasons and motivations of citizens who avoid registration, and then proposing solutions and encouraging honesty is the best way to deal with this practice.
in writing. ‒ i support the idea of setting up a platform for unregistered work and the method of action set out in the report. although the debate on the report was dominated by the voices for more effective control, i believe that the focus of the platform will be on preventing unregistered work, not on controlling it. this is particularly important in the fast-growing domestic work sector, which is predominantly female, often migrant, and which is difficult to control because it is carried out on private property and employs a private person. the experience of belgium and france shows that a successful solution could be to extend and universalise cheque systems to include care, education and welfare services. care services are particularly important because they cannot be postponed or abandoned: this is a key barrier to women's access to the labour market and the number one reason for their being pushed into a grey area, as workers and employers. finding the right solutions in the form of clear legislation, tax incentives and incentives will not only bring thousands of women out of the gray area, giving them social protection and contributions to their pensions, but will also help to reconcile work and family roles. this will strengthen the institution of the family and the economic independence of women.
in writing. ‒ unregistered work is a very common phenomenon in europe, which leads to the exploitation of workers, deprives national budgets of significant revenues, persistent market distortions and the principles of fair competition, thus weakening the eu-wide economy. the fact that unregistered work is not confined to the borders of one country makes cooperation within the european union all the more important. the establishment of a platform involving all eu member states can contribute to the fight against undeclared work and to the development of a coherent approach to the issue of combating undeclared work. the platform should therefore lead to the exchange of information and best practices between national institutions such as employment promotion agencies, tax authorities and immigration authorities, while involving the economic and social partners. however, there is no doubt that it will be necessary to carry out a thorough assessment of the extent to which such a form of cooperation between the european commission and member states' authorities serves the objectives set out in the decision of the european parliament and of the council and whether the benefits of such a form of cooperation justify the costs associated with the functioning of the platform.
in writing. ‒ the functioning of the employment grey area is detrimental to economic growth, worker safety and the stability of the social benefits system. the high level of mobility in the european union is conducive to this phenomenon, especially in a cross-border context. closer cooperation between the national labour market monitoring authorities and inspectorates in the different member states is a necessary and welcome step. the establishment of a platform to improve cooperation on the prevention and deterrence of undeclared work is intended to develop best practices and joint initiatives to combat undeclared work more effectively. this will guarantee the independence of the national authorities, whose competences will not be reduced, and will allow the efforts of the member states and the social partners (including employers' and workers' organisations) and international institutions to be combined. the main tasks of this platform will be to define many phenomena that are perceived differently in different member states, to ensure the rapid exchange of information on cases of breaches of the law and to create a system of incentives for employers to register workers who use unregistered work. we must remember that the greatest victims of the grey area are the unregistered workers themselves, whose rights to limited hours, social benefits or insurance against workplace accidents cannot be enforced. they're the ones we need to protect first.
in writing. ‒ the report notes with concern the overall trend towards biodiversity loss and calls on the commission and the member states to make this a political priority in order to achieve the 2020 targets. the proposed measures should include the integration of biodiversity into other policy areas such as agriculture and forestry, an increase in the number of natura 2000 sites with management plans and an eu action plan on wildlife trade. at this point, it should be noted that environmental policy and economic development are not mutually exclusive, with the alternative socioeconomic cost of not meeting the 2020 targets estimated at eur 50 billion per year, and one in six jobs in the eu being dependent to some extent on nature and biodiversity. in view of the above, i have voted in favour of the relevant document.
in writing. ‒ the commission's review of biodiversity can make a decisive contribution to halting biodiversity loss and, above all, to increasing the european union's commitment to global biodiversity. i share the rapporteur's concern about the growing trend towards biodiversity loss. i would also like to point out that statistics show that one in six jobs in the european union depends on biodiversity and nature. unfortunately, i cannot fully support the mid-term review of the eu biodiversity strategy and all the solutions it proposes, because i am strongly opposed to the attempt to ban shale gas extraction, which is why i was forced to abstain from voting on this text.
in writing. ‒ europe's biodiversity is at risk. more than three quarters of important natural habitats in the union are in very poor condition and many animal and plant species are threatened with extinction. this is why the eu adopted a strategy in 2011 with the main objective of halting biodiversity loss by 2020. restoring natural ecosystems and protecting the environment are among the most important challenges facing the eu today. today, when the mid-term review of the adopted and implemented plan is being carried out, it is necessary to emphasise the need to put into practice what has been agreed and accepted by the member states. the first priority is to improve the application of environmental laws in the various areas. the european commission monitors and assesses the performance of countries in meeting the strategy's objectives and, as it says, while the current implementation results show improvements in many areas, the eu countries must continue to work to fully meet their commitments. environmental issues are close to our citizens, as the polls show, and the european union remains a world leader in biodiversity conservation.
in writing. ‒ in october 2015, the commission published a mid-term review of the eu's biodiversity strategy, analysing progress towards halting the loss of biodiversity and ecosystem services by 2020, restoring ecosystems where possible and increasing the eu's commitment to preventing global biodiversity loss. the mid-term review concluded that this objective can only be achieved if implementation and enforcement efforts are much bolder and more ambitious. parliament noted with concern the general trend towards biodiversity loss and called on the commission and the member states to make this a political priority in order to achieve the 2020 targets. the proposed measures include the integration of biodiversity into other policy areas such as agriculture and forestry, an increase in the number of natura 2000 sites with management plans and an eu action plan on wildlife trade. parliament also stressed that environmental policy and economic development are not mutually exclusive, with the alternative socio-economic cost of not meeting the 2020 targets estimated at eur 50 billion per year and one in six jobs in the eu being dependent to some extent on nature and biodiversity. since the adoption of paragraph 88 calling for the cessation of shale gas extraction, i abstained from voting
in writing. ‒ the protection and promotion of biodiversity is reflected in eu legislation, which is continuously committed to further strengthening the convention on biological diversity and its implementation. in this context, it is particularly important to maintain political commitment not only at the eu legislative level but also at the regional and local level in the member states, as these have the greatest potential and opportunities to inform and raise public awareness of biodiversity. in addition to the obvious environmental benefits, biodiversity conservation also has a very clear economic importance, especially when one in six jobs in the eu is dependent to some extent on nature and biodiversity, as this report shows. it is worth noting that agriculture plays a very important role in this context, which can be both extremely beneficial and detrimental if certain standards are not respected. good, sustainable farming practices can make a huge contribution to the conservation and protection of habitats, the containment of land degradation, the rational management of water resources, which can lead to effective climate change mitigation and the development of beneficial consumption patterns, while also serving important educational functions for those parts of society that are not in contact with nature and agriculture or forestry on a daily basis.
in writing. ‒ i voted in favour of the european parliament's draft resolution on the eu strategy for the protection of biological diversity. this strategy is an important part of the european union's overall strategy for the environment, society and the economy. to make the strategy a reality, heads of state or government have set a core objective of halting the loss of biodiversity and the degradation of ecosystem services. i agree with the proposed formula of the strategy, which is based on six pillars, each with its own objectives: full implementation of the birds and habitats directive; maintaining and restoring ecosystems and their functions; increasing the contribution of agriculture and forestry to the maintenance and enhancement of biodiversity; ensuring the sustainable use of fisheries resources; combating invasive alien species; and increasing the eu's commitment to preventing global biodiversity loss. the adopted report also envisages the implementation of additional innovative solutions, such as the trans-european green infrastructure network ten-g, which can bring mutual benefits for society, the environment and the economy. according to the eurobarometer on biodiversity, at least 8 out of 10 citizens stress that the consequences for biodiversity loss are serious. the survey also shows that citizens want to be informed about this issue on a regular basis. as has been rightly noted, nature and biodiversity are of great importance to citizens. i agree with the thesis that biodiversity and the environment must be at the heart of a smart, sustainable and integrated europe.
in writing. ‒ on 2 february 2016, a vote was held on the report by mr demesmaeker on the 'mid-term review of the eu biodiversity strategy', the european commission's report on the implementation of the eu biodiversity strategy by 2020. the objective of the european biodiversity strategy for 2020 is to halt and restore as much as possible by 2020 biodiversity loss and degradation of ecosystem services and to contribute to the prevention of global biodiversity loss. there is no doubt that biodiversity must be protected, since it affects the sustainability of ecosystems in which humans are an integral part. the draft resolution by mr demesmaeker was well balanced and correctly identified the issues in the eu's biodiversity strategy. unfortunately, the final version of the bill included a ban on shale gas extraction. i do not think there is any basis for claiming that shale gas extraction is more risky than other industrial activities. i did not vote for the whole report because of the wording.
in writing. ‒ i abstained in the vote on this report, which is the european parliament's response to the commission's mid-term review of the eu biodiversity strategy in 2015. while the general direction of this report is correct and i agree with it on many points, the content of article 88, which calls for a total ban on the use of hydraulic fracturing by member states, is unacceptable. biodiversity and ecosystem balance is not only an ecological issue, but also has an economic dimension, as one in six jobs in the eu depends on nature and a clean environment. this is particularly the case in sectors such as agriculture and tourism, which from poland's point of view are key sectors of the economy. however, proposals as far-reaching as banning shale gas extraction could threaten the future energy security of poland and many countries in our region. this is all the more unacceptable since there is no convincing scientific evidence of the environmental harmfulness of hydraulic fracturing. economic development is largely dependent on its own cheap energy. poland has a large potential for shale gas extraction and must be able to exploit this potential. in the face of the eu's decarbonisation policy, we cannot accept another reduction in our energy independence.

in writing. the potential withdrawal of certain active substances from plant protection products is the implementation of a regulation of the european parliament and of the council. endocrine disruptors, as we're talking about, are substances that have a potentially large impact on the environment. on the one hand, some of them pose potential risks to human health, some of them are carcinogenic, for example. they can also be a threat to wildlife: they can affect reproduction (they reduce the fertility of fish when they enter the water) or even cause the extinction of some species (the link between ed and the mass extinction of bees is being investigated). on the other hand, they are very effective and their use reduces the use of plant protection products in general. a total ban on their use could mean large crop losses due to the lack of effective alternative measures. there is also a risk that some farmers will start to unofficially import products, for example from ukraine, whose composition and harmfulness will not be known. in order to effectively protect the environment and at the same time not to impose a disproportionate burden on farmers, the assessment criteria should be revised so that not all active substances are included in the category of endocrine disruptors, but only those that have a negative impact on the environment and human health.
in writing. if we misdefined the criteria for endocrine disruptors, thereby preventing the use of extremely useful and safe plant protection products, we would cause enormous harm to our farmers. the deprivation of them - or rather of us, as a farmer myself - of the necessary tools will seriously reduce the productivity of agricultural production, reduce the competitiveness of european agriculture and lead to a fall in incomes. moreover, the reduction in investment in the plant protection industry will result in job losses and also, to some extent, in the suppression of scientific research carried out by industry representatives in conjunction with independent organisations. i strongly believe that we should establish criteria to define substances that are actually dangerous. however, first we need to carry out comprehensive, thorough studies to provide a full risk assessment of the use of hormonally active substances in protective and biocidal products. innovation in agriculture is very much needed, but development must be done sensibly, after careful consideration of the possible implications of legislative decision-making. the european commission's proposal to amend the legislation in the light of the partial results of the analyses seems to be a bad idea, which could complicate procedures and disrupt the functioning of the european market. let us wait until the full evaluation of the effects of endocrine disruptors is completed and then consider the appropriate legal regulation.

in writing. the next european summit will address the two most pressing issues in the eu today, namely the negotiations with the uk and the migration crisis. how and whether we meet these challenges will be crucial to the future of the european project. earlier this week, president tusk presented his proposal for changes to change the uk's attitude towards the eu. this is certainly a good basis for compromise, but much will depend on whether we can avoid a situation in which too much privilege for the uk will lead to an avalanche of claims from other member states. in this situation, integration can be reduced to a "menu" at best, and at worst, it can be disintegrated. the position of the so-called new member states, which have serious reservations about the restrictions on social benefits for immigrants demanded by london, will also be relevant. the migration crisis, which is now somewhat subsided by the winter, but which is certain to return with increased intensity in the spring, is certainly a greater threat to the community. recently, there has been a new approach to refugees among western european countries, such as sweden, which has started to send back people who do not meet the conditions for asylum. if this process is intensified, and perhaps combined with some form of financial support for the refugees being returned, it is likely to dampen the tide of new arrivals.
in writing. in the context of the upcoming european council summit, which will focus in large part on migration, i would like to draw particular attention to the use of the earth observation satellite systems developed in the eu in the field of internal security of the member states. to deal effectively with the millions of asylum seekers in europe, it is crucial to have reliable information on, for example, the number of people moving within the eu's external borders. the system that can provide this information is already in place in the eu. this is the copernicus earth observation satellite system. one of the five copernicus priority actions is border surveillance, border traffic, maritime traffic, and support for the eu's external action. satellites collect radar and optical data on both the sea and land. they cover national borders, coastlines or transport routes that are critical to security. in this way, copernicus is able to provide comprehensive information on migration movements. the key is to make good use of the information received, to coordinate actions and thus to cooperate more effectively between member states, and to support the further development of the programme, which will allow us to respond more quickly to potential crises in the future.
in writing. ‒ the association agreement with moldova of june 2014 includes a bilateral safeguard clause. the agreement provides, inter alia, for a so-called anti-circumvention mechanism, which allows the most-favoured-country duty rate to be reintroduced in the event that imports of certain agricultural products, vegetables and beverages from moldova exceed a certain threshold without duly justifying their exact origin. a regulation of the european parliament and of the council is needed to introduce into the internal legal order of the eu the instrument necessary to apply the bilateral safeguard clause and the mechanism to prevent customs duties from being circumvented. given the value of the eu's relations with moldova, i voted in favour of its adoption.
in writing. ‒ the proposal on the application of the safeguard clause and the anti-circumvention mechanism to the republic of moldova plays a very important role in the commission's trade policy. the association agreement with moldova protects the european union's industry without exposing it to economic losses. the republic of moldova, which is not a member of the european union, should supply agricultural products, vegetables and beverages without exceeding certain thresholds, as well as with a full justification of the exact origin of the products in question. i fully support the above proposal of the european parliament and the council and i support the obligation for the commission to report on the application and implementation of the regulation.
in writing. ‒ the association agreement with moldova signed in june 2014 includes a bilateral safeguard clause. this instrument allows preferences to be temporarily suspended if their application leads to an unexpected and significant increase in imports causing economic losses to the eu industry. in addition, the scheme also provides for a so-called anti-circumvention mechanism, which allows the most-favoured-country duty rate to be reintroduced in the event that imports of certain agricultural products, vegetables and beverages from moldova exceed a certain threshold without duly justifying their exact origin. a regulation of the european parliament and of the council is needed to introduce into the internal legal order of the eu the instrument necessary to apply the bilateral safeguard clause and the mechanism to prevent customs duties from being circumvented. the report emphasises in particular the commission's reporting obligation, under which the commission submits to the co-authors and subsequently publishes an annual report on the application and implementation of the regulation. reporting is important for parliamentary scrutiny of the commission's implementation of the common commercial policy and for enhancing its transparency. i hereby endorse the report.
in writing. ‒ the association agreement with georgia of june 2014 contains a so-called anti-circumvention mechanism which allows the most-favoured-country duty rate to be reintroduced if imports of certain agricultural products from georgia listed in annex ii-c to the agreement exceed a certain threshold without duly justifying their exact origin. the commission may decide to suspend temporarily the preferential customs duties applicable to the products concerned or to decide that such suspension is not appropriate. the temporary suspension of preferential duties shall apply for a maximum period of six months from the date of publication of the decision suspending the preferential duties. in order to introduce into the internal legal order of the eu the instrument necessary to apply the abovementioned anti-circumvention mechanism, a regulation of the european parliament and of the council is needed.

in writing. ‒ according to who, there are 314 million blind and partially sighted people in the world today. the polish blind union has about 60,000 members. at the same time, it is estimated that there are 300,000 people in poland who cannot read the printed page. this is a very important issue not only for our society, but also a global issue. the resolution, drawn up by the peti committee, calls for and appeals for the speedy ratification of the treaty, without having to wait for the ruling of the court of justice of the eu, given the importance of the treaty for blind and partially sighted persons and persons with print disabilities, and the fact that waiting for the ruling of the court of justice would significantly delay ratification. i fully support the motion for a resolution tabled by mr de gucht and i voted in favour.
in writing. ‒ the marrakesh treaty was adopted on 28 june 2013 at the diplomatic conference of the world intellectual property organisation (wipo). the aim was to establish an international standard for the use of copyrighted works by blind and visually impaired persons. in europe, there are 2 550 000 blind people and 23 800 000 visually impaired people, which equals more than 26 million citizens concerned about these changes. yet eu member states are delaying ratification of the treaty, and seven countries at council level are actually hindering the process. in many countries, including poland, there is legislation providing for facilitated access to works by the blind and visually impaired (in formats adapted to their needs), but this currently covers only 5% of publications in developed countries and less than 1% in developing countries. the eu and its member states signed the marrakesh treaty in april 2014 and have thus committed themselves to ratify it. furthermore, articles 24 and 30 of the un convention emphasise the right of persons with disabilities to education without discrimination and on the basis of equal opportunities, while ensuring that copyright protection provisions do not constitute an unjustified barrier to access to cultural materials. the vote today is a call to the european parliament to ratify the treaty by all the member states of the european union without delay and to bring its provisions into force as soon as possible.
in writing. ‒ i supported the resolution on the ratification of the marrakesh treaty on the facilitation of access to published works for blind, visually impaired and other print disabled persons. the entry into force of this treaty represents an opportunity for 30 million europeans to have easier access to publications in accessible formats for the visually impaired, and thus to increase their participation in education, cultural and social life and, in general, to improve their quality of life. according to article 14 of the charter of fundamental rights of the european union, 'everyone has the right to education and to have access to vocational and continuing training'. it is therefore our task to take urgent action to ensure that people with disabilities can fully enjoy their rights in this area. i would stress that this is a case of fundamental rights for these people, not some additional rights. given that only a small percentage of books worldwide are adapted to the needs of disabled people, it is necessary to facilitate access to and increase the current collections. the marrakesh treaty gives us that opportunity, and i therefore urge you once again to ratify it as soon as possible and to bring it into force.
in writing. ‒ at its meeting on 17 september 2015, the peti committee heard petition no 924/2011, by dan pescod (uk) on behalf of the european blind union (ebu) and the royal national institute of blind people (rnib), on access to books and other printed materials for blind people. in view of the numerous petitions on this subject, the peti members expressed their concern at the lack of approval by the council of the european union of the ratification of the marrakesh treaty on the facilitation of access to published printed works for blind and partially sighted persons and persons with print disabilities (marrakesh treaty). although many eu member states have already implemented the treaty, seven have not yet done so. the resolution calls for the treaty to be ratified more quickly without waiting for the court of justice of the eu to give its ruling, given the importance of the treaty for blind and partially sighted persons and persons with print disabilities, and the fact that waiting for the court of justice to give its ruling would significantly delay ratification. i hereby endorse the report.
in writing. ‒ participation in cultural life remains one of the key elements of community life. the world intellectual property organisation's treaty on the facilitation of access to published works of printed matter for blind and partially sighted persons and persons with print disabilities focuses on the right to participate in cultural life and the rights of users as such and aims to establish an international standard for the use of works of printed matter protected by copyright by persons with visual disabilities. according to who, there are 285 million people in the world today who are visually impaired. despite the fact that many countries have laws to facilitate access to works by blind and partially sighted people, less than 5% of the world's printed publications are accessible in accessible formats. the need to accept the marrakesh treaty is therefore urgent. the treaty requires ratification by both the european union and the signatory countries and will require the introduction or adaptation of a number of provisions. however, it should also be emphasised that the need to ensure satisfactory, more complete access to printed materials for visually impaired persons should go hand in hand with the protection of the interests of publishers in the production and distribution of printed formats of works.
in writing. ‒ we voted today on the motions for resolutions in which the european parliament opposes the european commission's executive decisions allowing the placing on the market of products containing genetically modified soybean varieties. as we know, the main ingredient in feed is protein, mainly contained in soybean meal. however, despite the increasing production of soybeans in the european union, we are not able to meet the demand for high-protein feed components necessary for animal production. the commission also found that the union industry was not able to compete with the union industry in the union market. almost all imported soybeans are genetically modified, which is about 30% cheaper than unmodified soybeans. the conclusion is therefore very simple: if we prevent the import of cheaper soybeans, without being able to produce enough to meet our own needs, the european union will be forced to import much more expensive soybeans or to increase imports of meat that has been produced using genetically modified soybeans. the european economy will suffer severe losses, farmers will lose their income and consumers will end up consuming products containing genetically modified organisms anyway. i therefore do not support the objection prepared by the committee on the environment, public health and food safety, because i believe that europe should use the latest scientific developments to develop its agriculture and compete internationally, while ensuring food security for its citizens.
in writing. ‒ i voted against the resolution opposing the possibility of trade in products containing fg72 modified soybean, because the content of this resolution is a threat to the interests of polish farmers. genetically modified soybeans are a rich source of protein and an important component of feed used in poultry farming. poland, as the largest poultry producer in the region, has a chance to maintain its position only if competitive conditions for producers are maintained. the gmo scientific panel of the european food safety authority (efsa) has published three scientific opinions on the safety assessment of, inter alia, genetically modified soybean fg72 and soybean mon 87705 × mon 89788, confirming the safety of both grains for health and the environment compared to their unmodified counterparts. however, gm soybeans are cheaper and thus their availability affects the competitiveness of agricultural production.
in writing. ‒ i voted against the resolution opposing the possibility of trade in products containing modified soybean mon 87708 x mon 89788, as it is in the interest of polish farmers to retain the possibility of buying soybean components for feed. only about 10% of the feed used is more expensive organic feed. the ban on the purchase of cheaper genetically engineered feed and its components would hit polish poultry producers first and would have a negative impact on poultry exports, in which poland is a leader.
