in writing. ‒ real driving emissions (rde) testing is to be introduced as a new requirement for the type-approval of new cars and vans as an additional laboratory test. the rde aims to provide real-world vehicle emission control and thus to solve the problem of high nitrogen oxide (nox) emissions from diesel vehicles and to eliminate the use of defeat devices, which occurred in the case of vw. the main reason why countries do not meet their airborne nox limits is that diesel vehicles emit significantly more under real-world conditions than under laboratory conditions. the introduction of rde tests will reduce the average nox emissions from these engines and help countries to meet their requirements, e.g. under the nec directive. looking at the document in question, i share the concerns of politicians from other groups, particularly those concerning the path to rde by a compliance factor of 2.1. the tests currently required by the commission have remained unchanged for almost thirty years. in view of the above, i supported the objection in the document.
in writing. ‒ i voted against the resolution of the envi parliamentary committee calling for the withdrawal of the draft ec regulation on urea emissions while driving (rde). the occurrence of increased nox with a significant reduction in co2 emissions by pe, greater than for petrol engines, was unexpected and was incremental rather than linear, resulting from exceeding a certain temperature threshold in the combustion chambers of diesel engines. the commission is right to take the time to remedy this clear defect. so i think by 2019, that emissions should be equivalent to what euro 5 diesel engines were. the ec project gives the car companies time to develop appropriate technical solutions. this is a realistic solution that will save the continuity of diesel engine production with great, promising potential.
in writing. ‒ i voted against the resolution for several important reasons, namely: i consider it scientifically incorrect to assume a linear increase in co2 and nox reductions in parallel, scientific opinions convincingly prove the absence of such a rule; convincing are the commission's statements on the revision of the way emissions are measured and the new timetable. i welcome with great hope and expectation the commission statement by commissioner e. bieńkowska.
in writing. ‒ the problem of the discrepancy between the laboratory and everyday emissions of passenger cars with diesel engines has caused a huge stir in both europe and the us. the lack of adequate tools to detect abuse and fraud in the approval process of new car models has caused a scandal that the european parliament will be looking into. the adoption of this objection will only delay the introduction of the obligation to test cars in real driving conditions. not only does this delay not necessarily lead to better solutions, but it may lead to further abuse by the automotive companies. the proposed standard allowing diesel cars to exceed the laboratory emissions of nitrogen oxides by 2,1 times in normal operation by 2017 and to achieve full compliance of both laboratory and real-world emissions by 2020 seems to be a reasonable proposal. the regulation also provides for some flexibility and an annual review of the proposed standards to better match existing legislation to the actions and efforts of the automotive industry. in deciding to adopt the proposed standards, however, we must bear in mind that concern for the environment cannot mean ignoring economic factors, including the functioning of such an important sector for the european economy and labour market as the automotive industry.
in writing. ‒ the tisa agreement provides the community with an opportunity to strengthen its position as the world's largest exporter of services with a 25% share of the global services market and a positive trade balance of eur 170 billion in 2013. the report adopted today was designed to assess the first two and a half years and 13 rounds of negotiations on the trade in services agreement (tisa). from the initial 16 parties, the agreement has been extended to 24 parties, including the eu, which in turn represents 28 countries. in total, 51 countries will be involved in the agreement: 32 in europe, 7 in asia, 10 in the americas and 2 in oceania. the aim of the agreement is to liberalize international trade in services such as banking, health care and transport. services account for 75% of the value of the us economy, and the european union does the same. the value of eu services exports has doubled over the last ten years, reaching eur 728 billion in 2014. in addition, the services sector employs 70% of the eu's workforce and generates 40% of the value of goods exported from europe. the agreement has the potential to further stimulate job creation in the eu. it is estimated that 90% of the new jobs that will be created in the eu by 2025 will be in the services sector.
in writing. ‒ most people have never heard of the trade in services agreement (tisa). it is an agreement on trade in services to which the 50 member states of the wto (world trade organisation), including 28 eu countries, are parties. the countries involved in the agreement account for 70% of the world market for services. the formal negotiations, held in geneva, began in the spring of 2013 and remained secret from the general public, despite the fact that some of the documents appeared on the website wikileaks in april 2014. as one might expect, the incident immediately triggered a wave of criticism of the agreement. the main objective of the agreement is liberalisation in the services sector: opening up markets and improving rules in areas such as financial services, telecommunications, online trade, maritime transport and the movement of workers to provide services abroad. each party shall make its proposals and take an active part in the negotiations. the european union is a leader in the export and import of services on the world market, and we therefore seek to regulate the legislation on international trade in services as best as possible. the report analyses the negotiations so far and calls for greater rights for consumers in the agreement, while also hoping that the agreement will eventually guarantee respect for community standards and the rights of workers.
in writing. ‒ the global economy is now a system of interconnected vessels. while wto agreements ensure very low tariffs for international trade in goods and thus contribute to an increase in trade, there are still many tariff barriers in the services sector. the negotiations on tisa, which have been ongoing since 2012, aim to change this and liberalise trade in services in areas such as banking, medicine and transport. a broad consensus on this issue is necessary because highly developed non-european countries make it difficult for eu service providers, including polish companies, to access their markets, while they themselves have much easier access to the eu services market. the european parliament prepared this resolution for the european commission to outline the guidelines and framework within which it should move in the negotiations. the most important issue we have to raise is the need to ensure that our companies and the representatives of the professions have equal access to the markets of the countries involved in the negotiations. when we agree to liberalise trade in services, we must be sure that the rules in force will benefit us as much as our partners. this report clearly sets out our interests, including the specific nature of the public services that should be excluded from the scope of this contract. i voted to accept it.

in writing. ‒ the new strategy on gender equality for the period after 2015 presented by the european commission is an example of modern thinking on the implementation of ambitious policies, focused on clear, achievable goals and concrete methods, free from abstract postulates. the strategy rightly recognises that gender equality requires the further integration of women into the labour market through the provision of care services for adults and children and the promotion of a more balanced division of responsibilities. greater participation of women in the labour market based on the principles of equal pay for equal work and fair promotion is the best recipe against women's poverty, the pension gap and the opportunity to fully exploit talents in the economy. the path to full equality between women and men does not, however, lead through the labour market alone, but is based above all on ensuring that women's fundamental human rights are respected. the anti-violence policy presented in the commission document is rightly based on the methods proposed in the istanbul convention and the obligation to ratify that document by the european union. i call on the commission to implement the actions proposed in the strategy systematically and effectively and to evaluate conscientiously the progressive change that is bringing us closer to the goal of equality between women and men.
in writing. ‒ the adoption of a new strategy on gender equality and women's rights after 2015 is necessary to achieve the eu's objectives in this area. this strategy requires a very comprehensive approach and a priority approach to violence against women and to all issues related to discrimination against different groups of women in the professional, economic, social and political spheres. equal access to quality education, irrespective of gender, national, social, cultural or religious origin, is essential to ensure full participation in socio-economic life, to improve its quality and to prevent inequalities from arising. in this context, it is also necessary to prevent early school leaving, which can lead to social exclusion and marginalisation. another issue is access to lifelong vocational education and training for women. women are more likely to be interrupted in their working lives for a variety of reasons. they should therefore be enabled and encouraged to participate in vocational education and training adapted to their needs, so that they can acquire new skills that will facilitate their return to work. gender equality education is non-discriminatory education that aims at personal, social and economic development in a spirit of tolerance, partnership, dialogue and responsibility for life in society.
in writing. ‒ the issue of equality of people before the law and with each other is one of the most important civilizational challenges facing humanity. the european union also has a leading role to play in achieving this objective. the actual implementation of this principle is necessary for the further development of society and should be applied not only in legislation but above all in everyday life. unfortunately, the commission's previous strategy for equality between women and men 2010-2015 did not achieve its intended objective, as it did not contribute sufficiently to ensuring gender equality in the eu. in june 2015, the european parliament therefore called for a new strategy in this area, which should give fresh impetus to the issue of equality and lead to concrete action. however, it is first necessary to identify the reasons for the lack of implementation of existing legislation in the member states in order to ensure that new legislative proposals in the area of gender equality are effectively implemented. given the importance of gender equality, i have decided to support the resolution.

in writing. investor-state dispute settlement (isds) is a mechanism used in international investment treaties to ensure that states' obligations to protect each other's investments are respected. there are currently over 3000 such agreements, 1400 of which are concluded by eu member states. the basic principles of commercial arbitration are very helpful in resolving disputes between an investor and a state. since these disputes often concern public policy or public finance issues, it is necessary to increase the transparency of their resolution by ensuring public access to documents. efforts to improve transparency have been ongoing since 2010. the european commission is working to ensure a high level of transparency in future eu agreements. in addition, it has helped to persuade the united nations commission on international trade law (uncitral) to establish global transparency rules and to apply these enhanced rules to the 3000 investment agreements currently in force. however, member states have not reached an agreement with the commission and have not signed the united nations convention to implement these global rules, which has a negative impact on the handling of many international disputes in which the union is the defendant and the claimant is a non-eu state.
in writing. - mr president, i would like to thank you for your kind words. in general, i support the introduction of transparency in investment arbitration and the appropriateness of disclosing some information about arbitration proceedings, but within reasonable and specified limits. in the case of arbitration proceedings, it is essential, first of all, that they be conducted with due regard to the interests of the state concerned. therefore, it is highly questionable that the proposed transparency rules provide for a significant increase in the scope of mandatory disclosure, while leaving out the possibility of reserving the confidentiality of important information, which is important both for the states and for investors. i would point out that the confidentiality of arbitration proceedings is recognised in the doctrine as one of the most important and valuable features of such proceedings. at the same time, the public's judgment in a dispute can result in the dispute being politicised and put under pressure, making it difficult to resolve amicably and to reach a satisfactory conclusion. i would point out that the accession of the eu to the convention entails the necessity for the member states to be bound by the energy charter treaty. energy disputes will require the parties to address sensitive information, the disclosure of which could be contrary to the state interest. in addition, the requirement to disclose, translate and publish all documents significantly increases the costs of proceedings. in my view, the issue of eu binding by the convention must be subject to a sound impact assessment and be taken without any pressure, especially in the face of such a significant expansion of the scope of information subject to disclosure.

in writing. violence against women is a global scourge, which takes different, sometimes drastic forms and is justified in different ways. these include the belief that everything that happens in the family is a private matter, or that religious traditions cannot be opposed, even if they prescribe physical and psychological punishment for women who break the rules (honour killings). cultural differences mean that the same behaviour can be understood and judged differently. to avoid the trap of relativism in relation to violence, the process of signing and ratifying the council of europe convention on preventing and combating violence against women was launched in 2011, which explicitly states that neither tradition nor religion can be used to justify violence. almost all eu countries have signed the convention, and several have ratified it. in an age of increasing cultural diversity in europe, the document takes on new meaning and becomes a direct tool to help resolve conflicts of values that can affect the assessment of events, such as sexual assaults on women, depending on the ethnic origin or religion of the offender or victim. the convention recalls that while cultural differences may give rise to misinterpretations of women's behaviour, this cannot be an excuse for the harm suffered by the victims, and that prevention of violence lies in educating perpetrators about women's rights, not in educating women about the permissible length of skirts.

in writing. ‒ according to the resolution, all islands have an accessibility rate that is lower than the european average, even taking into account maritime transport. human capital is a major problem for islands, especially mediterranean islands: education is particularly low even on islands with high gdps and universities. insularity should therefore be recognised as a natural characteristic which negatively affects, directly and indirectly, the attractiveness of islands by creating obstacles to their sustainability performance. this creates for these territories a more targeted and efficient use of existing funds as well as additional resources. furthermore, i believe that the proportion of cohesion policy funds spent on isolated regions should be concentrated on the poorest eu member states rather than on strictly defined french, spanish and portuguese territories. the resolution calls, inter alia, on the commission to establish an 'eu strategic framework for islands' to bring together instruments that can have a significant territorial impact and on member states and regional and local authorities to play an important role in island development strategies based on a vertical approach covering all levels of government, in accordance with the principle of subsidiarity, in order to guarantee the sustainable development of islands in the eu. given the seriousness of the problems, i voted in favour of the resolution.
in writing. ‒ the resolution underlines the key role of local and regional authorities in shaping and implementing eu strategy, while recognising the role of a wide range of stakeholders, from member states to local communities. it is very important to note that the close links between these authorities and citizens and the diversity of governments at local and regional level are an asset for the eu. parliament supports synergies and complementarities between the european structural and investment funds and other eu programmes, where local and regional authorities can play a useful role in achieving cohesion policy objectives. at the same time, the resolution stresses that improving the administrative capacity and addressing the structural weaknesses of local and regional authorities are essential for the programming and implementation phases of operational programmes and for achieving a higher absorption rate of european structural and investment funds. calls on the commission, therefore, to ensure that local and regional authorities and their administrations and institutions are supported in capacity building, enabling them to play a significant role in cohesion policy, especially in the case of delegation of executive tasks to lower levels of administration, especially to municipal authorities; i voted in favour of the motion.
in writing. ‒ poland is the best example of how european funds can change a country in a dozen years. the most important actors in this activity, both in poland and in other eu countries, are local government units. it is the regional authorities that are most often responsible for allocating and managing the huge amounts of funds, for example through regional operational programmes, and the successful implementation of these tasks often determines a significant leap forward for many regions. one of the most important beneficiaries of european funds is the 'small homeland', the municipalities. the activities carried out by municipal units, such as investments in road, water and sewerage infrastructure, municipal services, education and cultural and tourist offerings, are the most easily perceived and felt by residents, as they serve the whole community. the role of local authorities in informing and mediating the acquisition of european funds by natural and legal persons should not be forgotten either, which is why, in supporting local authorities in their activities, i voted in favour of the adoption of a document on the role of local and regional authorities in the european structural and investment funds.
in writing. ‒ local and regional authorities in the eu member states play a very important role, which is recognised not only in national but also in european legislation, as evidenced by the active involvement of these authorities in the discussions on the preparation and implementation of operational programmes. the knowledge of local and regional authorities is particularly important for shaping future policies, as they are the closest to citizens and communities, the ones who best understand their needs and are able to support work at european level by exchanging views and proposing concrete solutions in the context of job creation, healthcare, the environment, energy and transport. the development of urban-rural links will bring further benefits to eu citizens, as this approach allows both cities and rural areas to exploit their full potential through the mutual provision of specific services. the eu should also seek to make the most of the opportunities for international cooperation within and outside the eu. cross-border links and cooperation between border regions can serve many social and economic purposes, while enhancing the very important dimension of european territorial cooperation. it is also in this context that the shape of the european structural and investment funds should be discussed and decided, so that they are well-suited to the needs and opportunities of the eu's regions, cities and villages.
in writing. ‒ the european union's cohesion policy is the main investment instrument covering all eu regions and aims to reduce economic, social and territorial disparities between eu member states and their regions. the eu's adoption of the multiannual financial framework for 2014-2020 provided an opportunity to create a coherent framework for the five european structural and investment funds for the first time. it is thanks to them that the role of local and regional authorities in the formulation and implementation of eu strategies has been significantly enhanced. however, further action is needed to strengthen the role of local and regional authorities. the european parliament's report points, inter alia, to the need to improve administrative capacity and address structural weaknesses. in addition, community-led local development should be promoted, where local authorities are not just managers but become partners in the action. multi-level governance supports the eu's core policy objectives of economic growth, social progress and sustainable development, and strengthens the democratic dimension of the union and enhances the effectiveness of its policies. i therefore decided to vote in favour of the report on the role of local and regional authorities in the european structural and investment funds.
in writing. ‒ i support the resolution because the eu's cohesion policy is the eu's most important investment instrument. from my experience as minister of culture from 2007 to 2014, i can indeed confirm that the european structural and investment funds are a very important instrument with important benefits. i would like to stress that the success of the projects implemented depends to a large extent on good cooperation between government institutions and local authorities and communities. the role of local authorities, their competences and appropriate training are crucial in the process of using structural funds effectively. in the cultural sector, 100% of the investment appropriations were used in poland. that's what a very good team does.
in writing. ‒ effective regional and local government is the key to good management and spending of european funds. it is at this level that the needs of local communities can best be identified and the planned investments integrated into the overall development strategy of the country. the availability of many european funds to help redress regional disparities, modernise rural areas and improve skills is an undeniable asset of our membership. however, to make the most of this opportunity, it is necessary to identify the investment needs of each region. the role of local and regional authorities should be strengthened in this process, as they are the ones who make the most important decisions every day. it is in the regional or local authorities that the first line of defence is to be found in the face of major problems such as inefficient communications, natural disasters or the preparation of the conditions for investment that creates new jobs. of course, it is not enough to involve the local council or the regional council in the decision-making process. it is necessary to prepare local officials and to create mechanisms for public consultation to ensure that theory is brought into line with practice. this approach will not only ensure that european funds go where they are needed most, but also allow local businesses to be more involved in the implementation of these investments. i voted in favour of this report because i believe that the polish local authorities deserve to have a say in a matter of such importance to them.

in writing. on 18 and 19 february 2016, the european council adopted a strategic programme which set out the long-term priorities for the eu's actions and work. the main topics were the uk's status in the eu and the migration and refugee crisis. after hours of negotiations, eu leaders have reached an agreement that strengthens britain's special status in the eu. the decision taken by the 28 heads of state is legally binding and irrevocable, as david cameron has stressed. under the new arrangements, the uk will be permanently excluded from the process of progressive eu integration and immigrants from other member states will be subject to restrictions on access to the social welfare system. moreover, the united kingdom will never join the euro area and will remain outside the schengen agreement. in the context of the migration crisis, the european council decided to protect the eu's external borders, curb illegal migration and guarantee the integrity of the schengen area. the decision by nato to provide assistance in the detection, monitoring and control of illegal border crossings in the aegean sea was also welcomed. nevertheless, full and rapid implementation of the eu-turkey action plan remains a priority for halting migration flows and combating traffickers' and smugglers' networks.
in writing. at the last summit, eu leaders agreed to make concessions to the uk to prevent it from leaving the eu. commenting on the situation, the european media focused on the issue of restricting social assistance for europeans in the uk, but also in other member states. it is important to note that this is an important but not crucial issue for the future of the union. the risk of a three-speed union is a more serious problem. this is because there is a risk of the community breaking up into the following countries: (1) the euro area, (2) the united kingdom and (3) the other member states. these three 'zones' will be subject to, inter alia, different integration rules and different rights and obligations of membership. this threatens to weaken and perhaps to break up the union. this risk may also be reinforced in the future by the fact that other member states, especially those with strong eurosceptic parties, may now put forward their own demands similar to those raised by the united kingdom. that is why i am afraid that the european union has been weakened rather than strengthened by recent decisions, which threaten its good future.

in writing. i am pleased that the tripartite talks have resulted in an interinstitutional agreement on the eures instrument. i believe that the new directive, which re-establishes this instrument if it is implemented efficiently in the member states will help to give a new impetus to interregional cooperation in the field of recruitment. the european union has been struggling for some years not only with unemployment but also with the problem of unfilled vacancies in certain sectors of the economy. the european network of employment services in a new, strengthened form has the potential to facilitate the recruitment of workers from different member states. the network will be made up of both public employment services and social partners, who will be subject to the same minimum criteria. i think it's a good basis for cooperation. i am also pleased that the issues of mobility of workers in crossborder areas have been identified and clarified. in fact, this is a group of workers who have slightly different problems, and therefore require special attention and often individual solutions. i therefore think that the creation of separate crossborder partnerships within eures is a good solution.
in writing. i have repeatedly called for the creation of a european information bank on traineeships and placements. i therefore strongly support the inclusion of apprenticeship and traineeship offers in the eures network. in this context, i stress the need to provide comprehensive information to jobseekers or trainees on the terms and conditions of employment and the benefits associated with potential work. in order to be a useful and effective tool for job search and traineeship, eures needs to be accessible to the widest possible audience. therefore, it is important to ensure that it is user-friendly and promoted in the media. it is also important to monitor the functioning of this tool so that any shortcomings can be corrected on an ongoing basis. i also propose new initiatives to make the eures portal a comprehensive information point on employment and vocational skills. the eures portal should provide information on, inter alia, language courses, conditions for the recognition of academic and professional qualifications, and accommodation options in the country concerned.
in writing. the right to free movement of workers already appeared in the 1957 treaty of rome. it is also guaranteed in article 39 of the treaty establishing the european community, in its consolidated version. it is estimated that more than 7 million european citizens lived and worked in another member state in 2013, of which 78% were in employment and 68% were in employment. however, due to the financial crisis, the flow of labour within the union has recently decreased by one third. in addition, there is a trend towards a shortage of qualified personnel. in order to counteract the further effects of the developing trend, the committee of permanent representatives approved on 2 december 2015 the agreement reached with the european parliament on the re-establishment and reorganisation of the european network of employment services (eures). the aim in itself is to make the eures network an effective tool for jobseekers or employers. in addition, removing barriers to mobility will increase access to employment throughout the eu, facilitating the creation of new jobs. moreover, this employment network will contribute to combating unemployment by helping to better match supply and demand in the labour market. eures is also expected to play an important role in providing concrete information and services to employers and cross-border workers in european border regions. i believe that the idea of a single market without major national borders is based on a high level of mutual trust and on the equivalence of regulatory systems.

in writing. ‒ the european union and san marino will automatically exchange financial information on each other's residents under this agreement, in line with the updated requirements of the administrative cooperation directive and the 2014 oecd global standards. this will take place from 2017. the aim is to address situations where the taxpayer attempts to conceal capital representing income or assets that have not been taxed. similar updates have been made to the agreements with switzerland and liechtenstein, and the agreements with andorra and monaco will also be updated. i welcome this update as the agreement has been brought into line with current eu standards and oecd global standards, without applying double standards with respect to the exchange of information. i voted yes.
in writing. ‒ agreement between the european community and the republic of san marino establishing measures relating to the taxation of savings income in the form of interest payments. i voted in favour of the agreement between the european community and the republic of san marino. as in the case of switzerland and liechtenstein, this will avoid a situation where the taxpayer conceals capital constituting income or assets without paying taxes. the exchange of financial information of residents of each party in accordance with current requirements is an integral part of transparent relations with the european union and effective prevention of irregularities in this area.
in writing. ‒ the eu and san marino will automatically exchange financial information on each other's residents in accordance with the updated requirements of the administrative cooperation directive (dac2) and the 2014 oecd global standards. this will take place from 2017. the aim is to address situations where the taxpayer attempts to conceal capital representing income or assets that have not been taxed. similar updates have been made to the agreements with switzerland and liechtenstein, and the agreements with andorra and monaco will also be updated. i welcome this update as the agreement has been brought into line with current standards and the oecd global standards, without applying double standards with respect to the exchange of information. the amendments include, for example, a more detailed set of data protection provisions, provisions on the exchange of information on request following the oecd model and a mechanism for the rapid adoption of amendments to the oecd global standard with the agreement of the other party to the agreement. the information to be exchanged concerns not only income, such as interest and dividends, but also account balances and proceeds from the sale of financial assets. that is why i supported the report.
in writing. ‒ the convention on the protection of the european communities' financial interests and its protocols aim to establish a common legal framework for the protection of the communities' financial interests under criminal law. abuses affecting both expenditure and revenue should be subject to effective, proportionate and dissuasive criminal sanctions, including custodial sentences, which may provide grounds for extradition. i voted in favour of the proposal because i support the position of the european commission.
in writing. ‒ the convention on the protection of the european communities' financial interests and its protocols aim to establish a common legal framework for the protection of the communities' financial interests under criminal law. abuses affecting both expenditure and revenue should be subject to effective, proportionate and dissuasive criminal sanctions, including custodial sentences, which may provide grounds for extradition. this convention was adopted on 26 july 1995 and entered into force on 17 october 2002. croatia acceded to this convention and the protocols thereto by virtue of the act of accession. the council should adopt a decision to set the date on which that convention should enter into force for croatia. in the light of the above, the commission recommends that the council take a decision on the accession of croatia to the convention on the protection of the european communities' financial interests and the protocols thereto. that is why i supported the report.
in writing. ‒ eures is a cooperation network between the european commission and the public employment services of the member states, focusing on professional mobility in the eu. the purpose of this regulation is to make the eures network a tool for jobseekers or employers by making available a pan-european pool of job vacancies and jobseeker profiles. the regulation also aims to strengthen the institutional and organisational basis of eures services, to improve the quality of information provided to workers and employers, to improve the exchange of information to better reflect technological change and to increase the mobility of workers, in particular in cross-border regions. the regulation also covers apprenticeship and vocational training, provided that the applicants are in an employment relationship. in view of the above, i have voted in favour of the draft.
in writing. ‒ i voted in favour of the amendment of the rules on the operation of the european job mobility networks (eures) because the current system was flawed. the collection of available jobs and cvs of unemployed persons was incomplete. the automatic matching of cvs and offers was limited and the scope of cross-border information on available offers and competences was insufficient. only 7.5 million people, or 3.1% of the working population, are employed in other member states. our aim is to tackle unemployment by better matching supply and demand in the eu labour market. i believe that the new rules will take into account the needs of young people and the specificities of crossborder regions better than before. the reformed eures portal should be 'smarter', as it will automatically search for job vacancies based on the competences listed in the cv of the jobseeker and include all job vacancies published by public employment offices in the member states throughout the eu, and importantly, access for workers is free of charge. i believe that the prohibition of discrimination on grounds of nationality in employment, remuneration and other working conditions and the guarantee of access to the portal services for disabled persons are justified.
in writing. ‒ eures is a cooperation network between the european commission and the public employment services of the member states aimed at professional mobility in the eu. the purpose of this regulation is to make the eures network a tool for jobseekers or employers by making available a pan-european pool of job vacancies and jobseeker profiles. the aim of the proposal is to strengthen the institutional and organisational basis of eures services, to improve the quality of information provided to workers and employers, to improve the exchange of information to better reflect technological change and to increase the mobility of workers, in particular in cross-border regions. the regulation also covers apprenticeship and vocational training, provided that the applicants are in an employment relationship. the new eures network will include the european coordination office, the national coordination offices and eures members and partners. public employment services enjoy preferential status in the eures network and are automatically designated by the member states as eures members. the regulation opens the eures network to the various players in the market for recruitment services (public, private, service sector, social partners). organisations that are not able to carry out all the tasks will be able to become eures partners, and those that are able to carry out a wider range of services will become eures members. i hereby endorse the report.
in writing. ‒ free movement of workers is one of the key conditions for the development of a more integrated eu labour market, especially in cross-border regions, allowing for greater labour mobility, thus contributing to greater diversity and finding people with the right skills for job vacancies. the recent financial and economic crisis has forced both the member states and the european union to take a number of measures to increase the employment opportunities of workers and to help employers fill vacancies better and faster. unfortunately, there is still a relatively low level of intra-eu labour mobility, which is to be countered by the creation of a european network of employment services. the platform is intended to provide the widest possible pool of job vacancies and jobseeker profiles at european level. it is also intended to provide opportunities for apprenticeships and traineeships. as the parliament pointed out in its report, it is necessary to ensure that the platform is easily accessible and as user-friendly as possible, while cooperating appropriately with the already existing national employment agencies. i think the european commission's initiative is right, but only if it does not in any way restrict the ability of individual member states to pursue their own employment policies.
in writing. ‒ sustainable employment growth in the member states and the reduction of the risk of unemployment is a goal that can only be fully achieved through close cooperation within the european union. the free movement of workers is one of the greatest advantages of poland's membership of the eu, but to exploit its full potential, the exchange of information on job vacancies in different member states should function much better. eures, which has been in existence since 1994, is a tool for coordinating national employment policies at european level. however, the functioning of this system requires adaptation to new conditions, including increased mobility of workers and new communication channels. the traditional structure of this network requires the complementation and inclusion not only of public employment services but also of successive partners representing the private sector and non-profit organisations. the scope of eures activities also needs to be extended, which, in addition to job-search, should include training and traineeships, which are an essential part of vocational education and training. the creation of new tools based on digital technologies that will allow employers to be matched with employees quickly and efficiently also seems to be a valid proposition. i also agree with the proposal to increase the role of this platform in the process of collecting and sharing knowledge about the recruitment process, especially for small and medium-sized enterprises that require special support. in view of the above, i voted in favour of this regulation.
in writing. ‒ the terrorist attack in sousse on 26 june 2015 has triggered a debate in the eu on the need to continue to support tunisia's political and economic transformation in a concrete and targeted way, through actions that can be effective in the short term. in this context, the european commission is proposing a temporary, unilateral and duty-free tariff quota of 35 000 tonnes per year for the export of olive oil from tunisia to the union, in the form of autonomous trade measures. olive oil is tunisia's main agricultural product exported to the eu, and the olive oil sector is an important part of the national economy providing direct and indirect employment for over one million people, representing a fifth of employment in the entire agricultural sector. given the nature of the support tool, i voted in favour of this document.
in writing. ‒ implementation of the emergency autonomous trade measures for the republic of tunisia. the difficult political and economic situation in tunisia has prompted the european union to take effective action to support the country in its transition. the solutions proposed by the european commission have my full support. tunisia, which is facing many difficulties, needs help that will bring short-term benefits. the european union's approval of the temporary unilateral duty-free export of olive oil from tunisia to the member states of the european union will certainly contribute to positive changes in tunisia, which relies heavily on the olive oil sector for its economy.
in writing. ‒ the terrorist attack in sousse on 26 june 2015 has triggered a debate in the eu on the need to continue to support tunisia's political and economic transformation in a concrete and targeted way, through actions that can be effective in the short term. the council identified actions to be taken to support the political and economic transformation in tunisia. in this context, the european commission is proposing a temporary unilateral duty-free tariff quota of 35 000 tonnes per year for the export of olive oil from tunisia to the union, in the form of autonomous trade measures. this quota will be available for two years from 1 january 2016 to 31 december 2017. the additional quantity will be opened after the current duty-free tariff quota of 56 700 tonnes has been exhausted. olive oil is tunisia's main agricultural product exported to the eu, and the olive oil sector is an important part of the national economy providing direct and indirect employment for over one million people, representing a fifth of employment in the entire agricultural sector. the commission notes that the commission has not provided any information on the level of the duty rate applicable to the imports of the product concerned from the prc. i hereby endorse the report.
in writing. ‒ building a lasting and stable state requires a solid economic foundation. this economic success is the engine of the rule of law and of a modern state that effectively meets the needs of its citizens. the situation in tunisia is far from being that of a democratic state, and the recent years of internal destabilisation in that country have had a negative impact on our continent as well. as in the case of ukraine, so in the case of tunisia, we must make an effort to open our market to products which will, on the one hand, enrich the offer to european consumers and, on the other, strengthen the weak foundations of economic development of our north african partner. the commission notes that the tunisian authorities have not provided any evidence that the aid is compatible with the internal market. of course, the measures taken are temporary and limited, since such action cannot cause lasting damage to european oil producers and destabilise the internal market. i believe this decision is the right one and will bring more benefits to the stability of the region than any other political or military action. given the important role of the north african states in tackling the migration crisis affecting europe, the actions taken by the european parliament and the council are fully justified.

in writing. ‒ the annual growth analysis, presented by the european commission, opens up the annual cycle of economic governance, called the european semester. the economic and social priorities identified in the 2015 growth survey, namely investment, structural reforms and fiscal responsibility, remain undoubtedly relevant. one of the key challenges facing member states is the continued poor implementation of the country-specific recommendations. without political will and commitment at national level, the required reforms to boost competitiveness, create new and stable jobs and achieve sustainable growth cannot be implemented. there is no doubt that the european commission also has an important role to play in this process. it should seek to make better use of the european structural and investment funds to support the key priorities identified in the country-specific recommendations, including through the application of actions combining the effectiveness of those funds with sound economic governance and the strengthening of the european single market, which is a prerequisite for economic growth in europe.

in writing. ‒ although the unemployment rate in the european union is slowly falling, it remains relatively high, especially among young people, of whom almost a quarter are unemployed. the cost to the community as a whole of such high youth unemployment is estimated at over eur 150 billion per year. member states need to overcome barriers to job creation and improve the functioning of labour markets. i therefore welcome the fact that the european semester based on three main pillars, namely stimulating investment, structural reforms and increasing budgetary accountability has been complemented by a new pillar, employment and social affairs, in the framework of the 2016 european semester. i hope that this will not only put more emphasis on analysing the social and employment situation in the european union, but also make it easier to monitor any disruptions in the member states that are undermining growth and creating new and stable jobs.
in writing. ‒ while understanding and accepting the reasons for the need to strengthen economic policy coordination in the european union in the context of the european semester, a rational approach to the actions proposed to the member states must be maintained. it is difficult to accept the demands to limit the freedom to shape the rules and conditions of employment in poland with the help of european regulations. creating growth requires the right tools, and one of those tools is the ability to influence the labour market. while forms of cooperation at european level to promote employment, such as the eures network, are needed, the possibility of direct intervention by the european commission in the social policies of the member states or in the employment relationship between employer and employee, based on national law, is a bad proposal which i cannot support. this is an example of an unjustified extension of the commission's powers, which will increase the level of bureaucracy in the eu and weaken the ability of member states to respond quickly to employment crises. of course, the report's strengths should be highlighted, including its call for more investment in human capital, the need to protect the market economy and the role of infrastructure investment in generating growth. unfortunately, given the proposals which go too far in restricting the freedom of member states in the area of employment policy and the rejection of many favourable amendments, i abstained.

in writing. ‒ progress in the integration of the single market in the member states is measured regularly to ensure that it is effectively translated into growth, job creation and competitiveness. the report highlighted the need to improve the governance and transparency of this process and to strengthen the member states' sense of responsibility for the implementation of the eu's my aim is to highlight the potential benefits of the single market, while also highlighting unjustified barriers at national level. the report draws attention to the following issues: a single market pillar in the european semester fully respecting the principles of subsidiarity and proportionality and a set of analytical tools to better measure the economic and regulatory performance of the single market; effective implementation, application and enforcement of single market rules and the need to further develop and strengthen existing mechanisms, tools and instruments to improve governance; action to ensure that problems are effectively addressed at national level and, where possible, through informal means, which could create more opportunities for consumers, lead to the establishment of quality standards and foster competition; coordination of single market priorities in the context of the european semester should be deepened with the involvement of the member states, in a democratic parliamentary process. that is why i supported the report.
in writing. ‒ the european semester, the procedure under which the member states of the european union coordinate their economic and budgetary policies, is based on three main pillars: stimulating investment, structural reforms and increasing budgetary responsibility, which have been complemented by a new pillar on employment and social affairs. however, i believe that the european semester cannot be assessed in the abstract from the assessment of the state of management of the european single market, which is a prerequisite for economic growth in europe. as rapporteur of the ppe group for the report on the governance of the single market in the european semester, i am pleased that the document adopted by the european parliament contains proposals which i support, in particular in the areas of deregulation of business conditions, strengthening the position of smes, the development of innovation, technological progress, the spread of e-government, and the elimination of non-tariff barriers and national protectionism. these are just some of the conditions that must be met in order to unleash the entrepreneurial energy of the citizens of the union. this is necessary to keep the european economy competitive on the world market. the number of new jobs created and the future prosperity of community citizens will depend on this.
in writing. ‒ the single market remains the central element and the main driving force of the european union's economy. i agree with the rapporteur that, despite the progress made since the creation of the single market, its growth potential has not yet been fully exploited. one of the key needs in managing the single market is to carry out tailor-made economic and social reforms, tackle excessive bureaucracy and protectionism, in order to improve the productivity and competitiveness of the eu economy. it would therefore be justified to include the single market pillar as another pillar of the european semester. this pillar would be treated as a system responsible for regularly monitoring and assessing the integration of the single market and competitiveness. the single market of the 21st century is radically different from that of the 20th century. these changes are largely due to the digital revolution. to this end, appropriate measures should be taken to eliminate the differences that have arisen. i am convinced, as the rapporteur is, that easy access to information for businesses and consumers is a prerequisite for good governance of the single market. i appreciate the work of both the commission and the member states on a number of information portals for different users. a simple, user-friendly portal is needed to improve and simplify access to information and to promote the existing platform, provided that national and local authorities make such a portal available and publicly inform citizens about the possibility of using it.
in writing. ‒ it is hard to disagree with the report's statement that the single market is one of the pillars of the european union. apart from the free movement of persons, this is where the success of european integration is most visible, although we still face shortcomings and the use of non-tariff barriers. the idea of a european semester seems to be the ideal tool to address these problems and to better coordinate national policies in order to strengthen the principle of free movement of goods. the fact that the potential of this tool has not yet been used to strengthen the foundations of the single market is a major negligence on the part of the commission, and i support the call in this report to change this. we have many challenges ahead of us, which are linked to the impact of the digital revolution on the european economy. today, the single market is not just about the traditional trade in goods, but also about the free access to the market for services, the huge potential of online trade and the emergence of new business models such as the sharing economy model. all these challenges of the present were not met in the past when the current shape of the single market was being designed, and we need to find a place for them within all four freedoms. i believe that the potential of the european semester can be effectively used to overcome the barriers to further european economic integration and that is why i voted in favour of this report.

in writing. ‒ i voted yes to the proposal for a regulation of the european parliament and of the council introducing exceptional autonomous trade measures for the republic of tunisia. the economy of the republic of tunisia is based mainly on agriculture and mining. agriculture accounts for 48% of the country's land area. more than 60,000 olive trees grow throughout the country, producing more than 150,000 tons of oil. tunisia is thus the second largest exporter of olive oil and the fourth largest producer in the world. the olive has become the main source of livelihood for the people of tunisia, and for good reason it is called the green treasure of the country. the commission has also provided information on the number of persons killed in the violence in tunisia, including the number of civilians killed in the violence in the country. in addition, the eu remains tunisia's largest trading partner (currently 72% and 75% of tunisian exports). it is one of the european union's most established trading partners in the mediterranean region, having signed an association agreement with the european union in july 1995. for this reason, i agree with the rapporteur that the european union must contribute to the economic recovery of tunisia. however, in order to prevent abuses, it should also be ensured that the envisaged autonomous measures actually benefit the tunisian economy they must be conditional on tunisia's compliance with the relevant union rules on the origin of products and related procedures, as well as on effective administrative cooperation between tunisia and the union.
in writing. ‒ the lack of political and economic stability in the european union's immediate neighbourhood is the cause of many threats to our security, including terrorism and uncontrolled immigration. to tackle these phenomena at the root of the problem, we need solid and reliable partners in the north african region; partners who, with strong institutions and a stable economic situation, can provide their citizens with an alternative to escape to europe from poverty and violence. tunisia has many conditions to become such a reliable partner for europe, but it needs our support. the negative experiences of recent years, including the disappointment with the political transformation caused by the arab spring, the disastrous effects of terrorist attacks on the tourism industry, and the pressure from radical islam have significantly delayed the process of building a modern tunisian state. the launch of free trade negotiations with the eu has the opportunity to become a catalyst that will significantly accelerate this process. i am, of course, aware of the unequal position of our economies and all the potential problems that may arise in the course of these negotiations, but i believe that both sides will be able to properly identify the areas of dispute and find a compromise that is beneficial to both sides. i am convinced that only this kind of cooperation, and the resulting rebuilding of a politically and economically stable eu's immediate neighbourhood, will help to address the months-long immigration crisis. i voted for this report.

in writing. ‒ the european ombudsman investigates complaints about maladministration in the eu institutions and bodies. complaints can be lodged by eu citizens or residents, and by companies and institutions established in the eu. complaints of maladministration may concern, among other things, cases of unfair treatment, discrimination, abuse of power or improper procedures. the european ombudsman's tasks also include protecting the rights of persons with disabilities. in 2014, the ombudsman opened 325 complaint and 17 own-initiative inquiries and closed 387 complaint and 13 own-initiative inquiries. the main sources of complaints were citizens (335) and businesses, associations and other legal entities (52). as regards the country of origin of the complaints, spain is the first (309), followed by germany (219), poland (208) and belgium (147). the ombudsman's annual report shows that the main subject of complaints is public access to documents of the eu institutions. in 2014, 86 (21,5%) of all closed cases concerned access to documents. i welcome the fact that the eu institutions have followed the ombudsman's recommendations by 80%. however, i am concerned that the percentage of non-compliance with its recommendations remains at 20%. although the ombudsman's suggestions are not legally binding, the institutions, bodies and organisations should be required to respond quickly and effectively to his critical remarks and draft recommendations.
in writing. ‒ the european ombudsman, and in particular his work, deserves special attention. mrs o'reilly has worked hard to ensure transparency in the composition of expert groups and drug trials, among other things. i also enthusiastically supported the ombudsman's initiatives to improve access to institutions for people with disabilities and to improve the functioning of the european citizens' initiative.
in writing. ‒ every citizen of the union and every natural or legal person residing or having its registered office in a member state of the european union has the right to apply to the european ombudsman in cases of maladministration by union institutions, bodies, offices or agencies. in its report, the european parliament expressed its support for the key issues examined by ms o'reilly, including the transparency of the work of the institutions and their advisory groups, as well as conflicts of interest and access to documents and information. the eu transparency register, an online platform that allows the registration and sharing of information on the interests of a large number of organisations active in the eu institutions, was established in 2012 and is of particular importance for the transparency of the work of the eu institutions and for the involvement of citizens. in conclusion, i believe that the ombudsman's work and her close cooperation with the european parliament are of the utmost importance. i appreciate the commitment of ms emily o'reilly and that is why i have decided to vote in favour of the report assessing her activities in 2014.

in writing. ‒ the european parliament in its document supported the monetary policy pursued by the european central bank, which is designed not only to guarantee price stability but also to support economic recovery towards job creation, growth and stability, including by increasing the scale of low-interest lending to the real economy. nevertheless, in my view, the use by the european central bank of unconventional monetary policy instruments even if to some extent justified given the situation surrounding the debt crisis, falling inflation, negative credit developments and slow economic growth cannot continue indefinitely. it is up to the individual member states to take decisive action to ensure full implementation of structural reforms and compliance with the rules in force, especially in the area of budgetary discipline. i am glad that this conclusion is also included in the european parliament's document. in addition, in its report, the european parliament welcomed the efforts made by the european central bank to increase its transparency, including by publicly explaining monetary policy decisions immediately after they are taken or by publishing summary minutes of its meetings. for these reasons, i have decided to support the european parliament's report which gives a positive assessment of the european central bank's performance in 2014.
