in writing. ‒ european animal health law will replace some 40 different european legal acts in this field. union legislation on animal diseases and potentially also on human diseases will bring together and update fragmented previous legislation to prevent or contain new outbreaks and to keep pace with scientific developments. these rules will be the first ever to combine animal welfare and public health in eu law and will be an important tool in the fight against antimicrobial resistance in humans, animals and the environment. all farmers and owners of animals and persons dealing in them will be required to observe the rules of animal husbandry and to apply veterinary measures with prudence and responsibility. to tackle the problem of stray animals carrying diseases, legislation has been introduced requiring registration of all owners and sellers of animals, which entitles the commission to ask eu member states to set up a computerised database of dogs and other domestic animals if the need arises. i hereby endorse the report.
in writing. ‒ it is clear that current eu animal health legislation has been successful in significantly reducing animal diseases and responding well to emerging crises. however, its main weakness is the existence of more than 50 scattered legal acts and several hundred implementing regulations. the lack of a horizontal approach and the complexity and often contradictory rules make life very difficult not only for member states' administrations but also for breeders, veterinarians and traders. it is therefore welcome that the new regulation creates a unified legal framework in this area, which is well in line with our efforts to simplify the cap. another long-awaited move is to put more emphasis on prevention of animal diseases, in keeping with the motto: prevention is better than cure. this will include increased responsibility for those handling animals, better monitoring and certification. the current legal framework is more focused on fighting epidemics than on preventing them. it is also worth highlighting the issues of increasing antibiotic resistance, increasing biosecurity on farms and the need to improve the skills of animal handlers. these are among the main demands that parliament put forward in the course of its work and it is pleased that they have been incorporated in the final text of the regulation.
in writing. ‒ there are currently two separate eu-funded grant programmes the school milk and school fruit programmes. participation in the programmes is voluntary. the commission proposed that the two programmes be covered by a common legal framework. this is to increase their efficiency, reduce the administrative burden and improve overall performance. the agreement reached is in line with the ep's budget position: eur 150 million per year for the 'fruit in schools' programme and eur 100 million for the 'milk in schools' programme (i.e. eur 20 million more than the commission's proposal). the list of products covered by these programmes has been considerably extended. in addition to fresh products, member states will be able to distribute other low-processed dairy products such as natural yoghurt and cheese. as regards processed fruit and vegetables and other dairy products such as fruit yoghurt and chocolate milk, they were covered by the scheme under additional conditions. given the objectives of the programmes, i voted yes.
in writing. ‒ obesity and overweight among school-age children is now an epidemic in highly developed economies. it is spreading at an ever-increasing rate and is reaching ever younger people. bad eating habits acquired in childhood can affect health in adulthood and, as a result, contribute to many diseases. the european union is trying to combat this phenomenon, which is why we voted today on the draft resolution of the european parliament and the council on a programme of aid for the supply of fruit and vegetables, bananas and milk to educational establishments. eu financial assistance for the supply of selected products to schools is intended to help promote healthy eating habits and the consumption of local products by children. the programme aims to increase the distribution of vegetables, fruit, milk and other products, i.e. cheese, yoghurt and lactose-free milk, in schools. it is essential to introduce nutrition education among children, promote healthy food and develop food programmes in educational institutions.
in writing. ‒ the conclusions of the eu's existing aid programmes show that their continuation is of great social importance and benefit to citizens. the european union's financial support for children in educational establishments is undoubtedly helping to promote healthy eating habits, reduce obesity among the youngest and thus promote healthy, local products such as fruit, vegetables and dairy products. i personally think that the aid programs that provide fruit, vegetables and milk to schools are a proven investment in children's health. we need to ensure that such programmes are continued, improved and more effectively implemented and managed. the member states, and above all local authorities, which are closest to citizens, should play a major role in this. therefore, in supporting the aims and principles of the marc tarbella report 'programme to assist the supply of fruit and vegetables, bananas and milk to educational establishments', i voted in favour of its adoption.
in writing. ‒ there are currently two separate grant programmes funded by the eu under the cap: the 'school milk' and 'school fruit' programmes. all eu member states are involved in the 'school milk' programme. the 'fruit in school' programme was open to 25 member states in 2013/2014 (uk, sweden and finland did not participate). participation in the programmes is voluntary. the commission proposed that the two programmes be covered by a common legal framework. this is to increase their efficiency, reduce the administrative burden and improve overall performance. the list of products covered by these programmes has been considerably extended. in addition to fresh products, member states will be able to distribute other low-processed dairy products such as natural yoghurt and cheese. as for processed fruit and vegetables and other dairy products such as fruit yogurts and chocolate milk, they have been covered by the scheme under the following conditions: only the milk component of chocolate milk and other flavoured milk (which must contain at least 90% milk) and fruit yogurts (which must contain at least 75% milk) will be financed by the eu; sweeteners and artificial flavour enhancers will now, for the first time, be completely banned in products distributed under the school schemes. i hereby endorse the report.
in writing. ‒ consumption of fruit, vegetables and milk continues to fall in europe. at the same time, more than 20 million children are overweight, and young people on average eat only 30 to 50 percent of the recommended daily intake of fruits and vegetables. that's why the eu programmes: milk at school and fruit and vegetables at school are so important. parliament's success is to win an additional €20 million per year for milk-related programmes, bringing annual funding for milk and milk products to €100 million, against a budget of €150 million for fruit and vegetables. increasing budgetary flexibility is also a good solution. in the area of transfer between programmes, it is provided that member states will be able to transfer 20% from one programme to another, and an additional 5% of the transfer will be possible in the event of an exceptional difficult situation, such as low consumption or market conditions, which is what we are currently facing, for example, in the milk market. it is good that both programmes have a ban on artificial sweeteners and flavour enhancers. in principle, products containing added sugar, salt and fat will also be prohibited, which should also have a positive effect on health and education. finally, it is a good move to promote the eu more in these programmes, which are funded by the eu. in these difficult times for the community, every form of emphasis on its activities for its citizens is needed.
in writing. ‒ i supported the proposal for a european parliament regulation on a programme for the supply of fruit and vegetables, bananas and milk to educational establishments, increasing funding by eur 20 million per year. unfortunately, there is a downward trend in the eu in the consumption of fruit, vegetables and milk, especially among children and adolescents aged 6 to 10. this trend is driven by the increasing number of children who are overweight, obese and lactose intolerant to dairy products. given the length of time children spend in school, it is crucial to use increased funding in facilities to provide milk and fruit to children. it would be directed both at distribution and at activities promoting healthy eating habits, including the consumption of local products. member states that join this voluntary aid scheme commit themselves to promoting healthier eating habits, local food, organic farming and the fight against food waste. children should also have a better understanding of farming and cultivation, for example by visiting farms.
in writing. ‒ i believe that competition between ports is more conducive to the efficiency of the port industry than mandatory regulation of port activities. while welcoming some of the improvements, the polish governments, port owners and trade unions have maintained a strong opposition to the document. concerns were also frequently raised that the social legislation introduced by the rapporteur would result in an overly strict implementation of the existing provisions on the transfer of workers due to a change of service provider and the current ilo guidelines on training and occupational safety. with that in mind, i voted against.
in writing. ‒ i voted against the package because the current draft is flawed, inconsistent and lacks logic. it will not improve the business situation but will create additional bureaucratic burdens. i do not find any proposals to improve the competitiveness of ports or factors that can level the playing field in the sector in question. the diversity of the european port sector makes it impossible to establish a common legal framework for all ports and their managing authorities without sacrificing their specificity and without reducing the particular role they play in the national and regional economy. i am particularly critical of the form of regulation that the commission has chosen to achieve its objectives. i do not agree with the conditions set out in article 14 of the draft regulation which establishes the fees and defines the components of the port infrastructure. this will lead to economic uncertainty and discourage investment. competing port service providers must be able to set charges for their infrastructure. i also oppose the creation of new administrative structures or the mandatory setting up of port user committees, which the draft regulation introduces. these provisions are contrary to one of its explicit aims, namely to reduce red tape. the project seriously interferes with the structure, organisation and independence of ports.
in writing. ‒ trans-european transport networks (ten-t) contribute to the smooth functioning and development of the internal market and ensure economic, social and territorial cohesion. the ten-t programme is a european union transport assistance programme and is addressed to all member states. it is designed to increase economic activity and cooperation and to contribute to the long-term competitiveness of european industry on world markets. the draft legislative resolution of the european parliament and of the council establishing a framework for market access to port services and financial transparency of ports aims to contribute to a more efficient, integrated and sustainable functioning of the ten-t network. the amendments and additions to the regulation are aimed at modernising port services and operations and creating a framework to increase investment in ports. administrative simplification will allow for faster customs clearance and thus improve port efficiency. there are currently many systems of port and port services organisations, and this resolution does not impose a single, specific model. it opens the door to port managers and gives them greater freedom in their decision-making. a well-functioning port such as the one in poland will avoid additional burdens, while the remaining ports will have the conditions to solve their own structural problems.
in writing. ‒ the draft regulation is the third attempt to regulate the market for port services. the ep did not take a position in the previous term and the work was suspended mainly because of the provisions of chapter ii on market access. eu action in the field of maritime transport is a shared competence under the tfeu. the management of maritime ports is a matter for the discretion of the member state, which itself establishes the regime governing maritime ports in its territory, monitors and supervises it, controls the management of public funds and ensures that the principles of competitiveness in the provision of port services are respected. eu member states have sufficient powers to support ports to improve the quality of their services, modernise port facilities and increase their financial independence without additional new eu regulations. the solutions in place in polish seaports are good enough to avoid the need to adopt new ones, and the polish port market is more competitive than the market in the old eu. the regulation may weaken the competitive position of polish ports and worsen their operating conditions, worsen the operating conditions of companies servicing ships in ports or even drive them out of the market, and result in arbitrary deprivation of the possibility of providing services in a port, the possibility of limiting the number of port service providers and chaos in port activities, already regulated since 1996 by the law on ports of special importance in poland. i could not support the report.
in writing. ‒ for the third time in recent years, the commission has put forward a proposal for a regulation to contribute to a more efficient, integrated and sustainable functioning of the ten-t network by creating a framework to improve the performance of ports, their financing, management and competitiveness. the commission's objectives seem to be justified, but the specific legal proposals contained in the document may raise some concerns. the proposal includes solutions such as imposing public service obligations on specific providers, differentiating charges for the use of port infrastructure according to commercial practices and environmental and energy efficiency. i believe that this is an overreaching interference which, instead of meeting the objectives of the regulation, may in effect lead to a reduction in the competitiveness of the sector and to the introduction of charges which some providers of port services will be unable to bear. moreover, the application of the 'one-size-fits-all' principle may lead to worse effects than those currently achieved through national legislation. moreover, eu action in the port sector should also take into account the local and regional dimension, as well as the specific hydrological and ecological conditions of marine areas. i therefore decided to vote against the ep report on access to the market for port services and transparency of port financing.
in writing. ‒ ports are a vital part of the transport sector in the european union and their proper functioning is of great importance for the economic development of the member states. the current regulations leave a significant part of the port infrastructure management competence in the hands of governments, which allows for a coherent policy, stimulating investment and defending the interests of national port operators. the commission proposal will have a negative impact on the situation of ports in many countries, increasing bureaucracy and limiting the influence of member states in shaping their own policy in this area. the commission notes that the polish ports have a significant market share in the polish ports market, which is expected to grow by around 10% in the near future. in western europe, ports have enjoyed generous public support for many years and have built up a strong position in the european market. now, through eu-level regulation, the polish government, among others, is trying to prevent similar actions, which will consolidate the competitive advantage of western european ports, especially german ports. we've seen this kind of mechanism work before in the shipbuilding industry. we must remember that the right slogans about the need to open up the market, simplify procedures and reduce costs are often hidden by particular national interests. given the possible negative effects of the commission's proposal on polish ports, i voted against the adoption of this report.
in writing. ‒ the purpose of the regulation is to examine changes in the prices of services and consumer goods purchased by households over time. the regulation provides for comparable inflation rates in the euro area, the eu, the european economic area and other countries, including acceding and candidate countries, calculated on the basis of a standardised approach and a single set of definitions. the commission proposal for a regulation establishes a uniform legal framework for the development, production and dissemination of data on harmonised indices of consumer prices (hicps) and house prices (hpis) at union, national and sub-national level. the current hicp regulation dates from 1995. new trends in consumer price statistics therefore require a review of the legal framework in order to ensure the greatest possible comparability for the main users of the hicp. this regulation takes into account the changes in the eu decision-making process introduced by the treaty of lisbon, which gives the commission (in this case eurostat) the power to adopt implementing measures (implementing acts) or legislative measures that may amend non-essential elements of the regulation (delegated acts). i voted in favour of the motion as it stands.
in writing. ‒ the hicp regulation measures changes in the prices of services and consumer goods purchased by households over time. the hicp regulation provides comparable inflation rates in the euro area, the eu, the european economic area and other countries, including acceding and candidate countries, calculated on the basis of a standardised approach and a single set of definitions. the commission proposal for a regulation establishes a uniform legal framework for the development, production and dissemination of data on harmonised indices of consumer prices (hicps) and house prices (hpis) at union, national and sub-national level. the current hicp regulation dates from 1995 and new trends in consumer price statistics therefore require a review of the legal framework to ensure maximum comparability for the main users of the hicp. this regulation also takes into account the changes to the eu decision-making process introduced by the treaty of lisbon, which gives the commission the power to adopt implementing or legislative measures that may amend non-essential elements of the regulation. the final agreement provides that the oef regulation will be possible if a uniform way of collecting these indicators in each member state is established, which currently does not exist. the national statistical authorities will maintain control of the details by means of implementing acts, while eurostat will focus on the specific details of the euro area by means of delegated acts. i hereby endorse the report.
in writing. ‒ i voted in favour of the proposal for a european parliament regulation on harmonised indices of consumer prices. these indicators are used to measure inflation adequately in all countries of the european union. in addition, they are used in the assessment of national competitiveness in the context of the commission's macroeconomic imbalance procedure. it is therefore essential that statistics based on harmonised consumption indicators are objective, impartial and comparable in all member states and across all product categories. in order to ensure comparability of indicators, uniform conditions for the categorisation of hicps are needed. in addition, in order to help member states to produce comparable consumer price indices, it is essential that methodological guidelines are drawn up and regularly updated by the european commission in close cooperation with the member states within the framework of the european statistical system.
in writing. ‒ the draft report submitted is based on the 2014 olaf annual report and the commission's report. the rapporteur supports the implementation of the anti-fraud strategy by all commission services and recommends that eu agencies, executive agencies and joint undertakings do the same. it also asks the commission to include a chapter on results in the forthcoming report on the fight against corruption in the eu. the document calls on the commission to take full responsibility for recovering funds unduly paid from the eu budget and to maintain a strict policy of withholding and suspending payments. member states must take the same measures to combat fraud affecting the financial interests of the european union as they take to combat fraud affecting their own financial interests. however, in view of the fact that compromise amendment no 9 (paragraph 52, paragraph 53) was adopted in the commission vote, i decided to abstain.
in writing. ‒ the report supports the implementation of an anti-fraud strategy by all commission services and recommends that eu agencies, executive agencies and joint undertakings do the same. it also asks the commission to include a chapter on results in the forthcoming report on the fight against corruption in the eu. the commission was called upon to take full responsibility for the recovery of funds unduly paid from the eu budget and to maintain a strict policy of withholding and suspending payments. the rapporteur points out that member states must take the same measures to combat fraud affecting the financial interests of the european union as they take to combat fraud affecting their own financial interests. the report nevertheless supports the regulation on the european public prosecutor's office and calls for the adoption of a directive on the protection of financial interests covering vat-related matters. i hereby abstain from voting.
in writing. ‒ safeguarding the eu's financial interests while increasing citizens' confidence by ensuring that their money is used properly, efficiently and effectively is at the heart of the community's action. one of the key issues raised in the ep's report on the protection of the union's financial interests is the call on the european commission to develop a corruption index to assess member states' policies. according to this index, countries where the risk of corruption is highest will be subject to special controls on the spending of eu money. the document also highlighted the adoption by member states of a regulation establishing a european public prosecutor's office to combat fraud more effectively and more quickly across europe. every year, up to 10-15% of eu funds are misused or illegally spent, to the detriment of the eu and its citizens. in recent months, the court of auditors' report has also shown that the union is not sufficiently effective in controlling and combating crossborder fraud, especially in the field of tax policy.
the omission of references to the family in the report on the gender dimension of european parliament policy is an act of disregard for the rights of millions of families in europe who want to devote themselves to raising children and for the millions of women in europe who, often having to work, aspire to devote themselves to housework and child rearing. these women bring enormous value to the lives of their children first, their nations and europe as a whole. it is a pity that the european parliament has once again shown such disregard for family rights, although of course the parliament has those it supports support for the political claims of the homosexual movement was of course not lacking in this report.

in writing. ‒ in the european union, equality between women and men is a fundamental right and a necessary condition for achieving the community's objectives of growth, employment and social cohesion. there are still structural differences in the treatment of women and men in our society. despite the efforts of the commission and the member states, the growth rate of women's employment remains unsatisfactory. since 2002, it has changed from only 58,1% to 62,8%. if current trends continue, the 75% target of the europe 2020 strategy will not be reached until 2038. gender mainstreaming, the report stresses, must be two-dimensional both by mainstreaming it into different policy strategies and by addressing the unequal representation of women and men in policy areas. i welcome the outcome of today's vote and the rapporteur's proposed package of measures to make the current gender mainstreaming framework more effective and efficient. in this context, the most important aspects are to strengthen cooperation with national parliaments to increase the exchange of information and contacts for further strategy development and to increase the influence of the committee on women's rights and gender equality on budgetary issues.
in writing. ‒ the report 'gender mainstreaming in the work of the european parliament' was produced to ascertain the extent to which the co-legislator on equality in the european union applies the principle of equal treatment to itself. unfortunately, the report goes far beyond the evaluation function, which was the first motivation for the document, and contains many proposals that, in my opinion, will not improve the situation of women, are counterproductive and, above all, do not result from any obvious need, such as the amounts for women and men in the various committees. i voted against many of the specific solutions which i consider to be unnecessary or even harmful, but in the final vote i supported the report because it is an imperfect but necessary step towards a systematic evaluation of parliament's compliance with eu law on the principle that order must always come first.
in writing. ‒ the report provides an opportunity to assess the results achieved and to propose new solutions for the three-year gender mainstreaming policy plan, as mentioned in previous parliament resolutions on gender mainstreaming in the european parliament. the report contains a number of controversial proposals, including: gender parity for committee chairmanships; gender budgeting; systematic gender impact assessments of new legislative proposals or commission policy proposals; gender training for all ep staff (mandatory), as well as for meps, political group staff and parliamentary assistants (where available); gender neutral language guidelines and training for interpretation and translation services; numerous references to the situation of lgbtiq people. the whole idea of gender mainstreaming is unconvincing, because there is no evidence that it actually improves the situation of women. for example, the main instrument of gender amendments is in most cases the addition of one word to the existing text, which is 'gender', 'woman' or 'female/feminine'. it's a small relief for women. i could not support the report.
in writing. ‒ equality between women and men is a fundamental right, a common value of the european union, and a necessary condition for achieving the union's objectives of growth, employment and social cohesion. there is no doubt that women have been discriminated against and treated much worse than men for centuries. moreover, unfortunately, in many areas, women still face problems, barriers and clear inequalities. promoting gender equality is more than just prohibiting discrimination on the grounds of sex. positive action to support women is the basis for their full inclusion in the labour market, social life and political and economic decision-making. but the fight for equality cannot be carried out thoughtlessly and at any cost. it is not possible to impose that questions of competence or mere human trust should be less important than arithmetical proportions, which would be the case if quotas were introduced for middle and senior management positions in the european parliament. it would also be a bad idea for political groups to make it compulsory to nominate candidates for chairmanship of parliamentary committees, groups or delegations on the basis of gender, rather than knowledge, experience (and therefore competence). even less clear is the assessment of the union budget in terms of gender equality. that's why i decided to abstain.
in writing. ‒ the problem of gender inequality is one of many that cannot be solved by creating absurd regulations that defy common sense. the report we voted on today is an example of the kind of activity of this house which contributes to the consolidation of the view of the european union as the source of many nonsensical ideas. ideologising the gender aspect does not help to solve existing problems, but creates a climate of absurdity and makes a mockery of the efforts of those communities that really fight against discrimination against women. as a member of parliament from poland, i am familiar with the climate of legal absurdity that existed during the era of real socialism, when the communist authorities tried to regulate matters that did not require such regulation by means of manifestos or special resolutions. this has been a laughingstock for policy makers and public institutions alike, and i fear that the european parliament may suffer a similar fate. gender mainstreaming in every, literally every, element of parliamentary work, document or regulation is an absurdity that will undoubtedly increase bureaucracy but will not bring real results. but should we not strive for the opposite, where the sexes are no longer the subject of argument and controversy? tracing discrimination in every piece of legislation and organising ideological training for meps and staff will not improve the lot of women, but it will certainly improve the well-being of some of my colleagues on the left of the chamber. i voted against this ridiculous report.
in writing. ‒ the content of the document calls on member states to immediately establish safe and legal asylum routes, reform frontex, establish community-wide guidelines on women as part of wider migration and asylum reform, guarantee special accommodation for lgbti people, review the eu's policy on safe countries of origin for migrants, pay special attention to asylum applications by women and avoid detaining asylum seekers. the report pays particular attention to: the gender dimension in the determination of refugee status (preferential treatment for women refugees, both girls and boys, but no mention of young boys); the needs of women asylum seekers (specifically trained gender advisers); human trafficking and sexual violence, including free access to abortion; detention policies; social inclusion and integration. because of the nature of the document, i voted against. we need clear action to ensure equal treatment not only in terms of gender but also in terms of origin.
in writing. ‒ in 2015, around one million people arrived in europe. 38% of these are women and children, who make up one third of all migrants seeking asylum in the european union. women and girls have different needs than men. treatment varies from country to country. they are often discriminated against and subject to physical and sexual violence. improving the safety of women and girls in refugee situations, including asylum procedures, is not the only change in the european parliament's draft resolution on the situation of refugees and women seeking asylum in the eu. asylum policy and procedures should be gender-sensitive and take a personalised approach. the creation of safe and legal pathways to asylum will reduce the influence of smuggling networks and allow people to find refuge without risking their lives. the protection of refugees and women seeking asylum from any form of exploitation, abuse, violence or trafficking is also an important issue. the common european asylum system (ceas) established between member states is not uniform. legal, political and practical differences contribute to unequal treatment of women seeking protection in europe, and women's safety and respect for their rights cannot be mutually contradictory political objectives.
in writing. ‒ the honeyball report calls on member states to ensure that the rights of refugees are adequately protected, by providing them with separate accommodation, toilets and showers in reception centres, basic medical care, including for pregnant women, and legal advice. it condemns sexual violence against refugees, both in their country of origin and on their way to europe, and in reception centres already in the eu. condemns the forced prostitution of refugees (to pay for their journey), unregistered work, exploiting their desperation and need to raise funds for themselves and their children; calls for support in search and family reunification programmes. in addition to these undoubtedly correct points, the report contains many controversial points. the objections concern the report's content, which is not within the remit of the libe committee, which is responsible for asylum law, but also ideological political issues such as free access to abortion and an excessively wide range of budget-guaranteed goods and services that even the richest eu countries cannot afford. however, the main theme of the report - the situation of refugee women - is extremely important and urgent. i have had the opportunity to visit both reception centres and offices and organisations working for migrants and i believe that the women's issues are addressed in the report in a reasonable and appropriate way. that is why, despite voting against the articles with which i disagree, i supported the report in the final vote.

rapporteur.– madam president, i would like to start by saying that under rule 140 of parliament’s rules of procedure, the president of the european parliament may sign an interinstitutional agreement after examination by parliament’s committee on constitutional affairs (afco) and after approval by parliament. it is my honour today to recommend to parliament the approval of the new interinstitutional agreement on better law-making and its signature by the president. the current agreement on better law-making dates back to 2003. it was concluded before the 2004 enlargement of the european union when we still had a union of 15 member states, and well before the entry into force of the lisbon treaty. parliament repeatedly called for the 2003 agreement to be renegotiated to take account of the new legislative environment created by the treaty of lisbon, to consolidate best practices and to bring the agreement up to date in line with the modern understanding of the better law-making agenda. so we took it as good news when, in january 2015, the then newly-elected juncker commission committed to presenting a proposal for a new interinstitutional agreement between the three institutions: parliament, the council of the european union and the european commission. afco provided its contribution to the position of the european parliament in the negotiations, in april 2015, on the revision of the 2003 agreement. the conference of presidents then endorsed the president’s proposal that mr guy verhofstadt would be parliament’s lead negotiator, conducting the negotiations in close cooperation with afco and the committee on legal affairs (juri), and also reporting to the conference of presidents. finally, in december 2016, the conference of presidents endorsed the new agreement. and the resolution on the conclusion of this agreement on better law-making adopted by the committee on constitutional affairs, to be voted on tomorrow, expresses, in general terms, its view on the outcome of the negotiations. it also calls for the impact of the new agreement on the framework agreement and other related interinstitutional agreements to be ascertained with a view to simplifying the architecture of the numerous arrangements. it also identifies a range of issues that need further follow-up at technical or political level. it recommends the approval of the agreement and contains a mandate for afco to examine the extent to which amendments to or interpretations of the rules of procedure are necessary for the implementation of the agreement. let me mention just some elements of particular importance for the european parliament of the content of the new agreement. these include multiannual and annual programing; the commission’s follow-up to parliament’s legislative initiative requests and justifications for and consultations on envisaged withdrawals of legislative proposals; better law-making tools – which are important for a well-informed, inclusive and transparent decision-making process – and the impact assessment issue. we agreed that the impact assessment should be comprehensive and balanced and take into account the costs of not legislating. the independence and objectiveness of the new regulatory scrutiny vote is also an issue of particular relevance for us. the impact assessment should not, however, replace the political decision-making. gold-plating is also an important issue, in the context of avoiding over-regulation and administrative burden for citizens, administrations and businesses, especially small and medium-sized businesses. with regard to delegated and implementing acts, we have moved forward, but parliament expects today a swift agreement between the three institutions on the appropriate criteria for delineating delegated acts and implementing acts and a prompt alignment of basic acts via the legal framework of the lisbon treaty. to conclude, having examined the content of the new interinstitutional agreement, afco has identified a number of issues that need further follow-up. these issues will be subject to further analysis in a joint initiative report drafted by afco and juri. we trust that the new interinstitutional agreement on better law-making will be an important tool in establishing and developing a more open, more transparent relationship between the institutions with a view to delivering better law-making in the interest of the union’s citizens.

in writing. the agreement between the commission, the council and parliament replaces the 2003 agreement and aims to streamline eu legislation. the aim is, inter alia, to achieve the intended effect of union legislation at the least cost and with the least administrative burden. the new interinstitutional agreement assumes that the law-making process will be open and transparent and based on the best information possible with the relevant participation of stakeholders. improving the existing interinstitutional agreement is particularly important at a time when the functioning of the eu institutions is increasingly being called into question and their distance from the problems of european citizens. in brussels, laws are often created that no one understands, and the benefits of these laws are often disputed by many. the agreement is intended to improve the whole policy cycle - planning, developing, adopting, implementing, assessing and modifying new legislation. this will be done, inter alia, through multiannual and annual work programming by the european commission, an impact assessment of the introduction or non-introduction of legislation at union level, and public consultation of stakeholders. i am very pleased that the final document also included the need for the institutions to assess the impact of the new eu law, especially on small and medium-sized enterprises, as they are the most sensitive to legal changes both negative and positive.
in writing. i believe that an effective agreement on better law-making between the european parliament, the council of the european union and the european commission has a fundamental impact on every aspect of our lives in the european union. with the newly proposed rules, we are well on our way not only to reducing costs and administrative burdens, but also to increasing the openness and transparency of the law. the agreement is important because it covers the entire policy cycle, from the planning phase, through implementation, to evaluation and possible modifications. i think one of the most important tools we should use is public consultation, which allows interested parties to have their say on a given issue. active citizen participation in the eu law-making process, even before the european commission presents a new legislative proposal, significantly reduces the distance to the institutions and gives us practical guidance on the expectations and potential concerns of citizens, businesses and organisations.

in writing. the agreement with turkey on migrants is a landmark step in eu policy in the face of the growing migration crisis, as was donald tusk's appeal to economic migrants: do not come to europe. the agreement provides for an additional eur 3 billion (totalling eur 2 billion) to be provided by the eu to turkey to maintain refugee camps in turkey and to introduce them to the turkish labour market. in addition, and i consider these agreements to be key the eu will open legal migration channels for asylum seekers in return for curbing illegal migration. this particular exchange is designed to regain control of the crisis and stop the criminal activities of the traffickers, smugglers and forgers of documents who have created a lucrative and inhuman empire of pathological business more lucrative than the arms or drug trade. the eu is therefore counting on stopping the illegal flow of migrants; in return, it will accept war refugees in a legal and controlled manner and introduce visa-free travel at the eu-turkey border for eu and turkish citizens. of course, stopping illegal migration is only part of the solution, which must also include checks at the eu's external borders, biometric passports, effective information exchange within the eu and other elements of control, complemented by active action to integrate migrants and respect the european value system by all eu citizens and residents.

in writing. ‒ the eu and the principality of andorra will automatically exchange financial information on each other's residents in accordance with the updated requirements of the administrative cooperation directive (dac2) and the 2014 oecd global standards. this will take place from 2017. the aim is to address situations where the taxpayer attempts to conceal capital representing income or assets that have not been taxed. similar updates have been made to the agreements with switzerland, liechtenstein and san marino, and the monaco agreement will also be updated. the report was drawn up under the simplified procedure (rule 50). welcomes this update as the agreement has been brought into line with current eu standards and oecd global standards, without applying double standards in terms of information exchange. the amendments include, for example, a more detailed set of data protection provisions, provisions on the exchange of information on request following the oecd model and a mechanism for the rapid adoption of amendments to the oecd global standard with the agreement of the other party to the agreement. the information to be exchanged concerns not only income, such as interest and dividends, but also account balances and proceeds from the sale of financial assets.

in writing. ‒ the aim of the directive is to provide procedural guarantees to children (i.e. persons under the age of 18) who are suspected or accused of committing an offence in an eu member state. children's rights vary widely across the eu, with people under 18 often suspected or accused of a crime in a country other than their country of origin, or being questioned in that country. the aim of the directive is to introduce basic rules in this area and to establish fundamental rights throughout the eu, as well as to improve cross-border cooperation in criminal investigations. this directive will provide additional safeguards to those already applicable to adult suspects and accused persons in criminal matters. the main provision of that directive concerns the assistance of a lawyer. member states should ensure that the child is assisted by a lawyer, providing legal aid to that end where necessary. in view of the importance of the matter, i voted in favour of the above document.
in writing. ‒ more than one million children are subject to criminal proceedings in the eu every year, representing 12% of all those who are subject to criminal proceedings in the union. beyond the figures themselves, there are major differences in the treatment of children under criminal proceedings in the member states. the right to a fair trial at all stages of the proceedings is a fundamental right which should be enjoyed by all persons, regardless of age. unfortunately, this right is treated differently in many eu countries. currently, only 6 member states have prosecutors specialising in child cases, while 9 member states do not even have specialised courts. the commission's proposal for a directive, which aims to define a limited but essential set of rights for children who are suspects or accused persons in criminal proceedings, is clearly a step in the right direction. the parliament's report rightly points out the need to include in the directive the right to compulsory legal aid, closely linked to the right to free legal aid, the right to individual assessment, the organisation of hearings, the admission of children to proceedings, special training for judges, etc. for these reasons, i have decided to vote in favour of the ep's report and i believe that the directive on procedural guarantees for children who are suspects or accused persons in criminal proceedings will be adopted as soon as possible.

in writing. ‒ the 'better lawmaking' instrument is an important tool for streamlining the eu legislative process, for transposing the law in the member states and for ensuring that the law is respected under articles 258 and 260 tfeu. it needs to be more transparent and open to the needs of the citizens of the union in order to work. to this end, a new interinstitutional agreement will be established, including a new better regulation agreement, which will ensure that eu rules are respected with the least possible administrative burden. it assumes that policy decisions are developed and taken in an open and transparent manner, based on accurate information with the relevant stakeholder involvement. the programme covers all the legislative stages: planning, adoption, implementation, application and evaluation of the impact of the law. at each of these stages, specific rules and procedures would be in place to ensure that the regulation is appropriate. it should be borne in mind that delays and irregularities in transposition and the incorrect application of eu law lead to inconsistencies between member states and consequently negatively affect citizens. i therefore welcome the outcome of the vote, which underlines the need to continuously improve the eu's legislative process.
in writing. ‒ the resolution on the tobacco agreement (the pmi agreement) is drawn up on the basis of oral questions from the political groups. there are currently four cooperation agreements between eu member states: philip morris international (pmi), japan tobacco international (jti), imperial tobacco limited (itl) and british american tobacco (bat). the agreement with pmi expires in july 2016. the european commission has consistently delayed the publication of its assessment of the pmi agreement. the ecr group therefore submitted an oral question on, inter alia, the state of play and timetable of the negotiations and stressed that the european parliament should be kept regularly informed. in particular, the european parliament should be informed of the main results achieved under the existing agreements with tobacco manufacturers and whether the commission intends to renew existing agreements or to conclude new ones. the commission's technical assessment was only published on 24 february. the main ideas of the document, namely the protection of the union's financial interests, the contribution of the pmi agreement to the fight against illicit trade in the past and the possible criminal consequences of smuggling, led me to vote in favour of the document.
in writing. ‒ the fight against illicit cigarette trade is very important for the european market, because we do not know what ingredients are in these cigarettes and, in addition, we lose budget revenues. experience so far shows that the arrangements in place at present, which were signed back in 2004, have worked. the agreement with pmi has so far significantly reduced smuggling of products, but it has also provided a system for tracing the origin of cigarettes. i think that this agreement should be extended and for these reasons i voted in favour of it.
in writing. ‒ in the late 1990s, in response to the huge growth in the illicit trade in tobacco products, the european commission decided to sign agreements to combat this practice with the four largest tobacco companies. the agreement with philip morris international (pmi) signed in 2004 will expire in july 2005. the contract assumptions were undoubtedly met, as the smuggling of pmi products was reduced by 85%. however, overall illicit trade has not decreased and pmi products have been replaced by non-brand cigarettes. the funds that pmi transferred to the european commission and member states under the contract were intended to effectively combat cigarette smuggling, for example by purchasing specialised equipment. moreover, pmi provided its own codentify tracing system, which made the work of customs officers much easier. since the signing of the pmi agreement, the eu has adopted a tobacco products directive and a protocol to the framework convention on tobacco control, which can effectively replace it. unfortunately, they will only be fully operational from 2019 (directive) and 202223 (convention). given the need to find an effective solution to the legal gap that will arise between 2016 and 2019, when customs officers will have to work without pmi assistance, i have decided to vote against the proposed draft resolution.

in writing. ‒ the european commission's proposal concerns the harmonisation and conversion of the market access regulation governing imports of products originating in certain african, caribbean and pacific (acp) countries. it is a temporary instrument providing duty-free and quota-free access to the eu27 market for acp countries which are not classified as least developed countries by the world bank and which do not benefit from preferential access to the eu market under an economic partnership agreement in accordance with wto rules. as vice-president of the eu-acp delegation, i voted in favour of the commission's proposal.
in writing. ‒ the fisheries agreement between denmark and greenland gives eu vessels access to mixed fisheries in greenland waters (the most commonly caught species are northern prawns, halibut, cod and redfish). the greenland agreement is the third most important for the eu in terms of economic value. in 2013, the agreement generated €10 million in direct profits for the eu fisheries sector. in view of the above, i voted in favour of the proposed agreement.
in writing. ‒ the european commission has negotiated an agreement replacing some provisions of the 15 existing bilateral air services agreements between eu member states and the macao special administrative region of the people's republic of china. one of its main elements is the designation clause, which allows all eu carriers to benefit from the right of enterprise, aviation fuel taxation and the prohibition of anti-competitive practices. i voted yes.
in writing. ‒ directive 92/77/eec introduced a system of minimum vat rates. according to its terms, from 1 january 1993 to 31 december 1996 the basic rate could not be lower than 15%. the period of validity of this provision has been extended five times. the last expiry date was 31 december 2015. in this proposal, the commission proposes to maintain with retroactive effect the current requirement for eu countries to apply a minimum basic vat rate of 15%. the proposal will therefore have no impact on tax rates. the commission proposes to extend the validity of the provision for two years, until 31 december 2017. given the nature of the document, i voted in favour of the report.
in writing. ‒ vat is levied at every stage of the marketing of goods or services and, by its very nature, should not have a direct impact on the activities of undertakings. unfortunately, 60 years after its creation, it has become a burden for many companies and a means of unfair competition for others. the eu loses almost €200 billion every year to vat fraud and almost €50 billion to so-called 'tax carousels' in cross-border transactions within the single market. it is good that the european commission is planning to introduce a new system to combat current abuses next year. it will make it possible for a company delivering goods to another eu country to pay tax in its own country at the vat rate in force in the country of destination, and only then will the tax office transfer the amount received to the tax office in the country where the importer is established. but cross-border abuse is only part of the problem. as vat has developed, most countries have opted for various reduced or zero rates. these decisions were intended to be part of a combination of two policies: fiscal and social. but they have resulted in an increase in tax evasion and fraud, with little effect on the poorest. for these reasons, i believe that vat legislation requires much deeper, systematic and comprehensive changes, rather than just the piecemeal ones that have been made so far.
in writing. ‒ i support the extension of the minimum basic rate of vat, defined as a value of not less than 15%. i am convinced that this type of decision will help to maintain the structural balance throughout the european union. this directive has been in force for several years and has proved to be a key instrument in the elimination of distortions of competition in the economic sectors concerned. in the context of the functioning of the internal market of the eu countries, the proposed vat rate is still an effective safeguard against the loss of its stability.
in writing. ‒ increasing the effectiveness of the fight against serious crime and terrorism is particularly important in today's world. by improving the exchange of information between law enforcement agencies, we reduce the opportunities for criminals to exploit loopholes. any agreements in this area must be concluded in compliance with the data protection provisions contained in the new europol regulation. the text of the report expresses parliament's agreement to the conclusion of a cooperation agreement between europol and brazil to promote and enhance the effectiveness of actions and mutual cooperation in the prevention and combating of organised crime, terrorism and other forms of serious crime affecting at least two member states. the terms of the agreement shall provide for the exchange of information and may include expertise, general situation reports, results of strategic analyses, information on investigative procedures and crime prevention methods, participation in training activities, and advice and support in specific investigations.

in writing. ‒ the own-initiative report deals with the international management of areas beyond national jurisdiction, sometimes referred to as 'full seas'. un members are responsible for the protection and conservation of the world's waters under two international agreements: (1) the un convention on fisheries and (2) the un convention on the law of the sea (unclos). this report is a positive response to the decision to develop an international legally binding instrument under unclos to address the challenges of protecting the high seas. illegal, unreported and unregulated fishing, mining, energy drilling, pollution and marine litter all contribute to the damage done to marine habitats and ecosystems. the report calls on the commission to work with stakeholders to support the new instrument and highlights the eu's important role in ensuring the sustainable management of marine resources on the high seas. i voted in favour of the above document.
in writing. ‒ the great wealth of man is the natural environment and all that mother nature gives us. but we can't always respect what we have. in addition, our population is growing very rapidly, which results in an increasing demand for raw materials and natural resources. one such resource is the sea and the animals that live in it. the un initiative is therefore very welcome and gives great importance to the issue of marine biodiversity and the creation of an instrument that will allow the control of marine resources. in the management of marine resources, it is necessary to take fisheries into account. the creation of an effective instrument that ensures fisheries that are sustainable for ecosystems, respect conservation periods and respect endangered species should therefore be encouraged. in order to ensure that such an instrument is at least minimally effective, it is necessary to establish a control system which allows for the accounting of all operators using marine waters. such an instrument must take into account the specificities of developing countries and the difficulties that will arise in the implementation and enforcement of this instrument in the future. we must therefore ensure that the european union plays a significant role in the creation and implementation of this instrument.
in writing. ‒ the commission proposal combines four pieces of legislation on the fundamental principles for the management of farmed animals of the bovine, porcine, ovine, caprine and equine species into a single horizontal directive. the purpose of this directive is to provide a simplified and clear legal framework for the structuring of the breeding sector, rules for the management of breeding books/breeding registers, breeding and use value or genetic evaluation, rules for intra-eu trade and imports from third countries and rules for zootechnical official controls. the directive will facilitate free trade in high-quality breeding animals and their genetic material, contribute to the protection of breeds throughout the eu and improve cooperation between the competent authorities of the different member states in this field. i voted yes.
in writing. ‒ good legislation on trade in animals and their biological material is a prerequisite for high-quality breeding in europe, animal welfare and the provision of high-quality food to european consumers. the details of trade in animals are very important for the preservation of purity of breeds, which is of no small importance for example in the breeding of horses. just as consumers have a right to know where the products they buy come from, breeders need to know the origin of the breeding material they buy in order to be able to provide reliable information about their products to buyers. simple and transparent procedures to facilitate compliance with the rules laid down are also important for producers. simplification of procedures and modifications to official controls will allow effective enforcement of the new legislation. such a law will make a well-functioning livestock sector the perfect basis for all animal production in the european union.
in writing. ‒ a well-functioning livestock sector is essential for animal production in the eu, with an estimated value added of almost €2 billion. at present, there is a separate basic directive for each species and specific decisions and directives concerning, among other things, the recognition of trade organisations, the registration of farmed animals in books, certificates, valuation, genetic evaluation, etc. the european commission's proposal to consolidate all existing zootechnical legislation into a single regulation is a definite step in the right direction. the amendments proposed by parliament are equally important. particular attention should be paid to the decision on simplification of official controls, which aims to minimise the bureaucratic burden on breeders, many of whom are small and medium-sized enterprises. the production of livestock not only contributes to economic and social development but is also one of the fundamental pillars of food security in the union. i am therefore pleased that an agreement has been reached between the institutions to simplify the existing legislation in this area considerably, and that is why i have decided to vote in favour of parliament's report.
in writing. ‒ the european parliament's own-initiative report is a response to the migration agenda presented by the european commission in may 2015. this report was intended to present an ambitious and horizontal approach to all forms of migration within the eu, including legal migration, refugees, irregular migration and the schengen area. the proposals in the final report include, among others, a call for a mandatory eu-wide refugee relocation scheme, the replacement of the current dublin regulation with a centralised asylum application procedure via european hotspots (to allow for effective asylum applications throughout the union rather than in individual member states), and a call for humanitarian visas. in the absence of increased emphasis on strengthening external border controls, making returns and readmission of persons denied asylum more effective and combating trafficking in human beings, i could not support this report as the policy recommendations made do not represent a reasonable or sustainable solution to the current crisis in europe.
in writing. ‒ while welcoming the effort made in the report on the need for a comprehensive eu approach to migration and supporting the overall direction of humanitarian assistance to migrants and the eradication of the illegal smuggling industry that has grown in recent years, i strongly oppose some of the theses and proposals contained in the document. first of all, i do not support criticism of those states that, in order to properly implement national and eu law on border protection, build walls and fences, carefully check every asylum application and call for assistance to migrants in situ or in non-european transit countries. secondly, i do not agree with the thesis, which has been repeatedly put forward, that only a binding relocation mechanism will bring a solution to the migration crisis. on the contrary, it weakens the determination of eu border countries to stem the flow of refugees and effectively combat illegal migration. third, i do not agree that accepting refugees can be the cure for europe's demographic collapse and the associated labour market deficit. a much better solution to this problem would be legal labour migration, where the process of integration into the labour market is faster, cheaper and less risky for infiltration by undesirable people. in this context, the european commission should consider amending the blue card directive to cover other groups of workers than only highly qualified professionals.
in writing. ‒ the european parliament's own-initiative report is a response to the migration agenda presented by the european commission in may 2015. the report aimed to present an ambitious and horizontal approach to all forms of migration in the eu, including legal migration, refugees, irregular migration and the schengen area. the proposals in the final report include: calling for the introduction of a mandatory eu refugee relocation system; replacing the dublin regulation with a centralised asylum procedure via european hotspots (to allow for effective asylum applications throughout the union rather than in individual member states); calling for humanitarian visas; and other ways for economic migrants to gain legal access to the eu. the report under-emphasises the need to strengthen external border controls, to make returns and readmission of non-asylum seekers more effective, to combat trafficking in human beings, to focus on resettlement rather than intra-eu relocation, to implement existing rules more widely and to prevent secondary movements of asylum seekers, and to fund agencies such as europol, easo and frontex to speed up the processing of applications, to take decisions on applications and to fingerprint all arrivals. policy recommendations do not provide a sensible or sustainable solution to the current crisis in europe. for these reasons, i could not support the report.
in writing. ‒ the conflict in syria has brought over a million refugees to the european union in the past year alone, creating a migration crisis on a scale not seen since the end of the second world war. so far, the eu countries have not found a solution to the influx of such a large number of people. first of all, europe needs to change its thinking on migration. you can't keep looking for emergency solutions to emergency situations. it's a long process to actually deal with this problem. the services must draw a clear line between those who need protection and those who come to the old continent for profit. those who flee war and persecution first have the right to eu protection. the latter must rely on the decisions of the member states, since they control their labour markets. the return system needs to be improved, as only 36% of those who were to leave the union were successfully returned in 2014. moreover, the abolition of internal border controls in the schengen area must go hand in hand with the strengthening of the union's external borders, and those who remain in europe must respect the values on which the community is founded. all these elements were included in the report on the situation in the mediterranean and the need for a holistic eu approach to migration, which is why i decided to support it.
in writing. ‒ the migration crisis is a problem that is the result of political instability and very poor living conditions in the middle east and africa. all the proposals to solve this problem that come from the european institutions relate only to current affairs and to the treatment of the symptoms of this crisis, but there is nothing new to be found in solving the fundamental problem of preventing the breakdown of the states in the closest neighbourhood of the european union. this report is another such voice, which does not bring anything new and repeats the previously erroneous reasoning. the demand, with which i particularly disagree, is the call to continue the policy of relocating so-called refugees. the eu has also been active in the fight against terrorism, and has been active in the fight against organised crime, including organised crime in the former yugoslavia. the eu should focus on countering mass immigration and improving living conditions in refugee camps in lebanon and turkey. liberalisation of asylum and schengen border crossing rules will increase the threat of terrorism and lead to an escalation of the migration crisis. as a result, many member states will take action on their own to secure their borders, threatening to break up the schengen area. this report gives the prospect of an effective solution to the migration crisis affecting europe. i voted against his acceptance.
in writing. ‒ the report stresses the importance of the principles of subsidiarity and proportionality and the need for a stronger involvement of national parliaments in the eu legislative process. the report proposes greater inclusion of suggestions from national parliaments, including on preparatory work such as green and white papers, an extension of the period of consultation with national parliaments in subsidiarity checks and a wider dialogue between the european commission and each national parliament through an annual debate. i voted to accept the report.
in writing. ‒ compliance with the principles of subsidiarity and proportionality is the basis for the functioning of the european union. they help to define when the eu has legislative powers and contributes to decision-making in accordance with the principle of 'nearby citizens' and which actions taken by the community institutions are necessary and essential to achieve the objectives of the treaty. the increased involvement of national parliaments in the european legislative process in recent years has resulted in a greater awareness of the principles on which the eu is based, including the principles of subsidiarity and proportionality in the interinstitutional context. the subsidiarity control mechanism is essential for cooperation between the european and national institutions. it allows national parliaments to give an opinion if they consider that a draft eu legislative act does not comply with the principle of subsidiarity. the number of such opinions has increased significantly in recent years, accounting for 25% of all applications in 2012 and 30% in 2013. in addition, in 2012 a yellow card procedure was initiated for the first time, which led, inter alia, to the commission's decision to withdraw the proposal for collective action in the context of the freedom of establishment and the freedom to provide services, due to a lack of political support.
in writing. ‒ the report on the european commission's report on the application of the principle of subsidiarity and proportionality comes at a time when the future of the european union and the principle of the common functioning of the member states are being discussed anew. the broad support for and positive feedback on this report shows that the fundamental principle of the eu's functioning, subsidiarity, should be addressed more often and more deeply in the legislative process, so that it can benefit the member states, provide added value, and be a tool that solves problems at european level better than the member states acting alone. this report, in addition to calling for greater involvement and a stronger voice of national parliaments in european law-making, recalls the already existing tools for assessing the effects of regulation in the context of the subsidiarity principle. this is necessary at a time when many ep reports go beyond the eu's remit, encroach on the member states' remit and cause unnecessary tension and division. the subsidiarity principle does not mean that the ep cannot have a say in national policies, but only that common solutions in this area require the voluntary cooperation of the member states and cannot be imposed from above as a 'european answer to a problem', but should be built from the bottom up, on the basis of the exchange of good practices and then the coordination of selected actions so as to benefit from cooperation without restricting the freedom of the member states.
in writing. ‒ the principle of subsidiarity is a very valuable tool in the process of european law-making. it provides an opportunity to verify that action taken at european level is justified and effective. this principle gives member states and national parliaments the opportunity to express themselves and to take a position that takes account of their perspective. in many cases, the application of this principle has avoided the adoption of regulations that would have been much more effective if the specific national circumstances had been taken into account and the matter had been left to the legislator of a particular member state. promoting the principle of subsidiarity and its particular importance should be an important task for the european institutions, and in particular for the european parliament, which is the voice of the citizens of the member states. in many cases, a wider inclusion of this voice would avoid legal absurdities and improve the functioning of the european administration. i agree with the report's theses, which show that the european commission does not listen enough to the member states' voices and to the concerns they raise. a constructive dialogue between the commission and the member states should be the basis for effective legislation. it should take account of the key role of the member states in shaping european policy and be more open to the reservations that national parliaments have about commission proposals. i agree with the conclusions of this report and support the call for a better application of the principle of subsidiarity in the work of the european institutions.
in writing. ‒ excessive bureaucracy is one of the most serious problems facing the eu today, affecting not only the quality of existing law but also the lives of european citizens and their relationship with the community. the refit regulatory efficiency and performance programme was designed to consolidate better law-making procedures and reduce administrative and regulatory burdens. since its introduction, some improvements have been made in legislative practice, but much remains to be done. the commission's decision of 2015 to review all legislative initiatives adopted to date and, if necessary, to update or eliminate them is in this respect welcome. the parliament's report rightly stressed that an ex post evaluation of the union's legislation is also necessary, as well as an obligation on the commission to carry out an impact test of the new legislation on smes, especially since 20 million smes represent 99% of all businesses in the eu. all these steps are important parts of the process of making the european union work better and should be taken as quickly and as effectively as possible, otherwise the union will remain a bureaucratic bogeyman, multiplying low-quality legislation that does not serve european citizens as it should.
in writing. ‒ the report highlights the issues that are important for the preparation of high-quality legislation to better meet the objectives of the single market. it complements the work on better regulation undertaken by the juri committee and the empl committee's report on business and job creation, prepared by the ecr rapporteur, which adopted the principles of better regulation in relation to the work of the employment committee. the report includes support for a number of ecr policy priorities, including: respect for the principle of subsidiarity; the value of impact assessments and consultation; and, importantly from the imco perspective, the need for an effective enforcement and monitoring system. these areas need to work together in order for the single market to function effectively and to ensure a level playing field for all. with that in mind, i voted yes.
in writing. ‒ the european union is currently under fire for its overregulation and excessive bureaucracy. effective action is needed to make the community more effective and clearer in demonstrating its usefulness to its citizens. the creation of more and more unnecessary regulations is definitely not a step in the right direction. this situation not only leads to a low quality of legislation but also creates a lot of confusion and uncertainty for consumers and businesses. the parliament's report aims to examine how to improve the functioning of the single market to make it more efficient. it rightly emphasises the importance of smes and calls for an assessment of the impact of legislation on smes at every stage of consultation, implementation, monitoring and enforcement. it is of the utmost importance for businesses that the law which is created is transparent, predictable, effective and interferes as little as possible with their activities. in my view, european legislative initiatives can only be justified if they have added value. this is also the position expressed in the report on the drive to improve the single market, and i have therefore decided to vote in favour of its adoption.
in writing. ‒ ensuring the effective functioning of the single market is a key task for the european institutions. the european union is a community of economic interests based on close economic cooperation between its member states. greater transparency in the legislative process and the simplification of many provisions will certainly contribute to improving the functioning of the single market. we need to create a better environment for entrepreneurship and job creation, including in a cross-border context. the report responds to many of the european conservatives and reformists group's calls for european law-making, including better application of the subsidiarity principle, preparation of a sound impact assessment of proposed regulations before they are adopted, wider public consultation on proposed legal solutions with the communities and actors targeted by proposed legislation, and greater emphasis on assessing the real impact of proposed regulations and their impact on the effective functioning of the single market. i believe that the report presented takes account of the demands of the juri, empl and imco committees to improve the legislative process in the european union on the regulation of the single market. i voted for this report.
