in writing. ‒ erasmus+ is the eu's programme for education, training, youth and sport. the report aims to highlight the tools used in lifelong learning and mobility and to suggest improvements. the final report, which was voted on in committee, contains a number of positive ideas, such as a call for the extension of existing initiatives on mobility in vocational education and training in terms of accessibility, especially for disadvantaged families, and measures to facilitate integration into the labour market. however, it also contains some problematic issues, such as the call for funding of language support for all participants in erasmus+ programmes without language restrictions, and unnecessary recommendations, such as the creation of an eu e-mobility card and the recognition of erasmus+ names and graphic symbols as trademarks, with the possibility of their use only in erasmus+ publications. in addition, the report calls on the member states to introduce a 'dual education' approach to secondary education, which is too prescriptive and beyond the eu's competence. some of the proposals in the report are not sufficiently detailed, for example the proposal to create a european standard on mobility in vocational education and training. in view of the above, i abstained.
in writing. ‒ the new erasmus+ programme is a great opportunity for young people. it is also a support for the european labour market and a response to challenges. the ageing of the population and the continuing rise in youth unemployment mean that we have to look for new solutions. we have always placed a great deal of emphasis on academic exchanges, and the labour market is also in need of highly qualified professionals. the economy also needs good workers with a lower level of education, who are experts in their field, have a good knowledge and do their job well. moving to another country and being able to practise your profession in a new environment is a unique experience that can help young people become more open, flexible, mobile and independent. and these are the qualities that employers are looking for most these days. such exchanges also provide an opportunity to compare the technologies and traditions of different countries. this programme will enable the most talented young people, as well as the poor who cannot afford private travel, to broaden their educational horizons and improve their skills. erasmus+ will help to level the playing field for young people, which will also support the balanced development of the economies of the member states.

in writing. ‒ coastal fishing is a very important form of fishing in the member states. in most coastal and island areas, coastal fishing is a traditional form of fishing, a way of life and an important source of livelihood. special measures and support are needed to ensure the growth and development of areas dependent on coastal fisheries. the report calls on the commission to step up its efforts to protect coastal fishing in fisheries-dependent regions and to adopt a definition of traditional coastal fishing that is consistent with the specific characteristics of the different regions. the report also looks at ways in which diversification and innovation could help coastal regions. it also analysed how the european maritime and fisheries fund (emff) has diversified the economic structure of coastal regions. the rapporteur stresses the importance of innovation and scientific research for coastal regions. i voted in favour of the report because of its content and the nature of the document.
in writing. ‒ the report focuses on the external dimension of the common fisheries policy (cfp), which provides a framework for the activities of eu vessels fishing outside eu territorial waters. the eu's fishing fleet is one of the largest in the world and ranks among the top three fishing powers in the world, so its reach is important. eu-flagged vessels may fish in waters outside the eu in two ways: on the high seas (areas outside national jurisdiction) and in the territorial waters of third countries under a bilateral fisheries agreement. the report addresses a number of issues related to fisheries in the territorial waters of third countries, including the obligation to strengthen cooperation between individual rfmos and ensure consistency between their measures, the training of fisheries inspectors and crew members, the transparency of fisheries partnership agreements, the fight against illegal, unreported and unregulated fishing, and the promotion of social and environmental standards in the fisheries sector in the third country concerned. i voted to accept the report.
madam president, last month many of us were personally touched by the attacks in brussels. we should act together if we want to ensure our security. the only answer is prevention. this means an obligatory model of sharing information among law enforcement in real time with coordination at european level, first of all cooperation on intelligence, implementation of pnr and ‘smart borders’ control with guarantees of real-time monitoring and processing of the data. we need to adopt pnr in its current form. fast work is also needed on the directive on counterterrorism, which is the key to fighting all kinds of supporters of terrorism and criminalising their activities. we need a coordinated approach to foreign fighters and returnees to challenge the radicalisation processes, to offer education for young people grappling with extremism in the public area, and to consider how to counteract the growing the role of the darknet in the promotion and support for terrorist groups. all of those elements are important for better prevention and achieving victory in combating terrorism.
in writing. until now, systematic checks on persons crossing the external borders have only been applied to third-country nationals. the amendment to the schengen borders code introducing mandatory and systematic checks on eu citizens based on the use of appropriate databases at the external borders should be adopted before the summer break. this will help to counter terrorist threats in europe. in addition, the commission should also present without delay a decision on the interoperability and systematic access to and exchange of information from european union-wide databases such as ecris, sis ii, vis, eurodac and the widespread deployment of an eu automated fingerprinting system that would be integrated into sis. the pilot project exists, but first it must be fully legalised. this is necessary to prevent further terrorist attacks. moreover, the systematic exchange of information contained in national databases between member states is also important. in addition, the european commission must ensure that data and information can be exchanged between agencies such as europol and frontex without further legal obstacles.
in writing. the successive attacks by the islamic state remind us that europe's and the world's fight against terrorism is a process that will not end quickly. the threat persists despite increased precautions and increased controls, especially in vulnerable areas that could be potential targets for attackers. it is necessary to continue to pursue activities in the field of the control, prevention and prosecution of crime, in particular in situations where it may be linked to terrorism. it is also important to be aware that the eu's internal and external security are closely interlinked and it is virtually impossible to achieve one without taking the other into account. in this context, it is particularly important to seal borders, to cooperate between member states and their authorities responsible for security and law enforcement, and to exchange efficiently the information needed to ensure reliable controls at the eu's external borders. security, control, migration, protection of sensitive data are issues that are relevant to our daily lives, and their boundaries will have to be redefined. europe is currently undergoing a change in the social order, and this is not a process that we can stop, but we should work to ensure that this new order guarantees us the protection of european life and values and security.

in writing. we already debated in the ep in may last year about tightening the rules on anti-money laundering and tax evasion. under the provisions of the then adopted anti-money laundering directive (amld), banks, financial institutions and persons with a legitimate interest in accessing the central register are obliged to pay attention to suspicious transactions. the discovery of the biggest financial scam in history, the panama papers, which revealed information on more than 200,000 offshore companies and their secret owners, who had committed billions in tax fraud, was the result of the insight and cooperation of hundreds of journalists affiliated with the international consortium of investigative journalists (icij). efforts should be stepped up in all member states to combat tax fraud effectively. the existence of tax havens should be categorically opposed. a european-wide blacklist of them, along with a list of where the information is hidden, should be drawn up and sanctions imposed on the organisations that use them. and representatives of the leaked law firm mossack fonseca and representatives of the panamanian government should appear before the special parliamentary committee on taxation, taxe ii.
in writing. panama's geographical location is favourable to the development of international trade and banking services. panama's reputation as a tax haven has been built over 100 years. the attractiveness of offshore companies operating in tax havens lies, among others, in: complete secrecy of information (including access to data on company owners), low or zero income taxation, no requirement for tax returns. tax evasion and money laundering through offshore have thus become some of the most lucrative financial crimes for many entities around the world. the law firm mossack fonseca, which has been in operation since 1977, has achieved perfection in financial arrangements based on the concealment of the real beneficiaries and bank accounts associated with the company. the scale of the activities disclosed requires the urgent establishment of an effective common policy to combat tax havens. while there are international rules on tax transparency and the eu, in cooperation with the member states, has developed a number of tools (a list of international tax havens, three fiscal reform packages focusing mainly on the exchange of information within the eu, agreements with third countries to exchange information also outside the eu), the panama papers scandal should be used to improve the effectiveness of existing measures and thus tackle such fraud.
in writing. it is good that the council and the commission have brought matters of tax avoidance and money laundering to the ep's attention as a matter of urgency. this is the result of the recent panama papers scandal, which showed that tax evasion is a mass phenomenon. it goes without saying that this has negative effects on economies, on the equality of market participants, on the increasing inequalities between people and, finally, on the ability to solve serious social problems. the scary thing is that this one case alone exposes the information of over 200,000 companies and their owners who, in order to avoid paying taxes, register their companies in tax havens. since this is not the first case of this kind, i am in favour of not ending the case with a debate. the european parliament should set up a special committee to deal with all tax matters in the european union. a european-wide blacklist of tax havens and places where information on tax avoidance is deliberately withheld should be established. the union's solutions, as well as those of the individual member states, must lead to the reduction of these pathologies.
mr president, i think we can all agree in this chamber that it is unacceptable that large corporations should not pay taxes in the country where they make their profits, and that small and mediumsized enterprises should bear the heaviest burden of taxation. it is particularly pleased that president juncker seems to share this view, which has not always been the case in the past, judging by his previous activities. country-by-country reporting seems to be the right tool to combat tax avoidance, not tax harmonisation. that is why i do think that the proposal put forward by commissioner hill is a good step in the right direction. it is noteworthy that corporations are required to disclose tax information to the public. it is important that the disclosed reports also include subsidiaries registered in countries designated by the eu as tax havens. however, it is worrying that only about 10 to 15 per cent of multinational corporations would be affected, as the commission's proposal would only make publicly reportable companies with an annual turnover of more than eur 75 million. and here's where you might want to think about changing that point of the proposal.
mr president, i welcome the proposal by the commission on mandatory disclosure by multinational companies of income tax information. this is yet another legislative initiative aimed at improving tax collection and reducing the scope for tax evasion and aggressive tax planning in europe. it responds to the growing demand from european citizens for more transparency and fairness in tax policies. i believe we are all keen to ensure as conducive a business environment as possible for european companies, but at the same time we expect these companies to pay their fair share of taxes in our countries. the draft directive requires multinational companies to make public information on a well-defined and limited set of tax information. it does not impose on them an additional administrative burden, as all the required information is already reported by companies to their shareholders and respective national tax authorities. it helps to re-establish a level playing field between eu and non-eu companies and it reduces the scope for aggressive tax planning by large multinationals. it also raises public awareness of tax issues and strengthens the sense of corporate social responsibility among european businesses. however, having said that, i would like to call on the commission and parliament not to go too far with the new requirements. the need for more tax transparency must not hamper the competitive position of european enterprises vis-à-vis their international rivals. our ambition should be to ensure that the eu becomes the most attractive and business—friendly region globally.

in writing. ‒ the european globalisation adjustment fund (egf) helps workers find new jobs and develop new skills when they have lost their jobs as a result of changes in the structure of world trade, such as when a large company closes a factory or relocates outside the eu or during the global financial and economic crisis. this application from sweden concerns the mobilisation of a total amount of eur 1 793 710 for the reintegration into the labour market of 500 of the 647 redundant workers, mainly in the upper norrland region. 470 workers were made redundant by the volvo truck operation emea group following the reduction at its umeå plant, and the remaining 177 by 4 suppliers and downstream manufacturers. i fully support actions that generate growth and jobs. i voted yes.
in writing. ‒ the european globalisation adjustment fund is crucial to keeping european workers competitive in the labour market. the fund supports the redundancies of large enterprises, which are often the main employers in the region, by offering them the opportunity not only to improve their skills in the profession but also to completely re-qualify themselves. in the case of the volvo plant in umeå, the redundancies were the result of a decrease in the production and export of heavy trucks to new asian producers. moreover, the region, whose capital is umeå, is known for its highly skilled industries, while the majority of the redundant workers have only a secondary education. the european globalisation adjustment fund was therefore necessary in this case. however, it should be borne in mind that globalisation also has a major impact on the functioning of small and medium-sized enterprises. unfortunately, they cannot count on such generous aid, even though they employ more people in total and account for a larger share of gdp than individual large enterprises. it would therefore be appropriate to create a similar support mechanism for european smes.
in writing. ‒ the european globalisation adjustment fund (egf) helps workers find new jobs and acquire new skills when they lose their jobs as a result of changes in the structure of world trade, for example when a large company closes a factory or relocates outside the eu or when we are faced with a global financial and economic crisis. on 22 february 2016, the commission adopted a new proposal to mobilise the egf. article 11 (1) of the egf regulation provides that during the year a maximum of 0,5% of the available budget (eur 150 million in 2011 prices) may be mobilised to provide technical assistance at the initiative of the commission. the commission wishes to use eur 380 000 (0.23% of the maximum annual budget in 2016 prices) to cover monitoring and data collection, information, knowledge base building, administrative and technical support and evaluation activities. i support measures that, when implemented, create growth and jobs. however, i do not believe that the egf is the appropriate instrument for such a policy and an effective tool offering the right value for money for the reintegration of redundant workers back into the labour market. in view of the above, i abstained.

in writing. ‒ glyphosate is an active substance used in plant protection products and authorised in all member states. it is subject to strict rules which allow its use as long as it does not have negative effects on human health and the environment. the marketing authorisation for glyphosate expires on 30 june 2016. the proposed renewal of the marketing authorisation objected was granted in accordance with regulation 1107/2009. it provides for a detailed safety and environmental impact assessment to be carried out by efsa and germany (acting as rapporteur). the investigation concluded that glyphosate does not cause unacceptable risks when used appropriately this result is consistent with other assessments. in addition, the implementing measure provides that the substance poe-tallowamine (mixed with glyphosate to produce a pesticide) should be excluded from the production of plant protection products containing glyphosate and that a negative list of similar substances will be issued in july 2016. given that the document does not ensure a high level of protection of human and animal health and the environment, does not respect the precautionary principle and is therefore not in line with the basic act, regulation 1107/2009, i voted against.
in writing. ‒ glyphosate is a substance used in the production of herbicides. in addition to its use in horticulture and forestry, it is used primarily for crop protection in agriculture, and since its introduction in 1974, glyphosate production has increased nearly 260-fold. i think that's a testament to its efficacy and safety for human, animal and plant health. in line with the 2002 findings, the european commission proposed by means of an implementing regulation the renewal of the marketing authorisation for glyphosate. i believe that one of the most popular and effective ingredients used in the production of plant protection products should not be withdrawn from the market without scientifically sound arguments and solid evidence of its harmful effects on humans and the environment. we must not create any additional difficulties for our farmers, who have already been in a difficult situation in recent years. at the same time, we must remember that if we ban the use of substances that have been tested and proven, we increase the risk of using substitutes that are much more harmful and are distributed illegally. and that would be a very unwise decision.
in writing. ‒ glyphosate is one of the most widely used herbicides by european farmers, foresters and gardeners, and it is currently difficult to find an alternative. on the other hand, there are rumors that it may be carcinogenic, but there is no conclusive evidence. it is therefore good that today's resolution, thanks to the efforts of our group, the group of the european people's party, has acquired a more balanced character than in the original version. on the one hand, we called for the renewal of the approval of glyphosate for 7 years, not 15 years, as proposed by the european commission, but on the condition that it is used only for professional use, and at the same time asking the relevant authorities to re-examine the case. hopefully, the final decision on the approval of glyphosate will take due account of the fact that i mentioned that the possible withdrawal of this active substance from the market will cause serious disruption in european agriculture, which may endanger the competitiveness of our production in relation to third countries that do not plan such actions.
in writing. ‒ in recent months, reports have circulated in europe about a controversial chemical called glyphosate, which is widely used as an ingredient in plant protection products. recent studies have shown that this substance is a real health hazard and increases the risk of cancer in humans and animals. however, the european commission has proposed to renew the approval of this substance for a further 15 years. in many countries, glyphosate is still allowed, while in others it is completely banned. in the context of a single market and unrestricted trade in goods, it is important that the union has a unified position on this issue, and therefore the european parliament's response calling on the european commission to reconsider or withdraw its decision on the renewal of the approval of this substance is justified. the union's objective should be to ensure a high level of protection of human and animal health and the environment, and to improve the functioning of the internal market, and i have therefore decided to vote in favour of a parliament resolution calling on the commission to take immediate action to achieve these objectives.
in writing. ‒ in many ways, the sandra kalniete report reflects the european commission's intentions for the creation of a military dimension to the eu. it is clear from its content that 'the main objective should be to promote permanent multinational troops and voluntary joint defence forces and to formulate a community defence policy which should ultimately lead to community defence'. as i believe that defence policy should remain a matter for the sovereign decision of the member states and nato remains the foundation of european security, i have decided to abstain.
in writing. ‒ in many ways, the sandra kalniete report reflects the european commission's intentions for the creation of a military dimension to the eu. one of the paragraphs states that 'the main objective should be to promote permanent multinational troops and voluntary joint defence forces and to formulate a community defence policy which should ultimately lead to community defence'. defence policy should remain a matter for the sovereignty of the member states and no action should be taken to increase the eu's role in this area. the foundation of european security remains nato. that's why i abstained.
in writing. - years of peaceful coexistence are coming to an end. the union must adapt to a new, complex and complex reality. therefore, in my view, one of the key objectives of our global foreign and security policy strategy should be to strengthen the eu's defence capability. the european security strategy of 2003 described threats that are now partly obsolete, which is why it is so important that the union develops a new global strategy that addresses the most important and urgent security challenges. the european parliament's report rightly outlines the need to take action to create a european defence union. because relying on the united states and nato forces in the face of so many threats in our immediate neighborhood can be risky. moreover, the need to focus on the security of the region first, rather than on all conflicts, as outlined in the document, seems to be the most appropriate. otherwise, the community may lose credibility. i am glad that parliament has proposed such a sound and appropriate analysis of the european union in a changing global environment, which is why i have decided to vote in favour of the report.
in writing. ‒ the european union is facing crises, both external and internal. the main challenges are migration, the situation in ukraine, but also terrorism, brexit and the economic situation in many member states. to counter them effectively, long-term solutions should be the main priority, not just short-term and piecemeal ones. in this context, compromise and solidarity are essential. the eu must speak with one voice on issues that affect our common security, such as the migration crisis, the conflicts in ukraine and syria, and energy security. a stable neighbourhood, as one of the essential conditions for international security, is a priority. the effects of political instability are being felt today in the wave of refugees seeking refuge in europe. the eu's eastern neighbourhood should therefore continue to be supported in its efforts to create conditions conducive to stability and prosperity based on the rule of law and respect for human rights. in addition, consistent cooperation in defence research, industrial base and cyber defence will be key in the coming years. the joint use of military capabilities, in particular of multinational military units such as the eurocorps, will contribute to a more efficient use of defence resources, while increasing the benefits of scale through mutual cooperation. however, such ambitious goals require adequate funding. it is therefore necessary to reflect in the eu budget the priorities of the eu global strategy.
in writing. ‒ the european union is very often trying to play a role in global politics that it is not meant to play. the eu was created from the outset with the desire for closer economic integration, rather than a desire to duplicate the role of the institutions that were created to deal with military security. defence matters are and should remain a matter for the exclusive discretion of the member states. the attempt to extend the powers of the european institutions to this area is incompatible with the fundamental values on which the eu is built. the only institution that can effectively support european countries in the development of their defence policy is the north atlantic alliance. it is thanks to close institutional cooperation with the united states that we have military capabilities that are of real value. i agree with many of the diagnoses in this report, but i think the solutions proposed are wrong. the european union, faced with an immigration crisis, has no capacity to play a greater role in shaping the security policies of its members. the failures of member states in the fight against terrorism show that instead of looking for new solutions, we need to learn more from our american partners. instead of multiplying tasks and objectives, we need to better enforce existing legislation and to be more effective in the tasks that lie ahead. i do not agree with the idea of increasing the eu's role in the defence policy of the member states, because this would undermine the integrity and effectiveness of nato's action. i voted against the adoption of this report.
in writing. ‒ the report on the implementation and review of the eu strategy for central asia underlines that the new eu strategy for central asia is adopted in the context of the growing importance of the region and the eu's increased engagement in neighbouring afghanistan, the extension of the european neighbourhood policy to the caspian sea region, the eu's continued support for the reform and modernisation of post-soviet societies, and the eu's energy security interests. the report also identifies security threats and challenges that require cooperation between central asia and the eu. the eu's efforts to improve economic and political stability in a region whose geopolitical position is becoming increasingly complex and fragile due to the growing conflict of interests between the russian federation and the eu in this area and the vulnerability to the influence of extremist and terrorist groups operating in afghanistan, iran and pakistan should be supported. i voted yes.
in writing. ‒ in june 2007, the european union adopted a strategy for a new partnership with central asia in recognition of the region's growing importance for the eu, especially in the areas of security, stability and diversification of energy sources. this strategy sets the framework for the union's relations with kazakhstan, kyrgyzstan, tajikistan, turkmenistan and uzbekistan. the 2007 strategy identified seven main areas of cooperation. these are: democratisation, human rights, youth and education, economic development, trade and investment, energy and transport, sustainable environment and water, common threats and challenges, intercultural dialogue. most of these priorities have not lost their relevance. despite the progress made in relations with the countries of central asia, there is a need to intensify cooperation, especially in the fields of trade and energy. a similar position was taken in the ep report, which stressed the need to strengthen economic ties, eu support for democratic change and better cooperation in the fight against organised crime and terrorism. furthermore, the report rightly noted that a differentiated approach based on conditionality and incentives is needed to achieve better results both bilaterally and regionally.
in writing. ‒ central asia is a region of immense political and economic importance, which has been in the orbit of many actors since the collapse of the soviet union. russia, china and the united states are trying to strengthen their presence and pursue their own economic interests there. europe should also be present in the region and take advantage of its advantageous position. the countries of the region present varying levels of economic development and political stability, but there is no doubt that the european union should deepen and continue cooperation with each central asian country. this cooperation must be multi-faceted, taking into account economic exchanges, the common fight against terrorism and radicalisation, and the fight against organised crime and drug trafficking. we cannot, of course, ignore the problems these young states face in building stable civil societies, but we cannot easily condemn and punish them for the difficult geopolitical and cultural conditions in which they have to operate. the european union should monitor the human rights situation in the region and provide all the assistance that the central asian states will need to build standards of democracy and the rule of law. we must place particular emphasis on the education of young people and the possibility of exchange of pupils and students. i agree with the present policy and future eu strategy towards central asia as set out in this report and therefore voted in favour of its adoption.

in writing. ‒ on 1 february 2016, the ihr (international health regulations) emergency committee declared that the zika virus outbreak had created a public health emergency of international concern. experts agreed that there is a strong suspicion of a causal relationship between zika virus infection during pregnancy and microcephaly, but this has not yet been scientifically confirmed. the consensus was that there was an urgent need to coordinate international efforts to improve surveillance, increase control of mosquito populations and accelerate work on diagnostic tests and vaccines for those at risk, especially pregnant women. the eu early warning and response system has been activated. studies on the transmission of the virus, the health effects of infection (including a suspected link to microcephaly) and ways of controlling the virus (including the development of vaccines) should continue. unfortunately, the proposals in many of the amendments are not based on scientific knowledge (suggesting a link between the use of a larvicide called 'pyriproxyfen' and microcephaly, with the additional suspicion that this larvicide causes an increase in the number of cases of microcephaly), and are also contrary to eu competence. the zika virus cannot be used as an excuse to pressure certain countries to change their abortion laws. that's why i couldn't support the report.
in writing. ‒ nearly a year after the first reported cases of zika virus infection, new cases have been reported in 45 countries and the number of cases is rising, especially in brazil. worse, there is evidence that the virus contributes to birth defects and serious neurological complications. however, no effective treatment or prevention has yet been found. due to the high mobility of people, epidemiological risks on other continents should in no case be disregarded. the approaching summer season means an increased risk of transmission of the virus to europe. so we need a proper strategy, especially to control the mosquitoes that are the main carriers of zika. so far, the commission has allocated €10 million for research into the virus and the european medicines agency (ema) has set up an expert group to find drugs or vaccines against the virus. the european commission's activities should therefore be multi-pronged. the situation needs to be monitored further and support countries where the situation is most critical, increase eu citizens' awareness of preventive measures to avoid the spread of the virus and develop modern treatments.
in writing. ‒ the zika virus epidemic is a serious problem that the european union should be actively involved in addressing. we have the funding, the scientists and the research institutes to support the efforts to find an effective vaccine. there are alarming signs that the epidemic is spreading to other countries. the authorities of the south american countries should make it a priority to halt the epidemic and europe should support these efforts to the extent of its resources. such a pragmatic approach would deserve full support, but - as is often the case in this house - pragmatism very often loses out in the face of ideology. the reference to abortion in this text and the call for countries facing the effects of the zika virus epidemic to liberalize abortion laws is a mistake and a misunderstanding of the problem. i cannot support a resolution in which parliament wants to use the tragedy of so many women and children to promote abortion as a universal cure for all the problems of developing countries. taking a life is never the right thing to do, and in this particular case, it's not going to get us any closer to ending this epidemic. i support taking all necessary action to combat the zika epidemic, but i cannot agree with the demands for easier access to abortion that are in this text. that is why i voted against this resolution.

in writing. ‒ this regulation updates the general data protection directive of 1995, which was adopted in december 1995. it has been more than 20 years since the adoption of this directive. the use and dependence of the data economy, including attitudes towards the use of personal data, have changed significantly over this period. this regulation reflects the change and the need to ensure that individuals have adequate legal protection and a right to redress and service providers clear guidelines on how they are allowed to process personal data. i hope that the new rules will increase consumer confidence and create a level playing field across the eu, which will contribute to future investment in the single market. i voted to accept the document.

in writing. ‒ the directive will oblige airlines to provide eu law enforcement authorities with basic data such as ticket number, name and surname, and how passengers arriving or departing from the eu make payments, to help authorities fight terrorism and serious cross-border crime. the proposed directive introduces clear rules on the collection, use and retention of pnr data, as well as a strong framework for data protection and passenger rights. the provisions of the directive include a five-year retention period, both in the case of terrorism and serious crime. after 6 months of storage, the data will be masked (anonymised) by the authorities. there is a specific, closed list of crimes for which data can be used in the investigation and prosecution. there is a set of clear rules on the use of data, including the requirement for a data protection officer to be present in the relevant law enforcement units, guidelines on data management, independent supervision and monitoring, and an explicit reference to eu data protection rules. the directive also provides for a two-year review mechanism. the review will include an assessment of the need to include non-carrier economic operators in the scope of the directive, as well as an assessment of all aspects of the directive in terms of proportionality and necessity, with particular regard to the requirements of the court of justice in relation to the data retention directive. given the nature of the document, i voted in favour of it.
in writing. ‒ i voted in favour of the report on the use of passenger name record (pnr) data. the pnr system has been in the works for some time, but we have not yet been able to reach a political compromise on this. however, recent events in brussels, paris and many other places around the world have shown that the threat landscape is changing dramatically and that this change requires us to develop effective solutions to protect the security of our citizens. there is no longer room for 'business as usual' or for disputes of a strictly political nature, nor can we afford to postpone this decision again. we need action here and now. with tools like pnr, we are better able to fight terrorism and organised crime, as we are able to identify those who pose a threat to the security of our citizens more quickly. i understand and support the arguments about the need to respect the security of personal data, but i believe that the pnr directive provides good standards in this respect as well.
in writing. - we cannot allow the world to be ruled by terrorism. the air passenger name record (pnr) directive is a very important instrument to enhance the safety of europeans. by analysing the data collected, counter-terrorism services will be able to identify suspicious patterns of behaviour and take action against them. the proposed legislation is not a panacea, but it is a very important tool in the fight against terrorism and organised crime. but it is important to remember that there must be a balance between the genuine need to fight terrorism and the rights of citizens to privacy and to function in a modern society. citizens of democratic societies cannot be forced to give up the civil rights, the human rights, that they have been fighting for for centuries. there is a risk that legislative measures adopted in response to the threat of terrorism may restrict civil liberties. therefore, a cautious approach is essential. the standards of protection of personal data proposed in the directive are of a very high standard. there is no mass collection of data, only the ability to give law enforcement access to selected information. the directive clearly states that data may be collected, stored and processed only for the purposes of preventing and detecting serious crime and terrorist acts
in writing. ‒ terrorism and organised crime are two of the most deadly threats to democratic and peaceful societies. we are losing more and more in this unequal battle, and we need to look for tools that will allow us to better detect and combat threats to the security of our citizens. pnr data is a source of information that enables services to identify and eliminate threats before a tragedy occurs. i understand the concerns about privacy and the shifting boundaries of government access to personal data, but in a situation where people are dying, we have to accept that compromise. the role of policymakers is to ensure that this data is used properly and does not fall into the wrong hands. we are at war with an enemy who does not take the necessary measures, who does not respect our freedoms and rights or our lives. we have to sacrifice some of our imagination and some of our dreams for the efficiency of our actions. of course, this boundary cannot be pushed indefinitely. each entity and service that receives access to pnr data must be subject to democratic control and operate within the limits of the law. i believe we can provide that control. the implementation of these rules should not, of course, impose any new obligations on airlines or passengers. member states should make every effort to ensure that the transmission and exchange of such data does not constitute an excessive administrative burden. i voted to accept these solutions as proposed.
in writing. ‒ the proposal for a directive is of particular importance as its main objective is to establish a set of rules to improve the competitiveness of european businesses through innovation, thus strengthening europe's position as a leader in the global industrial market. in the process of researching and developing new ideas, products or services, we are confronted with a lot of information that is crucial to our idea of competitiveness or business, but which does not fall within the scope of intellectual property rights. trade secrets are therefore a complementary tool for protecting such information, and it was necessary and important for the commission to regulate at eu level the acquisition, use or disclosure of such information. the directive also provides a legal framework for victims of trade secret theft to claim compensation. theft of trade secrets is a growing problem in the eu. given the nature of the document, i voted in favour of it.
in writing. ‒ trade secrets are valuable assets held by all companies, regardless of industry or size. this information determines the company's ability to innovate, develop and compete in the domestic and international market. europe has a strong position in science and innovation, which gives it the potential to become a global leader. at present, trade secrets are legally protected only if someone gains confidential information by unauthorized means. one in five companies has reported at least one attempt to steal its trade secrets in the last ten years. the conditions for the pursuit of innovative business activities should therefore be improved. there are considerable differences in the legislation of the member states. only some of them have a definition of trade secrets in their legislation or provisions to protect them. this means that they are not protected to an equivalent degree throughout the union, leading to a fragmentation of the internal market in this area and to a weakening of the deterrent effect that those rules should have. in this context, the commission adopted a comprehensive strategy on intellectual property in may 2011 in which it committed itself to examining the protection of trade secrets. the present proposal is a further step towards the fulfilment of this commitment to create a single market in intellectual property by introducing common definitions and rules in this area.
in writing. ‒ protecting against the unlawful acquisition, disclosure and use of trade secrets is crucial to ensuring that businesses have a fair business environment. of course, it is important to remember that the circulation of knowledge and information is also of great importance for the process of innovation and creativity. however, companies should be free to decide when, with whom and what information they want to share. the eu directive on the protection of trade secrets of the european parliament and the council offers concrete solutions to combat industrial espionage. it should be noted that the rules on the protection of trade secrets have been laid down in a wide variety of legal acts adopted by the member states. in particular, there was no european definition of a trade secret and no common catalogue of actions that an injured party could take. the creation of a common european framework for the protection of trade secrets in the form of directives is an important step towards building a secure environment for european companies, ensuring the protection of their intangible assets and know-how. at the same time, it should be noted that the adopted document contains appropriate mechanisms that minimise the risk of unjustified claims for improper acquisition or circulation of business secrets.
in writing. ‒ in accordance with the annual budgetary procedure, the committee on budgets prepares a draft report containing estimates of parliament's expenditure for the following year. the report shall be based on the preliminary draft of expenditure prepared by the bureau on the basis of information supplied by the secretary-general. the estimates for 2017 show that the total budget of the parliament will be eur 1 910 073 000. this will be an increase of 3,9% compared to the 2016 budget, with the largest increase expected due to the new security measures. the priorities for 2017 identified by the secretary-general are security and cybersecurity, the gradual withdrawal of the derogation for the irish language, strengthening the mandate of meps and making parliament more attractive to the public and visitors. i voted yes.

in writing. ‒ in 1987, turkey applied to join the european economic community and in 1997 it was declared that it fulfilled the conditions for eu membership. accession negotiations were opened in 2005, but until turkey agrees to apply the additional protocol to the association agreement with ankara to cyprus, eight negotiating chapters will not be opened and no chapter will be provisionally closed. although turkey is a functioning market economy and is increasingly aligning its legislation with the eu acquis, the overall pace of reforms in the area of policy criteria has slowed considerably and there have been regressions in some areas such as the independence of the judiciary, the rule of law, freedom of speech and the media. the security situation in turkey is deteriorating rapidly due to the increasing violence between kurds and the turkish army and the numerous terrorist attacks attributed to the islamic state. the report highlighted the resumption of the negotiation process following the adoption of the joint action plan on migration, but stressed that eu-turkey cooperation on migration should not be dependent on the content, timing and conditionality of the accession negotiation process. in view of the many doubts that accompanied the report, i abstained.
in writing. ‒ in 2005, the european union opened accession negotiations with turkey, which marked the start of a long and open process based on fair and rigorous conditions and a commitment to reform. any country wishing to join the eu must meet the criteria set by the community, such as respect for the principles of democracy and the rule of law, freedom of speech and the media, the fight against corruption and organised crime, etc. unfortunately, in recent years, the pace of political reform in turkey has slowed considerably and there has been a clear decline in the areas of freedom of expression and freedom of assembly. in addition, turkey has experienced a decline in rankings on corruption, media freedom and business conduct. it is essential that the country returns to the path of democratic reforms, otherwise the pace of the accession process will remain at its current low level. turkey is a key strategic partner for the union and further convergence of partners will be beneficial for both sides. the report's demands are therefore entirely justified and should serve as a basis for further reforms in turkey.
in writing. ‒ turkey is a very important country in the european union's immediate neighbourhood, which already in the 1980s declared its aspirations to join the community. however, despite many years of talks and negotiations, the prospect of full eu membership for ankara is still far off. despite many successes, especially in the economic field, turkey still faces many political problems that prevent the accession process from being finalised. it is not only the long-standing conflicts and disputes, such as the partition of cyprus and the lack of normalisation with armenia, but also new problems, in particular the military action against the kurds in syria and iraq and the insufficient involvement in the fight against the islamic state. the active involvement of turkey in the fight against illegal immigration to europe is commendable, but only time will tell whether and to what extent this involvement is sincere and effective. i support turkey's european ambitions, but i would like to see greater involvement of the authorities in ankara in solving the most important challenges for european security. i fully agree with the call in this report for turkey to step up its efforts to protect religious and ethnic minorities, especially christians and yazidis. unfortunately, the report also contains a number of words which i cannot subscribe to, and i have therefore abstained.
in writing. ‒ the annual report on albania's progress towards eu accession shows continued progress on the key systemic reforms needed to launch accession negotiations. however, albania faces challenges such as irregularities in the functioning of the judicial system, the general politicization of the electoral process, widespread corruption, organised crime with a low number of final sentences, the lack of professional, independent and pluralistic public and private media, the increase of islamic radicalisation in society, etc. nevertheless, i welcome albania's progress on its path to eu integration, and i would like to thank the european union for its support. i voted yes.
in writing. ‒ i voted in favour of the adoption of the report on albania for 2015. i am pleased that albania is showing steady progress year on year in implementing reforms and making efforts to move closer to the european union. i commend the government's efforts to combat crime, the adoption of a plan for administrative reform and the consolidation of public finances. in this context, it is worth noting that the albanian government is beginning to engage in dialogue with various political forces and social partners. a strong civil society is an important pillar of democracy and only with its support can the necessary reforms be effectively implemented. of course, our albanian neighbour still faces many challenges. the commission rightly pointed out that tirana has a particularly long way to go in reforming the judiciary and fighting corruption. i believe that the european union should continue to support the important reforms and transformation processes taking place in albania. it is in our interest to have a stable, well-developed democracy in our immediate neighbourhood, which will be ready for membership of the community in the long term.

in writing. ‒ this report aims to make the link between social policy and energy policy, highlighting that the eu is moving away from the europe 2020 target of reducing poverty. the report calls for eu social engagement through a minimum income framework and further changes to social and labour rights and anti-discrimination legislation. the report invites the commission to estimate the means of ensuring an adequate minimum income above the poverty line of 60% of the national median income in all member states. another pillar of poverty reduction is the reduction of household costs through targeted eu funds. the report introduces the concept of a european moratorium on winter heating cuts, to ensure that no household can be without electricity for a fixed period in winter, and that those who are in such a situation are restored, stressing that the costs are the responsibility of the public authorities, as stated in the report. unfortunately, despite the seriousness of the problem, i could not support this report, which proposes to initiate debate in policy-making, public intervention and increased public spending, but does not present any sustainable and balanced solutions based on improved labour and education markets and better public services. i abstained from the vote.
in writing. ‒ i voted in favour of the report on the attainment of the poverty reduction target in the light of the rising costs borne by households. unfortunately, progress towards one of the europe 2020 targets, namely reducing the number of people at risk of poverty and social exclusion, is insufficient. the report on tackling poverty in the face of rising household costs raises a number of important issues that can bring us closer to solving this problem. i agree with the rapporteur that there are links between social and energy policy. increasing the energy efficiency of households, as well as the better use of modern and renewable energy sources, will help to reduce the level of energy poverty still experienced by many households in the union. because of the interdependencies, this subject requires a holistic approach. i therefore believe that it is particularly important in this area to create synergies between the various existing funds and to manage the funds allocated to these objectives effectively, both at the commission and member state level and at local level.
in writing. ‒ this own-initiative report aims to link social policy and energy policy, while highlighting the eu's move away from the europe 2020 target of reducing poverty. the rapporteur calls for social engagement on the eu side through a minimum income framework and further changes in social and labour rights and anti-discrimination legislation. the report concludes that a minimum income is an essential instrument to be introduced to ensure respect for the fundamental right to decent living conditions. another pillar of poverty reduction is the reduction of household costs through targeted eu funds. this report describes poverty and proposes to initiate debate in policy-making, public intervention and increased public spending, but fails to present any sustainable and balanced solutions based on improved labour and education markets and better public services. i hereby abstain from voting.
in writing. ‒ the various economic and trade consequences of the current crisis, which affects almost all sectors of the economy, are often highlighted, but social issues are less frequently addressed. crises and their accompanying phenomena and changes often lead to an increase in household expenditure on media (electricity, water) and other housing, health, education and training costs. these trends are particularly dangerous, because they lead to an increase in poverty and the risk of social exclusion. this situation particularly affects people at risk of social exclusion and vulnerable groups. particular attention should also be paid to countering the negative effects of the social crisis and of low household income in rural areas, which often result in depopulation. once a certain limit is reached, and once the population has completely left the area, it is very difficult to get people to settle there again. supporting positive economic and social trends in rural areas is a way of reducing unemployment by promoting self-employment in agriculture and other services. supporting young people considering farming is crucial for the long-term development of rural areas in europe. particular protection should be provided to the unemployed, to families with children, to persons with disabilities, to the sick and elderly, to minors and to those who, for various reasons, are at greater risk of social exclusion and poverty. the growing number of one-person households in europe also deserves attention and a suitable approach.
in writing. ‒ the report is a response to the commission communication 'a stronger role for the private sector in achieving sustainable and inclusive growth in developing countries' adopted on 13 may 2014. the document highlights the crucial role that the private sector can play in achieving the objectives of our development strategy, with the estimated annual needs in developing countries exceeding current spending by usd 2.4 billion. the private sector drives prosperity and growth in every market economy and creates 90% of jobs and income, as well as 84% of gdp in developing countries. the report focuses on potential public-private partnerships in areas ranging from infrastructure, energy and water to other sectors where public funds are proving insufficient, such as healthcare and education, on support for the local private sector in developing countries and on the extension of the european investment bank's mandate to provide loans to third countries and the pooling of eu financing instruments in general. in view of the above, i have voted in favour of the report.
in writing. ‒ a huge capital injection is needed to develop local economies and further reduce poverty. its current shortfall can only be filled by a greater involvement of the private sector. the european union should provide technical support for european public enterprises in the partner countries. i am glad that parliament's report has so clearly supported the promotion of public-private partnerships (ppps), because it is this type of activity that can lead to long-term development based on new and innovative technologies. if we want to provide decent jobs for millions of people living in poverty, we need to see this as a mutual opportunity, not a problem. the adopted document rightly emphasises the need to establish a multilateral dialogue platform at eu level where the private sector, ngos, think tanks, donors, governments and other stakeholders could more easily cooperate on development and build mutual trust more effectively. development aid is often not properly matched or is duplicated by many actors. there is no doubt that the private sector should play a greater and more important role in development cooperation and in efforts to reduce inequality and poverty. the sector is the foundation of any economy, and business and development objectives are not contradictory but complementary.

on behalf of the ecr group. mr president, i would like to thank you for your kind words. transport is the lifeblood of the european economy. any serious disturbance in the smooth functioning of this sector results in losses for undertakings, delays in deliveries and, as a consequence, falling revenues and rising costs, and risks of redundancies in many sectors. the past year and the escalating immigration crisis is an unprecedented problem that the trucking industry is practically dealing with on its own. in recent months i have received a lot of signals from transport company owners and truck drivers from the kujawsko-pomorskie region, who described the working conditions in the calais area. attacks on cars while driving, threats, thefts, attempts to break into trailers to cross the uk border illegally are a daily occurrence for truck drivers not only from my hometown of bydgoszcz, but from all over poland, which has been a key player in the road transport market in the european union for many years. i'm very happy to finally be able to talk about these issues here in this forum, where we so rarely deal with the real issues of the people who elected us, who we represent here. looking at the images from the access roads to the port of calais and seeing truck drivers throwing rocks, it is impossible to ignore the fact that these attacks are being carried out by illegal immigrants. who pays for these robberies? who's funding the extra security on the trailers or the surveillance inside the trucks? after all, who risks their health and life to work under such difficult conditions? the drivers themselves, of course, and their employers, whose daily losses run into thousands of euros. this particular example is just one of many visible manifestations of the impact of the immigration crisis on the transport sector in the european union. the temporary closure of rail links between member states, the thousands of attempts to penetrate the eurotunnel, the huge uncontrolled movement of small boats and pontoons in the mediterranean, and finally the gradual unilateral reintroduction by member states of border controls in the schengen area, this is the present of the european transport sector. do we want his immediate future to be like this? will concrete action be taken only when, in addition to the financial losses, the pictures of the victims of road accidents caused by the lack of proper control over the movement of waves of illegal immigrants in europe appear on the front pages of newspapers? i would like to call for more commitment from the european commission, especially to transport companies and companies, including the launching of real support to finance investments to improve the safety of transport workers and compensation for losses incurred due to the ongoing immigration crisis. we invest a lot of money in infrastructure in the european union. we must help its users in a situation where their safety and working conditions are threatened by the irresponsible and inconsistent european immigration policy. our task is to do everything we can to support the member states at the union's external borders and to regain a real influence on the number of people coming to europe. if our external borders are not sealed, no temporary solution will help and the schengen area will simply cease to exist. the economic costs of such a scenario, not just for my country, would be enormous. in other words, i would appeal to the commission to ensure that the law that is already in place today is consistently respected and enforced.
i'm closing the debate.

rapporteur.– madam president, the main problem of the discharge procedure, which has been ongoing for years, is the discharge procedure concerning the council and the european council. starting from the weakness observed during the budgetary control procedure, we have to indicate the high underspending rate that covers almost all categories, the very high number of appropriations being carried over from 2014-2015, particularly those for property, plant and equipment, as well as major transfers within budget lines. these problems could be avoided with better budgetary programming. for better budgetary programming, key performance indicators have to be developed. moreover, the council has still not adopted a code of conduct, which is indispensable to the transparency, accountability and integrity of the institution. there is also a worrying lack of transparency with regard to the legislative process, negotiations and member states’ positions at meetings within the council. the council definitely should disclose the relevant documents and put in place a clearer reporting system that will enable the public to follow the legislative procedures in an open and transparent manner. there is also the problem of the lack of transparency of the trilogues and conciliation meetings. the council definitely has to increase transparency and integrity with regard to their negotiations. taking into consideration political problems, as far as cooperation between parliament and the council is concerned, we have to indicate that the council ought to be transparent and fully accountable to union citizens for the funds entrusted to it by taking part fully and in good faith in the annual discharge procedure, just as other union institutions do. in this regard, effective supervision of the union’s budget implementation requires cooperation between parliament and the council through a working arrangement. but, as a matter of fact, there is no cooperation, no dialogue. the council does not participate in the budgetary control procedure and does not provide answers to written questions asked by our committee on budgetary control or by particular members of our committee. the council does not participate in the hearings or debates concerning budgetary control procedure regarding the council. we cannot forget that the procedure of granting discharge separately to the individual union institutions’ bodies is a long-standing practice which has been developed to guarantee transparency and democratic accountability towards union taxpayers.

the next item is the debate on:- oral question with debate to the council by mr pavlo svoboda, on behalf of the committee on legal affairs, and ms cecilia wikström, on behalf of the committee on petitions, on the protection of the child's best interests across borders in europe (000027/2016 b8-0359/2016) (2016/2665 ((rsp)). - having regard to the question with oral answer by mr pavlo svoboda, on behalf of the committee on legal affairs, and ms cecilia wikström, on behalf of the committee on petitions, on the protection of the child's best interests across borders in europe (000028/2016 b8-0360/2016) (2016/2665 ((rsp))
mr. chairman, please! each year, the committee receives many complaints about children. the scale of the problem requires the urgent provision of tools to address cross-border issues, and the problems identified cover a wide range of areas. one is the inadequate implementation of the brussels regulation 2, the other is the lack of coordination of the transmission of child protection information between member states in cross-border cases. there are also cases of non-recognition and non-enforcement of judgments in another member state. the system you build has to be multi-directional, it has to have access to different tools. i know from polish experience that many problems arise from, for example, difficult access to information and legal aid. a system of funding and support for organisations providing information and assistance on family matters should therefore be established. an important element of this system would be a single european intervention number. a simple and widely accessible guide to the systems in place in each member state and the rights it confers should be produced as soon as possible. after all, many conflicts stem from ignorance of the legal system. these and other actions must be taken urgently if politicians' declarations that the welfare of the child is paramount are not just a matter of slogans.
in writing. the increase in mobility within the eu has led to an increase in cross-border child protection cases, as evidenced, among other things, by the mass petitions to the european parliament. in the light of the upcoming review of the brussels ii regulation, the commission should draw attention to the clear problems with the implementation of that regulation and consider strengthening its provisions. in addition, it would be important to remove the current procedural and bureaucratic obstacles in childcare proceedings. the best interests of the child must be a primary consideration in all care decisions at all legislative levels. all child protection systems should have transnational and cross-border mechanisms that take into account the specific characteristics of such disputes. in this context, i welcome the council's call for member states to establish monitoring and evaluation systems within the national framework for the coordination of cross-border cases involving children. in addition, the obligation for national authorities, as laid down in the brussels iia regulation, to recognise and enforce judgments given in another member state and the strengthening and improvement of judicial cooperation in all matters concerning children are necessary.
in writing. demographic changes in recent decades and the associated evolution of the family model have resulted in many domestic and care work being carried out within the framework of an employment relationship. unfortunately, people employed in domestic and care work may be exposed to discrimination. first, they are often people in a grey area, without any labour rights, with unregulated status and working hours. this leaves them without job security and social security. secondly, there are also cases of gender discrimination, harassment and bullying. this makes it necessary to take specific measures to lift the sector out of the grey area and to strengthen the position of those employed in it. however, i believe that the situation in the member states is so different that it is the governments that should take responsibility for solving this problem. intervention by the union would be a very clear breach of the principle of subsidiarity in this case. member states, knowing their own specificities, are able to prepare much more effective programmes of action to reduce pathologies in the domestic and care work sector. the european commission should focus on collecting and disseminating good practice and innovative solutions from individual countries.
in writing. human trafficking and exploitation and forced labour are problems that need to be urgently addressed. the persons in this situation are mostly women who work in the care of the disabled or elderly or who are engaged in domestic work as part of their profession. it should be our duty to ensure that this group of people has the opportunity to be given official legal status. illegal human trafficking is a felony. the financial exploitation and intimidation of these people is reason enough to change. the european union is committed to values such as respect for human rights and dignity, and the resolution on this issue rightly refers to the laws of individual eu member states. the introduction of bilateral agreements between the host country and the country of which the worker is a national will certainly be a positive change. the creation of a single rule will help to limit the growth of illegal trafficking in human beings and unregistered labour.

in writing. the implementation of the e75 rail baltica international route project, which is part of the core network of european transport corridors, namely the north sea corridor, fits perfectly into the debate on railway interoperability. it is a key railway project in north-eastern europe, running through the podlaskie region, the baltic countries and helsinki. in practice, this will be the only rail link between the baltic countries and poland and the rest of the european union. it is of great importance not only economically but also politically and strategically. rail baltica is an opportunity for increased access to the labour market, easier trade and enhanced cross-border and interregional cooperation. for the union, it also means faster transport of energy resources, security and less dependence on russia. rail baltica is also a priority railway investment in my region, which will result in shorter and safer journeys, new comfortable platforms, more trains on the route and, above all, jobs and economic development in podlasie. i am all the more concerned about the difficulties and delays that are piling up around it, initially related to the route planning through kaunas or vilnius, and now with the speed parameters. delays in the implementation of this project represent a missed opportunity to strengthen economic and political cohesion along the west-east axis. i am counting on the full commitment of the member states and the commission to this project.

in writing. i am pleased that the european parliament is finalising the railway package. in this package, we focus on three issues: increasing rail interoperability in the eu, rail safety and the functioning of the eu railway agency. the compromise focuses mainly on the technical problems that have so far blocked the creation of a single railway area in the union. this required the harmonisation of railway standards and procedures in the member states. the aim is that the authorisations granted for the placing on the market in the union of rolling stock, such as locomotives and wagons, are universally applicable. as well as the safety certificates issued by the railway agency and individual countries. the adoption of such uniform solutions reduces red tape and costs for carriers, as they have had to obtain certificates in all countries. this should also contribute to the safety and development of the railway sector in the european union. the development of the railway sector in the union is one of the conditions for sustainable development, economic and tourist recovery in many regions and improvement of the environment.

in writing. ‒ the draft resolution proposes that member states designate specialised chambers within family courts or cross-border mediation bodies to deal with child cases and establish minimum standards for hearing a child in national civil proceedings, setting thresholds for the duration of each stage of cross-border child custody proceedings to give parents or family members time to resolve their problems. member states that have not yet signed the hague convention for the protection of children are encouraged to do so. unfortunately, the resolution also contains problematic aspects concerning the removal of competences from national parliaments and courts and their transfer to the commission, as well as injunctive measures promoting the principle of one measure for all. in view of the above, i abstained.
in writing. ‒ i voted in favour of the resolution, which is the result of hundreds of petitions from across the european union in various child disputes. it is children who suffer the consequences of the lack of cooperation between the member states of the union and the ineffective application of the principle of the best interests of the child in cross-border custody and adoption proceedings. the establishment of specialised bodies in national family courts should speed up the settlement of such disputes. these cases are particularly relevant where the parents have different nationalities. this is the arbitrary placement of a child in a foreign institution, the abduction of a child by one of the parents, or a dispute over custody of the child. it is necessary for member states to regulate the automatic recognition of national adoption orders and documents issued in another member state without any bureaucratic barriers. when deciding whether to adopt a child or place him in a care facility, he should be given the chance to maintain cultural ties and to learn his mother tongue. member states should make every effort to avoid separating siblings. particular attention should be paid to the cases of parents who, as victims of domestic violence themselves, are automatically deprived of parental rights when they use violence against their children. they deserve support, because taking away their custody rights could mean making them victims again.
in writing. ‒ every year, the committee on petitions of the european parliament receives a large number of complaints concerning the welfare of children. increased mobility of citizens within the european union has led to an increase in the number of cross-border child protection court cases involving deprivation of care. the scale of the problem requires the urgent provision of tools to facilitate the resolution of cross-border cases. the european parliament resolution rightly emphasised that one of the major problems in this area is the insufficient implementation of the brussels ii regulation and the lack of coordination between member states in the provision of information on the protection of children's rights in cross-border cases. in its document, the european parliament also drew attention to the fact that multi-directional actions are needed at eu and national level, such as support for access to information and legal aid. however, to make this possible, member states should increase their financial contribution to supporting family aid organisations and the eu should consider setting up a single helpline and a platform to provide assistance to eu citizens who are not nationals of the country of residence in family proceedings. action in the area of the best interests of the child should be taken as soon as possible so that declarations are not mere slogans. that is why i have decided to support the european parliament's resolution.
in writing. ‒ i voted in favour of the ep resolution on the protection of the best interests of the child in cross-border custody cases. it is not directly binding, but it is a guide for the european institutions and individual countries. the resolution is the ep's reasoned response to hundreds of petitions and complaints concerning the application of family law in the member states. we are seeing an increase in parental disputes over child custody, adoption, and parental abduction. the minimum response to these frequent human tragedies should be for all member states of the union to designate specialised chambers in family courts to deal competently and as quickly as possible with disputes concerning children. it is also a matter of universally recognising national adoption orders and documents issued in another member state. perhaps this would at least partially alleviate the tragedies of many children and families.
