in writing. ‒ the three previous eu 'railway packages' have led to major changes to increase the competitiveness and interoperability of european railways, while maintaining a high level of safety. however, the railway sector continues to face challenges such as barriers to competition, discrimination and the lack of a liberalised, dynamic and entrepreneurial environment. in addition, there are too many national rules, procedures and standards that lack transparency. part of the solution is to strengthen the competence of the european railway agency, which should offer efficient and user-friendly authorisation and certification procedures. the increased role of the agency is intended to contribute to greater interoperability of projects, inter alia, by means of an assessment of the technical solutions envisaged by the agency before each publication of a call for tenders for track-side equipment. the agency will also be a 'one-stop shop', acting as a single point of entry for all applications. however, for rail transport to operate efficiently at european level, it is necessary to cooperate more closely with national authorities, share expertise and information. a strong, well-equipped and efficient railway agency is a prerequisite for the development and functioning of the european railway market.
in writing. ‒ in january 2013, the commission proposed the 4th railway package, which aims to improve the quality and efficiency of rail services by removing remaining market barriers to create a single european railway area. the fourth railway package consists of the so-called technical pillar and the political pillar. the three proposals forming the political pillar are still being negotiated in parliament and the council, while the technical pillar (containing the interoperability directive in question, as well as the railway safety directive and the era regulation) was agreed at the end of june last year. the agreements have been confirmed by the council and now need to be confirmed by parliament. the purpose of the document is to establish a european vehicle register. the national vehicle registers maintained by each member state will be integrated into the european vehicle register and this register will gradually replace the need to maintain national lists. the european vehicle register will be fully operational within 5 years of the entry into force of the interoperability directive. i am opposed to the above proposals. i voted against it.
in writing. ‒ the eu rail market has undergone profound changes over the past decade. despite the significant evolution of the european union acquis on the rail transport services market, rail transport still accounts for a small share of intra-eu transport. the overall share of rail transport in the eu market currently stands at 6%, and according to eurobarometer, as many as 54% of users are dissatisfied with its services. the interoperability directive is part of the fourth railway package and focuses mainly on removing existing administrative and technical barriers, in particular by: introducing a common approach to safety and interoperability rules to increase the benefits of scale for railway undertakings across the eu, reducing administrative costs and speeding up harmonised procedures, and preventing hidden discrimination. for these reasons, i have decided to vote in favour of the report on the interoperability of the rail system in the eu. the new european union regulations should significantly enhance interoperability between the different national rail systems. the directive will make it easier and more effective to reduce and simplify existing regulations. by drastically cutting red tape and increasing standardisation for vehicle manufacturers and service managers, rail transport will become much easier to operate.
in writing. ‒ the regulation is a response to a number of high-profile index manipulation scandals, the most serious of which was the manipulation of libor rates. the disclosure of these irregularities over the past few years has cast a shadow over the way financial indicators are produced and used. the document aims to enhance investor protection by providing an eu-wide framework for administrators of indicators and indices used in financial products. it introduces a framework applicable to all indicators to reduce their vulnerability to manipulation and conflicts of interest by creating a regulatory framework around the administrators of the indicators. while it is possible to have reservations about the wide scope of the regulation, a degree of proportionality in the final result was achieved by distinguishing between many different types of indicators and applying different systems to different types and categories of indicators. i voted yes.
in writing. ‒ in recent years, financial indicators have been subject to numerous manipulations, which have prompted the european union to take appropriate preventive measures. i voted for the introduction of an appropriate regulatory framework applicable to all indicators. this will reduce the vulnerability of indicators to variations and conflicts of interest. the introduction of a distinction between types of indicators and the inclusion of different systems for the types and categories of indicators has allowed the achievement of a degree of proportionality and the ordering of such a wide range of indicators. it should also be mentioned that a system of recognition of third country indicators has also been established.
in writing. ‒ the provisions on the supervision of market indices such as libor and euribor are designed to prevent manipulation and ensure that the indices are set in a transparent manner. benchmarks are essential for the functioning of our financial markets. manipulating them is tantamount to robbing investors and consumers. the new rules could prove to be a step in the right direction and help rebuild confidence in eu financial markets, which has been significantly damaged by numerous scandals involving manipulation of interbank interest rates and commodity indices (e.g. oil, natural gas and biofuels) or exchange rates. it should be noted that market indicators affect the prices of financial instruments in the trillions of euros. they are also important for financial markets, mortgages and the savings of millions of union citizens. however, as yet, they are neither regulated nor supervised. the european parliament's document suggests that the establishment and application of indicators should be supervised by the relevant institutions in the eu countries where the indicator is produced. for critical indicators, i.e. benchmarks for financial instruments with a value of at least eur 500 billion, additional scrutiny is to be carried out by an international college of supervisors, whose work is coordinated by the european securities and markets authority.
in writing. ‒ i am in favour of a transparent process for monitoring financial indicators in the market. the cause of the continuing scandals resulting from the manipulation of financial instruments should be eliminated. the lack of confidence of investors in both the interbank euro interest rate and the london rate is causing huge losses for market participants. the global consequences are a weakening of the economy, and therefore a rise in mortgage interest rates, loans or currency fluctuations. i am in favour of the agreement between the european parliament's committee on economic and monetary affairs and the council on the creation of three categories of indicators to be monitored.
in writing. ‒ to fulfil its tasks, the eib grants loans and guarantees on a non-profit basis to facilitate the financing of projects in all sectors of the economy. in 2014, the eib financed, among others, 285 000 smes, securing 3.6 million jobs and contracts for 413 projects in the european union (in total) at a cost of eur 69 billion, as well as 92 new projects outside the eu for eur 7.98 billion. in the same year, the eif allocated eur 3.3 billion (from equity and guarantees) to smaller enterprises. this successfully delivered one of the eib's most ambitious business plans, totalling eur 80.3 billion in eib group financing. in 2012, the member states agreed to increase the eib's capital by eur 10 billion. the report's issues are first and foremost calls for a stronger european union. the author sees the eu as a 'convergence engine' and calls for 'strengthening european integration'. moreover, 'strengthening and developing the european investment bank's network within the eu' can have a significant budgetary impact and is not necessary. the rapporteur also calls for the further development of the efsi and calls on the eib to stop funding motorways. in view of the above, i abstained.

in writing. ‒ the 2014 discharge report to the european commission (ec) and the executive agencies focuses on compliance and results. in its annual report on the eu budget, the european court of auditors (eca) calls for a new approach to the management of eu investment and expenditure and for the budget to be better aligned with the eu's long-term strategic objectives. this new approach was consistently reflected in the rapporteur's report. the estimated level of error for payments for 2014 was 4,4%, which is close to the level of 2013 (4,5%), and consistently exceeds the materiality threshold of 2%. it is worth mentioning that the eto found the same estimated level of error of 4,6% for shared management with member states and for expenditure managed directly by the commission. the highest levels of error were found in expenditure under the headings 'economic, social and territorial cohesion' (5.7%) and 'competitiveness for growth and jobs' (5.6%). in a joint statement, the united kingdom and sweden regret that for the 21st consecutive year, the eto has not been able to issue a certificate of assurance without reservations with regard to the eu budget as a whole. with that in mind, i voted against the discharge.

in writing. ‒ the eu domestic and care workers sector is a major challenge for those who stand on the side of human dignity and workers' rights. people who do this type of work as a job have the lowest qualifications. it is usually a hard life situation that forces them to work this way, so they accept both low pay and unpleasant working conditions. it's mostly gray area work, and the workers are usually women. as guardians of the rule of law, we should ensure that this situation is regulated in such a way that the most vulnerable people in the labour market are not harmed. every man has the right to dignity, to a fair wage for his work. the more so the people who often cannot fight for their rights, should not suffer because of the gaps in the legislative system.
in writing. ‒ colleagues, women make up a significant proportion of those who do housework and care work, often in a gray area or for very low pay. in many member states, there is a lack of legislation regulating this market and of a definition of domestic and care work. this is essential, especially as the ageing of europe's population will increase the need for this. we must therefore regulate this segment of the workforce by adopting appropriate regulations at european level, which will help to counter the grey area and to gain recognition and respect for those who do this work. that is why i voted in favour of mrs kuneva's report on women in domestic and care work in the eu.
in writing. ‒ the issue of regulating the status of domestic and care workers is of paramount importance to the european economy. in recent decades, the old continent has witnessed significant demographic and socio-economic changes. the population is aging, while the birth rate is falling. family life patterns are also changing, with the result that the closest family has less and less opportunity to care for its most needy members. in addition, women are becoming more active in the labour market, which means that the tasks traditionally performed by them must be taken over by their carers. the employment of domestic and care workers should be a free choice of occupation, ensuring that workers in these sectors enjoy adequate conditions in terms of rights, social and health insurance, social benefits, and a dignified life and prospects for personal development. it is therefore difficult to accept a situation in which the growing demand for domestic and care work is met in a grey area due to the need to reduce public expenditure and the possibility of using inward labour from third countries. however, i believe that the proposals in the european parliament's report are too much an interference with the private life of citizens, with the relations between the state and the citizen and with the competences of the member states. i have therefore decided to abstain.

mr president, nothing in this discussion is anti-china. we need to have a good relationship with them, but we need to decide the rules by which this relationship in trade and economic issues is played. china today has a massive overcapacity in many things we produce, from steel to chemicals. it is an economy that functions on the idea of flooding our markets with their subsidised production. whether we like it or not, free trade is on the defence. people are waking up to the fact that ideological free trade has a massive cost on society and on workers. granting china market economy status is yet another step in this direction. we cannot subject our companies to the oncoming onslaught of chinese export without any means of defence, and we will not. we believe that there is sufficient room in the remaining provisions of article 15 of china’s wto protocol to warrant a china-specific methodology, and we ask the commission to include this in its proposal.
in writing. under the rules of the world trade organisation, countries that join the organisation may be considered 'free market economies' for 15 years after accession. products from countries not having such status may be subject to higher than normal duties in order to protect the internal market from dumping and unfair competition. for china, the transitional period expires on 11 december 2016. however, 15 years after its accession to the wto, china has still not implemented the reforms necessary to be considered a free market economy. five eu criteria, such as respect for property rights and an economy free from state influence, were not met. in this respect, the european parliament's position on the non-acceptance of the automatic granting of market economy status seems to be most appropriate. this is particularly important, because otherwise the interests of european companies and hundreds of thousands of jobs could be seriously jeopardised. the commission therefore concluded that the chinese exporting producers were not able to compete with the union producers. before taking a final decision, the eu should first assess the impact of this decision on jobs and industry, and then adopt appropriate regulations to ensure a balanced start and protect the most vulnerable sectors, such as the chemical, metallurgical and related industries. otherwise, we risk an uncontrolled flood of chinese products into our market.
in writing. ‒ the commission was required to present to parliament and the council several feasibility studies on the extension of the obligation to indicate the origin of certain categories of food. they do not contain any legal proposal, as such a proposal would, according to the commission, have to increase the cost to the industry and consumers are not willing to bear the additional costs. i support the principle of mandatory country of origin labelling of food where it is practical and consistent with consumer needs. i therefore do not share the commission's conclusion. the commission's analysis is useful, but the conclusion does not address the important aspects, i.e. the benefits of better consumer information. mandatory labels already exist for many products, including meat, eggs, fruit, vegetables, fish, honey, oils, wines and alcoholic beverages. the call to the commission to come forward with a proposal for a mandatory labelling which would be limited to milk and lightly processed dairy products such as cheese and cream, as well as lightly processed meats (i.e. bacon and sausages) should be accepted if there is evidence of consumer interest in such information. i therefore voted in favour.
in writing. ‒ the regulation aims to transpose into eu law the rules on subsidies and countervailing measures (subsidies agreement) of the world trade organisation (wto). the regulation lays down the detailed conditions determining the existence of a subsidy, the rules governing the application of countervailing duties which may be imposed in order to offset any subsidy granted, directly or indirectly, for the manufacture, production, export or import of any product whose release for free circulation in the eu causes injury, and the criteria to be used in calculating the amount of countervailable subsidy. the purpose of the regulation is to transpose into eu law the anti-dumping provisions contained in the agreement on the application of article vi of the general agreement on tariffs and trade 1994. in view of the unifying nature of the legislation, i voted yes.
in writing. ‒ the agreement is the first sustainable fisheries partnership agreement between the european union and liberia, which has a 570 km coastline along the atlantic ocean. the 246 152 km2 exclusive economic zone is home to many bottom-dwelling and pelagic fish stocks. the commission carried out an ex-ante assessment in 2013 of a possible sustainable fisheries partnership agreement with liberia. the procedural document concluded that the union tuna fisheries sector has a strong interest in the fisheries in liberia and that the sustainable fisheries partnership agreement would help improve monitoring, control and surveillance and contribute to improving fisheries management in the region. in view of the above arguments, i have expressed my support for the conclusion of this agreement.
in writing. ‒ the european union and the islamic republic of mauritania initiated in 2015 a new four-year protocol which allows eu vessels to fish in mauritanian waters for around 300 000 tonnes of shrimp, demersal, tuna and small pelagic fish per year. in line with the union's fisheries policy, the protocol will contribute to responsible fishing and sustainable management of fisheries resources, including greater transparency. the aim is to minimise the impact of fishing on marine ecosystems and to preserve mauritania's traditional coastal fishing. considering all these aspects, i voted yes.
in writing. ‒ the purpose of the negotiated agreement is to stimulate, facilitate and enhance cooperation between the parties in the field of civil global navigation by satellite within the framework of the european and korean involvement in the gnss system. it is an initiative which i personally support, which is why i voted in favour.
in writing. ‒ in a world where accurate location and time information is of the utmost importance, action is needed on a global satellite navigation system. as early as the 1990s, the european union began work on the largest industrial project in the integrated european structures - the galileo programme, which aims to ensure satellite independence from the us for the eu countries. the eu's galileo project has also attracted interest from outside the community due to its innovative nature. in 2006, south korea and the european union concluded talks on korea's participation in the programme. the agreement provides for cooperation in scientific research, training, market development and trade. it also involves industrial cooperation and cooperation in the development of legislation, standardisation, certification and the development of regional aid schemes. the conclusion of the agreement with korea reaffirms the european union's commitment to the development of international cooperation. the growing interest of third countries in galileo is stimulating a market for gnss-based services with an estimated potential of 3 billion receivers and global revenues of eur 275 billion per year by 2020. the european parliament's agreement to the agreement with korea is a symbolic confirmation of the need to intensify international cooperation in the field of satellite navigation under the leadership of the european union.
in writing. ‒ the entry into force of the cooperation agreement on a civil global satellite navigation system between the eu and the republic of korea is further evidence of the high level of interest, but also of the need for the full implementation of the eu's galileo satellite navigation programme. this is a very important initiative that deserves our support. at present, 12 of the 30 planned galileo satellites are in orbit. by the end of this year, six more satellites are planned to be placed in orbit. the acceleration of the work on this system is due to the urgent need to build an autonomous, alternative to gps, but at the same time compatible with it, global positioning system. galileo will be even more accurate than its competitors and thus have a huge commercial potential, as most of its services will be open to a wide range of users. international cooperation in implementing, but also exploiting, galileo's potential is key to its success. we want our eu partners to be aware of our capabilities and to have access to the technologies we are developing. the agreement with the republic of south korea is proof that galileo is and will be an added value and that our partners want to benefit from the skills we offer.

in writing. ‒ under the european structural and investment funds (esif), integrated territorial investment (iti) and community-led local development (clld), initiatives are a significant step forward in developing the capacity of local actors to link funding streams and well-targeted local initiative plans. the commission's focus on results and outcomes should also help local policy to move away from over-absorbing funds towards actually identifying concrete objectives that will bring about concrete changes for local businesses and residents. member states were required to indicate in their partnership agreements how the iti and clld would be applied by member states and to indicate the types of areas and challenges covered by these mechanisms. the bottom-up approach is of great importance, as is the involvement of local actors in the use of the new instruments, which will contribute to better coordination and a more targeted use of the esi funds. targeted action is necessary to bring these tools closer to local actors and to build their capacity to participate effectively in strategies targeting their territory. it is also important to use the multi-fund opportunities created by the new rules, which should be used in such a way as to achieve a truly integrated/holistic approach to cohesion policy interventions. i hereby endorse the report.
in writing. ‒ this document focuses on the development needs and potential of mountain regions in the european union to become a source of jobs and sustainable growth. it calls for the definition of mountain regions from a regional policy perspective. the document proposes an 'agenda for the eu's mountain regions' which would provide an additional framework within cohesion policy focusing on these regions and calls for coordination of eu policies that have an impact on these areas. i supported the tabling of a number of amendments concerning the carpathian region. however, the amendment calling for a separate strategy for the carpathian region and rejecting the idea of including this region in the danube macro-regional strategy was rejected. i abstained because of the rejection of the amendments i supported.
in writing. ‒ cohesion policy rarely focuses on the eu's mountain regions, which often leave them on the margins. the difficulties in investing in these areas are mainly due to the lack of adequate infrastructure and therefore to the additional costs of distance from larger conglomerates. i welcome the outcome of today's vote, which reflects the need to define precisely the mountain regions, to make a concrete policy proposal for these areas in future eu policies and programmes, especially in the framework of the european structural and investment funds. mountain areas are attractive for tourism, but they are also often rich in natural resources, the exploitation of which can improve employment by creating new jobs, especially 'green' ones, which support sustainable development. the wide variety of renewable energy sources can contribute to the achievement of the union's energy policy objectives. the development of many of these assets, in combination with eu funds, will lead to greater social, economic and territorial cohesion in mountain areas. only a coordinated, holistic approach to these regions can be essential to ensure that union funding is properly targeted towards achieving sustainable and inclusive growth.
in writing. ‒ i agree with the rapporteur that eu policy should take a special approach to mountain regions. similarly, the potential and importance of macro-regional strategies for the sustainable development of eu mountain regions with a strong cross-border cooperation dimension. however, it is difficult to agree that the carpathians constitute a danube subregion. in the face of the large economic and social disparities, it is virtually impossible to reconcile the interests of the carpathian region with those of the danube region. of course, cooperation must continue in areas such as flood control and nature protection, but in many other areas it is much more difficult to do so. the carpathian region is an extremely important geopolitical area today, where the strategic political interests of the eu as a whole intersect. the carpathians as a region meet the criteria of the macro-regional strategies described by the european commission. therefore, it is far premature to say at this stage that the european parliament welcomes the current initiatives for the carpathian region under the eu strategy for the danube region. i hereby abstain from voting.
in writing. ‒ a proper and thoughtful integration of the cap and cohesion policy can bring great benefits to rural and mountain regions in the eu, contribute to food security, achieve a real leveling of living conditions, counteract negative demographic phenomena and bring numerous benefits. cohesion policy itself can, however, address many of the adverse social and demographic trends by better targeting measures and actions. mountain areas in the eu are home to around 17% of eu citizens, making them an area of great economic and social importance. mountain regions require a special approach due to the difficult management conditions for agriculture, the higher costs of building and maintaining transport infrastructure, and the greater dependence on weather and climate change. at the same time, they are also a treasure trove of culture, tradition and numerous food products known throughout the world, which are an important part of european identity. these areas also face demographic challenges, caused by the outflow of young people to cities, underinvestment and difficulties in accessing broadband internet and modern services. at the same time, these areas have specific potential for renewable energy sources such as wind, hydro and biomass. in this context, it should be borne in mind that the necessary modernisation measures should not unduly affect the local way of life, which is an invaluable asset.

in writing. ensuring a high level of harmonised data protection in the european union, including police and judicial action, is crucial for respecting and protecting the fundamental rights of eu citizens. close and effective cooperation between the supervisory authorities at national and union level is necessary, based on security and the area of freedom and justice. over the years, europol's operational powers have gradually expanded. recently, units have been created to increase the agency's powers to analyze and combat terrorism. they include the european cybercrime centre and the eu suspicious content unit, which is tasked with combating terrorist propaganda and other extremist activities online. the most recent entity is the european counter-terrorism centre, which was established on 1 january 2016. the new europol regulation (2013/0091 ((cod)), which enters into force in all eu member states on 1 may 2017, establishes legal tools that are intended to contribute to strengthening the security of eu citizens and to the effective fight against terrorism. the commission should also be able to provide information on the implementation of the union's policy on the protection of personal data. close european cooperation and coordination between the different bodies is paramount.

in writing. ‒ the capital requirements regulation (or crr) currently exempts commodity traders from large exposure and own funds requirements. both exemptions shall expire on 31 december 2017. that date was originally included in the crr to give the commission time to review the prudential supervision system applicable to commodity traders and investment firms by the end of 2015 and, where appropriate, to propose a legislative system adapted to the risk profile of commodity traders and investment firms. the review in question is still ongoing. the results of this review will be the basis for establishing the appropriate precautionary approach to traders in goods. therefore, the purpose of this proposal is to extend the current treatment of traders in commodities until the review of investment firms is completed and any changes to the existing prudential framework are introduced, or until 31 december 2020, whichever is earlier. the commission will also consider whether the measures to be taken to address the risk of a loss of capital in the banking sector are appropriate to address the specific risks of the banking sector. i hereby endorse the report.
in writing. ‒ exemptions for commodity traders from the large exposure and own funds requirements expire on 31 december 2017. however, the review of investment firms is a complex undertaking which will not be completed by the end of this year. it is therefore very unlikely that any legislation that could be adopted as a result of this review will be prepared, adopted and applied before the expiry of the current exemptions. it is therefore necessary to extend the existing exemptions laid down in the capital requirements regulation. that extension should take into account the time needed to complete the review of investment firms and to prepare, adopt and apply any rules that may result from that review. in the absence of such a requirement, from 2018 onwards traders in goods would be subject to the obligations of the capital requirements regulation and the capital requirements directive, which would be disadvantageous for such companies. the fact that parliament has agreed to accept the commission's proposal for exemptions for traders of goods at first reading is the right decision and i have therefore decided to vote in favour of the report.

rapporteur. – mr president, the proposal for a council directive amending directive 2011/16/eu is part of the package of four new laws prepared recently by the european commission. the purpose of this legislative offensive is to radically reduce the scope for aggressive tax planning, tax evasion and tax avoidance and create a level playing field for all businesses in the eu. i congratulate the commission for this initiative. the purpose of the present proposal is to further strengthen and improve administrative cooperation between tax authorities in member states and to increase transparency of tax policies across the eu. the directive proposal provides for the mandatory automatic exchange between national tax authorities of information regarding country—by—country reports filed in each member state by multinational enterprises involved in cross-border business activities. the obligation of filing country—by—country reports extends to all multinationals with a combined turnover of more than eur 750 million. the directive proposal is in line with accepted international standards and specifically with the oecd report on the action plan on base erosion and profit shifting – the so-called beps report. the oecd package was also endorsed by the g20 leaders. it is therefore essential for the good functioning of the internal market that member states transpose political commitments until beps enters their national legal systems. we broadly support the commission proposal. we think it is timely, proportionate and goes in the right direction. we propose however two amendments. first, we want to involve the commission to become part of the automatic mandatory exchange of information between member states and this is for two reasons. firstly, we want the commission to be able to control the process of exchange of information in order to ensure the compliance of multinational companies and of member states with the directive. secondly, there is a state aid dimension to tax exemptions granted by member states and the commission should have access to this information to make sure that no illegal state aid is involved. the second amendment we propose is to request the commission to report systematically on the results achieved under this directive and to present publicly the aggregate summary of country—by—country reports. there were also two other changes proposed by some meps. the first proposal was to lower the threshold required for filing country—by—country reports from eur 750 million down to eur 40 million. the other proposal was to make all country—by—country reports public. both these proposals were rejected in the vote in the econ committee because they would introduce double standards – one more demanding for eu companies and the other less demanding for non-eu companies. if accepted, these two proposals would clearly put eu companies at a competitive disadvantage vis—à—vis non-european companies. mr president, dear members of parliament, i would like to thank the shadow rapporteurs for their cooperation in preparing our report and the parliamentary services for technical support. i call on this house to vote in favour of our report. citizens in our countries are waiting for a strong signal from this parliament that we are in favour of more transparency, fairness and efficiency in tax policies in the european union.
mr. chairman, please! in recent years, the challenges of tax fraud have increased significantly. the automatic exchange of information is intended to be an important tool in the fight against this phenomenon. however, it is very important that smes are not affected by these solutions. remember that they account for almost 70% of jobs in the european union. the functioning of multinational groups can lead to distortions of competition in national markets, which is why the solutions proposed by the european commission are so important. it is crucial that tax rules do not impede economic growth. the draft proposes to introduce specific arrangements for the automatic exchange of tax information, to increase the involvement of the european commission, the exchange of information process and to ensure greater transparency. however, this should not affect the principle of confidentiality.
mr. chairman, please! the obligation to report on financial and tax matters by country of operation of large companies can contribute to a partial levelling of the playing field for smes, and as we have heard many times here, smes have on average a 30% higher tax burden than corporations. the amendment of the current directive is therefore also important in this respect. however, such a system will not be fully effective unless this information is made public and this seems to me to be much more important than the dangerous extension of the european commission's powers and as long as we continue to tolerate tax havens like luxembourg in the european union. i also believe that the revenue threshold of eur 75 million per year for companies subject to reporting obligations will leave a significant number of companies de facto outside the scope of the proposed control system.
madam president! the european commission estimates that corporate tax relief across the european union amounts to some eur 120 billion per year. this means that in many countries the cost of these cuts is simply greater than the revenue from this tax. this is the case in my country, poland, where the revenue from corporate income tax is about pln 30 billion, and the cost of these cuts, according to the european commission's calculations, is as much as pln 46 billion. so we welcome this initiative of the european commission on automatic exchange of information, but it seems that the adoption of this solution should only concern companies with a turnover of more than 750 million euros. this amount should be absolutely reduced so that the rules that the commission proposes will cover a wider range of companies than before.

rapporteur. – madam president, i address my thanks to all the speakers for this interesting debate. i am very happy to see this overwhelming unity in which we all share concern about the growing scale of tax evasion and tax avoidance across the globe. this is a very worrying phenomenon as it undermines national budgets, as it puts small and medium-sized enterprises in a disadvantaged position and of course undermines the fairness of the taxation systems in all our countries. i would like therefore to express my satisfaction that we all agree that this issue has to be tackled and that we all agree that taxes should be paid where the value is created. on several contentious points let me make a quick comment. on the threshold, i think commission muscovici has explained what is the rationale behind adopting this relatively high threshold. if we went for a lower threshold that would certainly cost us much more, with marginal revenues from that move diminishing, so that i think we have to be ambitious, but not perhaps ambitious to the point as to undermine the efficiency and effectiveness of the tax system. if we manage to collect more than 90% of taxes within this system with a threshold of 750, i think we should start with this; example, the eu has no competence to adopt legislative measures setting requirements on minimum income at eu level. as minimum income schemes aim to combat poverty and social exclusion, they fall within the remit of article 153 of the treaty on the functioning of the european union: the legal basis for the adoption of measures in the field is therefore article 153.2 and it lies in the hands of the member states. nevertheless, the commission has been providing policy guidance to the member states to help them to develop adequate levels of minimum income, notably through the 2008 commission communication on active inclusion, the 2013 social investment package and various country specific recommendations within the european semester. the commission has also been funding the establishment of the european minimum income network and is elaborating a methodology to develop across nationally comparable reference budgets in member states. this will serve as means of helping both member states, to design efficient and adequate income support, and the commission, to monitor the adequacy of income support at union level. of course we must strive for upward convergence in employment and and the protection of all throughout their life cycle. we have already put fairness at the core of our agenda. the commission work programme 2016 made it clear that tackling inequalities in the union in writing. the employment rate for women in the eu is currently only 63.5%. consequently, further action is needed to support women's employment and retention in the labour market. despite efforts to date, the gender imbalance in the use of parental leave remains significant. eurostat data show that the number of people taking parental leave in 2010 was 3 518 600, of which only 2.7% were men. the aim of this report was to assess the parental leave provisions in the various member states. the analysis did not reveal any weaknesses in the implementation of parental leave in the eu countries, but it did note some discrepancies in the conditions for parental leave, especially in terms of combining it with the other two types of leave - maternity and paternity. the use of parental leave by fathers was also found to be very low, mainly due to the fact that it is low paid and transferable in most member states. in this context, a further detailed review of legislation and analysis of european legal acts on all types of parental leave should be carried out with a view to streamlining them in terms of duration, remuneration and scope.

madam president! i voted in favour of the report on the mandatory automatic exchange of information in tax matters because it introduces a very important instrument to counter the unfair practices of multinational corporations which, through aggressive tax planning, seek to minimise the taxes paid. the main cost of such activity is not only lower revenues to the member states' budgets but also the weakening of the competitiveness of small and medium-sized enterprises. mandatory exchange of information on reports between countries will increase the transparency of the operation of multinational companies and thus help eliminate tax fraud. i agree with the rapporteur that the european commission has very modestly outlined its role in the proposed amendment. certain amendments to the legislative proposal under discussion are therefore necessary, in particular those concerning the involvement of the commission in the exchange of information process so that it has access to the tax reports transmitted. this would allow it not only to safeguard the interest of the union as a whole but also to prepare annual reports to the parliament and the council presenting the main conclusions of the activities observed.
in writing. ‒ the draft proposes to amend the administrative cooperation directive by introducing specific requirements for the automatic exchange of information on country reports. these amendments concern, inter alia, the scope of information to be provided by multinational enterprises in respect of each tax jurisdiction, the threshold from which reporting obligations arise, the rules for the automatic exchange of information between national tax authorities, and other practical issues. such consultations shall not require the provision of information to the public. the project aims to involve the european commission more in the process of exchanging information on country reports, but it was noted that the european commission must respect confidentiality rules in this respect. i agree with the provisions and amendments to the previous directive and therefore voted in favour of the proposal.
in writing. ‒ today's vote reflects the need to increase transparency in tax information to combat cross-border tax avoidance, aggressive tax planning and harmful tax competition. the automatic exchange of information is an important tool in this regard as a future european and international standard for transparency and exchange of information in tax matters. the proposal also sets out the threshold for reporting by country by multinational enterprises, the scope of information exchanged, the timetable for implementation and the frequency of reporting. once the new rules come into force, multinational groups of companies established or operating in the eu with revenues of at least eur 750 000 000 will be required to submit such reports. the european commission should participate in the automatic exchange of information in the field of taxation and, like the national tax authorities, should have access to the reports, subject to the principles of confidentiality.
in writing. ‒ the draft proposes to amend the administrative cooperation directive by introducing specific requirements for the automatic exchange of information on country reports. these changes concern, inter alia, the scope of information to be provided by multinational enterprises in respect of each tax jurisdiction (profit before tax, tax due and paid, number of employees, etc.), the threshold at which reporting is required (consolidated group revenues totalling at least 750 000 000), the rules for the automatic exchange of information between national tax authorities upon receipt of a multinational enterprise's country-by-country report, and other practical issues. such consultations shall not require the provision of information to the public. the proposed amendments aim to involve the european commission more in the process of exchanging information on country reports, but it was noted that the european commission must respect confidentiality rules in doing so. the compromise reached is balanced against previous versions of the administrative cooperation directive. i hereby endorse the report.
in writing. ‒ in recent years, there have been a number of cases of incorrect labelling of fish and fishery products sold in supermarkets, cafeterias and restaurants across the union. when we are dealing with mislabelling, high-quality species are deliberately replaced by lower-quality species, misnamed and sold to the consumer at the price he would pay for high-quality species. it is unfair to fishermen and consumers. member states were therefore invited to step up national controls to detect and prevent mislabelling. it was also found that the incorrect labelling constitutes an infringement of the rules of the common fisheries policy. this was a call for a robust and robust traceability system from the landing stage to consumption. on the labelling front, the draft resolution supports the idea of the commission exploring the possibility of introducing an eco-label scheme for fishery and aquaculture products within the framework of the common organisation of the markets, and states that a sound eu labelling policy in the fisheries sector is a key factor in stimulating the economic development of coastal communities. i agree with the above and fully support it, which is why i voted in favour of the draft resolution.
in writing. ‒ on 11 december 2016, section 15 (a) (ii) of the protocol on the accession of china to the wto will expire. the exact legal effect of this phenomenon remains unclear and is the subject of considerable debate among industry experts. both the commission and the legal services parliament envisage changes in the functioning of european anti-dumping law, in particular in the methodology used to determine the so-called normal value, which is ancillary to anti-dumping investigations. i believe that instead of identifying the legal changes that may result from the expiry of chapter 15 (a) (ii), it is worth supporting the four basic principles that should accompany any commission decision on this matter. 1. the need to ensure that the eu's obligations under its wto commitments are fully consistent with eu law; 2. the need to take into account not only the consequences of the expiry of the abovementioned chapter but also those provisions that will remain after 11 december 2016; 3. the need to ensure that the eu remains a decisive player in solving problems and taking important decisions; 4. any legislative proposal should be based on a thorough assessment and recognition not only of the legal aspects of any decision but also of the medium and long-term economic, social, industrial and strategic implications. in view of the above, i voted yes.
in writing. - i voted for the resolution. the current recognition of china as a market economy would be associated with a sharp decline in the competitiveness of european industry. china is not yet a fully market economy, as the state subsidises some of its private companies, applying rules that are difficult to reconcile with free market rules and deliberately undercutting export prices. the high level of chinese production capacity thus obtained results in cheap exports of industrial products to the eu countries. the commission therefore concludes that the measures in force are in line with the principles set out in the basic regulation. europe will need time to adjust its economy to the strong competition from china. i believe that china will continue to be a great partner for the eu and i am in favour of the introduction of a draft new but fair anti-dumping regulation as soon as possible. the union should make clear to its chinese partner that the recognition of its economy as a market economy is a process and not a one-off and simultaneous act.
in writing. ‒ in september 2015, the un general assembly adopted the new 2030 agenda for sustainable development and the sustainable development goals contained therein. the objectives and tasks shall be geared to economic growth, social development and environmental protection. the agenda, objectives and tasks are universal, covering both developing and developed countries and all people. the focus is on issues such as improving people's quality of life, social protection and the environment in which they live. the joint draft resolution focuses on the issue of the eu's common position on the high level political forum on sustainable development (hlpf). i voted to pass the resolution.
in writing. ‒ the european union, together with its member states, is the largest donor of development aid and it was the eu that led the process leading to the adoption of the 2030 agenda. this is a great success, largely the result of coherent and coordinated action by all the actors involved. the adoption of the 2030 agenda is also a promise by world leaders to end extreme poverty, achieve sustainable development and ensure dignity and justice for all. before the high-level political forum on sustainable development, the eu external affairs council should develop a common and coherent eu position on the follow-up and review of the 2030 agenda for sustainable development. the parliament's report rightly expressed concern at the european commission's failure to publish a communication on the follow-up and review of the 2030 agenda before the forum. what is needed now is to turn words into action and implement the 2030 agenda. as a world leader in development, the union has the primary responsibility for promoting the implementation of the 17 sdgs, both internally and externally. therefore, it is necessary for the eu's credibility in the international community that the common position of the eu and its member states be presented as soon as possible.
in writing. ‒ i voted in favour of the resolution on the 2030 agenda because i believe that only through the use of regular review mechanisms can we achieve the sustainable development goals. i hope that the commission will present a strategy in this area soon, covering all the relevant internal and external aspects. it should include a transparent framework for monitoring and evaluating progress towards those objectives. the 2030 agenda, agreed last autumn, is an ambitious project to eradicate poverty altogether by integrating economic, social and environmental sustainability. the eu has repeatedly stressed the integrated nature of these three aspects during the negotiations and has committed itself to implementing them both within the community and in external relations. the traditional model of development cooperation is becoming increasingly irrelevant and should be limited to countries affected by conflict and crises. the need for more flexible and innovative instruments, based on measurable and verifiable development outcomes, is increasing. the new objectives are based on a partnership model between developed and developing countries, taking into account their different capabilities and needs. this is why cooperation at all levels is so important - from governments through the private sector to regional and citizens' initiatives.
in writing. ‒ the commission was required to present to parliament and the council several feasibility studies on the extension of the obligation to indicate the origin of certain categories of food: these reports were published in june 2015 (com ((2015) 0204) and com ((2015) 0205). they do not contain any legislative proposal, as the commission considers that this would have to increase the cost to industry and consumers are not willing to bear the additional costs. i personally support the principle of mandatory country of origin labelling of food where it is practical and consistent with consumer needs. the commission's analysis is useful, but the conclusion does not address the important aspects, i.e. the benefits of better consumer information. i am convinced that in the case of feasibility studies for milk and milk products, the cost estimate for the industry is exaggerated, as all these products are in one category. if the scope were limited to lightly processed products, the costs would be much lower. many manufacturers and retailers in the eu already provide such information on their own initiative, reflecting the actual needs of consumers and low costs. mandatory indication of the country of origin of lightly processed products would be an important step towards restoring consumer confidence following the horse meat scandal and would allow consumers to make more informed choices. in spite of the above, i consider this draft to be favourable and have therefore voted in favour of it.
in writing. ‒ the principle of mandatory country of origin labelling of food, if practical and consistent with consumer needs, is to be welcomed. the commission's analysis is useful, but the conclusion does not address the important aspects, i.e. the benefits of better consumer information. the feasibility studies for milk and milk products overestimate the costs for the industry, as they assess all these products in one category. if the scope were limited to lightly processed products, the costs would be much lower. many manufacturers and traders in the eu already provide such information on their own initiative, reflecting the existing need among consumers and low costs. the mandatory labelling already exists for many products, such as meat, eggs, fruit, vegetables, fish and many others. the commission should propose a mandatory indication limited to milk and lightly processed dairy products such as cheese and cream, as well as lightly processed meat, if there is evidence of consumer interest in such information. however, any proposal must minimise costs for producers and consumers. the commission would welcome an additional assessment of how to implement such a proposal in a cost-effective and proportionate manner. mandatory indication of the country of origin of these lightly processed products would be an important step forward in restoring consumer confidence and allowing them to make more informed choices. i hereby endorse the report.
in writing. ‒ the s&d implementation report aims to assess the implementation of eu parental leave legislation by member states. the author has tried to present the current situation in all member states. it is clear that the s&d group has used this report to set out its ambitious policy priorities for legislation on maternity and paternity leave at eu level. many amendments were introduced to make the text more factual. these amendments covered issues such as subsidiarity, competences, better regulation and the eu's role as an intermediary in exchanges between member states. references were made to overly rigorous implementation, to the fact that social benefits are a competence of the member states, and to the call on the commission to take account of non-legislative initiatives and the importance of the principles of subsidiarity and proportionality. unfortunately, the final text contains two obvious lines that are insurmountable for the ecr group and for me, including the call for an eu directive on minimum paternity leave and an ambitious eu proposal on maternity leave. with that in mind, i voted against.

in writing. there are many loopholes in eu rules that hinder the proper functioning of the digital single market, which could generate profits of up to eur 415 billion per year and 0.4% gdp growth by 2020. intellectual property infringement is a big problem. in 2013 alone, customs authorities recorded as many as 87 000 cases of such abuses, and the estimated value of 36 million articles detained is over eur 768 million. in this context, the european commission has presented a three-pillar e-commerce development plan to prevent the above mentioned problems and to achieve the goals of the digital agenda. its elements are: preventing unjustified geo-blocking; reducing the cost and efficiency of delivering foreign parcels; and improving protection and enforcement. in terms of geo-blocking, the new package takes into account both the consumer's right to shop freely online in different countries and the legal certainty needed by businesses. the proposal also reflects the commission's new approach to online platforms. after a thorough assessment of the social and economic role of these new entities, the commission concluded that a one-size-fits-all approach was not appropriate to meet the diverse challenges of the multitude of types of online platforms.

ladies and gentlemen! the question is familiar to everyone, so i'm going to focus on commenting on the question, on the rationale for it. it is safe to say that the situation on the milk market is a crisis. the milk market has always been sensitive, as there have been serious disturbances even during the quotation period, as was demonstrated in 2008/09. after the milk quota was abolished, the situation became complicated. even before the quota expired, milk producers had decided to increase production in order to have a stronger position on the liberalised market. the commission established the profitability of the sampled union producers by expressing the pre-tax net profit of the sales of the like product to unrelated customers in the union as a percentage of the turnover of those sales. it is understandable that each producer wants to increase its income, hence the above-mentioned favourable conditions have led to an increase in production. most farmers also have to finance the repayment of loans. the milk market is a global market, and therefore it is affected by production, supply and demand in different regions and countries of the world. in 2015, production also increased in the usa, australia. the commission established the profitability of the sampled union producers by expressing the pre-tax net profit of the sales of the like product to unrelated customers in the union as a percentage of the turnover of those sales. imports of milk and milk products from china also decreased. at the same time, there was no increase in consumption, which was probably due to the media coverage of the harmful effects of lactose on human health. the excess supply over demand has led to a very significant drop in milk prices, which are below production costs. the situation on the european market is therefore worrying, with just over half of the 420 million allocated to intervention on agricultural markets last autumn having been used up. in this respect, commissioner hogan has left member states a great deal of room for manoeuvre in the use of these funds. we have always proposed greater flexibility for countries, which commissioner hogan has done. it can be seen that, despite the various positive and very important actions taken at commission and country level, the effects are very little visible. there is an urgent need to create a balance between supply and demand. however, no instruments were proposed to reduce production. the assumption that farmers will do this voluntarily is not supported by the facts. farmers protect themselves from bankruptcy by increasing production. some form of payment for the reduction of production should therefore be applied, while ensuring that farms are able to maintain their financial liquidity so that they do not undertake to eliminate the stock earlier and on a larger scale. the efforts of the member states and commissioner hogan to increase sales in third countries are to be welcomed, but at the same time the consumption of milk products on the domestic markets, especially where it is relatively low, should be increased. we are also thinking of using the free food distribution scheme adopted by the european union in this respect, or of allocating more milk products to the group of people coming to europe. the above situation illustrates the extent to which the european milk market is dependent on the world market, other external factors, often of a political nature, such as the russian embargo, or far-reaching concessions to the detriment of agriculture in trade agreements concluded by the union with third countries, where agricultural matters are often sacrificed for advantages in other areas of trade. the first priority is therefore to improve the efficiency of the milk chain from the milk-producing cow to the consumer. there are many elements that need to be improved in terms of vertical integration and the functioning of cooperatives, because there too, the various cooperatives are owned by the members, the costs are borne by the farmers. there is scope for efficiency gains through better vertical integration.

in writing. ‒ this very balanced report discusses the opportunities and risks associated with virtual currencies and decentralised ledger technology in the area of payments. the issue of dlt applications in areas other than payments was raised and recommendations were made on the approach to be taken. the report highlights the potential of virtual currencies to reduce transaction and handling costs for cross-border money transfers, reduce the cost of access to finance for those without a bank account, and develop secure online micropayment systems. as regards risks, the report highlighted the lack of governance structures, the limited capacity of regulatory authorities, consumer protection aspects and the potential for use for money laundering and terrorist financing. i support the compromise reached on these issues, as the proposed extension of the scope of the aml directive was limited to virtual currency exchange platforms after an impact assessment, and therefore does not cover e-wallet services. in view of the main points of the report and the compromises reached, i voted in favour of its adoption.
in writing. ‒ i supported the jakob von weizsäcke report in which the european parliament calls on the european commission to set up a working group on virtual currency. this is all to develop regulatory tools and promote virtual wallets. virtual currencies are a very fast growing segment of the global market, the value of global transactions has already exceeded eur 1 billion, so i think we should not remain passive towards this segment of the market. it is very important to establish surveillance to avoid potential systemic risks. at the same time, i support the european commission's initiative to extend the anti-money laundering directive to virtual currency exchange platforms to combat money laundering and terrorist financing.
in writing. ‒ the report discusses the opportunities and risks associated with virtual currencies and dlt in the area of payments, addresses the issue of dlt applications in areas other than payments and provides recommendations on the approach to be taken. the report highlights the potential of virtual currencies and dlt to reduce transaction and handling costs for cross-border money transfers, reduce the cost of access to finance for unbanked people, and develop secure online micropayment systems. as regards risks, the report highlighted the lack of governance structures, the limited capacity of regulatory authorities, consumer protection aspects and the potential for use for money laundering and terrorist financing. the most controversial points in the report concerned the regulatory approach to be adopted and the proposal to set up a task force under the chairmanship of the commission. the compromise reached limited the proposed extension of the scope of the aml directive to virtual currency exchange platforms after an impact assessment and therefore excluded electronic wallet services. the report recommends that an analysis be carried out on virtual currencies and that, on the basis of this analysis, changes be made to the relevant payment legislation, where appropriate. i hereby endorse the report.
in writing. ‒ virtual currency, i.e. unregulated digital money, issued and usually controlled by its creators, used and accepted by users of a specific virtual community, has gained popularity in recent years. seven years after the launch of bitcoin, the first and most popular virtual currency, with a venture capital value of over €1 billion, it is clear that the technology has huge potential. although it is not yet systemically important, its innovative nature and pace of development can be astonishing. in its report, the european parliament calls on the commission to set up a task force on virtual currencies and to strengthen surveillance of virtual currencies to prevent potential negative effects of their use for money laundering or the financing of criminal and terrorist activities. the report also rightly stressed that the scope of the directive on the prevention of the use of the financial system for the purpose of money laundering or terrorist financing should be extended to virtual currency exchange platforms. for these reasons, i have decided to vote in favour of the report on virtual currency.
