in writing. ‒ data flows are an essential element of the eu's security, economic and trade relations. smes accounted for 60% of enterprises relying on a secure transfer of personal data agreement, which allowed them to benefit from targeted and cost-effective compliance requirements. there are already agreements on the exchange of information in certain policy areas, including the terrorist finance tracking programme and the eu-us agreement on passenger name record data. following the ets schrems ruling and in response to allegations of mass surveillance, the us congress and administration have made more than 20 changes to surveillance laws and programs since 2013. reforms include the us freedom act, which prohibits the bulk collection of data, the presidential proclamation (ppd-28) that makes the protection of privacy and civil liberties of non-eu individuals an integral part of us surveillance policy, and the judicial appeals act, which extends data protection measures to eu citizens. i personally support the implementation and adoption of the new privacy shield and i want the eu-us general data protection umbrella agreement to be adopted and implemented as soon as possible. i believe that these two agreements guarantee a high level of protection and legal certainty for businesses and consumers, a level that has not been achieved so far.
in writing. ‒ i voted in favour of a resolution calling on the european commission to continue negotiations with the us on better protection of citizens' data transferred to the us. the commission and the us administration are working to improve existing safeguards to protect the privacy of eu citizens whose personal data is leaked, for example, when they shop online. as the number of transactions increases, so does the risk that they will be used without the knowledge of the citizen, to his or her detriment, for example by intelligence agencies. to prevent this, the data protection guaranteed by union law should be maintained even after the data leaves the territory of the eu. the aim of the system is to replace the previous transatlantic data transfer system ('safe harbour') with a new, more efficient mechanism ('privacy shield'). unfortunately, there's been no significant improvement. the americans do not guarantee the level of protection required by eu law. they're proposing that the state department appoint a civil rights attorney to investigate claims by europeans. i doubt that an ombudsman who is dependent on the us executive and has too few powers could effectively carry out his duties. the commission and the us administration should create a more efficient and european citizen-friendly redress mechanism. the commission should periodically assess the compliance of its privacy decision with eu rules in order to strengthen data protection in the eu.
in writing. ‒ data flows are an essential component of the eu's security, economic and trade relations. there are already agreements on the exchange of information in some policy areas, including the terrorist finance tracking programme, the eu-us passenger flight data agreement and the safe harbor recently concluded privacy shield agreement. the recently adopted general data protection regulation and the data protection for law enforcement purposes directive also address data protection in relation to third countries. since 2013, the u.s. congress and the u.s. administration have made more than 20 changes to surveillance laws and programs. reforms include the us freedom act, the presidential proclamation (ppd-28) that makes the protection of privacy and civil liberties of non-eu individuals an integral part of us surveillance policy, and the judicial appeals act that extends data protection measures to eu citizens. the ecr group supports the implementation and adoption of the new privacy shield and wants the eu-us general data protection umbrella agreement to be adopted and implemented as soon as possible. these two agreements guarantee a high level of protection and legal certainty for businesses and consumers, which has not been achieved so far. i hereby endorse the report.
in writing. ‒ personal data of eu citizens that is collected for commercial purposes, e.g. when shopping online or registering on social media, and that ends up in the us must be adequately protected. the so-called safe harbour agreement of 2000 did not provide sufficient protection. the commission has not received any comments from interested parties. the new privacy shield agreement proposed by the commission aims to seal the system and improve safeguards protecting the privacy of eu citizens. in the new agreement, the americans committed themselves to having access to eu citizens' data monitored and subject to clear limits. in addition, the u.s. government has assured that there will be no surveillance of individuals whose data is sent across the atlantic. us companies that transfer data will have to guarantee the protection of the data they process. the resolution welcomes the proposed agreement, which rightly imposes specific obligations on companies to protect eu citizens' data processed in the us. the privacy shield can bring a number of benefits to european consumers and businesses, especially smes. enabling the free flow of data between the eu and the us is crucial for both economies, trade and investment. that's why i decided to vote for a resolution in favor of a new treaty.
in writing. ‒ the good points of the resolution we voted on are the right institutional ideas and the proposed mechanisms for claim recovery. the data flows between europe and north america should be subject to the highest possible level of protection of personal data, while respecting the principle of reasonableness. when data is collected for the purpose of fighting the worst crimes, the right to privacy must not be abused at the expense of citizens' security. the draft resolution put to the vote today met these criteria and i therefore voted in favour of it.
in writing. ‒ the exchange of digital information between the united states and europe is a necessity that underpins the operations of many businesses in the age of the data-driven economy. however, this need cannot be construed as a disregard for security and privacy. developing clear and effective data exchange rules is the best guarantee of their security and thus gives us confidence that the information we leave about us online will not be used by unauthorised persons. the united states is a demanding negotiating partner that takes a very liberal approach to many privacy law issues. of course, the eu's negotiations should be conducted with the best possible safeguard for our interests, but this cannot lead to a no-deal situation. the current state of these talks is encouraging and shows that even in such a delicate matter it is worthwhile to seek compromise. i believe that the proposals to improve the privacy shield mechanism, which is intended to ensure better definition of key terms for data exchange and to prevent abuse by controllers, meet the expectations of eu citizens. it also welcomes the development of a claim procedure for natural persons who, when the abuse is discovered, will be able to assert their rights through the courts. of course, while protecting our privacy, we can't forget that digital data analysis is an important tool in the fight against terrorism. we have to be willing to compromise on that.
in writing. ‒ this report is a response to the commission's communication on the implementation of the new energy contract, which is based on three pillars: saving consumers money and energy through better information; increasing consumer choice; and maintaining the highest level of consumer protection. i think it's very important to create an energy system that is fair to consumers and helps protect the poor who use energy. however, i am concerned that many of the amendments adopted in the draft report violate the principle of subsidiarity and are not practicable. for example, i am a big supporter of the idea of a broad, non-binding definition of energy poverty, because any attempt to establish a central definition would be useless, because nations define energy needs or low-income thresholds differently. it should also be noted that a large number of the provisions cited in the report already exist under the third energy package and therefore require better implementation rather than new provisions. however, these are not very negative records and in my opinion the report is appropriate and raises important issues. i therefore voted in favour of the report.
in writing. - i support the report by mrs theresa griffin. it stressed the need for better protection of eu consumers, especially energy consumers who have to pay high penalties for switching energy suppliers. we should strive to abolish such practices. this requires cooperation between member states good practices should be identified and the exchange of information should be encouraged. one way would be to develop a database of measures taken by different member states to prevent unfair practices by energy suppliers. local authorities, national regulators and energy companies can play a key role in addressing this issue. a common european approach is needed to find long-term solutions that benefit consumers and provide our industry with access to affordable energy.
in writing. ‒ this report is a response to the commission's communication on the implementation of the new energy contract, which is based on three pillars: saving consumers money and energy through better information; increasing consumer choice; and maintaining the highest level of consumer protection. the creation of an energy system that is fair to consumers and contributes to the protection of poor energy consumers should be encouraged. however, many of the amendments adopted in the draft report violate the principle of subsidiarity. for example, the idea of a broad and non-binding definition of energy poverty is a good one, but any attempt to create a central definition would be useless, as different nations define energy needs or low income thresholds. it should also be noted that many of the provisions cited in the report already exist under the third energy package. they therefore require better implementation and perhaps the introduction of new, necessary legislation. i hereby endorse the report.
in writing. ‒ consumers should have a greater say in the energy market. i think that there should be a system in place to ensure that consumers are able to benefit from fair offers. it is appropriate to introduce better tools for comparing the offers of energy suppliers on the market and to ensure a transparent contract for switching. we must prevent citizens from being forced to give up energy because of lower incomes. energy poverty is the result of incorrect regulation that does not take into account the financial situation of households. all consumers should be provided with comprehensive information on the proposed energy offers so that they are not subject to additional charges in the event of withdrawal. i believe that the introduction of innovative business models will make it easier for consumers to use energy efficiently.
in writing. ‒ electricity is a strategic asset whose trade should not be beyond the control of regulatory authorities. however, we must be aware that the current model of electricity generation and distribution must be constantly evolving to meet the growing demand of consumers. greater efficiency and flexibility in energy production and consumption are essential if europe is to be able to produce the amount of energy needed to maintain a constant level of household supply. of course, when designing the shape of the european energy market, we must take into account the differences between member states, especially in the energy mix. we cannot accept any solution which discriminates against countries such as poland, for whom coal is the main source of energy. the freedom of choice of the consumer's energy supplier must entail real price differences and the possibility of making an informed choice, for which the possibility of comparing the offers of all operators is essential. we must especially look after the needs of the lowest income groups, who spend a large part of their income on basic goods, including electricity. more attention and resources should be devoted to supporting individual forms of energy production that significantly reduce costs and improve resource efficiency. as the report takes account of the above considerations, i voted in favour of its adoption.
in writing. ‒ the problem of poverty and the social marginalisation of women has been a particular focus for many years. the issue of addressing the causes and consequences of various aspects of women's insecurity has been raised repeatedly in numerous resolutions. according to the latest statistics, 16.6% of citizens in the 28 eu member states are at risk of poverty as a result of social transfers. the risk of poverty for women is 17.2% and for men 16.1%. one of the main reasons is the persisting disparity in wages and pensions. the report contains many ideas which i fully support, such as the elimination of the gender pay gap, the adoption of measures to promote work-life balance, the introduction of flexible working hours, etc. however, it touches on a number of issues with which i do not agree, such as the commission's call to work on a proposal for a minimum wage, the individual examination of household income to determine social rights (assuming that women are always at a disadvantage), a new eu legal act on combating gender-based violence, combating stereotypes through educational programmes, etc. in view of the above, i was forced to abstain.
in writing. ‒ i abstained on the report by maria arena of the s&d group on poverty from a gender perspective, because it contains many articles that violate the principle of subsidiarity and poland's interest. these include proposals for a uniform eu definition of work of equal value and the universal implementation of minimum wages and pensions; proposals for gender-equitable taxation; calls for no spending cuts in public administration and no development of flexible forms of work. i consider the latter in particular to be harmful to women and to the proper functioning of the labour market in general, with particular reference to smes, including family businesses. that is why i voted against these proposals. at the same time, i supported the article welcoming the idea of carer's leave in the commission's proposal for a policy on reconciling domestic and occupational responsibilities. this proposal arises from the fact that the duty of care extends not only to the parents of minor children but also to adult children towards their aging parents, grandparents and other relatives. this perspective of thinking about barriers to women's entry into the labour market is more appropriate to the reality where caring responsibilities are not only for children but also for the elderly in the family. the search for a more universal response to the conflict of employment caused by caring responsibilities is more appropriate than imposing on member states inflexible solutions to the ec's withdrawn parent directive.
in writing. ‒ the problem of poverty and the social marginalisation of women has been a particular focus for many years. women are generally more at risk of poverty than men on average, especially single mothers, pensioners and women with disabilities. the report contains many ideas that deserve support, such as: closing the gender pay gap, adopting measures to promote work-life balance, introducing flexible working hours (on a voluntary basis), the role of education in improving the situation of women, promoting women's entrepreneurship, etc. however, it raises a number of issues with which we cannot agree, such as the commission's call for a proposal on minimum wages (taking into account national conditions; we believe, however, that this issue should not be regulated by the eu), the individual treatment of household income to determine social rights (assuming that women are always at a disadvantage), a new eu legal act on combating gender-based violence (and supporting the istanbul convention), the fight against stereotypes through educational programmes, etc. the report also contains points that are controversial, such as support for the maternity leave directive or numerous references to the rights of lgbt people. i hereby abstain from voting.
in writing. ‒ more than 122 million people in europe are at risk of poverty today. more than half of these are women, especially single mothers who struggle to make ends meet. it is important to remember that women's poverty is passed on to their children, often preventing an entire generation from functioning normally in society. the european parliament's report on women's poverty is a set of recommendations for the eu institutions and member states on how to combat this phenomenon. the document highlighted the persisting gender pay gap and the lack of public support for mothers. the eu's funding for social infrastructure and the creation of a european child guarantee, which would provide free education, decent housing and healthcare for every child, were among the recommendations. despite the very legitimate aim of combating poverty among women and children, the parliament's document contains many unrealistic assumptions and demands, which are also incompatible with the basic principles of the union, such as proportionality and subsidiarity. that's why i decided to abstain.
in writing. ‒ studies have shown that women are a group that is discriminated against in terms of access to the labour market, the capital market and public services. inequalities in this situation create barriers to effective economic development of countries due to the misuse of workers' potential. the discriminatory poverty of women is largely due to the historical construct of their identity in biology and society. the problems arising from widespread stereotypes about women will have a negative impact on the functioning of the sustainable economic process. promoting gender equality will contribute to the emergence of smart development policies, which will consequently have a positive impact on the future of the labour market and the private lives of its participants. i am in favour of taking action that will ultimately improve the working lives of women and will constitute new principles that will result in an increase in the well-being of the whole of society.
in writing. ‒ the fight against the economic exclusion of women and the improvement of their situation in the labour market is an important objective, which the european union should actively contribute to. women are undoubtedly much more at risk of poverty than men. the particular importance of women for the proper functioning of the family as the basic social unit cannot be overestimated and they therefore deserve special protection and effective opportunities to combine work and family life. many of the action proposals in the report deserve full support, including the call to close the gender pay gap, the call to create further mechanisms to enable women to reconcile family and work responsibilities, the call to enable women to benefit more from flexible forms of employment and access to training and upskilling tools. unfortunately, with so many proposed solutions that go beyond the need to improve the situation of women, i cannot agree. in particular, it is an attempt to subordinate the member states and transfer to the european level the mechanism for shaping the minimum wage or the ideologically motivated perception of the problem of violence against women and gender stereotypes. i understand the importance of this issue and, in view of the above arguments, i have decided to abstain from voting on this report.
in writing. ‒ this report introduces an alternative, trade-focused view of the development of the single market and its current status. it aims to encourage policy-makers to look at the single market and national rules affecting crossborder trade through the lens of international trade. member states may wish to introduce national rules in areas not covered by union or international law or standards for a number of reasons, but in order to remain compatible with the principles of the single market, such rules must be non-discriminatory and proportionate and must pursue a legitimate public policy objective. the report concludes that non-tariff barriers are an unjustifiable barrier to trade and that the commission should therefore give priority to their elimination. the report called for a report to be prepared by the end of this year identifying such barriers as they currently exist and called on member states and the institutions to commit themselves collectively to eliminating these obstacles to the smooth functioning of the single market. i fully agree with the report and have therefore voted in favour of its adoption.
in writing. ‒ more than 20 years after the single market was launched, unjustified non-tariff barriers continue to have a negative impact on trade and the free movement of goods and services between eu member states. the european commission estimates that the removal of these barriers would generate economic gains of eur 1.1 trillion per year, equivalent to 63% of the eu's gdp. the diversity of national regulations, due to the lack of transposition of eu directives and the accuracy of their implementation, that a company may face when it wants to trade cross-border or provide services in another member state, makes many companies give up this possibility. only 2% of new smes, micro-enterprises and start-ups have cross-border activities thanks to foreign direct investment. the commission has already repealed unnecessary eu rules, now it is the member states' turn, reflecting the result of today's vote. the continuing lack of conformity of member states' rules with those of the union is harmful not only to the single market but also to consumers. in this context, further efforts are needed to encourage member states to bring their legislation into line with the existing eu directives as soon as possible. moreover, it is often the case that national governments introduce numerous additional provisions which adversely affect the common market in the directives they transpose, and the commission should therefore monitor and prevent any modifications to eu law more closely.
in writing. ‒ through the years of the european union, the single market has remained one of the most important fundaments of the european integration. in order to keep it strong however, further harmonisation of free movement of goods and services needs to be pursued, so that unjustified and hampering practices of particular member states can be eliminated, and equal conditions for citizens across the europe can be granted. all of this can be achieved through gradual and step-by-step development of mechanisms. removing of non-tariff barriers is such a necessary step, which strengthens the principle of mutual recognition, and makes member states markets more accessible to foreign importers, ensuring that same conditions apply to both national and non-national producers.
in writing. ‒ this report introduces an alternative, trade-focused view of the development of the single market and its current status. it encourages a look at the single market and national rules affecting crossborder trade through the lens of international trade. the author has sought to define cases where national rules may constitute a non-tariff barrier to intra-eu trade. member states may wish to introduce national rules in areas not covered by union or international law or standards for a number of reasons, but in order to remain compatible with the principles of the single market, such rules must be non-discriminatory and proportionate and must pursue a legitimate public policy objective. the report identifies several sectors where this has been problematic in the past, including the application of the services directive and particularly bad experiences in the retail sector. the report concludes that these non-tariff barriers constitute an unjustifiable barrier to trade and that the commission should therefore give priority to their elimination. the report called for a report to be prepared by the end of this year identifying such barriers as they currently exist and called on member states and the institutions to commit themselves collectively to eliminating these obstacles to the smooth functioning of the single market. i hereby endorse the report.
in writing. ‒ even though since 1968 we do not have any tariff barriers on the eu’s single market, the functioning of a truly single market is hampered by non-tariff barriers such as excessive national regulations, various additional requirements that are imposed on trade by member states or bureaucracy. non-tariff barriers strongly affect the free movement of goods, services and people, which is supposed to be the backbone of the european project. this report, for which i was a shadow rapporteur on behalf of the epp group, defines, identifies and addresses a variety of ntbs, while also emphasising that the eu should not hesitate anymore to eliminate disproportionate and discriminatory barriers, which are often motivated by protectionism. the eu single market bears a huge potential, which we should use to the highest level, especially in the situation when the economic growth is weak. member states have to stop thinking in a protectionist manner and open their markets to products and services from other member states, fulfilling the idea of a truly competitive single market. therefore, i call on the commission to draw on this report while preparing legislative proposals on eliminating non-tariff barriers in the single market.
in writing. ‒ the persistence of non-tariff barriers to trade in goods in the eu single market is a situation that many operators still have to face. while the eu is committed to the full implementation of the fundamental freedoms for the movement of people, goods, capital and services, there are many cases of growing non-tariff barriers to the internal market, including for food exporters, imposed by individual eu member states. such practices are often discriminatory and distort the competitiveness of food imports in the eu internal market, thus having a negative impact on the eu economy. this situation can directly lead to a reduction in cross-border trade in foodstuffs in the eu internal market and have a negative impact on the functioning of smes in the internal market. in this context, it is necessary for member states to take measures to control and guarantee fair trading conditions, which is in the interest of both producers and consumers. to this end, consideration should be given to various types of action that could ensure the transparent and fair functioning of the internal market, in particular for food products produced by one of the eu's strategic sectors, agriculture.
in writing. ‒ the eu's single market still has many non-tariff barriers, and instead of being reduced, they are increasing in many respects, hampering the free movement of goods and services between countries. additional technical regulations, product or service requirements, lack of mutual recognition of qualifications, and red tape are just some of the methods of protectionism applied to non-domestic producers and service providers that are not applied to domestic companies. the parliament's report defines and identifies the different types of non-tariff barriers, stressing that the eu and the member states have a duty to eliminate them. the commission's role in the implementation of the new rules is to ensure that the existing rules are properly implemented and that the european commission responds quickly to new national restrictions. it is important to remember that the eu single market has enormous potential which must be exploited, especially in a context of unstable economic growth and a decline in europe's importance in world trade. eu countries must stop thinking in a protectionist way as soon as possible and open their markets to other players. only then will we be able to exploit the full potential of the single market.
in writing. ‒ the attempt to deny the fundamental principles on which the european union is founded is a dangerous trend that we are increasingly faced with. these fundamental principles are not, as the european commission very often wishes, abstract political values, but economic freedoms, which enable all member states to benefit from the single market on an equal footing. unfortunately, we are now faced with a situation in which these freedoms are restricted and limited by the internal legislation of the member states, which is contrary to european law. of course, in justified cases, such regulation of the free movement of goods and services is necessary and justified, but it must then be proportionate to the objective pursued, non-discriminatory towards operators from different countries with the same business profile and have a clear objective relating to the protection of the public good. an example that illustrates this problem well is the minimum wage regulations introduced by the government of the federal republic of germany, which lead to unjustified discrimination against polish transport companies. despite the clear breach of the rules on the functioning of the single market, these rules are still in force and the european commission is postponing a decision on the matter. such cases should be investigated and clarified quickly in order not to encourage other member states to take similar steps. i believe that the commission should do much more and enforce the economic freedoms of the eu more effectively.
in writing. ‒ this report sets out parliament's position on the commission's strategy for the single market. the report supported many of the main proposals set out in the commission's communication, although it also made a number of additional demands consistent with priorities previously identified by parliament's political groups. the report is overwhelmingly positive and recognises the need to improve the single market, particularly in the services sector. the report contains several points of concern for the group, in particular support for the product safety and market surveillance package currently under consideration, which is blocked in the council, instead of proposing an alternative approach that would allow the commission to rationalise the proposals and propose only those parts that are relevant. nevertheless, the report is generally sufficiently positive in terms of the priorities for improving the single market. given the small number of points of dispute in this report, i voted in favour of its adoption.
in writing. ‒ this report sets out parliament's position on the commission's strategy for the single market. the report supported many of the main proposals set out in the commission's communication, although it also made a number of additional demands consistent with priorities previously identified by parliament's political groups. the report is overwhelmingly positive and recognises the need to improve the single market, particularly in the services sector. it also echoes the call made in the dalton report for the elimination of non-tariff barriers. the report contains several problematic points, in particular support for the product safety and market surveillance package currently under consideration, which is blocked in the council, instead of proposing an alternative approach that would allow the commission to rationalise proposals and propose only those parts that are relevant. the report makes proposals on vat rates in e-commerce; mandatory labelling of certain types of products; geographical indications for non-agricultural products. nevertheless, the report is generally sufficiently positive in terms of the priorities for improving the single market. i hereby endorse the report.
in writing. ‒ last year the ec presented a strategy on how to boost the performance of the european single market. the document, focusing on services and product markets, underlines some ways to enable a balanced development of the collaborative economy and to help smes and start—ups to grow. all of those initiatives are aimed at releasing the full potential of the eu single market. however, the european parliament’s document addressing the single market strategy, with all its positive aspects, includes points that could even further divide the internal market. i believe the principle ‘equal pay for equal work’ is not only against the idea of the single market, but fundamentally inconsistent with the mechanism of competition and basic principles of economics. wages should reflect differences in productivity levels, and cannot be uniform. likewise, companies across europe differ in terms of quality and technological advancement of their products. moreover, the report again speaks about ‘social dumping’, which has never been defined in economic or legal terms. i believe both slogans ‘equal pay for equal work’ and ‘social dumping’ encourage protectionist measures that would further hamper the functioning of the single market and harm competition. hence, i abstained.
in writing. ‒ the single market creates an opportunity not only for businesses and workers, but also for consumers to have a wider choice of goods and services of higher quality and at lower prices. it is one of the greatest achievements of a united europe. however, these possibilities are not always fully exploited. this is why it is so important to work towards improving the functioning of the single market. the european commission's evaluation report of the single market strategy presented by parliament last year highlights a number of important issues that should be given priority. this includes support for smes and innovative start-ups, tackling payment bottlenecks, deregulating professions, promoting public-private partnerships and, finally, exploiting the full potential of the digital revolution. unfortunately, the parliament's document also contains a provision on the implementation of the controversial principle of equal pay for equal work at the same place. in my view, it is fundamentally contrary to the idea of the single market. different companies have very different operating costs and those from another country have additional burdens that local companies do not have. i believe that the slogan is more about protectionism and the desire to restrict competition in the common market than about protecting workers' rights. i have therefore decided to vote against this report.
in writing. ‒ the single market is one of the few indisputable achievements of european integration, which, in the face of the many crises affecting the eu today, is an example of the success of the cooperation model adopted by the member states. the creation of equal opportunities and non-discriminatory rules for the operation of economic operators in all member states is a historic opportunity for the countries of central and eastern europe to overcome the economic backwardness of their western european partners. the world is constantly changing and the shape of the single market as it was designed in the early 1990s must also change. the growing role of smes in the european economy and the digital revolution are issues that we need to better integrate into the definition of the single market. strengthening the principle of free movement of goods and services should be one of the priorities of the present european commission. this is particularly relevant in the context of actions taken by countries such as germany and france which are undermining the freedom of activity of transport companies from poland. the commission's proposed amendments to the posted workers directive, which could restrict the freedoms of the single market, are also a cause for concern. this is not something that should be allowed. i fully support all steps to ensure better enforcement of european law in the area of freedom of establishment in the eu and hope that this report will contribute to strengthening the single market.
i support the report by mr preda, which calls for greater involvement of the european parliament in development policy, with particular emphasis on migration, trade and finance, the environment, agriculture and international cooperation, both within the member states and with the united states and the bric countries. the european parliament should support the cohesion policy initiative, which has as its main objective an effective long-term development agenda. the report also sets out the mechanisms by which the european parliament has supported the implementation of policy coherence for development and the crucial role of appropriate documentation necessary for effective monitoring of the actions taken by the european parliament and the member states. the report's proposed amendment to the 2030 agenda emphasises the need to set universal targets for all countries, moving away from the developed country as donor and developing country as recipient model. as concord research shows, most countries do not carry out analyses to assess the impact of their cohesion policy actions on development, which makes it difficult to assess the effectiveness of our policies. the report by mr preda, while suggesting that member states should carry out more detailed studies of the concrete effects of cohesion policy actions on development, also proposes another solution: the introduction of an arbitration system under the direct leadership of the commission representative, acting in the event of discrepancies between the various actions of the european union, and an independent complaints system for citizens of developing countries directly affected by the actions of the european union.

chain. the report was initiated by mr dawid jackiewicz, currently a minister in the government of the republic of poland. i would like to highlight the significant contribution of the work of both the member and his colleagues and staff in the secretariat. the involvement of members from the various political groups, and in particular shadow members, was also important in the final shape of the report. i want to thank you all for your time and your commitment. i am aware that the subject matter of the report is extremely important to both the distributor and supplier communities, and its final text and message will be of great importance for the future of the relationship between the two groups. in the report we clearly stated that unfair trading practices are a problem that is acknowledged by all actors in the food supply chain and by national competition authorities. concrete examples of this problem in the uk and poland, among others, confirm the importance of this problem. the report was prepared in the course of numerous meetings with both international and national organisations. a number of suggestions and experiences were presented on the functioning of both voluntary and legislative solutions at national level. the commission and parliament have repeatedly drawn attention to the problem of unfair trading practices, including in the commission report of 29 january 2006 entitled 'the impact of the eu's trade policy on the eu's trade policy'. this was reflected in the numerous amendments submitted. we don't know what people think of him, but we do know that there are differences of opinion. for example, a review of the measures taken by member states to combat unfair trading practices confirms that voluntary initiatives are not currently sufficient. the report made recommendations supporting the need to work hard on solutions to improve supplier-supermarket relations, including on the issue of minimising the fear factor. we also included a call on the commission to take action to formulate new tools to strengthen action to counter unfair practices. almost all member states have introduced regulatory solutions to complement good practice. today we can already say that the experiences of other countries described in the context of the commission's report confirm that voluntary initiatives can only have a complementary effect. however, the current initiatives are fraught with imperfections, which we point out in the report. in recent times, most countries have introduced their own national regulations. member states should therefore be encouraged to exchange experience on regulatory solutions. you also have to ask if that's enough. i believe that the jointly developed contents of the report will be a significant step forward in the fight against unfair trading practices in the food supply chain. we all want to see transparency and equality in the relations between the trading parties. i therefore hope that you will support the draft report in the vote during the current parliamentary session.
in writing. as a member from poland, i welcome the report on unfair trading practices in the food supply chain. unfair trading practices in the food supply chain, which are mainly caused by economic imbalances in trade relations, have a significant negative impact on the entire economy of the european union. the abuse of a stronger market position by large companies deprives smes of their ability to invest and thus blocks the development of this sector of the economy in the eu single market. the prevalence of unfair trading practices and their application to small food producers and retailers shows the weakness of the self-regulatory mechanisms that have been in place to restore market equilibrium. the report also highlights the 'fear factor' that forces small and medium-sized producers to submit to unfair practices for fear of being disrupted by a larger company. i therefore call for decisive action to be taken to eliminate completely unfair trading practices in the food supply chain in the european union.

in writing. ‒ the world health organisation's framework convention on tobacco control (fctc) is the world's first international public health treaty. this treaty was the result of four years of negotiation and discussion among members of the world health organization. by 2004, 180 parties (including the european community) had signed the convention, with the provisions formally entering into force in february 2005. the main objective of the convention is to protect parties from the health, social, environmental and economic consequences of smoking and inhaling tobacco smoke. the protocol to eliminate illicit trade in tobacco products is based on article 15 of the fctc and was adopted by the conference of the parties on 12 november 2012 in seoul. the eu signed the fctc protocol on 20 december 2013. the protocol has so far been ratified by 9 of the 40 parties required for its entry into force. this is a mixed agreement ratification by the eu and its 28 member states will add 29 parties to the fctc protocol. i think the legislative resolution is substantive and correct. i agree with the rapporteur that ratification of the fctc will bring benefits to public health and will support the international fight against illicit trade in tobacco products, tax evasion and organised crime. the european parliament should give its consent to such ratification. in light of the above, i voted yes.
in writing. ‒ i voted in favour of the recommendation on the draft council decision on the conclusion, on behalf of the european union, of the protocol on the elimination of illicit trade in tobacco products to the world health organisation framework convention on tobacco control, with the exception of the provisions falling within the scope of title v of part three of the treaty on the functioning of the european union. illicit trade in tobacco products, in particular smuggling of cigarettes, is a major public health threat. in addition, access by consumers to illicit and therefore cheaper tobacco products weakens tobacco control policies and causes huge losses to eu revenues from unpaid taxes and duties. the ratification of the fctc protocol will, in my view, bring public health benefits and support the international fight against illicit trade in tobacco products, tax evasion and organised crime.
in writing. ‒ illicit trade in tobacco products is a serious problem for the european union. this procedure not only causes huge losses to the state budget due to unpaid duties and taxes, but also serves to finance other areas of organized crime, such as drug and addiction trafficking, prostitution and pimping. there are suspicions that recently also smuggling of immigrants and even terrorism. in addition to the social and criminal pathologies, the health effects of illicit tobacco use are equally important. they are not subject to any standards of hygiene or sanitation, let alone quality. the protocol to the who convention provides in particular for the establishment of a worldwide system for the identification and traceability of tobacco products. the rules cover licensing, record keeping requirements, regulation of online sales, duty-free sales and international transit. it also defines offences and liability and charges for seizure of goods, as well as handling of confiscated products. it also aims to enhance international cooperation, including mutual administrative assistance in customs matters. i am pleased that the european parliament has given its consent to the eu's accession to the international protocol to eliminate illicit trade in tobacco products. it is a major global initiative to combat the illicit trade in cigarettes by improving the security of the tobacco supply chain.

in writing. ‒ the decision to apply enhanced cooperation in the area of jurisdiction, applicable law and the recognition and enforcement of judgments in matters of international couples' property (covering both matrimonial property regimes and the property consequences of registered partnerships) is a purely procedural decision. both of the above-mentioned council regulations concern jurisdiction and the law applicable. they exclude matters relating to the capacity of the spouses, the existence, validity or recognition of the marriage, as well as maintenance obligations and the inheritance of property of a deceased spouse. the rapporteur proposes that parliament give its consent to enhanced cooperation in this area. the main controversy with this proposal is that the decision authorising enhanced cooperation is a precedent. for the first time, it obliges member states to be bound by two instruments simultaneously - one on civil partnerships and the other on marriage. this solution also raises concerns in the context of article 4 (2) teu, which guarantees member states respect for their national identities, in this particular case in the definition of the institution of family law. in addition, in order to benefit their citizens from the application of the matrimonial property regulation, states will also be obliged to be bound by the regulation on the property consequences of partnerships. because of the controversy surrounding this regulation, i voted against it.
in writing. ‒ i have improved the long-awaited council recommendation on the draft council decision authorising enhanced cooperation on matrimonial property regimes and registered partnerships (08112/2016 - c8-0184/2016 - 2016/0061 (nle)). the package has been in the works for several years and aims to harmonise the legal rules on matrimonial property regimes. it lays down the procedure to be followed in the event of a conflict of property laws between member states and lays down the rules for the recognition and enforcement of judgments, court settlements and authentic instruments in those matters. i very much regret that poland is not in the broad coalition of countries that have agreed to joint solutions. the government's statement of 11 march 2016 explains that the reason for non-cooperation is that the regulation also applies to same-sex marriages and partnerships. although the regulation does not apply in this passage to countries that do not have legislation for same-sex marriage/partnerships, the polish government vetoed it in 2015, thereby preventing thousands of poles who have decided to end their international marriages from enjoying the benefits of enhanced cooperation between eu countries in this area.
in writing. ‒ the decision to apply enhanced cooperation in the area of jurisdiction, applicable law and the recognition and enforcement of judgments in matters of property regimes of international couples covers both matrimonial property regimes and the property effects of registered partnerships. the regulations concern the recognition and enforcement of judgments on matrimonial property regimes and the property consequences of registered partnerships and apply to cross-border cases. they do not cover matters relating to the capacity of the spouses, the existence, validity or recognition of the marriage, maintenance obligations and succession. the main controversy with this proposal is that for the first time it commits the member states to be bound by two instruments simultaneously - one on partnerships and the other on marriage. a number of member states still do not have a partnership institution (cyprus, bulgaria, romania, slovakia, poland, lithuania, latvia) and, in order to have the effect of the matrimonial property regulation, they must accede to both regulations implementing enhanced cooperation and agree to recognise the effects of a partnership institution which they do not recognise under their domestic law and which may be considered contrary to their public policy in the field of private international law and, in the field of domestic law, to the fundamental principles of their legal system, including constitutional status. i could not support the report.
in writing. ‒ the modern world is a world of mobile people. we are born elsewhere, we study elsewhere, we live and work elsewhere. it is therefore not surprising that mixed-nationality unions, couples living in a member state of which they are not nationals, having assets in different member states or divorcing or dying in a country other than their country of origin are becoming more common. the main problem for international couples is that it is very difficult to know which courts have jurisdiction and which law applies to the personal situation and assets of the couple. it is therefore necessary to ensure equal treatment of couples throughout the european union. i believe that the necessary regulations should be put in place as soon as possible to ensure this, and i therefore welcome the initiative to establish enhanced cooperation between the 17 member states in the area of jurisdiction, applicable law and the recognition and enforcement of decisions in matrimonial property regimes and jurisdiction, applicable law and the recognition and enforcement of judgments in matters relating to the property consequences of registered partnerships. i also hope that other eu countries, including poland, will join the group of countries participating in this initiative in the near future so that all eu citizens can benefit from these facilities.
