in writing. ‒ through policy coherence for development, the eu seeks to take development objectives into account in all its policies that could have an impact on developing countries. this aims to minimise contradictions and build synergies between the different eu policies and to make development cooperation more effective for the benefit of developing countries. the european commission monitors progress in cohesion policy for development in the eu and its member states on the basis of its biennial report on the cdp. the latest report (published in august 2015) covers both cross-cutting and thematic issues and presents examples of progress in the cfp across different policy areas. the european parliament maintained its support for the pcd. the report makes concrete proposals to strengthen political engagement in practice. the report is playing an increasingly important role in raising awareness of the cfp in certain policy initiatives. i therefore support the approximation of the pcd and its improved version in the light of the recently adopted sustainable development goals, but at the same time i stress that we must be careful that the new regulation does not become an additional regulatory tool and a burden for citizens and businesses. with that in mind, i have decided to abstain in the vote.
in writing. ‒ i voted in favour of the report by mr preda on the eu's 2015 report on policy coherence for development. i believe that this report touches on one of the most crucial issues in development policy, because it is extremely important that our policy action be consistent with the objectives we have set ourselves. i am convinced that this is a necessary condition for ensuring sustainable development. i also think that the report rightly identifies the priority areas of development policy, particularly with regard to migration. development policy is undoubtedly one of the key tools for tackling the migration crisis and i agree with the rapporteur that eu migration policy must be consistent with poverty reduction policies and must effectively and efficiently support economic, political and social development in partner countries.
in writing. ‒ i voted against paragraph 30 of the report on policy coherence for development, because it provides for the financing of development aid from carbon taxes and levies on the exploitation of natural resources. understanding the need to promote clean environment and alternative energy sources and to seek new sources of financing for the necessary development aid, it is unacceptable to place an excessive burden on eu countries in this regard, as this puts european countries in a low competitive position vis-à-vis economies that do not have such regulations and burdens or have them at a lower level. paragraph 30 is particularly unfavourable for poland, which bases its energy policy on coal and its extraction from domestic resources. therefore, the proposals contained in paragraph 30, neutral for countries using nuclear energy and sounding pro-environmental, the polish delegation always rejects.
in writing. ‒ through policy coherence for development, the eu seeks to take development objectives into account in all its policies that could have an impact on developing countries. this aims to minimise contradictions and build synergies between the different eu policies and to make development cooperation more effective for the benefit of developing countries. the european commission monitors progress in cohesion policy for development in the eu and its member states on the basis of its biennial report on the cdp. the latest report (published in august 2015) covers both cross-cutting and thematic issues from 2013-15 and presents examples of progress in the cfp across different policy areas. however, careful attention should be paid to ensuring that the new provision does not become an additional regulatory tool and burden for citizens and businesses. i hereby abstain from voting.
in writing. ‒ the new alliance for food security and nutrition in africa (nafsn) was established in 2012 under the auspices of the g8 as a major public-private partnership to attract private investment in agriculture to improve food security and nutrition in sub-saharan africa. it seeks to address the critical funding gap for achieving global food security through partnerships with the private sector, g8 countries and other international donors. it also aims to create a business-friendly environment in the alliance countries through systemic reforms in infrastructure, taxation, good governance, land and trade policies. i believe that it is of paramount importance to boost investment in african agriculture, as well as to encourage private investment and innovation in this sector. the report stresses that action to promote agricultural investment in africa should in particular support the development of local economies, including small-scale family farmers. in addition, the report calls on african governments to invest in local food systems to stimulate rural economies, ensure social safety nets and labour rights, and improve arrangements for democratic control of access to resources. in view of the contents of the report, i have decided to abstain.
in writing. ‒ ensuring food security is a major challenge for european agriculture. as a continent well developed and self-sufficient, we should be responsible for the third world, where development is slower and the conditions for it are much more difficult. this human solidarity should determine the support for those who are unable to cope on their own. africa is a particularly challenging region because of its climate, limited water resources and education. however, the work done so far in this area is not satisfactory. it's good that there are improvements in the legal or tax systems of these countries, but the most important thing is to work at the bottom, and that's what's missing. the biggest beneficiaries should be small producers, not the business tycoons who are currently getting the most relief. the current arrangements facilitate land grabbing, marginalise small producers, make it harder for women to enter the labour market and promote unsustainable farming. the european union must play a key role in the process of genuinely supporting family farms and farms, in particular by creating sound management structures that guarantee a fair distribution of profits and losses between the parties.
in writing. ‒ in the report on the new alliance for food security and nutrition, which i supported, i voted against paragraph 72 which calls on g8 countries not to support gmo crops in africa. recognizing the controversy surrounding the use of gmos in agriculture and the need for control and monitoring and the strict rules that such crops should be subject to, i believe that africa is one of the places on earth where gmos are simply a necessity. unlike europe, whose fertile soils and climate give us a choice, africa - afflicted by drought, high soil salinity, diversity and pest abundance - has very little agricultural production capacity without gmos. added to this is the population explosion, with africa's growing population adding to the need for effective solutions to feed its population. i am opposed to the automatic transfer of european philosophies and solutions to continents where different climatic, natural, political and cultural conditions determine different solutions. in the eu, the use of gmos is a matter of choice. in africa, the use of gmos is the only effective means of fighting hunger that is currently available. the alternative of humanitarian aid is blocking africa's development, exploiting its own potential, and is a dead end and an example of the world's condescending treatment of western countries that should be able to find their own path to development.
in writing. ‒ the new alliance for food security and nutrition in africa (nafsn) was established in 2012 under the auspices of the g8 as a major public-private partnership to attract private investment in agriculture to improve food security and nutrition in sub-saharan africa. it seeks to address the severe funding gap in the pursuit of global food security through cooperation with the private sector, g8 countries and other international donors. it also aims to create a business-friendly environment in the alliance countries through systemic reforms in infrastructure, taxation, good governance, land and trade policies. the key issue is to boost investment in african agriculture, as well as to support private investment and stimulate innovation in the sector. the focus on granting land titles alone often results in insecurity for small food producers and indigenous peoples. large public-private partnerships will give large agricultural companies a dominant position in african agriculture, which will help to push local businesses out. i therefore abstained.
in writing. ‒ the main objective of the new alliance for food security and nutrition (nafsn), launched in 2012 under the auspices of the g8, is to mobilise private investment in agriculture to improve food security in sub-saharan africa. the countries involved were required to adopt a national cooperation framework setting out the political commitments and identifying the companies involved in the project. in its resolution, the european parliament rightly stresses that action to promote agricultural investment in africa should be linked and support the development of local economies, including small farms and family farming. it is necessary to promote inclusive growth, agriculture that supports small farmers, and reducing poverty, hunger and malnutrition. the new alliance for food security and nutrition is a remarkable initiative that promotes public-private partnership and engages both sides both african countries and the g8 on a mutually beneficial basis. that is why i have decided to vote in favour of the resolution.
in writing. ‒ a new alliance for food security and nutrition in africa was launched in 2012 under the auspices of the g8. as a large public-private partnership, it was intended to increase the share of private investment in the agricultural sector, inter alia, to improve food security. unfortunately, consultation with small farmers was marginal, even though they should be the ultimate beneficiaries of the new alliance. as a result, the new alliance has been widely criticised, including by civil society. because of the split, i abstained.
in writing. ‒ i believe that action should be taken to minimise the occurrence of unfair commercial practices in the food sector. the european union should be responsible for providing transparent rules that create an appropriate level of cooperation between suppliers, food producers and distributors. a situation in which there is an imbalance between income and input in the food supply chain should be avoided. serious abuses in the sale of products below their cost of production are a threat to the functioning of a sustainable trade policy in the european union. it is important to be aware that the retail sale of a very large number of goods and the access to the points of sale by suppliers are under constant supermarket control. i am in favour of new legislation which should help to stop unfair practices which in fact lead to excessive costs and too low revenues generated by less competitive firms.
in writing. ‒ this report assesses the activities of the ifrs foundation, the efrag and the iorp and raises key questions about the process of adopting ifrs financial reporting standards into european law. the eu is a major contributor to the funding of these organisations. in previous reports, the ep has expressed concern about the level of european involvement and the operation of certain mechanisms of the foundation and the efrag. moreover, the report is based on a broad consensus among the political groups. stresses that the process for adopting ifrss must be in line with the criteria set out in the ifr regulation; this requires, in particular, that the financial statements be kept in a true, fair and transparent manner. further aspects of the report deal with the responsibility of the international accounting standards board. given the amendments to the report, which state, inter alia, that the implementation of ifrss must not delay or lead to a leveling or distortion of competition between market participants, i voted in favour.
in writing. ‒ the introduction of international accounting standards is essential to increase competition and remove barriers to investment on a global scale. accounting standards are very important for the further development of the single capital market in the european union. i voted to accept the report.
in writing. ‒ geoffrey van orden's report on the european union's engagement in un and african union peacekeeping missions analyses the added value of eu engagement in missions dealing with complex and multifaceted challenges in conflict areas and failed states. in his report, mr van orden notes the increasing trend of sending numerous un-approved missions to the same areas, each involving different regional entities and organisations. the rapporteur believes that eu involvement should focus on areas where it is possible to provide added value, such as training, equipment supply and logistical support. the rapporteur believes that the problem is not money itself but rather how it is spent and how other sources are used. while i support the eu working with international partners to ensure lasting stability and lasting security and peace in conflict areas, the key question remains what added value, if any, eu involvement brings to peace operations organised by local actors or the un. i believe that the report raises very important issues concerning these peace operations and the consequences of involvement in the eu, which is why i voted in favour of its adoption.
in writing. ‒ eu, un and african union peacekeeping missions are conducted in increasingly complex environments and require a comprehensive approach. in addition to diplomatic and development cooperation, there is also a need for in-depth security awareness, intelligence sharing and information sharing. some eu member states have long been involved in peacekeeping operations on the african continent, not only through un and au missions but also under the eu's common security and defence policy. these actions are intended to help stabilise countries in crisis. however, the legitimacy of the mission in the eyes of the people is crucial to its success, and where possible, military forces should be drawn primarily from african union countries. it should also be stressed that the main problem with the success of peace operations is very often not, as is commonly believed, the lack of funds, but their misuse. regular and thorough reviews of the use of eu funds for peace-keeping operations in africa are therefore necessary to help reduce corruption, which is widespread on the continent.
in writing. ‒ peace operations are designed to stabilise a conflict area. the international community, on the basis of its authority, is engaged in solving it. the eu, which wants to be an active player in world politics, cannot shirk its responsibility for international security, which is particularly important in african countries. in view of the prospect of these operations achieving their objectives, i have voted to adopt the report.
in writing. ‒ africa is one of the greatest sources of instability in the modern world. the close proximity of this continent means that europe must be aware of and actively involved in combating emerging threats. cooperation with our african partners in the fields of training, logistical support and information exchange should be extended, and the involvement of european military capabilities on the african continent increased. i fully agree with the conclusion of this report that border management, and in particular efforts to ensure its integrity, should be of particular concern to us. this is the only effective way to stop the two biggest problems facing the eu today: international islamic terrorism and the uncontrolled flow of migrants. but we must not forget that the eu is only part of a global security system in which it does not play a leading role. the potential of the un, nato and the united states is the most important element of peacekeeping operations on the african continent. the eu member states, with their very good political orientation in this extremely complex area, should provide a valuable pool of expertise, strengthen their commitment to training local security forces, provide technical resources and offer the highest quality military equipment and equipment. the csdp's engagement in africa so far shows that the eu can and should be part of an international coalition to build lasting peace on the continent.
in writing. ‒ the aim of this report is to highlight the problem of unfair trading practices and by highlighting the initiatives that have already been taken at national or european level to consider possible further possibilities or to strengthen existing initiatives aimed at addressing the problem of unfair trading practices in the european internal market. in july 2014, the european commission published a communication to encourage member states to look at ways to increase the protection of small food producers and retailers against unfair trading practices that often occur in business relationships where market forces are differentiated. unfair commercial practices are generally defined as practices which are grossly contrary to good commercial practice and contrary to the principle of good faith and fair dealing. the report also draws attention to the so-called 'fear factor', which often prevents a weaker party from taking any legal action for fear of termination of the commercial relationship by the stronger party. the report recalls that many countries have recognised the harmful nature of unfair trading practices and have taken regulatory initiatives. however, the rules vary widely across the eu, also because of the scale of the phenomenon. i believe that this report can bring about many positive changes in the member states in terms of trade and market economy. with that in mind, i voted yes.
in writing. ‒ support for food producers is essential to ensure that consumers have good quality food. they do the most to keep the produce fresh and healthy. in particular, the smallest producers are often the suppliers of the best products, because small production allows them to take care of the smallest details of the whole process. we should therefore encourage such entrepreneurship and make sure that no one exploits economic inequalities in the market for their own benefit. such unfair practices, which eliminate the smallest producers, can deprive consumers of local, traditional products and lead to the use of 'moloch food products'. the existing regulations have proved ineffective. it is necessary to define such practices precisely and to create clear tools to combat them effectively at member state level. effective enforcement of such regulations by means of penalties or sanctions is necessary for the new law to be effective.
in writing. ‒ today we adopted a report on unfair trading practices in the food supply chain, including the amendments i tabled on behalf of the committee on agriculture and rural development, calling on the european commission to present the appropriate legal framework to ensure a fairer distribution of income in the food chain. there is no doubt that farmers are currently the worst off in the 'crop to table' chain, partly as a result of their low bargaining power in negotiations with traders or processors, which is the result of their low level of organisation on the one hand and the use of unfair practices by other operators on the other. there are examples of contracts in which farmers are given dozens of conditions to fulfil at a very low price for the product. there are also significant delays in payments to farmers, which cause serious difficulties for the financial liquidity of the holdings. nor do these practices serve consumers, who are receiving an increasingly less diversified offer. the crisis in agriculture and the fall in farm incomes make the need to tackle this problem even more urgent, and i hope that the commission will quickly propose appropriate solutions to improve the situation of our farmers.
in writing. ‒ unfair trading practices have a negative impact not only on small and medium-sized enterprises by depriving them of the opportunity to invest in innovation and thus develop their activities in the common market but also on the eu economy as a whole. disproportions and inequalities are particularly evident in the food supply chain and it is therefore necessary to look for ways to increase the protection of particularly small food producers and retailers against unfair trading practices, which are often used by the largest players in the market. many member states have already taken regulatory action to combat them. moreover, stakeholders themselves have developed a number of good self-regulatory principles and frameworks for their implementation, and are successfully developing less formal and widespread dispute resolution and redress mechanisms. the good practice guidelines and the list of examples of fair and unfair practices in the food supply chain should therefore be extended and strongly enforced. i fear that the creation of regulation at eu level will be another proof that the european union is overregulated, which will provide its critics with additional ammunition. i have therefore decided to abstain.
in writing. ‒ supporting small and local food producers is key to developing healthy trade. their protection against unfair trading practices, which often occur in a differentiated market force, should be enhanced. the dominance of large food producers can have a negative impact on the eu economy as a whole, hampering the development of small and medium-sized enterprises. the draft report can contribute to the fight against unfair trading practices.
in writing. ‒ food producers face many problems in the single market, including abuse by consumers of their products. in particular, large retail chains, because of their dominant position, engage in practices that may be considered contrary to eu rules. unfortunately, not all of them are explicitly described in the law, which is why it is so often difficult for injured parties to pursue their claims. the most commonly reported abuses include: problems in timely payment of receivables, arbitrariness in the formulation and interpretation of contracts with suppliers, passing on to suppliers the costs of product promotion in stores, the costs of price reductions, and the costs of transporting and storing products. all these practices, and many other similar unfair practices, put producers at a great disadvantage and deprive them of a large part of their meager income. this is a major challenge, and sometimes a threat to their business, especially for polish farmers and food processing companies. i agree with the conclusions and proposals for solutions set out in the report of mr poslas and mr česák. the european union should undoubtedly pay more attention to protecting the rights of the weaker operators who are discriminated against and exploited in the food supply chain. i voted in favour of this report.
in writing. ‒ reduced land availability, environmental degradation, water scarcity, increased energy demand, and unprecedented pests and diseases are putting significant pressure on european raw material producers. to meet these challenges, the eu should become a world leader in technology, innovation and sustainability in agriculture. attention should be paid to the need to develop agricultural technologies in all types of agriculture conventional, organic and other. the report stressed that the benefits of technological innovation must be available to all farmers and that finding solutions for small-scale farming in rural communities is as important as finding solutions to the problems faced by many large-scale farmers. the report highlights the importance of precision farming, which can rationalise the use of machinery and reduce the use of pesticides, fertilisers and water. it also stressed the importance of innovative plant and animal breeding and called on the commission to publish the final report of the working group on new techniques. i believe that creating a risk-based and innovation-friendly regulatory environment, based on scientific evidence, and ensuring that eu rules do not become an obstacle to innovation, is crucial for sustainable and competitive eu agricultural production on the world market. however, due to the doubts that have arisen about the content of the document, i abstained.
in writing. ‒ i voted against the report on technological solutions for sustainable agriculture in the european union, because it contains many inaccuracies and shortcomings. promoting sustainable development and innovation in agriculture, as well as the development of agricultural technologies, is of course important and can have a significant impact on the further development of agriculture. however, in this particular report, many key issues were left unanswered or simply omitted. the concept of 'new technologies' has not been properly analysed and it is therefore not known what these technologies would be and what agricultural sectors they might serve. these 'technologies' have not been studied for agricultural safety and environmental protection, and the use of any 'technology' without adequate research and analysis of its impact on agricultural production and the environment can be tragic and irreversible. as a member of the european parliament, i could not therefore support the vote on an incomplete report whose legal, social and economic implications had not been fully analysed.
in writing. ‒ the coming decades will present a major challenge for agriculture. the world's growing population, its aging population, environmental degradation, and the scarcity of fresh water are all issues that will soon be faced. the answer to these challenges is new production techniques, innovative solutions that allow for intensive, modern and sustainable production. a good sign is the positive feedback on genetic, mechanical and digital technologies, which now appear to be the tools that can provide the answers to the challenges ahead. innovative technologies will help both small and large farms, organic and conventional, to achieve sustainable development and to provide food to needy consumers outside europe. this requires adequate funding for research into new solutions, but also equal access to research for all interested parties, whether small farmers or large farms.
in writing. ‒ reduced land availability, environmental loss and degradation, water scarcity, increased energy demand, and unprecedented pests and diseases are putting significant pressure on european raw material producers and the environment. to meet these challenges, the eu should become a world leader in technology, innovation and sustainability in agriculture, but european agriculture still lags behind many of the union's international competitors. the rapporteur draws attention to the need for the development of agricultural technologies in all types of agriculture conventional, organic and other and calls for greater access to research and its commercialisation, which would allow farmers to benefit from the opportunities offered by new technologies and innovation. the report stressed that the benefits of technological innovation must be available to all farmers and that finding solutions for small-scale farming in rural communities is as important as finding solutions to the problems faced by many large-scale farmers. the rapporteur draws attention to the importance of precision agriculture, which can bring environmental benefits, rationalise the use of machinery and reduce the use of pesticides, fertilisers and water. it also stressed the importance of innovative plant and animal breeding using proven techniques and called on the commission to publish the final report of the working group on new techniques. i abstained from the vote.
in writing. ‒ i welcome the adoption by parliament of the report by our colleague from the committee on agriculture, anthei mcintyre. the world's population is growing steadily - forecasts say we'll be close to 10 billion in 2050 - and at the same time, the amount of arable land on earth is running out, and recently, it's been shrinking due to increasing pollution, deforestation, desertification and intensive urbanization. other challenges include increasing water scarcity, the threat of plant and animal disease outbreaks, and the unpredictable effects of climate change. action is therefore needed to develop more sustainable agriculture based on respect for the environment and local communities. one solution is precision farming, which, among other things, has the potential to significantly reduce the use of pesticides. there is no doubt that to meet the challenges of the near future in agriculture, major changes, if not a revolution, must take place, and efforts must be made to ensure that europe is at the forefront of these changes. that's why this report is so important. at the same time, we must bear in mind that innovative technological solutions are inherently costly, which can be a problem for most of the family farms that dominate europe. they must therefore be accompanied by appropriate actions and financial support to ensure that innovation is widely available to all farmers.
in writing. ‒ by 2050, the world's population is expected to reach 9.7 billion, which means that farmers will have to produce food for an additional 2.4 billion people. it is estimated that global food production will have to increase by 60 to 110%. meeting the challenge of ensuring food security by increasing production without exacerbating existing environmental problems is a very difficult task. innovation in agricultural technology is key to tackling some of the biggest challenges facing agriculture today, in view of climate change, the increase in food demand due to the world's growing population, and environmental threats. the european parliament's report rightly points to the need to encourage innovative research and support, for example, precision agriculture, genetic diversity, soil management, water management and plant protection measures. the document also encourages cooperation between scientists and farmers and stresses the need to ensure appropriate knowledge transfer to end-users. i think that the solutions proposed in the european parliament's report are appropriate, which is why i have decided to vote in favour of this document.
in writing. ‒ the agricultural sector is facing the demands of a rapidly growing population. it is under pressure from a variety of challenges, including climate change and evolving socio-economic dynamics. european agriculture must therefore produce enough food, while respecting the environment, consumer safety and supporting farmers. the potential for innovation in agriculture is not fully realised and the european regulatory framework is not adapted to keep pace with the pace of progress. i believe that there are key challenges to be addressed in order to accelerate and stimulate innovation and entrepreneurship in agriculture. the eu could make better use of the innovative power of agriculture, while ensuring that no legislative act stifles competition. farmers should be given more freedom to be entrepreneurial and innovative. for example, in precision agriculture, you can limit the amount of plant protection products you need, or the amount of fertilizer you need, or even the amount of water you need. agricultural technology will predict where crop pests are expected to be or whether they will attack at a specific location in the crop fields. i fully agree with the report's view that agriculture is part of the solution - not part of the problem - to tackle major challenges such as climate change, air and water pollution and animal welfare. i strongly support the report, and i will sign off on all the compromise amendments.
in writing. ‒ new social structures, demographic changes mean that food producers are constantly looking for new solutions to meet the expectations of the food market. not only are consumers getting older, but their food preferences are changing as well. all these challenges need to be addressed by farmers and processors. it is not enough to increase current production. new solutions must be sought that not only meet the increased demand for food in the future, but also are sustainable enough not to cause further environmental degradation. there is a great need for greater integration of agriculture with other sectors of the economy, such as the chemical, health and technology sectors, in order to make more effective use of knowledge, innovative innovation and interaction. this will create new jobs in the agri-food sector and inspire the production of more diversified products or services. meeting the growing and diverse needs of european and global consumers will ensure that european agriculture remains relevant and continues to set the standard for high-quality production.
in writing. ‒ the agricultural sector today faces demand from a rapidly growing population and is under pressure from a variety of challenges, including climate change and evolving socio-economic dynamics. european agriculture must therefore produce enough food, while respecting the environment, consumer safety and supporting farmers. the potential for innovation in agriculture is not fully realised and the european regulatory framework is not adapted to keep pace with the pace of progress. key challenges need to be addressed to accelerate and stimulate innovation and entrepreneurship in agriculture. the eu could make better use of the innovative power of agriculture, while ensuring that no legislative act stifles competition. farmers should be given more freedom to be entrepreneurial and innovative. for example, in precision agriculture, you can limit the amount of plant protection products you need, or the amount of fertilizer you need, or even the amount of water you need. agricultural technology will predict where crop pests are expected to be or whether they will attack at a specific location in the crop fields. i agree with the view expressed in the report that agriculture is part of the solution - not part of the problem - when it comes to tackling major challenges such as climate change, air and water pollution and animal welfare. i hereby endorse the report.
in writing. ‒ european agricultural policy must stop supporting the outdated status quo and focus on innovation. we must do everything we can to increase the quantity of high-quality agricultural products, ensuring food security for all, while effectively tackling climate change. agriculture, like other sectors of the economy, now needs to unlock its innovation potential and the member states and the union should be involved in this process. the european parliament's report has rightly outlined the current obstacles and the relatively small scale of innovation in agriculture. this is due to a variety of obstacles, including insufficient knowledge transfer to farmers by researchers, high initial costs for the purchase of the necessary machinery, in particular for small farmers, and the fact that the rules are not always adapted to the specific needs of the agricultural sector. in addition, it is also worth considering the creation of new financing opportunities for farmers in cooperation with the european investment bank and the further development of existing risk management tools.

in writing. the european skills agenda is a necessary and long-awaited document. the problem in the european union labour market is not only high unemployment due to too little labour supply. we also have many openings and the skills of employees are often not adapted to employers' expectations and to dynamically changing working conditions. i therefore welcome today's statement by the commission. i am glad that the problem has been addressed in a comprehensive way and that support will be directed both towards basic skills training for less-educated workers and towards more advanced technologies. i believe that teaching relevant skills, including especially digital skills and entrepreneurship skills, should be an integral part of the learning process from the earliest age and at all stages of education. it is also important to create the right climate and framework for lifelong learning, as its potential is still not fully exploited in many member states.
in writing. first of all, i am pleased that the commission has taken up the european agenda for new skills and that it has focused on basic and transversal skills and on strengthening cooperation between educational institutions and the labour market, and on vocational training. basic skills: reading, writing, counting and reasoning, which have been studied for years by the pisa test for 15-year-olds, among others, show that more than 20% of young europeans do not reach a basic level of skill. most worryingly, this rate is more than twice as high in low socioeconomic status and immigrant families, where it exceeds 37% on average, but in some eu countries it is as high as 70%. this creates a vicious circle of poverty and exclusion, social ghettos, limited access to the labour market and further education for entire social groups, with half or more of the population trapped in a lifelong low-skill trap. i agree with the commission that there is also a need to develop transversal skills, such as foreign language skills, digital skills, at all levels and specialisations of education. we also need continuously updated skill sets for the labour market, defined and developed in students in close cooperation with the business environment. the announced review of the qualifications framework and the building of partnerships with employers and other labour market partners will therefore be crucial to the success of this initiative.

in writing. ‒ i am strongly in favour of the creation of a commission of inquiry on the panama papers and i believe that national egoisms must stop paralyzing international efforts to combat tax fraud and that information about who actually owns a company must stop being a secret. at the same time, i think that the discussion on this topic should also include an aspect of analysing the reasons for the popularity of so-called tax havens in recent decades. the growing bureaucracy, the constantly new laws and regulations, the successive financial burdens, including taxes, sometimes reaching up to 70% of income, cause many companies to decide to move their activities to other countries, not only to so-called tax havens, but simply to other countries with a lower level of bureaucracy and fiscalism. this is often compounded by irrational and inefficient spending of public money and widespread distribution, which discourages entrepreneurs from giving a significant part of their earnings to the state. on the one hand, they feel that they are paying too much tax, and on the other hand, that their money is being squandered by certain countries. there is no doubt that criminals must be prosecuted, but i believe that the causes of these unacceptable phenomena must be analysed in order to develop effective mechanisms to eliminate them. i believe, therefore, that the committee of inquiry will also look into these matters.
in writing. ‒ money laundering, tax evasion and non-compliance with eu administrative rules have negative economic consequences not only for the global economy but also for the economies of individual member states and their regions. i believe that this type of criminal activity leads to a slowdown in economic growth as a result of the increase in financial crime and thus to a reduction in the cost of crime. i am convinced that the establishment of a commission of inquiry to investigate the functioning of institutions operating in tax havens such as panama will help to significantly reduce the number of criminal activities. the commission, which will have 12 months to prepare its final report, will certainly be able to look more closely at the 'panama papers' and identify actions to prevent financial crime.
in writing. ‒ in december last year, the eu signed identical short-stay visa waiver agreements with the republic of palau, the kingdom of tonga and the republic of colombia. under the agreements, eu citizens will be able to stay in these countries without a visa for 90 days in any 180-day period, as will their eu counterparts. to benefit from the visa-free regime, eu citizens and nationals of signatory states must hold a valid passport: ordinary, diplomatic, service/office or special. however, the short-stay visa waiver does not apply to persons travelling for the purpose of gainful employment. the agreements are already provisionally applied after receiving the unanimous support of the schengen governments in the council, but their full conclusion requires the consent of the european parliament. the united kingdom and ireland will not participate in the agreement as their visa systems remain subject to national legislation. i personally see these agreements as a way of promoting people-to-people contacts in the countries concerned. they should provide trade opportunities in the face of increased tourist arrivals and help promote economic relations between the eu and these countries. i therefore did not oppose these agreements and voted in favour of their adoption.
in writing. ‒ the european union should support countries that are pursuing the path of democracy, freedom and respect for human rights through its actions. visa liberalisation not only enables tourism and investment to flourish, but also provides an opportunity to promote the values on which the european union is founded. as a global political actor, the eu should seek to strengthen economic and cultural links with the different regions of the world. i hope that this agreement will allow us to intensify our cooperation with the pacific countries, which is why i voted to abolish short-stay visas for the citizens of the republic of palau.

in writing. ‒ in may 2012, five countries (the us, japan, korea, taiwan and costa rica) together with the eu started negotiations to extend the ita product range. they were later joined by 21 other wto members. on 16 december 2015, at the wto ministerial conference in nairobi, 53 wto members reached agreement on a second information technology agreement, which includes a schedule for the removal of tariffs on 201 it products worth over usd 1,17 trillion per year. the agreement provides for the elimination of approximately 65% of tariff lines by 1 july 2016. the ita extension is the first major agreement on tariff reductions since the establishment of the wto. it also has a huge potential to create jobs and boost gdp growth. i am a strong supporter of the multilateral agreement under discussion, which is why i voted yes.
in writing. ‒ the expansion of trade in information technology products is the european union's response to global technological progress. the rules will help european producers of such products to access a growing market. moreover, the development of trade in advanced technologies is also a step towards developing the innovation capacity of the european economy and improving the situation of manufacturers of such solutions.
in writing. ‒ the agreement on the development of trade in information technology products (ita), signed in 1996, was undoubtedly a milestone in the liberalisation of trade in it products. however, after 20 years, it has had to adapt to the enormous technological changes that have taken place in recent times. by amending and extending the scope of this agreement, the new generation it products will also be able to benefit from the customs facilities. this is an important step for the world trade organisation and it is good that the european union has been the driving force behind this change. this will effectively protect european companies from unfair competition in the global system. by joining the agreement, the 54 signatory countries commit to phasing out tariffs on as many as 201 information technology products, such as video game consoles, gps navigation systems, magnetic resonance imaging devices, telecommunications satellites, touch screens and video cameras. the extension and extension of the ita is of enormous economic importance. according to the world trade organisation, its products account for around 7% of world trade, or eur 1,1 trillion. the european parliament's green light is a confirmation of the eu's commitment to the process of liberalising trade in these products.
in writing. ‒ the first agreement on trade in information technology products (itp) entered into force in 1997. it required the parties to eliminate and bind duties at zero rate for products such as computers, telephones, computer equipment, etc. its implementation has led to a revival of trade in these products and lower prices for consumers and producers. the current amendment to the agreement extends the list of products contained in the 1997 agreement. i assume that the expansion of ita to new products will further develop trade, increase industrial employment and increase gdp. the eu has an important role to play in supporting the development of new technologies, which is why i voted in favour of the ita.
in writing. ‒ i support the positive recommendation of the european parliament's international trade committee on the signing of the information technology agreement (ita) by the 29 wto member states at the 1996 ministerial conference in singapore and on the future conclusion, on behalf of the european union, of an agreement in the form of a declaration on the development of trade in information technology products (ita). it is a very important document which aims to bind and eliminate customs duties on an additional 201 it products. the elimination and zeroing of duties should apply to as many it products as possible. it is very good that products such as gps navigation systems, medical devices, telecommunication satellites and other high-tech products have been mentioned in this list. however, sensitive products must not be forgotten. the seven-year transitional period for the total elimination of duties on such products is reasonable. however, it is important that the conclusion of the agreement in question contributes to the economic development of the european union. according to the calculations presented by the experts, if all parties ratify the agreement, exports of goods from the union could increase by around 0.7% to 1.4% of its base value, which amounts to eur 1224 billion.
in writing. ‒ on 3 august 2015, the council requested a risk assessment of the use and manufacture of the new psychoactive substance α-pvp. according to the risk assessment, α-pvp is a potent psychostimulant substance and its use has resulted in a total of 115 deaths and 191 cases of acute poisoning in the eight member states where α-pvp has been detected. i believe that if α-pvp were to become widely available and used, the consequences for individual and public health could be significant. on the basis of the findings of the risk assessment report, the commission concluded that there are grounds for imposing control measures on α-pvp across the union. i fully agree with the commission's conclusions and therefore support this report.

in writing. ‒ the new psychoactive substance α-pvp is a potent psychostimulant. despite the very limited information and studies available, it can be concluded that this substance poses a serious risk to human health and life. in the eight member states where α-pvp was detected, a total of 115 deaths and 191 cases of acute poisoning were reported. cooperation between eu countries can help fight the new drug and facilitate judicial cooperation. the overriding objective is to protect against the risks that may arise from the availability and use of this substance, which is why i voted in favour of subjecting α-pvp to control measures.
in writing. ‒ the 2010 sns convention applies to claims for damage arising from the carriage of sns by sea, except for claims arising from a contract of carriage of goods or passengers, and establishes the strict liability of the ship-owner for any damage arising in connection with the carriage of sns. the convention also introduces a new system of liability and compensation that not only covers damage caused by pollution from ships but also takes account of the risk of fire and explosion, including loss of life or personal injury and loss of or damage to property. importantly, the convention establishes a special compensation fund to compensate any person who has suffered damage in connection with the transport of sns by sea, insofar as such person has not been able to obtain full and sufficient compensation for the damage from the shipowner and his insurer. the convention also contains provisions on the jurisdiction of the courts of the states parties in respect of claims by persons who have suffered damage (as defined in the convention) against the owner or his insurer or against the sns fund. unfortunately, there were some points in the document that raised my doubts, so i abstained.
in writing. ‒ the states parties to the international convention are those which sign the protocol in their own name and not on behalf of the union. it is not the european parliament's responsibility to give them the power to do so, and that is why i abstained. my doubts do not concern the risk assessment of dangerous goods being transported, because i have a precise and firm opinion on this matter.
in writing. ‒ the main objective of the sns convention is to enable international cooperation to protect the marine environment from harmful and hazardous substances. the implementation of its provisions is in the interest of both the maritime economy (and tourism) and the people living in the coastal zone, as their losses and gains from pollution will be compensated. it is estimated that the convention will not lead to an additional burden on member states' budgets, but will change the responsibilities of the national maritime administration. the convention will also affect shipowners, who will have to take out insurance contracts, and recipients of dangerous and harmful cargo, who will be obliged to pay contributions to the sns fund. the sns convention has the potential to ensure the uniform application of the rules on liability and compensation in respect of accidents caused by ships carrying sns and, through the establishment of a fund, should ensure that sufficient funds are available to compensate victims of such accidents. however, there is a risk that the shipping sector will be subject to two different systems at once, one eu and the other international, which could result in unequal treatment of pollution victims. i hereby abstain from voting.

in writing. ‒ the rapporteur clearly states that harmonisation of european tax systems is the only way to achieve a well-functioning single market. in this spirit, it recommends that the commission submit as soon as possible a proposal for a common corporate tax base and that the council adopt it without delay. the report also proposes a number of stricter rules on efforts to combat tax base erosion, which in practice could harm the eu's global competitiveness and harm companies that invest and pay taxes fairly. this is the case, for example, of a provision which lowers the threshold for deducting interest, at a time when tax avoidance in multinational companies is most often intra-group. the report also suggests that the european parliament should be the appropriate monitoring body for the implementation of this tax avoidance directive and the member states should be accountable to it, which is something that, given the treaty's division of powers, sovereign governments cannot accept under any circumstances. i believe that the proposals in the report are very much interfering not only with the competence of the member states but also with the common rules being developed by the oecd. i therefore voted against.
in writing. ‒ the european parliament has endorsed new rules proposed by the european commission to tackle certain tax avoidance practices. oecd research shows that aggressive tax planning by multinational companies results in annual losses to national budgets of between usd 100 and 240 billion, or between 4% and 10% of global corporate tax revenues. such loss of income reduces the capacity of countries to invest and, consequently, does not contribute to employment and poverty reduction. the overarching objective of this report is to get companies to pay taxes where they generate profits. the commission is also proposing to introduce a tax on unrealised capital gains for multinational companies that transfer their profits to low-tax countries. there will also be strict limits on tax breaks and greater transparency for trusts and foundations. in conclusion, the rules introduced are a good step towards limiting the erosion of the tax base. a coordinated approach to taxation is essential to ensure the proper functioning of the single market and of the union's capital markets.
in writing. ‒ the report calls for the deductibility of interest to be limited to 20% or eur 2 000 000 (ec proposal: 30%) and furthermore limits the period during which deductions can be made to five years (no limit in the ec proposal). this item is not proportionate and risks hitting companies that apply for a loan for legitimate commercial use to make an investment. furthermore, the large variation in interest rates between eu member states is completely ignored. it also suggests that the so-called 'switch-over' clause (which does not exist in the oecd proposal) is also applicable within the eu. the commission proposes to refuse this exemption if foreign income is taxed at a rate lower than 40% of the national rate, which raises problems with the interpretation of bilateral double taxation agreements. i could not support the report.
in writing. ‒ i support all measures to ensure fair and effective taxation of businesses. according to an oecd study, aggressive tax planning by multinational corporations costs the national budgets worldwide between $100 billion and $240 billion annually. companies should pay taxes where they make their profits. however, i cannot agree to the unification of the tax systems of the member states of the european union. this area should be reserved exclusively for the prerogatives of national governments. they should take such tax policy measures as they deem appropriate. centralization of taxation powers can cause economic problems and hinder competition, which is beneficial for the average eu citizen. i therefore voted against.
in writing. ‒ i agree with the idea of fighting tax avoidance, but i voted against it because i believe that the ideas in the bayet report not only interfere too much with the competences of the member states and the common rules developed by the oecd, but also disproportionate to companies paying taxes honestly in the eu. the report clearly states that the harmonisation of european tax systems is the only way to achieve a well-functioning single market. in this spirit, the rapporteur recommends that the commission submit a proposal for a common corporate tax base as soon as possible and that the council adopt it without delay. in addition, the report proposes a number of stricter rules on work to counter tax base erosion that in practice could harm the eu's global competitiveness and harm companies that invest and pay taxes honestly, such as a provision lowering the threshold for deductions from interest, when most tax avoidance in multinational companies is intra-group. the report also suggests that the european parliament should be the appropriate monitoring body for the implementation of this directive on tax avoidance rules and that member states should be accountable to it, which is absolutely unacceptable for sovereign governments given the division of powers in the treaty. the report was adopted in committee by a very slim majority, indicating a lack of clear compromise on the part of this house.

in writing. ‒ chemicals with endocrine disrupting properties affect the endocrine system of animals and humans and provide a new way of assessing the toxicity of chemicals. there is now a scientific consensus in many areas, although there are differences of opinion in the scientific and regulatory communities around the world on specific issues. regulation (eu) no 528/2012 (the biocidal products regulation) provides that active substances recognised as having endocrine disrupting properties which may cause undesirable effects in humans are not to be approved, unless an exception set out in the regulation applies. i fully share the objectives of protecting human health and the environment and ensuring a high level of protection, but i do not support this resolution and question the validity of the arbitrary deadline for setting these criteria. in my view, this resolution has some added value, since the commission has already accepted the judgment and publicly committed itself to speeding up the adoption of the criteria. indeed, the parliament's legal service has admitted that further legal action will be pointless as their subject matter will be unjustified after the criteria are published in june. in view of the above, i voted in favour of the resolution.
in writing. ‒ the court of justice of the european union ruled in a judgment of 16 december 2015 that the commission had infringed eu law by not taking action to adopt delegated acts establishing scientific criteria for the determination of endocrine disrupting properties. the commission now has a clear, specific and unconditional obligation to adopt delegated acts. in this context, it should be borne in mind that the commission's work should be guided by the right proportions and a fair assessment of the risks to the health of citizens. only in this way will it be possible to maintain the highest safety standards, while promoting the competitiveness of the european agricultural market and other sectors at risk of negative consequences of the selection of inappropriate criteria for the determination of endocrine disrupting properties. eu standards must address cases where chemicals pose a real, rather than a theoretical, risk. i therefore strongly supported parliament's report on this matter.
in writing. ‒ the european commission has failed to fulfil its institutional obligations regarding the implementation of the judgment of the court of justice of the european union of 16.09.2015 (under article 266 of the treaty on the functioning of the european union). it should as soon as possible define scientific criteria for properties that may interfere with the functioning of growth hormone. a situation in which the eu institution fails to fulfil its obligations under the treaties is very dangerous. the european parliament calls on the commission to fulfil its obligations.

in writing. ‒ i voted against a resolution calling on the european commission to withdraw the draft implementing decision authorising the placing on the market of a genetically modified carnation. the resolution was prompted by concerns about the effects of using this ornamental plant in the catering industry, which cannot be excluded, and the environmental effects of marketing by composting waste after use of the product. in view of the potential, unrecognised or unconfirmed risks that the use of gmos may pose to the environment and to human consumption, i believe that adequate control and quality control of the production and use of products, as well as clear labelling of products so that consumers have full and fair information about the product, are better than a ban on marketing. prohibitions are easily circumvented and, with the obvious benefits of using gmos, there is a risk that the production and sale of genetically engineered agricultural products will be moved into a grey area, which would remove this production from the scrutiny and visibility of the market and thus create much more real risks to human health and the environment.

member of the commission. – mr president, freedom of movement gives millions of people in the european union unprecedented opportunities. cross-border personal and business relationships are thriving: 14 million citizens – and we already had this figure here from ms delvaux – reside in a member state other than their member state of origin; 13% of all marriages in the union are international; and 50% of smes are engaged in cross-border activities. i expect these numbers to continue rising. this proposal will make the life of millions of citizens and businesses easier by removing unnecessary and costly red tape. here we are: after three years of intense negotiations, with your vote tomorrow the union is about to take another important step. it might not make it to the front pages of the magazines, but many people will breathe a sigh of relief once this regulation enters into force. today, when people move to another eu country and they want to register a birth, get married, register a house, or apply for a residence card, the national authorities will ask for certified copies, certified translations and rubber stamps such as the apostille. this is time-consuming, costly, and perfectly unnecessary. this is now over for a whole range of life situations and corresponding documents. based on the principle of mutual trust, the regulation does away with the requirement to authenticate public documents with an apostille and simplifies obligations with regard to certified copies and translations. it also introduces multilingual standard forms to avoid translation requirements and reinforces the fight against false documents by setting up a system of cooperation between member states. parliament has been a strong supporter of this regulation from the start. i would like to pay tribute to mr rapkay, who gathered a solid majority in first reading under the previous legislature, and wish to thank ms delvaux and the shadow rapporteurs who skilfully negotiated the final compromise with the council. it was not easy; and we have a balanced compromise. the regulation covers several areas of immediate relevance to most citizens, in particular their civil status. we would all have preferred a broader scope of the regulation, covering additional areas for citizens as well as documents useful to businesses. it is thanks to parliament’s determination that the regulation provides for an early review of its scope. this early review will allow the commission to consider the inclusion in the scope of additional areas such as educational records, disabilities, and the legal status and representation of companies. parliament has also ensured that the fee that member states may charge to citizens for obtaining a multilingual standard form will be reasonable, and that member states will inform citizens of their rights under the regulation through their websites and also in individual contacts.
on behalf of the s&d group. several million eu citizens study or work outside their home country, exercising their right to free movement. each year, several hundred thousand official documents need to be legalised or certified in order to be recognised in countries other than those in which they were issued. in this context, simplification of formalities for citizens moving abroad is a very important issue. the introduction of standard multilingual forms for most of the documents covered by the regulation including residence, citizenship, civil status and criminal records will avoid costly translations and thus contribute to simplifying the procedures that union citizens have to complete when moving to other member states. i am pleased that the regulation contains review clauses providing for the extension of administrative facilities in the future. this is particularly important given that school diplomas and certificates, certificates of disability and many other documents relating to businesses are not covered by this regulation. the new rules will greatly facilitate the free movement of union citizens, who will be able to benefit from the new procedures as from 2019. finally, i would like to congratulate the rapporteur on the good compromise that has been reached.

in writing. millions of eu citizens study, work or live in a country of which they are not a national. however, in exercising their right to free movement, they often encounter administrative difficulties when submitting various official documents. many countries continue to recognise only their own documents or those of another country if they are notarized. work to abolish the requirement to legalise documents in this way and to reduce administrative formalities is therefore important. the principle should be adopted in the union that documents duly issued in one country are also valid in the other countries of the union. in order to prevent the falsification of documents and to confirm their authenticity, it should be provided that the administrative authority receiving a document may directly request, by electronic means, the authenticity of the document from the administrative authority issuing the document. the widespread use of this practice would make it easier for millions of eu citizens to move, study and work. i therefore consider the work on a regulation of the european parliament and of the council on facilitating the free movement of citizens by simplifying administrative requirements to be important and i expect that it will not be prolonged.
rapporteur for the opinion of the committee on constitutional affairs. – mr president, following the entry into force of the lisbon treaty, for the first time any modification of the statute of the general court has to be adopted in accordance with the ordinary legislative procedure. the proposal which we are addressing today meets the immediate efficiency and performance-related needs of the general court, and going beyond it seeks to strengthen the effectiveness of the european court system as a whole in a sustainable manner. i trust that its adoption will contribute to reducing the length of proceedings before the general court, and this in turn will reduce the risk that the union is found in breach of its duty, set out in article 47 of the charter of fundamental rights, to rule on cases within a reasonable time. furthermore, only one jurisdiction – the court of justice will be responsible for ensuring uniform interpretation of the law by hearing all appeals. this will simplify the judicial structure of the union, enhance its overall efficiency and promote consistency in its case law. it is therefore important that the european parliament support the current proposal in order to allow the european court system to work in a more efficient manner.
on behalf of the ppe group. mr president, i would like to thank you for your kind words. we are now close to the second stage of the reform of the court of justice of the european union. we had a political debate last year about the need for this reform. at the moment, this is just a consequence of our actions, a necessary consequence, which is to include the civil service tribunal in the court of first instance. the seven judges who have served on the civil service tribunal so far are judges who will not be new to the court of justice; they will be among the existing judges and therefore this change does not generate any additional costs but enormous benefits. i would like to draw your attention to the fact that until now the civil service tribunal judges have dealt exclusively with staff cases. no other matters could be entrusted to them, although these judges were often left without assigned cases to deal with. the change we are making, the second part of the reform, will allow firstly the transfer of labour cases to the court of first instance - so they are safe and will continue to be dealt with properly - and secondly the allocation of other cases to judges who will not be dealing with labour cases at that time, which has been impossible so far. this reform is obviously necessary because, as mrs danuta hübner said, it is important for the quality of the european judiciary. i therefore ask the court itself and the other institutions to remember that this is an important institution for all of us, that this reform will be assessed in the coming years because it has many opponents. i hope, therefore, that the review clause in the regulation will force everyone to make a proper assessment of the court's performance in the coming years, so that in a few years we can say whether we have made the right choices, whether we have made the right decisions or whether we may have been wrong. i think we're right.
mr. chairman, please! the absorption of the civil service tribunal by the european court of justice, one of its institutions, is, as mentioned in this debate, a fulfilment of the previous assumptions. but i would like to say that even this very brief discussion which has been going on for a dozen or so minutes here calls for a fresh look at the way in which this reform is to be implemented. there were very important arguments against this project, this reform. from within the court of justice - and therefore the judges themselves have serious doubts - there has been a question of costs. finally, all this should be placed in the context of the debate on the efficiency of the european court of justice, its accessibility and the openness and effectiveness of its decisions. frankly, after hearing the voices of colleagues from a wide variety of political parties, i would urge that we reconsider this reform before we take a decision in the vote. this is too delicate a matter to be rushed, and in this matter consensus, broad agreement is particularly needed.
in writing. this regulation follows the third regulation reforming the court of justice, which concerned the increase of the number of judges at the general court to 56, so that each member state could nominate two judges. this change was conditional on the civil service tribunal being wound up and its disputes returned to the general court, which is the subject of this report. the reform of the judicial system of the court of justice of the eu has been divided into three distinct stages. the first phase of the competition has 12 nominees. in the second seven judges will be transferred from the dissolved civil service tribunal, bringing the total number of members of the general court to 47 as of 1 september 2016. the third stage will be the appointment of nine additional judges in 2019. in conclusion, the procedure for the gradual increase of the number of judges of the general court will be completed in 2019, when the court of justice will consist of two judges from each member state, including seven judges from the dissolved european union civil service tribunal, who will join the general court as of 1 september 2016.

in writing. ‒ the main objective of the regulation is to abolish the legalisation and apostille requirement for official documents falling within its scope. a number of simplifications have been made with regard to certified copies and certified translations. the compromise text provides that the regulation should apply only to certain official documents, in particular those relating to civil status (e.g. birth, death, marriage, divorce, parenting, adoption) and certain other documents that citizens often need, such as residence, nationality and criminal records. however, given the doubts surrounding the regulation, i have decided to vote against it.
in writing. ‒ freedom of movement for persons is one of the key rights of eu citizenship. despite the fact that this right is firmly entrenched in eu law, many eu citizens who study, live, work or do business in another country encounter obstacles in their daily lives that make it difficult for them to exercise this right. the administrative formalities involved in authenticating in one member state official documents issued in another eu country are among the most frequently mentioned problems. the regulation identifies 13 categories of official documents, including birth, death, marriage, divorce and non-enrolment in the criminal register, which will be exempt from any form of legalisation. copies thereof certified as authentic shall also be accepted in all member states. multilingual standard forms will also be introduced to facilitate the translation of documents. the regulation of the ep and the council is an important step towards reducing costs, shortening the legalization process, while maintaining legal certainty. it is a response to the expectations of europeans to make their daily lives and contacts with the authorities of the member states easier.

in writing. ‒ this regulation is the fourth in a series on the reform of the court of justice, which aims to increase the number of judges at the court of justice to 56 in order to allow each member state to nominate two judges. the increase in the number of judges was made conditional on the abolition of the civil service tribunal and the referral of civil service disputes back to the tribunal. the number of judges of the general court at this stage of the reform will be increased by 7 judges of the civil service tribunal and will eventually reach 47. in his draft report, the rapporteur endorses the court of justice's proposal, proposing only a few minor technical changes, which concern:• the rules for referral of cases to the civil service tribunal;• changes to the court's rules of procedure and its internal organisation. i support the reform of the court of justice to make the european judiciary more efficient, but not by doubling the number of judges. i therefore abstained.

on behalf of the ppe group. – madam president, this first fisheries management plan under the new common fisheries policy (cfp) was hard fought and was the result of very difficult, long negotiations, in which parliament had to make many concessions. we did it in the trust that the provisions included would be enough to uphold sustainable fisheries in the baltic sea. this new plan must be put into action as soon as possible for setting total allowable catches (tacs) and quotas for the year 2017. it is crucial that the eu institutions act responsibly and show, now, that commitment to the principles is still alive. parliament has shown its commitment to sustainable fishing in the eu and to the future of the industry, and i must ask the commission and the council to do the same. that is why i have two questions: will the proposals from the commission for next year’s total allowable catch in the baltic be based on the scientific advice and the rules established in this new management plan; and is there any scenario where this new management plan and the rules within it to settle catches could not be used? it is crucial to use the new rules immediately, as the scientific advice regarding the western cod stock is very alarming. the stock has been under too much stress for a very long time, and so far the council has failed to follow the scientific advice. the results of this failure have now led to a piece of advice from the scientists more or less closing this fishery. luckily, the new baltic management plan has some new rules in place and safeguards to deal with such situations. after 10 months of difficult negotiations with the council and the commission, these negotiations gave us a plan that upholds and respects the objectives of the basic regulations. in the end, this plan will ensure that fishing activities in the baltic are conducted in a sustainable, reasonable and economically viable way, which will not put unnecessary strain on the environment – and now we will closely monitor the implementation of the plan.
on behalf of the ecr group. - madam president! - i have to go. the multiannual plan for the management of cod, herring and sprat stocks is a key document for the future of over 94% of the fish stocks caught in the region. it is the first multiannual plan in the european union to be based on the new common fisheries policy. the main good news is the so-called multi-species management, which takes into account the interactions between different species of fish. that's very good. we all know that there is an urgent need for the biological recovery of the baltic sea and that the current system must be effective. management must be sustainable and based on sound scientific knowledge. here are a few of my comments: the need for a regional approach in the formulation of the implementing rules for the plan should be taken into account, the area should be closed to fishing in order to protect spawning grounds and habitats based on up-to-date scientific knowledge, and the sources of funding should be identified in the event of temporary cessation of fishing, if such protective measures are applicable; fourth, so-called forage, i.e. industrial, catches should be clearly limited, and fifth, at least in poland, if wind farms are to be built in the baltic, this cannot be done in the best fishing grounds and spawning grounds and fish distribution areas. thank you, sir. i would like to congratulate you on a generally very good report.
in writing. cod, herring and sprat are the main species caught in the wild and are essential elements of the baltic sea ecosystem. scientific research shows that there are strong biological interactions between them. that's why i'm advocating a more flexible approach to resources. poland has for several years advocated the need for a multi-stage baltic sea management plan. as cod fishing has an impact on flatfish stocks, i believe it is appropriate to include in the plan the possibility of responding to the deterioration of flatfish stocks. the signals from the fishing community are alarming, and the cod situation is particularly dire. the feed stocks are extremely damaging here. i therefore particularly criticise the provisions of article 13, which leave too wide a tolerance for large-scale pelagic fisheries, including industrial fisheries. it is necessary to increase their transparency and to take action to minimise their impact on the baltic marine environment. the commission must take into account the joint recommendations of the baltic sea states. the commission's actions must be consistent with the provisions of regulation (eu) no 1380/2013 on the cap and with the results of the work of the interinstitutional working group on long-term plans. the scope of the commission's power to adopt delegated acts with the treaty division of competences in the eu and the provisions on regionalisation contained in regulation (eu) no 1380/2013 should be subject to legal and substantive analysis.
