in writing. the high mobility of eu citizens means that they are much more likely to marry in other member states with people from another country than their own. the commission identified the lack of certainty about the property rights of international couples as one of the main obstacles that eu citizens continue to face in their daily lives when they want to exercise their rights outside their own country. the main purpose of this proposal is to establish a clear legal framework in the union governing the conditions for determining the court having jurisdiction to hear disputes between international couples, the law governing property relations and to facilitate the movement of judgments and authentic instruments between member states. in conclusion, this regulation, covering jurisdiction and applicable law and the recognition and enforcement of judgments in matrimonial property regimes, will be a useful instrument to put an end to the many misunderstandings and legal difficulties that international couples may encounter.
in writing. no breakup is easy. whatever the cause, it's a kind of personal failure. deciding to get a divorce is just the first step. later, when the property is divided, there are huge legal problems, especially for international couples. both regulations seek to remedy this situation by laying down rules on jurisdiction and the recognition and enforcement of judgments in matters of division of property. and, frankly, it doesn't matter if they're heterosexual couples or not. everyone has a right to access justice. these regulations do not introduce by the back door the recognition of one or another definition of marriage or the institution of partnership. the only possible consequence is the enforcement of a judgment given in one member state in the territory of another member state. and that is also covered by the public policy clause. i therefore feel sorry for the citizens of those member states which have not joined enhanced cooperation, such as poland. they will be worse off, they will not be able to benefit from a clear set of rules, which will make legal proceedings longer and more costly.
the rapporteur. - madam president! - i have to go. in preparing this report, we consulted the commission's directorate-general for education and culture, european associations representing the various bodies involved in the education process, national organisations, including those operating at local level. we also consulted with the ministries of education in several countries. i have also tried to include in this report the results of evaluations commissioned by the european commission and various position papers published by the organisations. therefore, in order to avoid this report being an all-inclusive one, i decided to focus on three main points. as you'll notice, this report has three parts. one concerns some proposals on how to organise this framework for cooperation in the field of education. the second part concerns the quality of education and training. and finally, the third is a very topical but also, i will not hide it, a few words on this controversial topic: migration and education and training. i would like to highlight just a few points which i think are very important in this report and which deserve to be highlighted. they're particularly important to me. first, we focus on the role of the family in education. this seems to be a given, but a given that is often forgotten today, is that all of these data show the importance of the home environment for the development of a child's basic skills, and then the communication between school and parents, which is also important in such things as shaping civic attitudes and preventing radicalization. the other aspect that is being discussed is the community-based approach to education, which emphasises the importance of all local organisations and actors. unfortunately, it didn't pass a compromise amendment that we wanted to include religious organizations, local non-governmental organizations. and once again, we have emphasized the role of parents, their responsibilities and the need to ensure that they have an impact on the education of their children. this is important because the working groups that have already been set up do not yet include members of european organisations representing parents. finally, it is another aspect to acknowledge any successes of european policies in this respect, such as the bologna process, the student mobility programme or the teaching staff. i wanted to draw attention in this report - and this view was also shared by the counter-rapporteurs - to certain weaknesses of the process, namely the feeling in the academic community of ignoring the objections of academic teachers related to the bologna process. we therefore recommend that the university community be more involved in the et 2020 work cycle. more flexibility is needed in the use of modules or ect points and, most importantly, mobility outcomes should also be based on qualitative indicators, not just quantitative ones. and finally, the issue of migrants. i'm very brief on that, too. we focus on immigrants from outside europe, but all the data shows that the children of intra-european migrants also have great difficulty in adapting to society, and here education systems play a huge role. we also call for the inclusion of teachers of migrant origin in the education system, of course in exchange of experience, but also for the help of migrants, also intra-european, in adjusting to the requirements and standards of teaching in the host country. thank you very much, madam chair. i'm waiting to hear from my colleagues.

in writing. the optimal solution for wind power plants is to work flexibly with high-efficiency gas turbines (not to be confused with gas boilers). this combination on a macro scale, i.e. for large power grids, may soon be the basis for the most promising and efficient power generation systems in the world. this solution requires more gas supplies to the eu market, and while it significantly reduces co2 emissions, it does not eliminate them. unfortunately, clean technology, which involves storing large amounts of electricity, is still not very efficient. an alternative to large networks is small, prosumer installations, which are mainly for local use. however, there is insufficient progress in the better use of renewable energy sources in stand-alone heating and cooling systems. more intensive development of the daytime heat storage technology and suitable designs, as well as of 'free cooling' installations that would be available on the market, is needed. the potential of geothermal energy and heat pumps is huge, but i believe it is under-exploited and requires more intensive research to reduce the costs of these technologies. it requires that consumers have access to the market for appropriate equipment and apparatus.

in writing. eu greenhouse gas emissions decreased by 23% between 1990 and 2014. at the same time, eu gdp grew by 46%. with less and less of a burden on the climate, businesses and citizens achieve greater economic growth, create more jobs and generate more tax revenue. the european union is on track to meet its 2020 target of 20% less co2 emissions. this shows that there is no need for a drastic tightening of climate policy, which is proving to be an obstacle to the eu's reindustrialisation. it is therefore worth recalling that the eu has assumed that by 2020 the industry's share of eu gdp should be 20%. the bureaucratic reporting of energy and the high energy prices for medium-sized businesses and private households are a cause for concern. the energy efficiency directive should play a key role in eu energy policy. however, it should be noted that the european union has achieved its 20% efficiency target by 2020, even without full implementation of the directive in most member states. this shows the strength of the market and the ability of member states to shape their own energy policies. the european union should not be tempted to promote climate and energy policy at the expense of industrial policy.

in writing. ‒ the proposal aims to transpose into union law the measures contained in the multiannual recovery plan for bluefin tuna in the eastern atlantic and mediterranean, adopted by the international commission for the conservation of atlantic tunas (iccat) at its annual meetings in 2012 and 2014. the multiannual recovery plan for bluefin tuna was established in 2006 and entered into force in 2007. in order to ensure a uniform and effective application throughout the eu of all measures contained in the recovery plan adopted in 2012-2014, this proposal will incorporate them into the regulation on the multiannual recovery plan for bluefin tuna in the eastern atlantic and mediterranean. the proposal includes technical measures such as rules governing the use of stereoscopic cameras to estimate the number of bluefin tuna and the number of bluefin tuna released, rules on live bluefin tuna transfer operations and caging, as well as requirements for the implementation of the iccat regional observer programme and catch reports. i support these resolutions. i voted yes.

in writing. ‒ the proposal aims to transpose into union law the measures contained in the multiannual recovery plan for bluefin tuna in the eastern atlantic and mediterranean, adopted by the international commission for the conservation of atlantic tunas (iccat) at its annual meetings in 2012 and 2014. the multiannual recovery plan for bluefin tuna was established in 2006 and entered into force in 2007. iccat is the regional fisheries management organisation responsible for the management of tuna and tuna-like species in the atlantic ocean and adjacent seas to which the union is a contracting party. in order to ensure a uniform and effective application throughout the eu of all measures contained in the recovery plan adopted in 2012-2014, this proposal will incorporate them into the regulation on the multiannual recovery plan for bluefin tuna in the eastern atlantic and mediterranean. the proposal includes technical measures such as rules governing the use of stereoscopic cameras to estimate the number of bluefin tuna and the number of bluefin tuna released, rules on live bluefin tuna transfer operations and caging, as well as requirements for the implementation of the iccat regional observer programme and catch reports. i hereby endorse the report.
in writing. ‒ the international commission for the conservation of atlantic tunas (iccat) adopted a multiannual plan for the recovery of bluefin tuna in the eastern atlantic and mediterranean at its 2012 and 2014 meetings. the resolution aims to ensure the uniform application of the plan throughout the european union. the commission has already taken steps to ensure that the fishing opportunities for bluefin tuna are not reduced.
in writing. ‒ the main premise of the commission's conclusion that a multi-faceted management plan for the baltic sea is needed is correct. a multi-species approach is more effective than species-specific management. the plan should ensure the sustainable exploitation of those resources and the stability of fishing opportunities and thus the stability of the livelihood of fishermen. at the same time, this management is based on the most up-to-date scientific advice on the status of the stocks covered by the plan, interactions between species and other aspects related to the ecosystem and fisheries. it should also be noted that the plan is the first of its kind in the highly sensitive baltic sea ecosystem. in fact, it can be seen as a 'production in progress' as researchers are working on more advanced multi-species approaches which may be necessary to include in the plan at a later stage. it is therefore important that the first review is carried out relatively early, especially as the multi-level management plan is a new and evolving concept. i believe that the first review of the plan should take place three years after its entry into force and if the plan has positive effects, it should be reviewed after five years. this will also provide the desired flexibility in the implementation of the plan. in view of the above and its consequences for the baltic sea ecosystem, i voted in favour of the proposal.
in writing. ‒ proposal for a regulation of the european parliament and of the council establishing a multiannual plan for the stocks of cod, herring and sprat in the baltic sea and the fisheries exploiting those stocks, amending council regulation (ec) no 2187/2005 and repealing council regulation (ec) no 1098/2007. i support the creation of a multi-species management framework for cod, herring and sprat in the baltic sea, where these three species are mainly fished. the multiannual plan for the stocks of cod, herring and sprat in the baltic sea and the fisheries exploiting these resources was published by the european commission as early as 2014. multi-species management for the baltic sea seems to be a more effective plan than managing each of these fish species separately. the proposed plan will ensure the sustainable exploitation of cod, herring and sprat stocks in the baltic sea, which will directly translate into a stable livelihood for fishermen.
in writing. ‒ the main premise of the commission's conclusion that a multi-faceted management plan for the baltic sea is needed is correct. a multi-species approach is more effective than species-specific management. the plan should ensure the sustainable exploitation of those resources and the stability of fishing opportunities and thus the stability of the livelihood of fishermen. at the same time, this management is based on the most up-to-date scientific advice on the status of the stocks covered by the plan, interactions between species and other aspects related to the ecosystem and fisheries. the plan is the first of its kind in the highly sensitive baltic sea ecosystem. in fact, it can be seen as a 'production in progress' as researchers are working on more advanced multi-species approaches which may be necessary to include in the plan at a later stage. it is therefore important that the first review is carried out relatively early, especially as the multi-level management plan is a new and evolving concept. the first review of the plan should take place three years after its entry into force and, if the plan has a positive impact, it should be reviewed after five years. this will also provide the much-needed flexibility in the implementation of the plan. i hereby endorse the report.
in writing. ‒ the european union's multiannual plan for cod, herring and sprat is the first plan under the new eu fisheries policy to take account of interspecies interactions. until now, the union has managed individual species that could have led to their extinction in order to protect the stocks from overfishing. this approach did not take into account that cod prey on herring and sprats, and that sprats feed on cod eggs. in practice, this means that the size of cod shoals affects the size of herring shoals and sprats, and vice versa. the basic principle of the new management plan, which takes account of interspecies dependencies, is to establish ranges within which the council can set fishing limits and catch quotas. management is to be based on the most up-to-date scientific data on the state of fish stocks, interactions between species and any other aspects of the ecosystem and fisheries. the new law is designed to ensure balanced and sustainable exploitation of the resources and to guarantee stable fishing opportunities and livelihoods for fishermen. this could significantly improve the situation of polish fishermen, among others. the plan will also ensure that fishing activities in the baltic are sustainable, sensible and, above all, economically viable, without imposing too much pressure on the environment. for these reasons, i have decided to vote in favour of its adoption.
in writing. ‒ cod, herring and sprat are the main species caught in the baltic sea, accounting for nearly 94% of all catches. it is therefore vital to develop a new fisheries management programme that is relevant to today's challenges. the previous plan, dating from 2008, is not adapted to the current situation and did not include herring and cod. a new and comprehensive baltic sea fisheries management plan covering all species should be developed. this resolution is a response to the challenges of our time, which is why i voted in favour of it.
in writing. ‒ the purpose of the regulation is to establish a clear legal framework in the eu for the determination of jurisdiction, the applicable law, and the recognition and enforcement of judgments in matrimonial matters and property matters. they do not cover matters relating to the capacity of the spouses, the existence, validity or recognition of the marriage, maintenance obligations and succession. the main controversy with this package is that the decision authorising enhanced cooperation obliges member states to commit to two instruments simultaneously - one on partnerships and the other on marriages. a number of member states still do not have a partnership institution (italy, bulgaria, romania, slovakia, poland, lithuania, latvia) and in order to have the effect of the matrimonial property regulation, they must accede to both regulations implementing enhanced cooperation and agree to recognise the effects of a partnership institution which they do not recognise under their national law and which may be considered contrary to their public policy (e.g. the principle of the protection of marriage and the family). because of the controversy, i voted against it.
in writing. ‒ the proposal aims to establish a clear legal framework in the eu for the determination of jurisdiction, applicable law, recognition and enforcement of judgments in matrimonial matters and property matters. they do not cover matters relating to the capacity of the spouses, the existence, validity or recognition of the marriage, maintenance obligations and succession. within the framework of the regulation, mutual recognition of administrative documents must not be contrary to the principle of subsidiarity. this regulation may not impose on member states the harmonisation of their national family law, including matrimonial property regimes. this solution raises concerns in the context of article 4 (2) teu, which guarantees member states respect for their national identities, in particular as regards the definition of the institutions of family law whose effects member states wish to recognise under their legal systems. i could not support the report.

in writing. ‒ the aim of the proposal is to establish a clear legal framework in the eu for the determination of jurisdiction, applicable law, recognition and enforcement of decisions on the property consequences of registered partnerships. the european parliament, at its vote at its strasbourg session on 9 june 2016, gave its consent to the decision on enhanced cooperation in the area of matrimonial property regimes and the property consequences of registered partnerships. the main controversy is that the decision authorising enhanced cooperation requires the member states to be bound by two instruments at the same time, one on partnerships and the other on marriage. a number of member states do not recognise the institution of a partnership and their effect under the matrimonial property regime requires accession to both the enhanced cooperation regulations and consent to recognise the effects of an institution of a partnership which they do not recognise under their national law and which may be considered contrary to their public policy. i could not support the report.

in writing. ‒ agriculture is a special sector, not only because of its strategic importance in producing and delivering food to the market, but also because it is a very important supplier of raw materials to industry and, increasingly, to the energy sector. this issue is of particular importance in the context of the union's efforts to reduce its energy dependence, which is 50% imported. the eu is now the world's largest energy importer, with energy-related expenditure of around eur 400 billion per year. moreover, in the context of climate challenges, agriculture and forestry are sectors with a huge natural potential to capture co2 from the air, in addition to carbon dioxide emissions from production processes, which should be taken into account when making the relevant conversions. it is therefore worth encouraging research and innovation in the development of bioenergy installations and avoiding excessive administrative burdens and difficulties that would hamper the development of this sector, which also has significant potential for creating new jobs. the possibility of selling surplus energy to the electricity grid and designing a system that would buy energy from such sources in the first place could be of great importance for the development of rural areas now and in the future. a stable mechanism for individual energy producers providing price predictability in the longer term is also likely to be necessary for the proper development of the sector of such energy.

in writing. ‒ improving energy efficiency by 20% by 2020 is one of the eu's key energy policy objectives. action in this area is important because of the economic cost of energy production, environmental and trade issues (half of the eu's energy needs come from imports). developing energy efficiency schemes stimulates the search for new and innovative solutions, which in turn stimulates the european labour market and brings climate and environmental benefits. one area where efficiency gains are particularly important is the housing sector. this requires investments to modernise existing buildings and incentives to increase energy savings in heating and cooling systems. in the longer term, these changes also lead to better and more efficient resource management, which also translates into real savings. improving energy efficiency should provide an attractive opportunity for small and medium-sized enterprises to increase their competitiveness by reducing their expenditure on different energy sources. in a social context, better use of energy resources and the provision of energy at reasonable prices are key elements in the fight against energy poverty in the eu. however, it should be borne in mind that energy efficiency improvements are intended to reduce energy consumption while maintaining living and productive standards, and are not intended to be a pretext for wasting energy.

in writing. ‒ peru has recorded economic growth of over 80% in the last 10 years, placing it among the 10 fastest growing countries in the world in terms of trade. moreover, the eu remains the largest investor in peru, which underlines the importance of this agreement in the context of further promoting this type of market opportunities. in march this year, the eu concluded an agreement with the republic of peru on the short-stay visa waiver. this new visa system allows union citizens to travel without a visa to peru and peruvian citizens to travel without a visa to the eu for a maximum of 90 days in any 180-day period. citizens of the union and peru shall be required to hold a valid ordinary, diplomatic, service, official or special passport in order to travel under the visa waiver. however, the short-stay visa waiver does not apply to persons travelling for the purpose of gainful employment. the agreement is already in force on a provisional basis, having received the unanimous support of the schengen governments in the council, but its final conclusion requires the prior consent of the european parliament. the provisions of this agreement will not apply to the united kingdom and ireland, as their visa systems are subject to national legislation. with that in mind, i voted to accept the document.
in writing. ‒ i voted in favour of the draft council decision on the conclusion, on behalf of the european union, of the agreement between the european union and the republic of peru on the short-stay visa waiver. the agreement on the short-stay visa waiver is of the utmost importance for the deepening of the relations between the european union and the republic of peru. it will allow for closer economic and cultural relations and deepen political dialogue on a range of issues, including human rights and fundamental freedoms. the agreement could also be an opportunity to improve regional cohesion as peru is one of the few latin american countries whose citizens still require visas and is a significant factor in bringing europeans and peruvians closer together.

in writing. ‒ the agreement concerns the conditions for emission limits and type-approval for internal combustion engines intended for low-cost mobile machinery. these machines include lawnmowers, sprinklers, railway locomotives and inland waterway vessels, and account for around 15% of total nox emissions and 5% of particulate matter pollution in the eu. the agreement tightens the existing limit conditions for these emissions, introduces higher power categories for engines for low-cost mobile machinery covered by the regulation and generally aligns the limit conditions to those in the us and japanese markets, where these values are currently more stringent than in the eu. a very important issue in the document is to ensure that life-saving equipment, such as lifeboat transport vehicles, which could not meet the new proposed boundary conditions due to technical non-adaptation, could be excluded from the scope of the regulation because of its social value. this shutdown has been approved by the council. in conclusion, i believe that this agreement is a good example of better lawmaking in action.

in writing. ‒ the report covers a wide range of issues, including ensuring a holistic eu approach, cooperation with third countries, eu funding through the esf, the erdf and humanitarian aid, definitions, processing, recognition of qualifications, access to eu labour markets and social inclusion (including housing, healthcare and social protection). the report first sets out the political and strategic context and then outlines a number of recommendations, including a call to increase the esf budget, the creation of a single european asylum system and the amendment of the reception conditions directive and the blue card directive. since the beginning of the procedure, there have been concerns about the direction of some of the proposals, in particular the link between legal migration policy and policies to address the current crisis. the ecr group tabled a number of amendments calling for a greater focus on the implementation of existing measures, eu relations with third countries and the fight against trafficking in human beings and discrimination. the ecr also called for a clear distinction between legal migration, asylum seekers and refugees to avoid any confusion between the different categories, using the revision of the blue card directive as a potential solution (meaning that more legal migration, especially highly skilled blue card workers, will not solve the migration crisis). unfortunately, because of the s&d group's uncompromising attitude, which did not intend to take the ecr group's most important demands into account, i voted against.
in writing. - ladies and gentlemen! the key challenge of the refugee crisis is the effective integration of newcomers to the union, which will not be possible without their inclusion in the european labour market. i therefore agree with the rapporteur that, alongside the new european agenda on migration, there is a need for rapid action to integrate refugees and asylum seekers into the labour market. indeed, integration is the foundation of social inclusion, and without it, social inclusion is unlikely to be possible. two challenges emerge in this area and require rapid action. the first is the language skills of refugees. the second problem is the recognition of the refugee's education, qualifications and skills. people coming to the union very often have the qualifications needed in our market, but they are not recognised for legal reasons. it is therefore worth paying attention to the obstacles to this which arise from the european qualifications framework. i voted against the permanent mechanism for the relocation of refugees proposed by the rapporteur and against the equal treatment of refugees and asylum seekers. persons who have not completed the asylum procedure should not be granted full rights in the member states until their situation and identity have been established.
in writing. ‒ in the report on social inclusion and integration of refugees into the labour market, i voted against the amendments supporting the issuing of work permits for those awaiting a decision on asylum. the integration of migrants into the labour market is obviously necessary, but for security reasons it should not concern people who are waiting for their asylum application to be examined, nor impose too short deadlines on member states, as there are differences in the procedures applied between member states and in individual cases the time taken to examine the application may be longer. i was also against the deletion of the adjective 'european' from paragraph 1 in relation to the values and rights that should be respected by migrants coming to the eu. i supported the articles and amendments that spoke of the need to strengthen the protection of women and children and stressed the importance of language education for the effective integration of refugees into the labour market. i disagree with the alternative resolution issued by the enf, which questions the efforts for integration because of the temporary status of refugees. there is no way of predicting how long the crisis in the countries of origin will last. the economic independence of persons in protection in the eu is crucial not only for their quality of life, dignity and acceptance in local communities, but also for social services and security budgets.

in writing. ‒ in october 2015, the european commission, following several proposals from the european parliament, adopted a communication setting out the european union's trade strategy for the coming years. for the first time, the strategy emphasised a values-based approach to trade, stressing not only the importance of market access issues but also the importance of the principles and values that underpin and are reflected in new trade agreements, such as the increased need to make trade policy more inclusive and more transparent. i support open and free trade and have welcomed the new strategy. the ecr group tabled a number of amendments in an attempt to underline parliament's continued support for the conclusion of ongoing trade negotiations with major partners such as the us and japan, and for the opening of new negotiations, not only with like-minded partners such as australia and new zealand, but also with some of the major emerging economies in the asia-pacific region. as the final text was balanced by some demands for increased market access for large and emerging economies and increased support for small and medium-sized enterprises to take advantage of the opportunities offered by trade, i voted in favour of the above document.

in writing. ‒ the report reflects the agreement at second reading on the commission's proposal on cybersecurity for both critical infrastructure (electricity stations, airports, road infrastructure, etc.) and certain digital service providers (e-commerce platforms and search engines). it also lays down new rules on the level of security required to protect such infrastructure from attack and sets out the obligations of member states to coordinate and respond to cyber threats. the work has been limited to e-commerce platforms and search engines, i.e. where these providers provide the services you rely on to use the internet. the approach for digital infrastructure has been liberalised compared to traditional infrastructure, which means that companies will only be able to comply in one of the member states during the compliance procedure under this directive. this is similar to the approach adopted in the field of data protection. critical infrastructure operators will be required to have a resilience plan for network threats and to report any incidents to their national cyber threat teams. i believe that the final text, which sets out the basic measures to improve cybersecurity across europe and reflects the benefits that can result from greater exchange of information between member states on the evolving threats we face in the field of cybersecurity, should be supported. i voted to accept the report.
in writing. - fellow workers! in the digital world, the distinction between sender and receiver of information disappears. the internet remains a free and unfettered medium for the free exchange of opinions, thoughts, knowledge and even criticism. but such advances can be used for both good and bad purposes. network and information systems security affects all aspects of our lives, be they private, social or economic. of course, on the one hand, if we want to be globally competitive, we must fully exploit the opportunities of digitalisation in every sector and every company, and on the other hand, the security of all information is important. statistics show that the digital transformation is particularly lagging behind in traditional sectors (such as construction, metallurgy, agri-food, textiles and steel) as well as in smes, and therefore the security of network and information systems is essential for the smooth functioning of the internal market, as the main objective of the european union should be to deploy new technologies and stimulate research and innovation. i therefore voted in favour of adopting a document on a common high level of network and information security within the union.
in writing. ‒ the rise of cybercrime is a major threat to security today, and its importance is growing. i support a proposal that takes account of the importance of these crimes and aims to increase cybersecurity in europe. effective exchange of information between member states on security matters, while respecting the right to privacy, is a major challenge facing the european union, but there is no other way to deal with such threats.
in writing. ‒ this regulation establishes a process and a timetable for the return to the original eu energy label ag scale (generally within 5 years). the reason for this decision is the limited consumer understanding of the labels of type a+, a++ and a+++. the green to red color scale will be retained. the european commission must review the current labels and then propose delegated acts to return to the ag scale. the regulation also provides for cases where a product will need to be rescaled in the future, for example when:• 25% of products sold in the eu fall into the top energy efficiency class a; or• 50% of products sold in the eu fall into the top two energy efficiency classes a + b. the planned expiry date of the rescaled labels is at least 10 years, which is intended to reduce the burden on businesses. given the nature of the document and its compactness, aimed at simplifying labels and thus making them more legible, i voted in favour of adopting the regulation on the labelling of foodstuffs.
in writing. ‒ this legislative proposal is part of the commission's proposals to strengthen the protection of europe's external borders, including european cooperation in the field of coast guard functions. this package consists of three proposals: for the european border and coast guard agency, for the european fisheries control agency and for the european maritime safety agency (emsa). the main objective of the set of proposals is to strengthen european cooperation in the performance of the coast guard function, to improve cooperation and coordination between relevant eu agencies and their services/functions. the emsa is entrusted with additional tasks: exchange of information and data available in the ship reporting system; provision of surveillance and communication services; capacity building through the development of guidelines, recommendations and best practices and training; capacity sharing, including the planning and implementation of multi-functional operations to cooperate with and support the european border and coast guard agency and national authorities with a coast guard function at national and union level. as it is desirable to strengthen the role of the european border and coast guard agency, emsa and the european control agency in the area of control of the eu's external borders, both in view of the terrorist threat and the issue of uncontrolled inflows of migrants from third countries, i voted in favour of adopting the document.
in writing. ‒ i voted in favour of the report on the proposal for a regulation of the european parliament and of the council on the european border and coast guard and repealing regulation (ec) no 2007/2004, regulation (ec) no 863/2007 and council decision 2005/267/ec. the schengen area is one of the greatest and most visible achievements of european integration. but the idea behind it has now been called into question. the current situation with regard to the migration crisis and the terrorist threat shows that the tools and mechanisms for the functioning of the schengen area that have been developed so far are not sufficient. the european border and coast guard (ebcg) responds to the need to ensure adequate controls at the external borders of the schengen area. i am convinced that this institution, while not solving all the security problems, has a chance to ensure an adequate level of security while guaranteeing the free movement of people within the eu.

in writing. ‒ the purpose of this proposal is to strengthen the independence of the olaf supervisory committee secretariat, thereby ensuring a more efficient functioning of the supervisory committee. the european parliament has repeatedly called on the commission to take action to strengthen the independent functioning of the olaf supervisory committee secretariat. in its annual activity reports for 2013 and 2014, the supervisory committee stressed the importance of its independent and effective functioning, which requires an independent and adequately staffed secretariat. it should be underlined that the exercise by the director-general of olaf of his powers, including decisions on promotions and transfers, may potentially lead to a conflict of interest. under the proposed regulation, the secretariat of the supervisory committee will be established by the commission and not by olaf. the budgetary appropriations for the secretariat of the supervisory committee will be transferred from the budget line and the establishment plan of olaf to the commission. the proposed amendment will therefore have no financial impact. i am in favour of ensuring greater independence for the olaf supervisory committee secretariat, which is why i voted in favour of the document.
in writing. ‒ the purpose of this proposal is to strengthen the independence of the olaf supervisory committee secretariat, thereby ensuring its more effective functioning. under the proposed regulation, new members will be appointed by the european commission and not by olaf (article 15 (8)). the budgetary appropriation for the secretariat of the supervisory committee will be transferred from olaf's budget and establishment plan to the commission's budget (article 18). the proposed amendment will therefore have no financial implications for the european budget. the proposal amends the wording of article 10 (4) and (5) so that the powers of the olaf data protection officer will continue to concern data processed by the secretariat. in addition, the secretariat staff will continue to be subject to the same confidentiality rules as before. the cooperation between olaf and the supervisory committee has not been very good in recent years. i hope the growing independence of the oversight committee will solve this problem.
in writing. ‒ the european anti-fraud office's supervisory committee plays an important role in assessing the legality and integrity of how european taxpayers' money is spent. the effectiveness of the secretariat has a direct impact on the quality of the committee's work and, consequently, on the quality of its tasks. that is why i am in favour of amending the regulation on this matter.
in writing. ‒ the multiannual financial framework (mff) sets limits on both the maximum and minimum amounts that the eu can spend in each year of the framework's operation, as well as spending limits in the different policy areas. the current mff covers the years 2014-2020. the report in question is parliament's contribution before the publication of this review and covers both the situation in the current mff and the prospects for the next mff after 2020. the report indicates that a comprehensive review is a 'pre-requisite' given the number of crises the eu is facing today that could not have been foreseen when the current mffs were agreed in 2013, and the lack of budgetary capacity to deal with these crises. for the next mffs, the report considers reform of their duration and decision-making process, as well as new sources of own resources. the ecr group made a number of amendments to the draft report, mainly concerning the maintenance of the 2013 agreed spending ceilings, the preservation of the distinction between review and revision of the mff, and the call for the mid-term review to place greater emphasis on performance, public opinion and the budgetary situation of the member states before recommending substantial changes. since the final report reflects these changes in part, i have decided to vote in favour of the document.
in writing. ‒ the multiannual financial framework (mff) approved by the european parliament in 2013 reflected the union's priorities at the time of its negotiation, and provided a gateway to future challenges with a mandatory review clause and new and strengthened provisions on flexibility and the creation of a high level group on own resources. the migration and refugee crisis, the eu's internal security issues, the european fund for strategic investments (efsi) funding and the persistently high level of unemployment, especially among young people, are just some of the factors that need to be taken into account in the current review. in order to finance additional urgent needs, it was considered necessary to use the flexibility mechanisms and the so-called special instruments available under the mff, as the mff ceilings in some headings proved to be too low. however, as provided for in article 312 tfeu, the previously allocated country-specific envelopes will not be reduced by such a revision. i welcome the outcome of today's vote, which reflects the need for a systematic review of the mff, a key element of the management of union expenditure.
in writing. ‒ i voted in favour of the report on the preparation of the post-election review of the mff for 2014-2020. the multiannual financial framework adopted in 2013 was tailored to the needs of the time and could not have anticipated the challenges we face today. of course, some of the challenges we face - such as youth employment and the crisis in the agricultural sector - are still relevant, but we also have to face the most serious crises in decades, such as the refugee crisis and the growing threat of terrorism. there is no doubt that the review and revision of the mff must take account of these changes and propose solutions to deal effectively with these problems. to do that, you need the right level of funding. but this cannot be done at the expense of commitments already made, as this would make the union look like an unreliable partner, which we cannot afford. therefore, if the currently available resources prove insufficient, the ceilings should be raised accordingly.
in writing. ‒ the report contains good solutions for raising the ceilings of the 2014-2020 mff (increasing the ceilings for commitment appropriations under titles 1a, 1b, 3 and 4 as well as increasing the overall ceiling for payment appropriations) and provisions to increase the flexibility of the current mff. the reform of the union's financing system is also important, as is the reference to the idea of tax justice by adding the proposal of corporate taxation as a potential way of raising own resources. attention should also be paid to the impact of the uk referendum on the eu budget. brexit means that the eu budget will be 9 billion euros less per year.
in writing. ‒ it is good that parliament has prepared its position on the revision of the mff before the publication of the commission proposal. this gives hope that it will be possible to influence the draft review, which should appear in the autumn. there is no doubt that much has changed within the union itself and in its international environment since the 2014-2020 mff was agreed at the end of 2013. i would mention the migration crisis, the russian embargo and the crisis in the agricultural sector, and brexit, which will also have significant financial consequences for the eu budget. although some shifts will be necessary to find the means for the most urgent actions, there can be no interference with the so-called national envelopes on which the compromise on the budget is based. the problem of accumulated commitments not covered by the budget should also be addressed as soon as possible in order to avoid the risk of budgetary insolvency at the end of the period, as was the case in the years 2007-2013. the ongoing crisis in the agricultural sector, particularly in the milk market, the lifting of sugar quotas next year and the negative effects of the ongoing russian embargo mean that the cap's restrictive ceilings for 2020 are now at a much lower level than in the previous funding period, which could have a negative impact on the income of millions of farming families in the eu. in the review of the mff, the commission must take this into account.

in writing. ‒ japan is legally bound by a global moratorium on commercial whaling imposed by the international whaling commission (iwc). despite the moratorium, it is fishing on a large scale, taking advantage of a loophole in the rules that allows fishing on special terms for 'scientific purposes', particularly in the arctic. i believe that there is no case for allowing deadly scientific research on whales, and the japanese program is completely unnecessary and undermines the global moratorium. hunting of all whales (whales, dolphins and porpoises) beyond the limited activities of the indigenous population for survival should be strongly opposed. whaling involves unnecessary cruelty, and the only legitimate use of their existence is responsible tourism practices. i support the joint text of the resolution, calling for the iwc moratorium to be maintained and encouraging japan to develop alternative industries that support local communities, such as whale watching. i voted to accept the procedural document.

in writing. ‒ following the release of political prisoners on 22 august 2015, the eu lifted sanctions against 170 belarusian individuals and three companies. however, since then, the human rights situation in the country has not improved. the authorities have not restored the civil rights of former political prisoners, nor have they taken steps to abolish the punishment of littering. the osce/odihr observation mission during the 2015 presidential elections concluded that 'significant problems, especially during the counting and reconciliation of votes, undermined the integrity of the electoral process'. however, until now the belarusian authorities have not implemented the recommendations set out in the final report of the osce/odihr mission. the upcoming parliamentary elections on 11 september 2016 will be a crucial test to see if the authorities are really willing to engage with citizens in accordance with democratic values. the ep would therefore only be able to take a fully informed decision and properly assess the delegated act after the elections and on the basis of the osce/odihr report. this unfortunate confluence of dates could have the opposite political consequences and a negative impact on the situation of the democratic opposition. for this reason, i supported the resolution which opposes the granting of an eu guarantee to the eib to cover losses in respect of belarus at this particular time. i am not against the launch of the guarantee procedure, but it should be after the elections, after some progress has been made in electoral standards.
in writing. ‒ the delegated act requires the institution supervising the winding-up to set minimum requirements for own funds and eligible liabilities (mrel) that will sufficiently ensure that the institution under winding-up can absorb losses, recapitalise sufficiently and continue to operate. the ecr group did not express the need to object for the following reasons: (1) the minimum contribution requirement is sufficiently reflected in the current delegated act by reference to the requirements set out in article 44 of the bank restructuring and orderly liquidation directive (brrd); (2) as regards the amount of recapitalisation, the supervisory authority applies the most recent values to determine the appropriate total risk exposure ratio or leverage ratio when estimating the capital needs of the institution. (3) in the case of a transitional period, the supervisory authority may set an appropriate transitional period to achieve the final minimum requirement for own funds and liabilities (mrel) and it should be as short as possible. the cor also agreed with the rapporteur for the brrd, mr hökmar (epl), that banks need legislative certainty in setting mrel requirements. with that in mind, i voted against.

in writing. ‒ the document concerns the approval of health claims for caffeine. the objector justifies it as being incompatible with the objectives of the basic act, arguing that statements concerning alertness and concentration cannot be made to children, including adolescents, stressing that adolescents are the largest group of consumers of energy drinks. furthermore, the resolution states that in the absence of the nutritional profiles that the commission was required to establish under the food claims regulation (1924/2006), the claims on caffeine can be used for energy drinks that have a higher sugar content. experts say the objection is flawed and exaggerates certain aspects. contrary to what the text says, this measure applies to all products containing caffeine, not just energy drinks. energy drinks account for only 1% of the total eu soft drink market, and calories from all drinks account for only 3% of all calories consumed in the eu. in addition, efsa estimates that the vast majority of calories in the diet of adolescents come from chocolate, coffee and tea. i personally think that some of the concerns raised in the document are valid. experience with caffeine use may give the illusion that the consumption of caffeine and caffeine-containing products (including energy drinks) is good for health. however, i believe that the substance of the document should be further developed, and i therefore abstained.

in writing. the widespread introduction by member states of non-tariff barriers to food exporters in the internal market and the fact that these actions are contrary to eu law undermine one of the four fundamental freedoms of the eu, namely the free movement of goods. barriers faced on a daily basis by food exporters include the requirement to have additional certificates not required by community law, increased frequency of health checks and long detention of trucks, the obligation to keep documents relating to the transaction for a long time, the obligation to keep these documents in the country of destination, the short period of authorisation, and the frequent change of administrative fees. additional barriers also apply to negative media campaigns about poor food quality. the commission should examine as soon as possible the possibility of introducing eu rules prohibiting such practices in relation to food imports in order to guarantee the proper, fair and transparent functioning of the eu internal market in the interests of food producers and retailers.

the rapporteur. mr president, i would like to thank you for your kind words. heating and cooling accounts for about 40% of the total primary energy, which is a major energy problem, and for about 50% of the total useful energy in the form of heat. while electricity generation can be standardised in the single energy market, heating and cooling require local solutions. however, the dependence of heating and cooling on the energy market is increasing, which may, for example, use cogeneration at local level for both electricity and heating or cooling. the diversity of the needs of the union's citizens for thermal comfort is demonstrated by the fact that the annual energy consumption per square metre of heated area varies in the member states from around 60 to even 300 kwh. the greatest potential for thermal energy efficiency lies in the thermal retrofitting of around two thirds of the so-called old material of residential, public and commercial buildings, as the simplest, fastest way to make the most efficient use of energy, reduce co2 emissions and create many jobs. this means that public funding for this priority objective should be increased and existing limits, for example in the regional development fund, removed, especially for whole settlements built, for example, with large plate technology. unfortunately, we have marginalized this issue in the past. it was a mistake. we've wasted a lot of time. the next step is to replace the outdated district heating with the so-called district heating from high-efficiency cogeneration plants. it is essential to phase out outdated small, non-ecological district heating and switch to high-efficiency cogeneration systems. this could be facilitated, for example, by temporarily phasing out the use of the ets in these heat and power generation systems. the difference between the west and the east of the union in the use of more efficient gas for heating purposes should also be taken into account. this is many times higher in the eu countries of western europe, while in central and eastern europe the heating sector is still mainly based on coal, which requires a gradual reduction in its inefficient burning. we need to improve that efficiency. the agglomeration of this region of europe is characterised by low emissions, i.e. emissions into the atmosphere of partially flared pyrolitic organic gases, including aromatic hydrocarbons and nitrogen and soot oxides, as well as fly ash. in the southern european member states, seasonal cooling is a growing problem due to climate warming, with around 5% of the total energy used for heating and cooling. the issues discussed today require the application of a number of complex future solutions, including: architectural and urban planning; the use of natural sources of heat and cooling. it requires the urgent development of innovative research and industry-wide development of new thermal insulation materials and sustainable green heating and cooling technologies, with a particular focus on solar panels and reverse heat pumps. in the future, the thermal comfort of the inhabitants of the european union will depend primarily on zero-emission thermal retrofitting and the use of renewable energy sources that are optimal for the entire climate zone. the priorities are well known, but they must also be financed and implemented as a matter of priority, although the hierarchy of priority varies from one member state to another, so as to ensure that the solutions we have found are optimized and that we can combat energy poverty.

member of the commission. – mr president, i am here on behalf of my dear colleague neven mimica, and i would like to welcome this report and congratulate the rapporteur, mr corrao. the eu trust fund for africa was created as a swift and flexible implementing tool to, inter alia, better manage migration and deliver quick results. the trust fund reduces the risk of aid fragmentation and provides a platform for political visibility and engagement with countries of origin, transit and destination. in the three regions concerned – the sahel and lake chad, the horn of africa and the north of africa – the root causes of instability, forced displacement and irregular migration are diverse, complex and often inter-related. they thus require a holistic and integrated approach. i have personally witnessed this in my visits to mali, somalia, ethiopia, kenya and lately in the last few months to niger and chad. i saw the situation on the ground and i strongly believe that the eu trust fund is definitely supporting programmes aimed at creating employment opportunities in local communities of origin and return, with a focus on vocational training and the creation of micro and small enterprises. it also supports actions aimed at strengthening access to basic services across a variety of resilience programmes. it particularly targets young people and women as well as other vulnerable groups. the eu trust fund for africa complements existing eu instruments, national and regional frameworks as well as bilateral programmes of eu member states. development cooperation addresses migration issues in two ways: firstly, by helping partner countries to improve migration governance, tapping into the development potential of migration; and secondly, by addressing political, economic and social instability, development cooperation addresses the causes of irregular migration and forced displacement, in order to help ensure that migration takes place in an orderly and safe manner. the trust fund supports programmes aiming at better migration management, including affording international protection, offering long-term solutions to displaced people and facilitating the safe, and also dignified and sustainable, return of migrants. this is in line with the united nations’ 2030 agenda for sustainable development and these are clearly development objectives. in the design and implementation of activities, the commission follows three key principles. firstly, the need for a strong human rights focus, especially in actions in support of law enforcement and border management; secondly, the need for continuous monitoring to ensure that european union support is used for its intended purpose and is delivering the expected results; and thirdly, the need to be transparent and inclusive with eu member states, african partners, and relevant international organisations and civil society.

in writing. ‒ i voted in favour of the report on the cohesion policy and the strategy for research and innovation for smart specialisation, ris3. ris3 strategies are a valuable tool to minimise the innovation gap and increase employment and growth in europe. the strategy still needs to be improved and public authorities should continuously monitor the strategies to maximise their results and ensure the most effective interregional cooperation possible. furthermore, simplification and coordination of existing programmes is essential for the proper implementation of these strategies in the coming years. in this context, a review of the post-2017 strategy should be mandatory in order to increase the efficiency and effectiveness of the ris3 strategy, taking into account the experience gained in the first years of its implementation.
in writing. ‒ during its last term, the european regional development fund (erdf) decided, in the context of supporting the implementation of the first thematic objective, that in the 2014-2020 programming period, regions must target investments in the areas of research, technological development and innovation through a smart specialisation strategy. ris3 is therefore an ex ante condition for eu member states and regions to receive support through the european structural and investment funds (esif). all european regions have a ris3 strategy in place. these strategies were developed and started to be implemented in 2014 and 2015. the application of the ex ante conditionality has proved to be an important step forward, as most regions have already adopted the ris3 strategy. however, some of them must continue to work to meet the requirements of the ex ante ris3 condition. the report highlights the key role of ris3 in the contribution of cohesion policy to the europe 2020 strategy, the role of multi-level governance in the strategy-setting process, the role of the eu urban agenda in creating synergies and strong links to enable efficient use of resources, and the role of monitoring and evaluation. i have hereby endorsed that report.
in writing. ‒ in the face of the ongoing crisis and related budgetary constraints, and with increasing global competition from countries such as the us, china and south korea, it is crucial for the eu to continuously increase its innovation capacity. europe 2020 is the eu's strategy for growth up to 2020. in a changing world, we want the eu to become a smart, sustainable and inclusive economy. the union wants to achieve five ambitious targets by 2020 related to employment, innovation, education, social inclusion and climate/energy. each member state has also set its own national targets in each of these areas. this strategy is backed up by concrete actions at national and union level. national and regional authorities across europe will develop smart specialisation strategies to use european structural and innovation funds more effectively and to increase synergies between different eu, national and regional policies, as well as public and private investment. those strategies should contribute to closing the innovation gap and increasing employment and growth in europe. it is now clear that there are a number of improvements that can be made in the development of the strategy. public authorities should endeavour to attach particular importance to monitoring and reviewing strategies in order to maximise their results.
in writing. ‒ ris3 strategies are a key driver of the economy, filling innovation gaps, enhancing investment efficiency and stimulating employment growth. public institutions that monitor interregional cooperation and promote regional specialisation can ensure stable growth and economic development across europe. in view of the experience gained in the early years of the project, it is important to listen to the local authorities of the various areas involved in the project in order to increase the possibilities for grassroots initiative and to highlight the importance of civil society. the strategy is an important element in shaping economic development and strengthening the regions, which is why i voted in favour of the proposal.
in writing. ‒ the precondition for receiving financial support from the european structural funds to businesses, eu member states and regions was to target investments in research, technological development and innovation through a smart specialisation strategy. the strategy is an instrument for implementing development policy and its purpose is to support eu countries in developing their own economic development paths, stimulating the development of businesses and ensuring their continued growth. the eu's limited budget, as well as the global economic recession, have forced businesses to become more competitive by increasing their capacity to innovate. all european regions now have a smart specialisation strategy. these were developed and started to be implemented in 2014 and 2015. the report encourages the support of enterprises by stimulating their development, which in turn increases their competitiveness on the international scene.
in writing. ‒ i support the report on european territorial cooperation (interreg) because it tackles very important issues such as: description of best practices, contribution to territorial cohesion, simplification and eu added value. interreg provides a framework for the implementation of joint actions and the exchange of policy experience between national, regional and local actors from different member states. i supported this report because i consider the implementation of cohesion policy to be very important and the interreg programme referred to in the report is part of it.
in writing. ‒ i voted in favour of the report on european territorial cooperation best practices and innovative actions. in order to achieve better results and make more efficient use of investments, european territorial cooperation (interreg) has been redesigned in the 2014-2020 programme. this was made possible by focusing on thematic areas and focusing on results. raising public awareness and exposure of european regional cooperation is very important at this time, as most people in eu border regions are not aware of the eu-funded cross-border cooperation in their regions. i therefore believe that both effective dissemination of results from completed projects and better coordination between the commission, the managing authorities and all stakeholders in the implementation of crossborder programmes are very important. this will allow for a critical analysis of projects in terms of their achievements in the specific thematic areas and will facilitate the further implementation of the programmes beyond 2020, while ensuring high quality and transparency of projects.
in writing. ‒ territorial cooperation within the european community is an important element of cohesion policy. it is developing a number of programmes to facilitate transport by building transnational transport networks, which is an important aspect in border areas where many people cross borders every day to get to work. it also facilitates the transport of goods, thereby reducing delivery costs, and contributes to the development of tourism. countries that cooperate in border areas are better able to address environmental challenges. many of the sites at risk are located in several member states, so cooperation to protect them is much more effective than action taken by individual countries. the same goes for the sea and water pollution control. territorial cooperation also results in increased innovation and research by research institutes and enterprises from different countries, and also provides opportunities for international cooperation between universities across borders. it is also important to make these areas more attractive to commercial enterprises. harnessing human, regional and cross-border potential provides opportunities for the development of border areas and also creates new jobs, preventing depopulation.
in writing. ‒ interreg european territorial cooperation is one of the two objectives of cohesion policy and provides a framework for joint action and policy exchange between national, regional and local actors from different member states. the report focuses on issues related to the description of best practices and the contribution to territorial cohesion. a number of paragraphs concern the period after 2020 and contain specific proposals in this regard. calls for an increase in the budget for european territorial cooperation in the next programming period and considers that cross-border cooperation can bring added value in managing the migration crisis. it also encourages the use of interreg programmes and calls for their implementation to meet the challenges of the refugee crisis. it considers that european territorial cooperation has proved its worth, but regrets that its full potential has not been realised. the report considers that crossborder cooperation is a key tool for the development of border regions, which are recognised as true laboratories of european integration, and stresses that, despite the existence of a separate regulation on european territorial cooperation, the implementation of territorial cooperation programmes should be further simplified. i hereby endorse the report.
in writing. ‒ the european territorial cooperation (interreg), established 25 years ago, remains a key tool for achieving territorial cohesion between more than 60 european border regions. over the last quarter of a century, progress has been made in many key sectors, such as transport, innovation, knowledge, culture and education. moreover, interregional cooperation has allowed cities and regions to cooperate in a wide range of thematic areas, including the exchange of experience and best practice, which has improved the effectiveness of many regional and local policies. despite these achievements, many obstacles to further convergence remain, such as divergent national legislation in the fields of employment, healthcare and social security. the report properly identifies the current problems of territorial cooperation and the objectives on which we should focus in the coming years. research and innovation, joint research projects, the creation of international cross-border universities, cross-border clusters and business networks, and the joint attraction of foreign investors are challenges that need to be given particular attention.
in writing. ‒ the resolution identifies effective decisions taken in the member states under territorial cooperation and focuses on the main plans for the future. the success of the programme is guaranteed by: territorial and communication cooperation; competitiveness and support for smes; research and innovation achievements; regional identity and territorial cohesion; and institutional capacity and social capital. european territorial cooperation is an important instrument for the positive development of european integration, which is why i decided to vote in favour of the resolution.

in writing. ‒ i voted in favour of the adoption of the preliminary report on the inquiry into emission measurements in the automotive sector. on 17 december 2015, the european parliament decided to set up a 45-member committee of inquiry to investigate alleged breaches or maladministration in the application of union law with regard to emission measurements in the automotive sector, without prejudice to the jurisdiction of national or union courts. the scope of this inquiry is limited by the mandate of the commission and must focus on the compliance of the commission and the member states with the obligations imposed by regulation (ec) no 715/2007. in addition, the emis committee is responsible for collecting and analysing information to determine whether the commission and the member states have evidence of the use of devices to reduce the effectiveness of the operation and for collecting and analysing information on the implementation of directive 2007/46/ec by the member states. finally, the committee is also required to make any recommendations it deems necessary in this regard. because of the importance of the subject and its impact on the environment and therefore on the health and lives of eu citizens, i supported this report.
in writing. ‒ pursuant to parliament's decision of 17 december 2015 to set up a committee of inquiry on emission measurements in the automotive sector, the committee is to present an interim report within 6 months of its establishment. the report shall be put to the vote on 13 september 2016. given that the emis hearings are still ongoing, the coordinators agreed that the report would not contain any political content. it is therefore purely technical and describes the timeframe and stresses the need for full cooperation between the conference of presidents, the ep bureau, the european commission and national authorities. i have hereby endorsed that report.
in writing. ‒ the work of the commission of inquiry, which aims to investigate allegations of breaches or maladministration in the application of european union law in relation to emission measurements in the automotive sector, is valuable from the point of view of the proper management of climate policy and the automotive industry. the fact that information missions are being organised, that a timetable has been set, that documentation is being collected on a continuous basis and that information is being made available to the public, convinces me of the importance of the matter being discussed by the committee, and i therefore vote in favour of the motion for a resolution.
in writing. ‒ on 17 december 2015, the european parliament set up a 45-member committee of inquiry to investigate allegations of maladministration in the application of union law in relation to emission measurements in the automotive sector. the report put to the vote is the mid-term outcome of the committee's work, in which it asks the conference of presidents and the bureau to support all measures to enable hearings and extraordinary meetings to be organised, reimbursement of the costs of experts and witnesses, missions and any other duly justified technical measures. it also asks the commission to guarantee its support for the work of the committee of inquiry. i voted in favour of the report in order to ensure that the work of the committee of inquiry proceeds smoothly.

in writing. ‒ i voted in favour of the european parliament legislative resolution on the draft council decision on the conclusion of the agreement in the form of an exchange of letters between the european union and the people's republic of china pursuant to article xxiv:6 and article xxviii of the general agreement on tariffs and trade (gatt) 1994 relating to the modification of concessions schedules of the republic of croatia in the course of its accession to the european union. the accession of the republic of croatia resulted in the enlargement of the customs union by the european union, which in turn obliged the european union to enter into negotiations with wto members with negotiating rights in respect of the croatian concessional list in order to agree on the compensation to be paid if the adoption of the eu external tariff system results in an increase in rates above the level to which the acceding country has committed itself in the wto. in my view, the european parliament should give its consent to this agreement, as it restores to the people's republic of china trade rights that were restricted as a result of the enlargement of the eu customs union following the accession of croatia.
in writing. ‒ with the accession of the republic of croatia, the european union has expanded the customs union. therefore, in accordance with the rules of the world trade organisation (wto), the european union was obliged to enter into negotiations with wto members having negotiating rights in respect of the concession list of croatia in order to agree on a settlement. such compensation shall be due where the adoption of the eu external tariff system results in an increase in rates above the level to which the acceding country concerned has committed itself under the wto. these adjustments concern in particular the reduction of the current eu customs duties on footwear and window or wall air conditioners, and the increase of import quotas for garlic and mushrooms. i hereby endorse the report.
in writing. ‒ as a result of the accession of the republic of croatia to the european union, the people's republic of china was to be compensated, on the basis of wto rules, for the withdrawal of concessions and the increase in rates resulting from the eu external customs tariff. facilitating trade by removing barriers is an important objective of international trade policy, which is why i supported the resolution.
in writing. ‒ i support the agreement between croatia and uruguay on the alignment of tariff quotas for beef. this is an important agreement, given that the customs union was automatically extended when croatia joined the eu. the opening of negotiations between croatia and uruguay is an important step towards establishing an external eu customs tariff so that these rates are not high. these are the shenanigans i voted for.
in writing. ‒ i voted in favour of the recommendation on the draft council decision on the conclusion of the agreement in the form of an exchange of letters between the european union and the eastern republic of uruguay pursuant to article xxiv:6 and article xxviii of the general agreement on tariffs and trade (gatt) 1994 relating to the modification of concessions schedules of the republic of croatia in the course of its accession to the european union. following the accession of the republic of croatia, the eu has expanded the customs union and, since the eu's external tariff system results in an increase in rates in accordance with wto rules, the eu was obliged to open negotiations with the eastern republic of uruguay on the croatian concession list. the negotiations with uruguay culminated in the draft agreement, which was initialled on 18 december 2015 in nairobi. in my view, the european parliament should give its consent to the conclusion of the agreement in the form of an exchange of letters between the european union and the eastern republic of uruguay relating to the modification of the concession lists of the republic of croatia in the course of its accession to the european union.
in writing. ‒ with the accession of the republic of croatia, the eu has expanded the customs union. it was therefore obliged to open negotiations with the eastern republic of uruguay on the croatian concession list. the aim of these negotiations was to agree a countervailing duty, as the eu's external tariff system causes rates to rise. negotiations with uruguay led to the draft agreement in 2015 which agreed on alignments for the tariff quotas for beef. i hereby endorse the report.
