in writing. ‒ the purpose of the regulation is to align regulation (ec) no 421/2009 on external trade statistics with the tfeu in terms of conferring on the commission the delegated and implementing powers to adopt certain measures. following the first reading vote in plenary on 12 march 2014, the ep and the council negotiated with the intention of reaching an agreement at an early stage of the second reading on the basis of the council's position at first reading, which the ep can approve as reflecting a compromise reached between the co-legislators and covering a combination of delegated acts, implementing acts, as well as transposing certain matters into a basic legislative act. one issue remains unresolved: the consultation of experts from the member states during the preparation of delegated acts, which the council insisted on. it was then decided to suspend the negotiations pending the outcome of an interinstitutional agreement on better law-making. following the adoption of that interinstitutional agreement, the draft regulation was amended accordingly. the cor supports the balanced outcome of the negotiations following the interinstitutional agreement on better law-making and, consequently, the recommendation that the second reading be held without amendments. i voted yes.
in writing. ‒ i voted in favour of the recommendation for second reading on the council position at first reading on the adoption of a regulation of the european parliament and of the council amending regulation (ec) no 471/2009 on community statistics relating to external trade with third countries, as regards the conferral on the commission of delegated and implementing powers to adopt certain measures. following the changes following the entry into force of the treaty of lisbon and the adoption of regulation (eu) no 182/2011 (on implementing acts), the commission had to adapt its rules for taking decisions in trade policy to the new system of delegated and implementing acts. most of the legislation in this area has been adapted by means of a consolidated act and by means of several individual adaptations. the commission has undertaken to present by the end of the seventh term of office a second set of adjustments to the committee procedure for legislative acts involving a regulatory procedure with scrutiny. the commission therefore proposed to amend regulation (ec) no 471/2009 on community statistics, which is the only legislative act in the field of the common commercial policy that refers to the regulatory procedure with scrutiny. i think the council's position on this point is to be supported.
in writing. ‒ i agree with the regulation that states that member states are obliged to collect and submit statistical data on natural gas and electricity prices for industrial and household customers. these data would cover electricity prices, network access charges, taxes and fees and their sub-components and would be reported every six months. the proposed regulation aims to replace directive 2008/92/ec, which imposes such an obligation on industrial customers. the collection and submission of data is intended to monitor the internal energy market and the effects of various energy policies, such as the promotion of renewable energy sources. i voted to accept the document.
in writing. ‒ under this regulation, member states will be required to collect and submit statistical data on natural gas and electricity prices for industrial and household customers. price data would be reported every six months for different consumption volumes and would cover electricity prices, network access charges, taxes and fees and their sub-components. gas and electricity price statistics are required to monitor the internal energy market and the effects of various energy policies, such as the promotion of renewable energy sources. in the context of the european union strategy, the commission has committed to reporting on energy costs and prices every two years, starting in 2016. the commission's preliminary proposal was presented after extensive consultations and in agreement with the member states and the national regulatory authorities and no significant differences in the issues were identified between the positions of the parliament and the council. the agreement reached in the june 2016 trilateral talks now requires approval by the plenary assembly. i hereby endorse the report.
in writing. ‒ collecting data on energy and gas prices is important for gaining knowledge about the market. the aim of the regulation is to make data collection compulsory rather than voluntary, in order to avoid the data collection problems that some member states have experienced. it is in the interest of the union to ensure high quality data in order to avoid misunderstandings arising from different methodologies and statistical surveys. i considered the proposed amendments appropriate and amended the draft resolution accordingly.
in writing. ‒ for the promotion of transparency within gas and electricity prices, i will be voting in favour of the first-reading agreement regarding this issue. comprehensible and comparable are the two main words in this context. the member states have to guarantee to provide comprehensible and comparable high-quality data, which needs a proper system for data collection and the compilation of those statistics, to truly represent the prices of natural gas and electricity, in order to truly serve the citizens of the eu.
in writing. ‒ i voted in favour of a regulation to collect statistics on gas and electricity prices. up-to-date, reliable and harmonised data are essential for the efficient monitoring of the energy market of the member states and for shaping energy policy. until now, this costing function has only been available to industrial customers in the eu, but now it is to be made generally available so that every eu citizen has access to reliable and comparable gas and energy prices. the regulation does not harmonise the structure of gas and energy prices in the eu, but only collects data for statistical purposes and to ensure price transparency.
in writing. ‒ i do not support the policy objectives set out in the consultative communication on the structure of the electricity market, which is part of the report on the european internal market published by the european commission on 15 july 2015. i am not in favour of creating a union-wide electricity market with clear price signals for new investment. i do not think it is appropriate to consolidate the european approach to energy security and to strengthen regional cooperation on energy policy, in particular in investments in new power generation facilities, interconnectors and support systems and in the integration of renewable energy into the european internal market. the fact is that i find positive elements in the report, but the negatives are predominant, hence my decision to vote against.
in writing. ‒ the resolution on the structure of the energy market is not an attractive project from the point of view of the polish market and polish resources. reducing the production and consumption of fossil fuels in order to increase the role of renewable energy is possible for countries that have reached a high level of economic development. the creation of a european electricity market to guarantee european security based on new installations and integration around renewable energy sources is not the best solution from the point of view of poland's energy interests, which is why i am opposed to this resolution.
in writing. ‒ i voted in favour of the eu's heating and cooling strategy, which is the first step in analysing the problems and challenges in the sector and addressing them through eu energy policy. to achieve the eu's climate and energy goals, the sector covered by the strategy must undergo a radical change to reduce energy consumption and reduce the use of fossil fuels. studies show that 84% of the energy used for heating and cooling is still from fossil fuels, and only 16% from renewable sources. i think it's important to make changes in this sector. the main objectives of the strategy are to link electricity systems to heating and cooling systems and to recover energy from industrial waste.
in writing. ‒ i voted in favour of the report on the eu's heating and cooling strategy. the heating and cooling problem is of varying concern in the member states. the hierarchy of importance of the different activities in these countries therefore varies. the biggest efficiency reserves for the new eu countries that joined the eu after 2004, including poland, lie in the thermal retrofitting of buildings as the simplest way to use energy efficiently and to reduce co2 emissions significantly. the financing of thermal modernisation works for whole settlements, especially those built using large plate technology, needs to be increased significantly. at least 25% of the total appropriations from the european energy efficiency and renewable energy fund should be allocated to this purpose. it is also necessary to replace outdated district heating plants with high-efficiency cogeneration plants. a different problem, which is currently increasing in the european mediterranean countries, is cooling, which is associated with the process of gradual warming of the climate. architectural solutions such as thermal insulation and reverse heat pumps can play a major role in solving both problems, and intensive research is needed on new innovative solutions in this area. in my view, the adoption of an eu strategy on heating and cooling is essential.
in writing. ‒ in february 2016, the commission presented the eu's strategy for heating and cooling. this is the first step in analysing the problems and challenges in this sector and addressing them through eu energy policy. in the context of the heating and cooling strategy, the commission organised an ad hoc consultation forum on 9 september 2015. in total, 84% of the energy used for heating and cooling is still from fossil fuels, and only 16% from renewable sources. to meet the eu's climate and energy targets, the heating and cooling sector needs to radically reduce energy consumption and reduce the use of fossil fuels. the main focus is on decarbonising heating and cooling, renovating existing buildings, connecting electricity to heating and cooling, increasing the share of renewable energy in heating and cooling, and recovering energy from industrial waste. it is also important to involve consumers and industry in this process. i hereby endorse the report.
in writing. ‒ heating and cooling involves converting about 40% of total primary energy into about 50% of total useful energy in the form of heat. while electricity generation can be standardised in the single energy market, heating and cooling require local solutions. however, the dependence of heating and cooling on the energy market is increasing, e.g. local cogeneration for both electricity and heat (cooling). the diversity of the needs of the union's citizens for thermal comfort is demonstrated by the fact that the annual energy consumption per square metre of heated area varies between 60 and even 300 kwh in the member states. the ep report focused on a number of important issues, including the drive to phase out outdated, small, non-ecological district heating and the transition to high-efficiency cogeneration systems. the need to take account of the differences between the west and the east of the eu in the use of more efficient gas for heating purposes has been rightly emphasised. in the coming years, member states and the eu should focus strongly on architectural and urban cooling and heating activities, on the use of natural sources of heat and cooling, and on intensifying the development of innovative research and the creation of an entire industry of new thermal insulation materials.
in writing. ‒ the work of the committee on the heating and cooling strategy is relevant from the perspective of the energy and climate union and the security of energy supply. the use of modern heating and cooling technologies, the use of biogas, biomass in energy production, the implementation of high-quality insulation in buildings and the modernisation of older buildings, investments in small, high-efficiency heaters these activities increase energy management efficiency. i have decided to vote in favour of the motion for a resolution.
in writing. ‒ i support the report because it highlights a number of key aspects. both the role that smes should have in the eu economy and their role in the implementation of cohesion policy. another aspect is the need to reduce red tape and diversify funding sources, as well as to engage early in discussions on investment priorities in future funding rounds, and to exchange best practices between member states. i would just like to point out that i do not think that support for smes should be linked to the integration of refugees and migrants.
in writing. ‒ as the programming phase of the european structural and investment funds is coming to an end, the regi own-initiative report focuses on the first lessons to be drawn from the involvement of smes, and more specifically on the implementation of the third of the eleven thematic objectives of the common provisions regulation (article 9) to strengthen the competitiveness of smes. the report contains many positive elements, including an emphasis on the key role of smes in the eu economy and in the successful implementation of cohesion policy, reducing red tape and encouraging the use of financial instruments, simplifying access to loans, diversifying funding sources, the importance of technical assistance and early involvement in discussions on investment priorities in future funding rounds, and the exchange of best practices between member states. i hereby endorse the report.
in writing. ‒ smes are crucial to the economies of eu regions, both in terms of employment and competitiveness. it is therefore to be welcomed that eur 70 billion has been allocated to support enterprises, mainly smes, in the 2007-2013 cohesion policy period, and that the aim is to double this amount between 2014 and 2020, to which an increased use of the various financial instruments is to contribute. in the european parliament, we often stress that smes are the backbone of the eu economy and have a huge employment potential, accounting for 85% of new jobs. it is also estimated that over 20 million smes provide over 67% of private sector employment in the eu, with micro-enterprises accounting for 30%. smes are thus the main drivers of long-term european growth and sustainable job creation in the member states. increasing resource efficiency for smes offers great opportunities for reducing production costs and increasing productivity. it is estimated that better use of resources represents an overall savings potential of eur 630 billion for european industry. preventing environmental damage and moving to a low-carbon economy are societal challenges that create new opportunities for companies to market green products and services. smes need a conducive environment in which green solutions can be easily developed, financed and marketed.
in writing. ‒ small and medium-sized enterprises account for around 99% of all eu enterprises, providing 67% of total employment in the unfunded business sector. the eu regulation establishing common rules for the european structural and investment funds lists 11 thematic objectives setting out the rules for funding. thematic objective 3 on strengthening the competitiveness of smes has one of the highest pools of resources. the eu's sme support is expected to reach almost eur 64 billion between 2014 and 2020. the additional use of financial instruments to stimulate bank lending is aimed at doubling this amount. the expected results are 300,000 new jobs and support for almost one million smes. specific measures include support for entrepreneurship and business creation, investment in research and innovation, development of new business models, products and services, knowledge transfer and business cooperation, upskilling of workers, promotion of self-employment, or the creation of social enterprises. this is why it is so important to assess early on the achievement of this key objective of improving the competitiveness of smes, both in terms of the achievements to date and the lessons to be learned for the future.
in writing. ‒ i am optimistic about the draft resolution on promoting the competitiveness of smes, given the impact of their activities on economic growth, job creation and innovation. local authorities can support the most effective actors through careful selection, partnership and good management. increasing the efficiency of the sme sector can contribute to a more economical use of resources, lower production costs, increased productivity and thus generate savings for subsequent innovation. i have decided to vote in favour of the above initiative.
in writing. ‒ smes account for 85% of employment in the eu labour market and have the potential to create new jobs. the report highlights their dominant role in the structure of the european economy and also examines the lessons to be drawn from the implementation of the third objective, namely the strengthening of the competitiveness of smes, in the programming of the european structural and investment funds. the report highlights obstacles that prevent and hinder smes from having a broad access to funds, such as the large number and fragmentation of aid schemes, the high degree of complexity of rules and procedures, the delays in implementing implementing acts and the risk of overly rigorous implementation. i voted in favour of the report, which points out that excessive regulation and administrative burdens undermine innovation potential and hinder the development of smes, and recognises the need to promote market competitiveness by encouraging the use of financial instruments, simplified access to credit and diversification of sources of finance.
in writing. ‒ i support the eu strategy for the alpine region, which covers 7 countries, 5 of which are eu member states (austria, france, germany, italy and slovenia) and 2 non-eu countries (liechtenstein and switzerland), as well as 48 regions with a population of over 80 million citizens. i believe that the strategy covers three important thematic areas. i appreciate that the strategy does not require the use of additional resources, but emphasises the use of funds already in existence (implementation of the esi funds). at the same time, i believe that this document and the experience gained from its development can help in the work on the eu strategy for the carpathian region, which should also be developed and implemented.
in writing. ‒ i voted in favour of the report on the eu strategy for the alpine region. the eusalp strategy is being implemented in a region where different forms of cooperation are already underway, e.g. within the framework of the alpine area and the alpine convention, as well as the various interreg cross-border programmes. eusalp is made up of 48 regions in seven european countries: italy, france, slovenia, austria, germany, switzerland and liechtenstein. the region has a population of about 80 million and is highly attractive for its natural, economic and cultural values. the alpine lowlands and the alpine mountain area are part of an inseparable natural and human system whose interdependence has influenced the entire history of the region. however, difficulties in connections and production logistics have often had a negative impact on the development of mountain areas. in addition, the alpine macro-region is also highly vulnerable to the effects of climate change today. this is why i believe that the public authorities should, in accordance with the principle of subsidiarity, respond to the economic and ecological challenges of the alpine macro-region.
in writing. ‒ the eu strategy for the alpine region covers 7 countries, 5 of which are eu member states (austria, france, germany, italy and slovenia) and 2 non-eu countries (liechtenstein and switzerland), as well as 48 regions with a population of over 80 million citizens. the strategy covers three thematic areas: growth policy, mobility and connectivity, and environmental and energy protection. eusalp provides a framework for policy coordination and territorial cooperation; it aims to ensure mutually beneficial links between mountain regions and the surrounding lowland and urban areas. the report focuses on the potential of the esi funds and other eu funding options for strategic planning in both urban and alpine areas. this strategy does not require the use of additional resources. the existing funds shall be used to implement it and to ensure appropriate coordination. i hereby endorse the report.
in writing. ‒ the main objective of the eu trust fund for africa (eutf) is to promote stability in the regions and to help better manage migration. the union's external action should be directed towards the implementation of the union's external action programmes, in particular the european neighbourhood policy, the european neighbourhood policy and the european neighbourhood policy. then take action to promote equal opportunities in the fields of economy, security and development. the countries covered by the fund are located in three regions of africa (the horn of africa, the sahel and lake chad basin, and north africa). they are some of the most unstable countries on the continent. i shall abstain on that point. the resolution in particular draws attention to the low contribution of the member states, stressing that words and promises alone are not enough this must be translated into action. it stresses the eutf's purpose and calls for a more comprehensive eu solution for emergency funds in the context of this year's review of the 2014-2020 mff. it also warns against a scenario where it is the poorest countries with the least access to other sources of funding that lose out.
in writing. ‒ given the migration crisis, aid to african countries is important and can help to curb illegal migration to the eu. the important aspect is to promote stability and economic development in these countries, because it is the lack of opportunities for decent wages and a sense of security that has forced many people to emigrate. the main condition for ensuring economic development is peace and stability. to this end, african countries should be supported in state-building, the promotion of the rule of law and conflict prevention. the development of employment in local sectors and the guarantee of finding work, as well as the prevention of exploitation of human resources by foreign companies, are also of great importance. in a world of ever-increasing population, young people need to be provided with the right conditions. they should have access to education and employment prospects, leading to sustained economic growth. in addition, efforts must be made to ensure basic public services such as access to medicine, safe food and water. nor should we forget the basic rights of migrants. eu action should focus on humanitarian aid and on combating illegal migration routes and trafficking in human beings. the measures to encourage return and reintegration in the countries of origin should also be promoted.
in writing. ‒ the main objective of the eu trust fund for africa (eutf) signed by the president of the commission together with the 25 eu member states (plus norway and switzerland) and launched at the valletta summit on migration in november 2015 by european and african partners is to help support regional stability and contribute to better migration management. the eu trust fund aims to address the root causes of destabilisation, forced displacement and irregular migration by promoting flexibility, economic opportunity, equality of opportunity, security and development. the eu trust fund for africa was established to provide assistance to 23 countries in three regions of africa (the horn of africa, the sahel and lake chad basin, north africa), covering some of the most fragile african countries, which as countries of origin are vulnerable to migration, transit or destination, or all three, and which can benefit most from this form of eu financial assistance. i hereby abstain from voting.
in writing. ‒ the idea of an eu trust fund for africa was first raised at the valletta european leaders' summit on migration in november 2015. in view of the unprecedented levels of illegal migration, the fund was established to support the african countries most affected by the crisis, to strengthen stability in the region and to promote closer eu-africa cooperation on migration management issues. the report addresses many questions and concerns raised in the context of the establishment of the fund in the areas of financing, implementation and control. the document also called for greater transparency, accountability and policy coherence in the design and implementation of projects, while fully respecting the principles of development effectiveness. the fund must contribute primarily to the long-term objectives of ensuring peace and strengthening governments in countries of origin of illegal immigrants.
in writing. ‒ the african trust fund (eutf) is a vital tool for the development of areas affected by poverty, social and economic destabilisation, migration and lack of access to finance. however, the results of the work so far show that the financing of these actions has not produced the intended effects. the current immigration crisis has contributed to the security of eu citizens. it is our duty to provide humanitarian aid, but we must do so in a responsible and thoughtful manner. in my opinion, the draft resolution does not meet this condition, which is why i opposed its adoption.
in writing. ‒ the eu trust fund for africa (eutf), which was launched in november 2015 in valletta, aims to support stability in african regions and contribute to better migration management. the fund is intended to support the elimination of the root causes of destabilisation, forced displacement and irregular migration in 23 countries in three regions of africa: the horn of africa, the sahel and the lake chad basin, north africa. i abstained from the vote because, while the report promotes a proper approach to migration, it also promotes access to reproductive rights, including abortion.
in writing. ‒ i abstained from the vote on the report, even though i know how important it is to maintain a balance between my personal and professional life. however, most of the calls for action in the report violate the principle of subsidiarity. the maternity leave directive of 2008 has been a failure, and i don't think this is any different. i believe that finding this balance should be the responsibility of each family, not regulated by legislation, as the report seems to suggest.
in writing. ‒ the european union is an ageing society. the decline in the birth rate over the past decades is clear, and it is therefore essential to improve labour market conditions. action should focus on improving access to the labour market for women: creating conditions for women to return to work in the same position after the birth of a child and preventing discrimination on grounds of sex when applying for jobs. in addition, we should facilitate access to parental leave among fathers. the pay gap in the same jobs is still a major problem, which means that mothers are the ones who take leave to look after their children. we must not forget the single mothers who often work overtime to provide a decent living for their children. the conditions must be created in which they can combine work and child-rearing. to this end, we must strive to improve care services and increase their availability. balancing work and private life will not only contribute to an increase in births, but also to economic growth, greater gender equality and a reduction in the risk of poverty.
in writing. ‒ i supported the report on creating a work-life balance in the labour market. in the context of this report, i would like to highlight the need to ensure access to quality childcare and early education for all. we need more investment in creating and expanding child care infrastructure. every child should be guaranteed a place in a care facility after the parents have completed their parental leave. following the resolution, i call on member states to implement the 2002 barcelona targets for childcare infrastructure and to endorse the 2014 quality framework for early childhood education and care. providing adequate childcare, as part of a work-life balance strategy, is also key to increasing women's employment.
in writing. ‒ there is no doubt that for many families, reconciling private life with work is a huge challenge. it is therefore necessary to take initiatives to increase the flexibility of work, to promote part-time work and different forms of remote work. in addition, improving the availability of places in daycare centres, kindergartens and full-time childcare facilities is a key aspect of work-life balance. however, action in this area should be taken at national level by the governments of the individual member states, not at union level. the issue of maternity, paternity, parental or carer's leave is a matter for the member states alone. the european union's intervention in these areas violates the fundamental principle of subsidiarity, which requires that only those actions are taken at european level which cannot be implemented effectively and efficiently at national level. unfortunately, many of the proposals in this report fall short of this principle, which is why i have decided not to support it in the vote.
in writing. ‒ the report is a response to the european parliament's roadmap on the challenges faced by working families in balancing family and work life, published in august 2015. it addresses issues relevant to the family: the demographic crisis, the risk of poverty (including among children), the importance of work-life balance, the condemnation of the culture of employee availability, family care for the disabled and the exchange of good practices in family policy. however, it should be noted that work-life balance is about allowing families and other working people to find their own ways of dividing time between work and family or time for themselves, rather than bringing more women into the workforce and leaving more men at home, as the report seems to suggest. moreover, most of the calls for action in the report violate the principle of subsidiarity by interfering with the competences of the member states. that is why, despite the many positive comments in the report, i abstained.

in writing. ‒ in the year 2000 an agreement on the free movement of persons between switzerland and the eu-15 was signed. coming into force in 2002, this agreement has since then been extended. it was applied to the 10 new member states, only to be amended yet again after the accession of bulgaria and romania. now it has to be extended once again for the newest member of the european union, croatia. switzerland and the eu have an undeniably strong tie in several aspects, which both parties benefit from. with this in mind, we have to apply the principle of non-discrimination, including equal treatment, and therefore vote in favour of this protocol. from political, to economic, to cultural aspects, the signing of protocol iii will enable croatia and switzerland to profit in those areas, and will additionally expand the internal market, where the free movement is essential.

in writing. ‒ the issue of workers' rights is one of the most widely discussed in the eu today. the increasing popularity of flexible forms of work or the forcing of workers to self-employment, especially in a cross-border context, is contributing to the development of pathology and to the non-compliance by employers with the existing rules on social security or working time. it is one thing to criticise and actually combat such abuses, but quite another to try to attribute to them the objective economic differences between member states. the concept of 'social dumping' which is the subject of this report is extremely imprecise and should not be used in this discussion. it is a misunderstanding to treat the disparity between the minimum wage and social benefits in poland and germany as a form of unfair competition. this interpretation, which the report unfortunately indirectly supports, is extremely dangerous for polish companies that send their employees to provide services throughout the eu and for transport companies that have already been affected by the extremely restrictive minimum wage rules in france and germany. i agree with the intentions of the authors of this report, as long as they were sincere, that decent wages and adequate working conditions are non-negotiable and that workers' rights must be protected and enforced. however, i do not think that this report is acceptable in its present form, which is why i voted against its adoption by the european parliament.

in writing. ‒ i voted in favour of the report on the proposal for a regulation of the european parliament and of the council on the european travel document for the return of illegally staying third-country nationals. the increase in the rate of return of irregular migrants is crucial for the integrity of the eu asylum system, for cooperation between eu member states and third countries and for maintaining the trust of eu citizens. the eu's external action must be coordinated with the member states and the commission, and the eu's external action must be coordinated with the member states and the commission. the commission has also provided information on the number of returnees who have been granted a residence permit in the member state concerned. by standardising the format of the travel document, member states will reduce red tape, discrepancies, costs and waiting times in the hope of achieving wider recognition of the document by third countries. in my view, ensuring the exchange of information between member states on the issuing of travel documents and on persons registered as illegally staying third-country nationals without valid travel documents will contribute to increasing the level of mutual recognition of asylum decisions in the eu and to avoiding secondary movements of persons who have been refused asylum.
in writing. ‒ this report updates the european standard travel document, which was created in 1994 to speed up the return of third-country nationals illegally staying in eu countries without valid passports or identity documents. many eu countries are currently facing serious difficulties in organising the safe and legal return of these people to their countries. the acceptance of the replacement documents used by the member states by the countries of destination is currently low due to insufficient security details and different formats. the lack of valid travel documents issued by certain third countries is also a major obstacle to the success of the return process. the review of this document creates a common format for the european travel document. the new technical data contained in it would also include personal data. the application of the same security features as those established in 2002 for visas issued by eu countries to residents without valid travel documents should result in greater recognition of documents and a reduction in the administrative burden both within the eu and for the authorities of the countries of destination. i hereby endorse the report.
in writing. ‒ in 2014, eu member states issued almost half a million return orders for migrants who do not have the right to enter or stay in the eu. however, only 40% of them actually returned to a non-eu country. one of the main obstacles to return is the lack of valid travel documents for returnees. the effective return of third-country nationals who do not fulfil or no longer fulfil the conditions for entry, stay or residence in the eu is essential to ensure the credibility and proper functioning of the eu's migration policy and to reduce and deter illegal migration. the report rightly emphasises the need for eu member states to ensure the effective use of the european return travel document, which will contain information on the departure and arrival of a third-country national. it is also necessary to strengthen cooperation with diplomatic missions in this regard, while respecting applicable international law and european union law.
in writing. ‒ the european travel document is an instrument essential for the proper management of asylum policy. the european union has a duty to protect and ensure the security of its citizens and it is therefore unacceptable that it does not exercise control over persons who are not covered by the union's asylum policy. it is necessary to speed up the process of issuing and standardising documents and to introduce a security system so that such persons can leave the borders of the european union without undue delay. i voted to support the resolution.

in writing. ‒ the conference of the parties to the convention on international trade in endangered species of wild fauna and flora (cites) will take place in johannesburg from 24 september to 5 october, with the eu as a party for the first time. cities is an intergovernmental agreement designed to ensure that trade in endangered species does not lead to their extinction. i supported this report because it contains specific recommendations on transparency of decision-making, improved reporting, financing and enforcement, rules to combat illicit trade and corruption, and species-specific proposals. the project also supports the proposals of the eu and its member states, in particular those relating to the fight against corruption and the establishment of standards for trophy hunting, and the extension of the cites scope to protect certain species imported into the eu as pets and certain movable objects.
in writing. ‒ i voted in favour of the report on the application of the postal services directive. the 2008 amendment to the postal services legislation has allowed the key objectives of liberalising european postal services to be achieved. since the full opening in 2008, the postal market has undergone a major transformation. on the one hand, the volume of paper correspondence has decreased in many member states. on the other hand, new technologies are increasing the convenience of online shopping and, as a result, the number of parcels delivered by postal operators is increasing. good quality postal services are an essential part of communication in the eu internal market and the eu postal sector continues to make a significant contribution to strengthening social, economic and territorial cohesion and to the development of the digital single market. in my view, promoting competition in this sector is also important in achieving the europe 2020 strategy's objectives of sustainable growth and a more competitive economy.
in writing. ‒ i voted in favour of the report on the application of the postal services directive. speaking of postal services. in my view, we must focus primarily on improving the free movement of services within the european union and increasing their availability and accessibility at national and transnational level, while adapting to economic, social and technical changes. i would like to stress the need to improve transparency and price attractiveness, to introduce a functional mechanism for resolving disputes and complaints, and to provide technological solutions to enable clear monitoring of consignments. it is also necessary to increase the universality and geographical coverage of postal services so that citizens living in rural, mountainous or remote regions have access to high-quality services that meet their needs. the rights of postal workers, whose high mobility requires, among other things, the guarantee of a safe working environment and health protection, remain an important issue.
in writing. ‒ the 2008 amendment to the postal services legislation has achieved the key objectives of liberalising european postal services. however, since the full opening in 2008, the postal services market has undergone a huge transformation. on the one hand, the volume of paper correspondence has decreased in many member states. on the other hand, new technologies are increasing the convenience of online shopping and thus the number of parcels delivered by postal operators. as a result, more than half of the postal sector's total revenue comes from parcel and express deliveries. the report stresses the obligation to provide, on affordable terms, a high-quality universal service covering at least five days of delivery and five days of collection per week for every eu citizen. it was also stressed that given the limitations of each market operators should be allowed some flexibility to organise this universal service. the independence of national regulatory authorities was noted and the emphasis was placed on interoperability and it was stressed that each member state has a certain margin of discretion in the application of the postal services directive. i hereby endorse the report.
in writing. ‒ good quality postal services are an essential part of communication in the eu's internal market. from the collection, transport, sorting and delivery of letters and parcels to homes and offices, postal service providers offer a wide range of services at affordable prices. other sectors such as e-commerce, publishing, mail order, insurance, banking and advertising are heavily dependent on the postal infrastructure. the eu postal sector therefore remains a key contributor to social, economic and territorial cohesion and to the development of the digital single market. in recent years, the postal services market has undergone a profound transformation, which has resulted in a decrease in the number of letters sent, a rapid increase in the number of parcels delivered, linked to the popularity of electronic commerce, and the emergence of new customer needs. the european union must therefore adapt its regulations to these changes. the focus should be primarily on improving the quality and accessibility of universal service provision and on making cross-border parcel delivery more accessible. moreover, emphasis should be placed on market surveillance to identify anti-competitive practices and to increase price transparency for retail users and businesses. it is also important to promote value-added services such as tracking of consignments and flexible delivery.
in writing. ‒ postal services are an important element in the efficient transmission of information, regional development and the overcoming of territorial barriers. the turnover of letter items is declining, while the number of parcels delivered is steadily increasing, to the benefit of the consumer market. employment in these services is expected to increase in the coming years. it is important that the member states of the european union continue to take care of the liberalisation of this market segment, which is why i voted in favour of the motion for a resolution.
in writing. ‒ the postal services market has undergone a major transformation in recent years. the demand for traditional postal services is decreasing due to technological developments, while the demand for parcel delivery is increasing, mainly due to the expansion of online shops. the provision of basic postal services is recognised as one of the obligations of the state, and it is therefore important to discuss the scope of the universal postal service obligation. a comprehensive knowledge of developments in the postal market is important in order to obtain a global picture of the market. the crossborder parcel delivery market, which has significant growth potential, should be an area of particular interest, and i therefore support the commission's efforts to support the development of this market sector. i also support the commission's efforts to launch a platform that brings together all the information on market players. such actions will be beneficial first and foremost to the customer and to the possibility of making the best choice for him.
in writing. ‒ the report focuses on the current situation of small and medium-sized enterprises in europe, highlighting the potential benefits and risks that european smes have had to face and still have to face. smes and midcaps are a significant part of the eu economy. that's why their access to funding is so important. during the crisis, smes had more limited access to finance than larger companies. factors such as the high reliance of smes on bank lending and the deleveraging of banks caused by the crisis have contributed to this. diversification of sme financing opportunities is therefore one of the priorities of the cmu initiative and the report considers such opportunities, with an emphasis on innovative financial instruments. the report also stresses the need for administrative and tax facilitation for smes, as a simple and fair tax system is the best way to guarantee the development of smes. the role of banks should not be ignored, as bank loans remain the most important source of sme financing. it is also important to increase the knowledge of smes themselves about all sources of funding. i hereby endorse the report.
in writing. ‒ small and medium-sized enterprises and midcaps make up a significant part of the european union's economy. increasing access to finance has long been a priority for the eu, but the crisis in recent years has severely limited the scope for its implementation. the aim of the capital markets union currently in place is to diversify funding opportunities for smes. the european parliament's report analyses the entire life cycle of smes from a financing point of view and proposes to improve financing conditions at all stages. the report concludes that bank loans remain the most important source of finance for smes, but that improvements are needed in this area. the document also stresses the need to maintain a supportive factor for smes in relation to capital requirements. in a situation where almost 99% of all enterprises are small and medium-sized enterprises, it is necessary to take measures to facilitate their access to finance. that is why i have decided to vote in favour of parliament's report.
in writing. ‒ the sme sector plays a vital role in the economic development of the member states, in generating their gdp and in creating new jobs, and it is therefore essential to open up new sources of finance for these entities. the focus should be on banking (loans, loans) and non-bank (public issue, securitisation, crowdfunding) methods of raising capital to enable enterprises to diversify their contributions to their business. i support the solutions presented in the report.
madam president! small and medium-sized enterprises are the foundation of the eu economy. as many as 99% of companies in the union are in this group and they account for nearly two thirds of jobs. moreover, in times of crisis, they have proved to be the most stable element of the european economy and the main creator of new jobs. on the other hand, it should be borne in mind that these jobs are not always of good quality. the source of this situation is to be found in the difficult situation of this segment of companies. member state governments very often give preferential treatment only to multinational corporations, offering them special legal status and tax benefits, while local, small and medium-sized enterprises do not enjoy these privileges. this unequal competition forces them to reduce their labour costs. if we want to improve the labour market, we should therefore first of all give more support to small and medium-sized enterprises in their unequal struggle against global corporations. this will not only help to create new jobs but also to improve the quality of existing ones. it also appears that in this context the european commission needs to assess the impact of the decision to grant china market economy status on the quantity and quality of jobs in the european sme sector. there is a high risk that a positive decision on this issue will contribute to the deterioration of the situation of small and medium-sized enterprises and thus to the deterioration of the situation on the european labour market. that is why i voted for the directive.
in writing. ‒ smes have created 85% of jobs in europe over the last decade. in 2015, small firms contributed to 71% of the increase in employment in non-financial sectors. despite the rules governing the internal market in the european union, there are still wide disparities in the regulatory framework for smes. the strong regional variation among member states should be taken into account more when assessing and measuring the impact of eu policies. due to the multiple obstacles to job creation, the principle of the universal model has proved to be discriminatory for the sme sector. in addition, the lack of macroeconomic stability and transparent regulations has resulted in a disadvantageous environment for smes in many countries that joined the union after 2004 and in euro area countries that are experiencing a crisis. the rapporteur stressed that in order to create a robust environment for entrepreneurship and to increase the potential for job creation, national and european policies should focus primarily on the issue of skills, legal uncertainty and administrative burdens, and the problem of unregistered work. the rapporteur also drew attention to the need to guarantee a level playing field for smes in terms of their competitive position compared to large corporations. small and local firms are particularly disadvantaged in over-regulated and bureaucratic administrative systems. i hereby endorse the report.
in writing. ‒ smes create more jobs than all other private sector jobs, providing about two thirds of employment in the eu. in recent crisis years, they have been the biggest job creators and are often innovative, active internationally and employ young people. the opportunities for smes are even greater, but action is needed at national and eu level to strengthen their job creation potential. the report rightly emphasises that the main issue is the reduction of administrative burdens. smes, because of their smaller size structure, do not have the same absorption capacity with regard to regulatory standards as large companies. over-regulation is hampering the competitiveness of businesses and their job creation potential. the parliament's report rightly emphasises the need to create an environment that encourages investment while promoting sustainable growth and the creation of quality jobs. it is also necessary to enforce the rules on equal access of smes to public procurement. the report also rightly highlighted the importance of the 'erasmus for entrepreneurs' programme, which helps young entrepreneurs to acquire the knowledge and useful skills necessary to start and run a successful business. i think it is a very good document, which is why i have decided to vote in favour of it.
in writing. ‒ the european labour market is facing a serious problem of unemployment and the need to match labour supply and demand, and therefore it is necessary to stimulate certain segments of the economy. supporting the sme sector through the launch of apprenticeship programmes, access to capital and unlocking potential through simplification of law and taxation, reducing the privileged role of large groups and reducing the share of undeclared work can be of great importance. i agree with the rapporteur's recommendation that member states implement the 'think small first' principle and therefore support the draft resolution.
in writing. ‒ the report shows that although there are internal market rules in the european union that create a regulatory framework for smes, there are still differences in the stability of this framework. the main problems facing smes are over-regulation and misapplication of the rules that favour and give preferential treatment to large and large enterprises in the eu, and the lack of adequately trained staff. in view of these problems, as well as the problems facing modern europe: unemployment, mismatched jobs, demographic crisis, immigration, it is appropriate to exploit and support the potential of small and medium-sized enterprises, which are the engine and pillar of the european economy and offer significant job creation potential. the report noted the need to look at the regulations and the environment in which they exist in order to make the most of their potential.
madam president! fifteen years after the adoption of the employment equality directive, we seem to have accumulated a certain amount of knowledge and experience which allows us to assess not only the effectiveness of the measures adopted in the directive but also the persistence of the discrimination phenomenon in the area in question. the fundamental problem for which we have not found an effective solution is the lack of awareness of the existence of discrimination, both on the part of the victims and on the part of the discriminators. so there is a huge difficulty in combating this phenomenon and its persistence. therefore, specific action by the union, the member states and the social partners is necessary to raise awareness of discriminatory behaviour and practices in employment. raising awareness will eliminate many pathological situations at relatively low cost. there is another reason why this seems justified: in recent months, we have seen a growing wave of hatred in the union, not only against muslims but also against citizens of other member states. the rise of nationalism and xenophobia has led not only to discrimination against workers within the single market, but also to the brutal assaults and beatings that poles in the uk have recently experienced. it is therefore urgent that action be taken to stem the tide. the conclusions of the european parliament on the application of the equal treatment directive are therefore necessary, which is why i voted in favour of mrs weber's report.
in writing. ‒ non-discrimination and respect for human rights are among the fundamental values on which the eu is founded. the union's objective is to strive to combat all practices of discrimination based on sex, age, religion, race, colour or descent. although many countries have incorporated the prohibition of discrimination into their legal systems, the law is still not fully applied. the labour market is one area where discrimination occurs. this is illustrated, for example, by the fact that women are more affected by unemployment than men. it's mostly pregnant women and mothers. this also applies to older people, who have a very high unemployment rate and can contribute their experience and knowledge to companies. to tackle this problem, we must work towards the elimination of all forms of discrimination, not just those in the labour market. existing law should be applied consistently and the enforcement of rights should be facilitated by providing for free legal aid and simplifying procedures. we should also develop programmes to facilitate adaptation to changing work environments.
in writing. ‒ this implementation report addresses the challenges of implementing the employment equality directive adopted 15 years ago, with particular attention to horizontal aspects, sexual orientation, religion and belief, age and disability. very little data on equality remains available, as the directive does not impose an obligation on member states to collect such data. the general nature of the report is to be welcomed, since its aim is only to give an overview of the current situation and to encourage member states to implement the provisions of the directive more fully. there are several elements in it that may be troubling, such as references to the proposed anti-discrimination directive, the maternity leave directive and lgbti. i therefore abstained.
in writing. ‒ equal treatment in employment and occupation is a prerequisite for the development of the eu economies. there is no doubt that despite the enormous progress made, women, disabled people and minorities are still treated worse by employers than men. moreover, unfortunately, in many areas, they still face problems, barriers and clear inequalities. this is reflected in particular in the different pay levels for men and women for the same work. in addition, the most discriminated social groups in the area of employment are jews, sikhs and muslims (especially women). religious beliefs should not have any influence on the assessment of the quality of the work of an employee or on the perception of the employee as capable or unable to perform his duties. the report presented touches on many issues that are crucial to achieving equality in employment and work, but the rapporteur has gone beyond the community's powers in the text she has prepared. the call on the european commission to submit urgently a new draft directive on maternity leave and to strengthen the rules on paternity leave cannot be implemented, as family policy is a matter for the exclusive competence of the member states. it should also be stressed that no proposals should impose disproportionate burdens on employers or service providers, as weakening them will have a negative impact on the labour market, with the main detriment being for workers.
in writing. ‒ the search for appropriate legislative solutions on equal treatment in the labour market is an important objective of the eu's common policy. however, the report addresses issues of worldview that are contrary to the traditions, culture, social and legal order of certain member states. the aspects of non-discrimination on grounds of age, sex and disability are fully acceptable, but the other provisions on the recognition of partnership or parental rights should be treated with a certain degree of reservation, so that these measures are not imposed against the will of the member states. that's why i decided to abstain.
in writing. ‒ despite cultural progress and the efforts of society and its institutions to reduce discrimination, we still cannot speak of equal treatment, in the case of this report, in the area of employment and work. there are still significant disparities between women's and men's pay and pensions. it is not just sex that is a differentiating factor the report also deals with inequalities due to religious beliefs, disability or age. it is our duty to eliminate all discriminatory practices through institutional action and to identify desirable solutions. however, this important report contains provisions which interfere with the competences of the eu member states, and i therefore abstained.

in writing. ‒ the egf has undergone a number of changes since 2006. these include a reduction in the intervention criteria from 1000 exemptions to 500 exemptions. this means that the egf is more accessible to regions and smaller member states. there have been proposals to further reduce the number of exemptions, which have been met with strong opposition. the intervention period was extended from 12 to 24 months. the egf is an exceptional fund and is outside the multiannual financial framework. a reserve has been created from which annual resources for the fund can be drawn. the annual appropriation for the egf in the eu budget has been reduced from eur 500 million per year in 2007 to eur 150 million in the current regulation. the average value of the appropriations allocated over 8 years (2007-2014) was eur 70 million per year. the co-financing rate was initially 50%, then increased to 65% in 2009-2011, reduced again to 50% in 2012-2013 and increased to 60% in the 2013 regulation for 2014-2020. eligible actions include personalised training to enable the acquisition of new skills and the change of skills, job search assistance, mentoring, entrepreneurship promotion, self-employment, business start-up and employee take-over assistance, and allowances for transfer costs, maintenance costs or training allowances. i therefore supported the report.

member of the commission. – mr president, i would like to thank the committee on development and its chair, ms linda mcavan, for putting nutrition high on the development agenda in line with our commitment to the un 2030 agenda and sustainable development goals. the resolution on malnutrition proposed by the committee is, in our view, an important step forward. since 2012, the commission has emerged as a world leader in the nutrition arena. this leadership is backed by a robust policy framework addressing both stunting and wasting. over the last three years, we have observed a trend pointing towards the decrease of stunting. our first progress report on the european commission’s nutrition action plan shows that we are well on track to reach the commitment of reducing the number of stunted children under the age of five by seven million by 2025. our further actions on nutrition and food security should be guided by the approach that would seek to strike the right balance between our preferred nutrition-sensitive interventions that address the multiple nature of undernutrition and malnutrition causes, including food insecurity, health, sanitation, social safety nets and inequalities, and the needed nutrition—specific interventions. this balance is to be better assessed in the programming exercise with partner countries and other donors. this may also include a further look into our development instruments in 2017. we have taken due note of parliament’s request to increase the commission’s funding for nutrition-specific actions. in this context, the commission has put forward the following approach: we should maximise the synergies and complementarities of our development and humanitarian responses to nutrition and food security needs, having in mind that humanitarian responses are, in principle, nutrition-specific. we will promote programming coordination with other donors, who can focus on nutrition-specific interventions, thus complementing the commission’s focus on nutrition-sensitive issues. we shall also advocate at global level, especially through the scaling up nutrition (sun) movement, to increase investment in nutrition, including nutrition-specific investments by both donors and developing countries. the first results of this three-pronged approach are encouraging, notably in rwanda, ethiopia, niger, mali, bangladesh, laos and guatemala. we support partner countries in developing and implementing their own true multi—sectoral nutrition action plans, which combine nutrition-specific and nutrition-sensitive interventions. this also allows donors to align their support to national priorities and coordinate the division of nutrition efforts. the commission has gained a strong record and evidence in supporting nutrition, mainly through the agriculture, education, water or health sectors. however, the commission is exploring other areas, such as social safety nets, which have proved to be successful in improving nutrition – particularly in mali. in this context, the commission and the club du sahel are organising a major event on social protection for nutrition in abuja in december. the objective will be to further increase investments and to reduce undernutrition faster, while putting women, children, and small farmers at the centre of nutrition actions. at the global level, the commission will continue advocating further investment in nutrition, notably through the scaling up nutrition movement. we should also explore with the sun movement the opportunity to organise a pledging event for nutrition in the coming years.

in writing. ‒ the paris agreement, signed by the 28 eu member states in new york in april 2016, underlines the importance of action to combat climate change and clearly sets the goal of achieving a 'climate-neutral world economy'. among its key provisions was the idea of limiting global warming to below 2°c compared to the pre-industrial era (targeted at 1.5°c), and a clear message that a shift away from the use of scarce natural resources such as fossil fuels towards clean renewable energy was needed. all countries have also committed to take mitigation measures that will enable them to meet their stated targets (the eu has committed to reducing emissions by at least 40% by 2030). they will also meet every five years to report on progress in reducing greenhouse gas emissions. in total, including the european community countries, 195 countries have signed and ratified the agreement, which is set to enter into force if ratified by at least 55 signatories, responsible for at least 55% of global emissions. the european union is playing a leading role in the international arena in combating climate change, and in the document adopted today we call for the agreement to be ratified as soon as possible.
in writing. ‒ a swift decision by the eu to ratify the paris agreement under the united nations framework convention on climate change (unfccc) will send a strong signal and highlight the primary role of the eu and its member states, as well as their efforts to prevent climate change at international level. implementation of the paris agreement will play a key role in global efforts to combat climate change and limit the rise in global average temperature to below 2°c pre-industrial levels. the formal entry into force of the paris agreement is a key priority for the eu. i hereby endorse the report.
in writing. ‒ on 4 october 2016, the european parliament approved the ratification of the paris agreement by the eu. this is a very important, first ever binding climate agreement. europe has built a front for ambitious environmental and climate goals, as president juncker also stressed in his speech. the eu, which has been the main architect of the agreement, has also signed it, symbolically crossing the threshold of at least 55 parties, representing at least 55% of global emissions, to allow it to enter into force. however, it should be emphasised that reduction efforts and the promotion of climate-friendly solutions must be pursued without prejudice to development and innovation, and must take into account in detail the specific nature of different sectors (e.g. energy, transport, agriculture). it is worth noting that agriculture and forestry have a special relationship with the climate and the environment, as they are the only ones that, in addition to emitting greenhouse gases into the atmosphere, also have a huge potential to absorb and store compounds that affect climate warming.
in writing. ‒ the paris agreement is the summation of global efforts to combat climate change and limit the rise in global average temperatures. it is part of the eu's sustainable development policy, which must reconcile economic growth with the need to preserve the environment for future generations. the member states of the european union played a significant role in the negotiation of this agreement. a swift decision to ratify will underline the primary role of member states in driving action at international level to prevent climate change. the european union's formal consent to be bound by the convention will mark the completion of the ratification threshold and thus the entry into force of the paris agreement as early as november this year. for the above reasons, i support this recommendation.
