in writing. ‒ i supported the recommendation on the eu-people's republic of china agreement on the short-stay visa waiver for holders of diplomatic passports, because in my view the agreement is beneficial. it is very important that china is a partner in many aspects of the eu. visa-free travel for holders of diplomatic passports would undoubtedly help to maintain contacts between these countries. i therefore voted in favour.
in writing. ‒ the eu and china launched a dialogue on migration and mobility in 2013. in this context, visa-free travel for holders of diplomatic passports is currently proposed. the council has already approved the agreement in january 2016. the agreement provides for visa-free travel for a maximum of 90 days in any 180-day period. the measure concerns the schengen area and does not apply to the united kingdom and ireland. in the case of france and the netherlands, the agreement applies only to european territories. both china and the eu can suspend the application of the agreement or terminate it only for all eu member states taken together. this means that situations such as the us and canada, which require visas only from some, but not all, eu member states, will not be possible. the agreement applies to all holders of diplomatic passports, including members of the european parliament holding diplomatic passports. i hereby endorse the recommendation.
in writing. ‒ the agreement on the short-stay visa waiver for holders of diplomatic passports is one of the fruits of the dialogue between the european union and china on migration and mobility that began in 2013. it is worth noting that under this agreement, china will not be able to suspend or terminate its visa-free regime only with selected eu member states. the council approved the agreement in january 2016. i believe that the european parliament should give its consent to the conclusion of this agreement, especially since it covers all holders of diplomatic passports.
in writing. ‒ i supported the proposal to address the problem in member states that are experiencing or threatened with serious difficulties in financial stability. given the consequences of the financial and economic crisis facing the member states, the smooth implementation of the european structural and investment funds is of particular importance. i believe that the proposed solution, which does not alter the annual ceilings of the mff for commitments and payments, is the best response to the temporary liquidity problems in the member states.
in writing. ‒ the financial and economic crisis put pressure on national economies and member states have taken austerity measures to balance their budgets. in this context, it is important to ensure the smooth implementation of the eu's main financial instrument, namely the european structural and investment funds. the proposed legislative changes may result in a temporary increase in payment appropriations, which would be offset by lower payments at the end of the implementation of the 2014-2020 programmes. this should not entail changes to the annual ceilings of the multiannual financial framework for commitments and payments set out in annex i to regulation (eu) no 1311/2013. i hereby endorse the report.
in writing. ‒ the economic crisis has shaken the balance of the economies of the member states of the european union. despite austerity policies, many of them still face, at least temporarily, serious difficulties in financial stability and require support. we should mobilise the resources of the structural and investment funds to this end. the proposed amendments to the regulation will provide for a temporary increase in payment appropriations. at the same time, such a move should not entail any negative changes to the annual ceilings of the mff. the increase will be offset by lower payments at the end of the 2014-2020 programming period, so it will remain budget neutral. in view of the above, i voted in favour of the resolution.
in writing. ‒ i voted in favour of the motion to waive the immunity of jean-marie le pen, because i wanted to express my disapproval of the behaviour of this mep. the commission of acts such as incitement to discrimination, hatred and violence against a person or group of persons on the grounds of their origin or ethnicity is simply unworthy and unacceptable. jean-marie le pen is accused of public incitement to racial hatred, and a video posted online on june 6, 2014 was presented as evidence in the case. although the situation described is not strictly connected with the performance of the duties of a member of the european parliament, i believe that such behaviour should be condemned and therefore voted in favour of the request for waiver of immunity.
in writing. - in view of the suspicion of a criminal offence, i have decided to comply with the request of the investigating magistrates of the grand tribunal in paris. parliamentary immunity is an additional safeguard for freedom of expression, so that judicial proceedings do not block the courageous work of active members of parliament. but the exercise of that freedom is subject to certain limits, which are determined by respect for the rights and freedoms of others.
in writing. ‒ i supported the application for privileges and immunities by jane collins, who was accused of defaming three labour party members (sarah champion, john healey and kevin barron). ms. collins' statement was about the fact that, according to her, they knew about the sexual abuse of a minor, but they didn't take any action because of political correctness, their cowardice and selfishness. the situation described took place in 2014, therefore the defamation is not linked to the performance of the duties of ms collins as an mep. i therefore voted in favour.
in writing. ‒ mep jane collins has been accused of defamation and libel in a speech she gave at a party congress. jane collins considered that the civil proceedings against her prevented her from attending parliamentary sittings. the mep considered that this was in breach of article 7 of the protocol on the privileges and immunities of the eu and therefore applied for the privileges set out in the protocol. it should be noted, however, that article 7 does not apply to restrictions resulting from judicial proceedings and therefore the member's request on that basis was inadmissible. there are also no grounds for applying articles 8 and 9 of the protocol in the jane collins case. the protection conferred by article 8 shall be limited to opinions expressed in the performance of the member's duties. jane collins' statement was not related to her work in the european parliament, but was made in a national political debate. the mps were also not entitled to protection under article 9. it provides that, during the ep session, its members enjoy the immunities accorded to members of their national parliament in their own country, whereas members of the united kingdom parliament do not enjoy immunity from criminal or civil proceedings. consequently, there is no legal basis for jane collins to claim immunity.
in writing. ‒ i supported the request for the exercise of the privileges and immunities of the member of parliament by mr mario borghezzi, in connection with the criminal proceedings against him in italy. the case concerns a statement by mario borghezio, in which he expressed racist and hateful attitudes, and thus insulted mr kashetu (born in congo), who was appointed minister of integration in italy. as this resignation took place in 2013, it is not related to the performance of the duties of maria borghezio as an mep. i therefore voted in favour of the request for the member to enjoy the privileges and immunities of a member of the european parliament.
in writing. - i voted in favour of the report. the provisions governing the privileges and immunities of members of the european parliament are intended, inter alia, to ensure that they are not subject to investigation, prosecution or detention for opinions or positions expressed in the course of their duties. it is clear that freedom of expression is protected, but only if there is a link between the conduct in question and parliamentary activity. in italy, a court found that mario borghezio, a member of the european parliament, had expressed views that allegedly reflected racial and ethnic hatred on a radio broadcast. under italian law, this constitutes a criminal offence and a ground for criminal proceedings. the termination was also contrary to the prohibition of discrimination laid down in the eu charter of fundamental rights. it cannot therefore be assumed that mr borghezio's views were expressed in the course of the performance of his duties as a member of parliament. i therefore consider that he should not be granted immunity in the criminal proceedings against him.
in writing. ‒ i voted against the proposal on the collection of data on goods, passengers and accidents in rail transport. in this respect, a balance needs to be struck between ensuring greater safety for passengers and the railway itself and imposing an excessive burden on member states that are required to collect data. i feel that the content of the conclusion suggests that there is a high risk of overburdening the state and i am against bureaucracy. those arguments were overwhelming in my decision to vote against.
in writing. ‒ more statistical data can contribute to better transport policy planning and to improving rail safety. on the other hand, a balance should be struck between those benefits and the possible burden on member states and respondents that would result from the collection of additional data. the compromise reached is that no new categories of data will be collected. this will facilitate access to existing data, for example on the accessibility of stations for disabled persons and persons with reduced mobility. in view of the above, i voted in favour of the resolution.
in writing. ‒ i voted in favour of the adoption of a regulation on rail transport statistics in the european union. in the current financial perspective, we are right to emphasise railway investment. they should reduce road traffic and protect the environment by improving the fluidity of rail transport. this growing scale of investment, which amounts to tens of billions of euros in the european union, also requires control of how the money is spent, which is not possible without reliable statistics. however, it appears that the information collected cannot relate exclusively to the number of passengers and goods carried. equally important would be data on infrastructure, in particular on the rail traffic management system. improvement in this area is essential for the operational performance of the rail transport system in europe. another problem is cross-border investment to improve rail traffic between countries. it therefore appears necessary to separate a specific part of the statistics for cross-border railway infrastructure investments.
in writing. ‒ i voted in favour of the compilation of statistics on inland waterway freight transport. the purpose of the proposal is to align the provisions on comitology in regulation (ec) no 1365/2006 with the delegated and implementing acts. in my view, it is important to try to align the rules with the delegated and implementing acts. i welcome the fact that, as agreed between the european union bodies, the conduct of pilot studies (to assess the feasibility and cost of such a study) will be voluntary. i am convinced that this is a good thing for the eu transport economy and i therefore voted in favour.
in writing. ‒ i voted against the directive on the eu legal framework for customs infringements and sanctions because it contains elements that are contrary to the principles of better law-making. in the context of the imposition of non-criminal sanctions, the directive aims at approximating the laws, regulations and administrative provisions of the member states. in my view, the text of the directive does not fulfil its intended purpose and i also believe that the implementation of the new rules could result in practical problems and a lack of flexibility in contacts between member states and trading partners. for the reasons i have just given, i voted against.

in writing. ‒ draft amending budget (dab) no 3 for 2016 concerns the security of the eu institutions in the light of the recent terrorist attacks in europe. the commission shall be empowered to adopt delegated acts in accordance with article 26 to supplement this regulation by laying down detailed rules for the implementation of this regulation. of this amount, eur 3,5 million will be allocated to the european schools, eur 5 million to the european commission and eur 0,2 million to the european parliament. the strengthening of parliament is achieved by the employment of 35 additional security staff to provide armed protection for strategic points in parliament's buildings. although the amount of eur 15,8 million for payments can be transferred from another budget line, the related commitment appropriations have to be covered by a margin in the administrative section of the eu budget due to the higher than expected depreciation of salaries and pensions last year. in view of the need to strengthen the security measures of the eu institutions, i supported the report.

in writing. ‒ i voted against the report which i feel lays out the eu's strategy towards iran after the nuclear deal in an inaccurate and unclear way. i believe that in matters of such importance, one cannot afford to compromise. the eu in exchange for the lifting of the draconian sanctions against iran received a promise from iran to curb its nuclear threat activities. the rapporteur is not optimistic about the eu's role in the nuclear deal and its relations with the country. and given the situation in the middle east, the human rights abuses and the regional conflicts, i voted against.
in writing. ‒ relations between the eu, its member states and the international community and iran are slowly softening following the successful agreement on iran's nuclear ambitions in july 2015. negotiations between iran and the p5+1 started in 2006, but have intensified recently, resulting in an agreement recently. the p5+1 wanted to limit iran's nuclear threat. under the vienna agreement, iran's nuclear program was removed from the list of dangerous activities. however, it remains unclear how these findings will affect broader regional issues in the middle east, including the iran-saudi arabia proxy war, the shia-sunni sectarian conflict, the conflict in syria, and relations with israel. the afet report commends the eu, in particular for its role in the nuclear settlement, and the rapporteur's assessment of relations with iran as a regional actor is positive. the eu has made rapid progress towards normalising relations with iran despite general reservations about the human rights situation in the country and its role in the regional conflict. however, a more precise reflection of the eu-iran relationship should be ensured. i could not support the report.
in writing. ‒ the july 2015 nuclear deal with iran and the country's internal political situation have created a unique opportunity for reform and improved relations with the european union. on the one hand, european businesses will be able to invest in iran after 10 years of a complete freeze on trade, and on the other hand, we have succeeded in eliminating a country that may have nuclear weapons. moreover, iran has some of the world's largest oil and gas reserves and deepening energy cooperation between the union and the republic of iran could play an important role in diversifying the eu's energy supply sources and reducing the energy dependence of member states on a single supplier russia. the european parliament's report rightly stressed the need to monitor the situation in iran on a continuous basis, in particular with regard to respect for human rights, democracy and the rule of law. i believe that there are values more important than economic growth and increased investment - and those are undoubtedly peace and security.
in writing. ‒ following strong pressure from the international community, the iranian authorities have agreed to negotiations aimed at limiting the country's nuclear programme. the member states of the european union have made a significant contribution to the adoption of these arrangements and to the normalisation of relations with iran. despite these achievements, we should continue to monitor the nuclear threat posed by iran and strive to ensure that the eu's relations with iran are balanced, transparent and based on facts. as a forum for international exchange and debate, the european parliament should not shy away from raising legitimate concerns, especially in the face of human rights violations and the escalation of conflicts in the middle east. recommendations are also needed for further progress in relations between the european union and that country. the report does not meet these expectations. that's why i voted against the resolution.
in writing. ‒ it is good that the nuclear deal with iran has been equipped with mechanisms to verify that it is fulfilling its commitments. however, despite the eu's diplomatic efforts, the agreement itself does not cover human rights issues. it is therefore very good that they have been raised in the strategy adopted. it makes clear that the union will engage in a dialogue with iran on the protection of human rights, which will facilitate the opening of an eu delegation in tehran. in this dialogue, the eu will do its utmost to ensure that iran abolishes the death penalty. even abolishing it for drug-related offences alone would reduce the number of executions by as much as 80%. it is therefore important to use the dialogue platforms that have been created by the strategy to persuade iran to abandon its current practices. for these reasons, i voted in favour of the eu's post-nuclear iran strategy, because i see it as an opportunity not only for iran, which will certainly benefit from opening up to the world, but also for the eu itself, which is deeply committed to the idea of promoting human rights in the world.
in writing. ‒ i do not support the report on the fight against corruption and follow-up to the crim resolution, as in my view these actions are not in line with the principle of subsidiarity. i have always been against the idea of a european public prosecutor's office and against eu membership of the group of states against corruption. the group i belong to proposed a number of amendments on this point, but they were rejected, so i voted against.
in writing. ‒ the commission set up in march 2013 was tasked with analysing organised crime in europe, assessing the implementation of eu policy on organised crime and examining the role of the eu's home affairs agency. the work resulted in a report which was adopted by the european parliament on 23 october 2013. the new own-initiative report, which follows on from the previous working document, underlines the substance and recommendations set out in the resolution of 23 october 2013, focusing on specific priority actions. the report has several positive aspects, such as increased information exchange and cooperation between law enforcement agencies, better protection for whistle-blowers, greater transparency and traceability of eu funds, links between organised crime and terrorism, or a call for specific measures to combat trafficking in human beings. however, the report calls for specific actions at eu level that are not compatible with the subsidiarity principle, namely the rapid establishment of a european public prosecutor's office, the recommendation that the eu become a member of the group of states against corruption (greco) established by the council of europe, or the call for eu action on the redistribution of criminal assets for their reuse for social purposes. i could not support the report.
in writing. - i voted against the resolution. the report underlines the need for better information exchange and law enforcement cooperation, more transparency in eu measures, a closer look at the links between organised crime and terrorism and an effective fight against trafficking in human beings. the issues raised are undoubtedly relevant. however, the report also calls for very specific action at eu level. among them, the call to speed up the work on the establishment of a european public prosecutor's office and the recommendation that the european union become a member of the group of states against corruption (greco) established by the council of europe are to be mentioned above all. the exercise of eu competence in this area also requires respect for the principle of subsidiarity and the powers of the member states.

in writing. ‒ i voted against the report on human rights and migration in third countries because i believe that it does not solve the problematic issues, but rather complicates the matter. i think this is a very important subject that needs to be examined in depth. it cannot be treated irresponsibly, as i believe the report does, with regard to the issue of safe and legal access for migrants, permanent and compulsory relocation programmes and family reunification. if you don't have a concrete idea of how to solve the problem, you shouldn't even try to discuss it. i therefore voted against.
in writing. ‒ this report by the gue rapporteur marie-christine vergiat contains a number of problematic points. almost a complete confusion between the terms 'migrant' and 'refugee'. in a number of places, the rights normally granted to refugees have been extended to a wider category of migrants, without distinguishing between legal and illegal migrants. the report is controversial in its discussion of issues such as return and readmission, and integration and labour market policies, which are outside the committee's remit. the report calls for 'safe and legal' ways for migrants to access. it also calls for the creation of permanent and compulsory relocation programmes. it calls for full rights, including housing and education, for irregular migrants and for recognition of their qualifications, and for family reunification, including for economic reasons, and including those with lower qualifications. there are also some positive elements, such as the right wording to pay special attention to the rights of women, children and other most vulnerable groups, or to funding for unhcr, fao and other organisations helping to shelter refugees close to their countries of origin. however, they do not offset the fact that in other areas the 'unbridgeable threshold' has been crossed. it is very important to maintain the distinction between the term 'migrant' and the term 'refugee'. i could not support the report.
in writing. ‒ migration is a global and multidimensional phenomenon with significant economic, political and social consequences. the most recent and largest migration crisis since the second world war has had a significant impact on the functioning of both the european union and its individual countries. it is therefore essential that parliament should take a clear and firm position in the face of such important challenges. unfortunately, the report presented contains many unclear statements, unrealistic objectives and is almost entirely devoid of plans and priorities to counter the current situation in europe and its immediate neighbourhood. while the report rightly draws attention to the obligations of the member states in the field of immigrant rights and the problem of violence against women and children migrating to the european union, it also includes provisions on the obligation to recognise qualifications acquired by migrants in their countries of origin or to provide them with work, which seems impossible to achieve. i have therefore decided to vote against the report.
in writing. ‒ the scale of the migration crisis means that we cannot lose sight of the issue of respect for human rights in the case of refugees. i agree that among these, special attention should be paid to women and children. the organizations that help these people also need financial support. in addition to these pertinent remarks, the report contains a number of points which raise my doubts. first, it erases the border between refugees and migrants. secondly, it does not focus on the core issues but also covers issues such as integration policy and labour market policy. an example is the call for full rights, including housing and education, also for illegal migrants. the report also calls for the creation of permanent and mandatory relocation programmes. these demands are too far-reaching and vague, which is why i voted against the resolution.
in writing. ‒ i decided to abstain on the report on corporate responsibility for serious human rights violations in third countries. i certainly agree that respect for human rights should be a core value for all member states. the report aims to encourage member states to ensure that rights such as human rights, labour and environmental standards and the fight against corporate corruption are respected. however, i feel that the report has raised issues which go beyond the scope of the report. therefore, i abstained.
in writing. ‒ the i. corrao report cites the un guidelines on business and human rights and the revised oecd guidelines for multinational enterprises, which require corporations operating in third countries to voluntarily adhere to values in the areas of human rights, labour standards, the environment and the fight against corruption. the report recognised human rights as core values of the eu and its member states. the main objective of the report is to encourage member states to apply these rights to companies whose owners are located in member states, which are established in member states or which are substantially active in member states. the need to address legal problems and uncertainties as to where responsibility for human rights violations lies is reiterated. it is also recalled that companies should assume legal liability. the eu, member states, third countries and all national and international bodies are called upon to adopt as a matter of urgency and to the widest extent possible binding instruments for the effective protection of human rights in this area and to give priority to the immediate establishment of a human rights due diligence obligation for state-owned or state-controlled enterprises. unfortunately, most of these statements are ambiguous. i hereby abstain from voting.
in writing. ‒ companies are among the most important players in the globalisation of the economy, financial services and international trade, and we should therefore be looking more carefully at their activities both at home and in the european union, but also outside the community. the european parliament report highlights the growing role of corporations in ensuring respect for human rights in third countries, while noting that trade agreements can contribute to strengthening global human rights and principles. the document also focuses on corporate social responsibility and the increasing number of voluntary commitments undertaken by companies in this area. the ep also calls on the eu and its member states to establish clear rules stating that companies established in their territory or under their jurisdiction must respect human rights in all their activities, in every country and in every context of their activities, including outside the eu. i have decided to vote in favour of the report on corporate responsibility for serious human rights violations in third countries.
in writing. ‒ according to the un guidelines on business and human rights and the oecd guidelines for multinational enterprises, corporations operating in third countries should voluntarily adhere to human rights values and labour standards. the report aims to encourage eu member states to enforce these rights and standards for companies whose owners are located in member states, which are established in member states or which do a significant part of their business in member states. however, the report contains a number of general and ambiguous demands, including a call on the eu, member states, third countries and all national and international bodies to adopt binding instruments to ensure effective protection of human rights in this area 'as a matter of urgency' and 'as far as possible'. the title of the report itself seems problematic. in view of these doubts, i have decided to abstain.
in writing. ‒ on the eu strategy for liquefied natural gas and gas storage, i decided to vote against. in my view, the strategy should focus on lng and gas storage issues, which are helpful in creating a strong energy union, and in practice it links to binding energy and climate targets for 2030. which i believe is designed to undermine the future role of lng and gas storage, and therefore i voted against.
in writing. ‒ there is a lot of talk about non-renewable energy and its dwindling resources. it is estimated that the most popular deposits, such as oil and coal, will run out around 2040. this is increasing the consumption of natural gas, which today accounts for only 20% of the world's total energy demand and whose reserves are still not fully exploited. it is usually found in association with other minerals, but it can also occur on its own. the largest natural gas reserves are in russia and the persian gulf. at the same time, the european union wants to reduce its emissions of greenhouse gases, which cause global warming, and to ensure that it has constant access to energy, thereby reducing its dependence on imports. the indirect solution is the use of liquefied natural gas (lng), which will significantly reduce transport costs as well as storage costs. this is important because the current pipeline system in europe is not fully harmonised and therefore the full potential of this mine cannot be exploited. and also, the liquid form is much more environmentally friendly. this requires the full integration of the energy policies of the individual member states of the union and the provision of stable gas supplies.
in writing. ‒ this own-initiative report is based on the commission communication entitled 'an eu strategy for liquefied natural gas and gas storage'. it should be seen as a guide with a set of key instruments on how to unlock lng and gas storage potential in order to achieve the goal of a strong energy union and complete the internal energy market. the negotiations have managed to maintain a balanced compromise, which focuses on lng and gas storage issues. s&d, alde and the greens have tried to broaden the scope of this report by adding themes on energy efficiency, renewable energy sources and shale gas. the aim was to extend the scope of this report to question the future role of lng and gas storage. the commission has also concluded that the aid is compatible with the internal market within the meaning of article 107 (3) (c) of the treaty. i could not support the report.
in writing. ‒ in february 2016, the european commission published a communication on an eu strategy on liquefied natural gas and gas storage as part of the sustainable energy security package. the commission considers that improving the access of eu member states to imported lng, as well as more efficient cross-border gas storage, will help to increase security of supply and reduce dependence on gas from a single supplier, and will allow member states to benefit from low global lng prices. the ep report on the eu's strategy for liquefied natural gas rightly stressed the need to create an internal market or to work more closely with international partners to create a truly global lng market. parliament was more cautious than the commission in its proposal about the need for new infrastructure. the risk of stranded assets, excess storage capacity and additional import capacity was noted. the report expressed particular concern about the eu's dependence on russian gas and criticised the proposed nord stream ii project. reducing europe's dependence on energy imports, especially from one direction, the east, should be a key element in building the european union's energy security. in this context, it is difficult to consider nord stream ii as an investment in line with the interests of the community, the foundations of the energy union and the european energy security strategy.
in writing. ‒ the operation of lng terminals is an important building block of the internal energy market in the european union, providing another source of natural gas supply. this will increase the energy security of the member states and their citizens. the potential of lng is already demonstrated by the terminals already in operation in klaipeda and świnoujście, among others. a coherent eu strategy for lng and storage is therefore needed. the commission notes that the commission has not provided any evidence that the measures in question are compatible with the internal market. that is why i have decided to vote against the report.
in writing. ‒ the strategy discussed in the plenary session is a very important step towards the creation of a well-functioning energy union, a project which poland was one of the initiators of. i am very pleased that it clearly highlights the risk of a potential doubling of the nord stream pipeline capacity, as this will only increase the eu's dependence on a single gas supplier russia. with this in mind, liquefied natural gas (lng) represents an opportunity to diversify gas supplies and thus increase the eu's energy security. the new eu strategy aims to facilitate the construction of not only lng terminals but also of the supporting pipeline infrastructure between member states, which is one of the key tools for implementing the principle of energy solidarity in times of gas shortages. the commission has identified 195 such projects as being of common interest which could be supported financially by the european fund for strategic investments. this is particularly relevant for member states in the central, eastern and southern european regions, which unlike the western eu countries do not have an extensive lng infrastructure and are therefore mostly dependent on a single supplier and vulnerable to disruptions in gas supply. i therefore voted today in favour of the eu strategy on liquefied natural gas and gas storage.
in writing. ‒ i support the report on how to harmonise fisheries controls in europe, because the solution proposed on this issue is consistent with respect for national competences. there is a need to standardise this issue, as fishermen point out, with regard to unequal treatment in the area of systematicity, frequency, severity, duration, accuracy, effectiveness and methods of fisheries control in europe. the objective of this report is ambitious. on the one hand, it is to identify shortcomings in the application of the rules that lead to a sense of inequality and to propose solutions to increase controls under the common fisheries policy. for these reasons, i voted in favour.
in writing. ‒ there is a uniform law for fishermen in the european union. however, they complain that the rules are not respected in the same way in every country and that fisheries controls are sometimes more rigorous and sometimes less rigorous. there are concerns that established procedures are not always followed, which may lead to inaccuracies. appropriate measures should therefore be taken to improve the common fisheries policy. the main reason for the controversy is that the number of checks at each stage varies from one country to another: in some regions, they occur at every level, while in others, checks on the sea-to-plate route occur only once. the solution proposed in this case is to simplify the common law so that it is simple and understandable to everyone, so that there are no discrepancies. comprehensive training should be provided throughout the community for both fishermen and inspectors. the creation of databases will allow the current status of fisheries to be monitored and knowledge to be acquired. action should also be taken to harmonise procedures across europe and to strengthen the role of the european fisheries control agency (efca). in particular, in all fishing areas where the catches of species are below the maximum sustainable yield (msy). however, the penalties for non-compliance should be the same for all.
in writing. ‒ this own-initiative report focuses on the issue of harmonising fisheries controls while respecting national competences. the report has two objectives: to identify the shortcomings in the application of the rules that lead to this feeling of inequality and to propose solutions to increase the degree of harmonisation of controls under the common fisheries policy. the question of the practical applicability of certain provisions of council regulation (ec) no 1224/2009 has been raised on several occasions, either because of the limited possibility of adapting the provisions to the reality or because of the contradictions in the provisions. this report contains a number of conclusions on the factors hindering the achievement of consistency. the proposals in the final report include: a call for simplification and improvement of eu legislation, as well as a reduction of administrative burden through the 2017 review of council regulation (ec) no 1224/2009 on fisheries controls; a call for the european fisheries control agency to allocate more resources to ensure the application of common standards in the field of control, inspection and surveillance and to facilitate operational cooperation between member states through joint deployment plans. for these reasons, i supported the report.
in writing. ‒ the burdens and controls faced by fishermen in europe vary widely from one member state to another. differences in the frequency, duration and methods of controls lead to a sense of unequal treatment in this sector. the practice to date in the framework of the application of council regulation (ec) no 1224/2009 indicates that some provisions are not sufficiently implemented. this concerns, among other things, control procedures, the system of sanctions, the method of data collection. the report identified existing shortcomings and rightly proposed greater harmonisation of controls under the common fisheries policy. the simplification of legislation through common standards of control, inspection and surveillance, the reduction of the burden on fishermen, the intention to strengthen operational cooperation between member states and the review of the application of the regulation planned for 2017 are steps in the right direction. i voted for the resolution.
in writing. ‒ i supported the report on improving connectivity and accessibility of transport infrastructure in central and eastern europe because it is innovative and comprehensive and is fully dedicated to the development of transport infrastructure in central and eastern europe (cee). it is important that it contains specific guidelines and recommendations on the direction of infrastructure development, areas of support and the need to implement specific projects in the cee region (construction of rail baltica, via carpathia, development of the eastern part of eusalp, creation of a new european corridor). for the reasons i have just mentioned, i voted in favour.
in writing. ‒ transport is a kind of bloodstream of the economy. without a well-functioning system for moving people and goods and without the possibility of relocating services, there is no clear economic growth. transport, by its very nature, also brings markets closer together, providing businesses with the opportunity to exchange goods, services and experiences with the outside world. unfortunately, despite the investments made with european structural funds, transport infrastructure in most central and eastern european countries is still much less developed than in other parts of the european union. priorities should include investments in particular to fill in missing links, to remove bottlenecks and to ensure smooth connections in long-distance and regional passenger and freight transport. in order to facilitate the implementation of transport projects, the european commission and the individual member states should seek to streamline and simplify tendering procedures, to issue guidelines on the public-private partnership formula and to simplify authorisation procedures. only then will the available funds be used effectively.
in writing. ‒ the european parliament's work to date has lacked a document that would comprehensively cover the development of transport infrastructure in central and eastern europe. i therefore welcome the report on this subject. the document under review not only discusses the development directions and areas of support, but also indicates specific projects that need to be implemented. the necessary investments concern rail, road and water links which will increase transport and communication opportunities throughout the region of central and eastern europe. in this way, the strengthening and development of trans-european networks will enable union citizens, economic operators and local and regional communities to derive full benefit from the establishment of an area without internal borders, as referred to in article 170 of the treaty on the functioning of the european union. for these reasons, i voted in favour of the resolution.

member of the commission. mr president, ladies and gentlemen, the european parliament and the commission are strong allies in the drive to reform corporate taxation in europe and to do so with ambition and determination. the strength with which you have taken up this subject, combined with our initiatives - which i believe are ambitious - have already brought about very significant changes. today we are closer to fair and efficient taxation in the european union than we were two years ago and, to be honest, closer than ever. we have made giant strides in tax transparency in the practices of member states and multinationals alike. we have built new barriers to tax base manipulation and profit shifting through new anti-abuse rules that will become binding throughout the european union. the package adopted by the commission today is much more than a mere set of new measures. it is more than an extension of what we have already done together. it is a comprehensive, structural and structural framework for corporate taxation in europe, a new framework that looks to the future and in which corporate taxation will by definition be fair and pro-growth. this framework will enable companies and investors to develop their activities in the european union, not through selective tax breaks or secret tax rescripts, but simply because they will benefit from a tax environment that is simple, readable, stable and also, of course, favourable to economic activity. for me, transparency and competitiveness go hand in hand. finally, it is a framework in which all companies, large and small, pay their taxes where they make their profits and create wealth. at the heart of the package adopted today is a project which i know is strongly supported and even wanted by this house: the revival of the common consolidated corporate tax base, namely the ccctb. the ccctb aims to tax enterprises in a way that reflects the true spirit of the single market, namely firstly uniform rules for the calculation of taxable profits; then a single tax return to be completed through a single window; finally, a system of profit sharing between member states which can then tax them at their national rates. companies will also be rewarded for their growth-oriented activities through important new elements in this version of the ccctb, because we have chosen - and i think it was rational - not to represent the same text that was rejected by the council, given the debates that had taken place and also the new context in which we are working. we've set up a super deduction for research and development. i would like to stress this point because we are really making a considerable effort in this area and we are showing a very strong will for research and development. in other words, companies investing in research and development will be able to deduct from their tax base one and a half times what they have spent. this incentive will be even more generous and will be up to 200% for young and innovative companies start-ups , which will be able to deduct the amount of the costs exposed to this amount. we have also introduced a measure in the ccctb which will promote corporate financing on the capital markets - consistent with our pursuit of a single capital market - by correcting the debt bias that currently exists in most corporate tax regimes. the objective is to foster and promote healthier financing, stronger capital markets and greater economic stability. the ccctb will also have the advantage of eliminating many cases of double taxation. however, until such a common consolidated basis is in place, we will still need an effective solution for non-ccisc companies. there are over 900 cases of double taxation currently being litigated in the european union, which of course generates enormous costs and a lot of legal uncertainty for the companies involved. that is why we are also proposing today an improved system for resolving double taxation disputes. we want to guarantee companies a solution, which is long-term, predictable and definitive, in cases where they are taxed more than once on the same income. the ccctb is a powerful tool for preventing and countering corporate tax evasion. as requested by the european parliament, we have proposed that ccctb be made compulsory for the largest multinationals. the ccctb will incorporate the measures already adopted by the member states in the directive against tax evasion and today we are adding to these provisions a final measure to combat hybrid arrangements with third countries and therefore outside the european union. why relaunch the accis? i know that this house has been waiting for this project for a long time and has long supported the benefits that should flow from it. i also know that companies are eager to get this device up and running as quickly as possible. and i can understand that some people are doubtful about the chances of success of the cfsp, given the lack of agreement on the previous proposal. let me try to instill a little optimism on this point because this time it's different. it is different because we have a better proposal, a better approach, a more favourable policy environment also, given all the events that have taken place in recent years and the progress that has already been made in corporate taxation. our proposal is strengthened. the fact that it is mandatory makes it a powerful tool in the fight against tax evasion, while the incentives, which i have already mentioned, improve the ability of our taxation to support employment, growth and stability. our approach is not only strengthened, it is also more pragmatic. we propose a two-step approach. first, member states must define the common base to start quickly to benefit from the benefits it offers. secondly, consolidation will also have to be implemented quickly. i would nevertheless like to emphasize strongly - because i know that this is a subject on which we can ask questions and that it may be tempting in the discussions to come in the council - that these two steps are closely linked. the commission does not consider that consolidation should be abandoned or postponed indefinitely, since consolidation alone will give the common base its full significance. we want a comprehensive agreement in two phases, not a first phase followed by another that would be postponed to the greek calendar and risk being split up. i aim to have this consolidation in place by 2021 at the latest. i am counting on the european parliament to continue to put pressure on our member states to achieve this objective because, as i said, we have your support, that of the businesses and the ngos, but the ball is, as usual, in the court of the member states. i'm getting to my very last point. today, i believe we have the environment, if not ideal, at least optimal to relaunch accis. given all the advantages of this project, we expect the member states to work towards adopting this proposal quickly. i would like to conclude by thanking this house for its long-standing support for the accis project and by urging you - but is it necessary? i know that it is not - to play your full part and to weigh in on the adoption of the proposals presented today. today we have the opportunity to build a fairer and more stable europe and a more competitive corporate taxation in europe for the benefit of our citizens, our businesses and our union as a whole. at a time when europe is under attack and populism is on the rise, this is a project that is part of a more transparent and fairer approach to taxation, the need for which is understood by our citizens and the usefulness of which. so this is a good example of europe again, and i invite you to support it.
on behalf of the ppe group. – mr president, i welcome the commission’s proposal for a single set of corporate tax rules for doing business in the eu. the present situation with 28 different corporate tax systems co-existing within one single market is untenable. it puts an unnecessary administrative burden on companies, reduces their international competitiveness and creates ample opportunities for them to engage in aggressive tax planning practices. why would you oppose the harmonisation of national tax rates across the eu? there is clearly a need to harmonise national regulations in the area of corporate tax base. firstly, we want to be serious about fighting tax avoidance and tax evasion in the eu. we want to make sure that taxes are paid where the value is created. that is why we need a common framework for corporate taxation that is simple, effective and transparent. secondly, we all want our companies to fully exploit the enormous potential of the single market. for that we need common european rules on corporate taxation, which would facilitate trade and investment across the eu, and eliminate unfair tax competition. that is why a european directive on common consolidated corporate tax base (ccctb) is urgently needed. let me draw your attention to three interesting novelties that were mentioned by the commissioner here. the first is the very generous tax treatment on r&d expenditure, the second is the preferential treatment of innovative start—ups, and the third is a rule against the debt-bias. all of them deserve our support. commissioner, we are ready to work with you on this proposal.
in writing. i would like to welcome the european commission's proposal for a common consolidated corporate tax base (ccctb). it is an important step in the right direction in the fight against tax evasion. however, i would personally be in favour of lowering the turnover threshold for companies subject to the rules below the proposed eur 750 million. i think the current system is unfair because it allows big multinational corporations to shift profits to the lowest tax rates, and taxes are levied on companies that don't have that option.
madam president! equal access for citizens to public authority and public institutions is the foundation of democracy and civil society. this is extremely important in both the real and virtual worlds, but it is particularly relevant in today's digital age, and it is particularly relevant for people with disabilities. for some of them, contact with public authorities, with public institutions via the internet is the only chance they have to have a connection with their country, their government or with a public institution. therefore, the idea that is being implemented in the project is extremely important and worthy of support. it is also important to remember that the virtual world today - and probably even more so in the future - will be one of the main areas of self-realization of the citizen, which is why the final outcome of these works is important. but it's also worth remembering that the responsibilities of the state, the public institution, and the private sector cannot be equated, and the issues we're talking about today need to be addressed effectively by the institutions and the public sector, but they shouldn't be imposed on the private sector.

if it is true that the european union develops through crises, then one can only envy mr tusk and mr juncker that they are leading the european union in such interesting times. but i am not envious, because i know that the battle for the credibility of european institutions, both internal and global, is being fought in fields where, unfortunately, fear and emotion now prevail over reason and argument. since the insecurity of europeans has been combined with migration and refugees, the future of the european union is being decided here. if the nation-state is the only safe haven in the imagination of europeans, the future of the community is in mortal danger. fortunately, there is a growing awareness that there is no effective national response, only an effective european response to these challenges. unfortunately, the european union's ability to act and its credibility as a global player are being overshadowed by the tragedy of ceta. we're hostages in the same region. it's a guilty situation. i hope (there is still a chance) that we will get out of this mess, but the european union's capacity to act and its credibility will be - even if we do - severely weakened. indeed, the mission of the european summits is to build a sense of usefulness and credibility in the european institutions, and i hope that the next summits will contribute to this.

in writing. the european council of 20 and 21 october 2016 summarised the issues on comprehensive migration policy. the entry into force of the european border guard regulation was an important step towards strengthening the union's external borders. the newly created patrol will, among other things, verify the ability of member states to control borders and organise joint operations to counter cross-border crime. however, increased efforts are needed to deter irregular migrants, especially those from africa. the council's position is that a lasting stabilisation of the situation along the eastern mediterranean route will require full implementation of the eu-turkey agreement and further support for the countries along the western balkan route. it is also necessary to complete and implement by 2018 the individual single market strategies, including the digital single market, the capital markets union, the energy union and the single market agenda. in this context, work on the recent european commission projects, including the draft reform of eu telecommunications and copyright law, and on the completion of the capital markets union should be undertaken urgently, in particular by rapidly reaching an agreement with the european parliament on the prospectus rules to improve access to finance for companies.
in writing. during today's debate on the european council conclusions, both the right and the left wing of the ep criticised the council for its ineffectiveness on the ceta agreement blocked by one of the belgian parliaments. there were also many voices to ignore the wallonia parliament's opinion and sign the agreement despite its opposition, since the other 27 states consider it to be beneficial. i don't agree with the criticism or the solution. meps who want a europe of the people, or at least a europe, must understand that the consequences are disruptive in decision-making, such as those at ceta. the 'europe of the peoples' approach means that the 'least common denominator' policy is now being criticised and that the council must be given the instruments to facilitate negotiations. secondly, i think the council's decision to take account of the wallonia veto is right: it is simply a consequence of the earlier decision to have a mixed agreement. if other countries or members consider the walloon decision to be harmful, they should persuade them to change their minds, not pressure the president of the council to ignore the accepted rules of the game. on the migration crisis, the council has taken the right decisions, including the conclusion of the agreement with turkey and the strengthening of the protection of the eu's external borders. the implementation of these provisions reduced the influx of illegal immigrants by 98%. this is a major step forward in a cause that has shaken the eu and remains one of its toughest challenges.
in writing. the entry into force of the european border and coast guard regulation, cooperation with african countries, support for lebanon and jordan, and the implementation of the agreement with turkey are further steps towards taking control of illegal immigration and the flow of refugees into the eu. according to the international organization for migration, 340,000 migrants arrived at the eu's borders in 2016. that's relatively much less than in previous years, but still, objectively, a lot! it is therefore important to be aware that we still have a long way to go before the systems agreed today are put into effect and fulfilled their role. we're on the right track, though. i was concerned to hear that the adoption of the canada trade agreement (ceta) was delayed. the european union is a testament to the positive effect of a balanced but above all open trade policy. consumers are benefiting from it. so we should not be swayed by the oversimplifications and half-truths of those who oppose the agreement. it is in our community interest to adopt it. i therefore hope that the deadlock on the approval of ceta can be overcome as soon as possible.

in writing. ‒ on the draft general budget of the european union for 2017, i have decided to vote against many amendments with which i do not agree. my group, the ecr, has consistently taken the view that the eu budget should be limited, that the same budgetary discipline applied to national expenditure should apply to eu expenditure. this is all the more so as the eu faces a number of new challenges since the spending ceilings were agreed in 2013. i believe that in the present situation the budget should be made more efficient without the need for increased contributions from the member states.
in writing. ‒ i voted in favour of the general budget of the european union for the financial year 2017 because i welcome its provisions. given the situation in the world, i consider it important to create a new budget line for the 'fund for victims of terrorism'. the purpose of this fund is to guarantee both financial and psychological support to victims of terrorism. the report referred to the need to increase the expenditure ceilings for specific actions supporting the youth employment initiative and the dairy sector. the report describes very important issues and proposes concrete solutions. those are the reasons i voted yes.
in writing. ‒ today we decided that the appropriations for commitments in 2017 should be eur 160.7 billion, eur 4.1 billion more than the european commission's draft, and that the amount for payments should be eur 2.5 billion more, for a total of eur 136.7 billion. an additional €1.5 billion is needed to help young people enter the labour market. in addition, measures are needed to support economic growth and to help third countries in the context of the ongoing migration crisis. in this context, we have not agreed to any cuts introduced by the european council. the addition of eur 1.24 billion to the amount provided for in the draft budget for the connecting europe facility for infrastructure projects and for horizon 2020, which supports research projects, will also contribute to economic growth in the union. the financing of the agreement with turkey and other temporary funds should not be set at the expense of the eu's existing external policy. the additional funds will be generated by new appropriations received as a result of the ongoing revision of the multiannual financial framework 2014-2020.
in writing. ‒ on 28 september, the committee on budgets voted on 2221 amendments to the council's position on the eu budget for 2017. the vote will result in a net increase of eur 4.07 billion over the commission's proposal. the proposal includes eur 160.6 billion in commitment appropriations and eur 136.7 billion in payments. the draft resolution on the 2017 eu budget is the political position of the european parliament before the annual budgetary negotiations with the commission and the council. in addition to the withdrawal of all council cuts, the most significant changes in the commission's estimates include €1.5 billion for the youth employment initiative, €600 million for support to the dairy sector and an additional €1.24 billion to offset the efsi through cuts to horizon 2020 and the connecting europe facility. however, these changes leave no room for manoeuvre in the event of unforeseen events in 2017, and the rapporteur therefore proposes to increase the expenditure ceilings by providing 'new resources' in the context of the review of the multiannual financial framework. i voted in favour of the report.
in writing. ‒ i voted in favour of the motion for a resolution on the mid-term review of the mff, which aims to increase the ceilings for specific actions (the employment initiative, horizon 2020, the migration partnership). in my view, if there is a possibility of increasing the amount for such important programmes with a number of benefits, it should be used. in addition, the resolution calls for greater flexibility and the removal of certain restrictions. i therefore voted in favour.
in writing. ‒ the challenges facing the european union today, such as migration, the internal security crisis and youth unemployment, have made it necessary to carry out a mid-term review of the multiannual financial framework for 2014-2020. the commission's proposals are good, with more flexibility and a crisis reserve. it is regrettable that the commission has not proposed raising the current ceilings of the mff. i hope that the solutions proposed by the commission are only a starting point for further negotiations. this revision is not only an opportunity to find money for new needs, but also an opportunity to prevent the lack of funds for unforeseen obligations.
in writing. ‒ changes to the mff are absolutely necessary. the ep report expressed the conviction that the revision of the mff represents a unique opportunity to respond to the budgetary difficulties currently threatening the credibility of the european union, while calling on the council to ensure a credible, coherent, realistic and balanced eu budget for the remaining years of the current financial perspective. the document reiterated its call for the full balancing of the cuts to the european fund for strategic investments (efsi) for horizon 2020 and the connecting europe facility. it also called for the youth employment initiative to be continued. moreover, the ongoing migration and refugee crisis, which was unforeseeable when the mffs were established, requires an increase in the available resources to deal with the impact of the current situation. at the same time, it called for a significant increase in the flexibility of the union budget to enable it to respond more effectively to the new challenges facing the community today.
in writing. ‒ i voted in favour of the launch of the european globalisation adjustment fund in the petroleum and chemicals sector. i support the overall objective of the fund to help workers find jobs and develop their skills when they are lost as a result of changes in the global trade pattern. the actions carried out under the fund include: providing training (including language training) to a group of around 800 employees, vocational counselling, and funding for studies. i welcome the fact that concrete measures will be taken to help workers re-enter the labour market, and i therefore voted in favour.
in writing. ‒ the european globalisation adjustment fund is an instrument to counter the negative effects of mass redundancies, which are a consequence of global changes in the labour market and trade. estonia's request to mobilise the fund is a reflection of the turmoil in world oil markets and the weakening of europe's position in international fertiliser trade. these changes have forced the closure of the estonian companies eesti energia as, nitrofert as and viru keemia grupp as in these two sectors and the reduction of production, resulting in the redundancy of 800 employees. training, traineeships, educational scholarships and incentives to learn estonian through the fund will be essential to support these workers in their return to the labour market. policies that promote growth and jobs deserve support. however, i have serious doubts that the european globalisation adjustment fund mechanism is a tool that can effectively help displaced workers to integrate into the labour market. i believe that each situation requires individual and careful evaluation. the commission's proposal is to be adopted by the council at the next meeting of the european council in brussels.
in writing. ‒ i voted in favour of the directive on the accessibility of public sector websites and mobile applications because i fully support its purpose. it is very important to harmonise the provisions in force in the member states on making both websites and applications more accessible, especially for people with disabilities (in particular blind, visually impaired and hard of hearing people). enabling text to change colour and size, providing speech to read text and describe images, and allowing browsing without a mouse are some of the main practical solutions to facilitate accessibility for people with disabilities. i am happy to accept the provisions of the directive, which is why i voted in favour.
in writing. ‒ there are about 80 million disabled people in the european union. by 2020, that number could rise to as many as 120 million as our population ages. the commission should also be able to use the information contained in the annual report on the implementation of the union's macro-financial assistance to the countries of central and eastern europe, the mediterranean countries and the countries of central and eastern europe, in order to provide the union with a comprehensive overview of the measures taken to implement the union's macro-financial assistance. the european parliament today backed the first eu legislation to make public sector bodies' websites and mobile applications more responsive to the needs of disabled and older people. the directive aims to ensure the accessibility of websites and applications by making them more functional and understandable. there are also a number of tools that enable disabled people to use websites, such as special screen readers or devices that allow you to work on a computer without using a mouse. joint action by all member states to ensure that websites are accessible to union citizens will contribute to the development of an inclusive digital society and to the benefits of the single market. the fulfilment of these requirements for public sector bodies is particularly important as it will provide citizens with access to a range of public services.
in writing. ‒ equal access to public information for citizens, including people with disabilities, is a cornerstone of modern democracy and civil society. it's incredibly important in both the real and virtual worlds. it is crucial for people with disabilities, because for some of them, access to public institutions via the internet is the only way to maintain a connection with their government, their state. the idea of the project therefore deserves our full support. the virtual world will be one of the main areas of citizens' self-fulfilment, which is why the final report of the european parliament is so important. however, it should be borne in mind that no confusion can be created between the responsibilities of public institutions and the private sector. the tasks we're talking about today need to be effectively done by the public sector, but they shouldn't be imposed from the top down on the private sector. i have decided to vote in favour of this report because of its particular importance for disabled people.
in writing. ‒ i voted against the regulation on protective measures against plant pests. although the report sets an ambitious objective of establishing principles for identifying the phytosanitary risks associated with any type of pest on plants or plant products, the regulation does not address the most important issues. in my view, the most important actions to be taken in this area are to protect trade and avoid excessive bureaucracy. the regulation does not focus on such important issues at all, which is why i voted against it.
in writing. ‒ the report is technical and sectoral in nature, but its political sense is positive. it is intended to enhance the enforcement of standards relating to the health and safety of plants, animals and humans. the restrictions on trade provided for shall not go beyond what is necessary to achieve the objective. the new law should not lead to excessive bureaucracy. i therefore voted in favour of the resolution.
in writing. ‒ i voted against the report on the european semester for economic policy coordination: implementing the priorities for 2016 because i believe that this report should focus on other aspects of the eu. in my view, the report should focus more on the role of member states in implementing structural reforms than on improving social sentiment, which is the objective of the eu's economic recovery. the report also calls for the completion of the banking union and the territorial alignment of the european fund for strategic investments projects. for these reasons, i voted against.
in writing. ‒ the european semester, the procedure for coordinating economic and budgetary policies in the european union, is also a great opportunity to see how the individual countries of the community are implementing reforms to build a well-functioning and integrated european single market. in my opinion on the report assessing the implementation of this year's priorities under the european semester, the committee on the internal market and consumer protection emphasised that many member states are delaying or not fully implementing eu directives and regulations. broad support for smes and start-ups, tackling excessive administrative burdens, full implementation and application of the services directive, recognition of professional qualifications and access to regulated professions, and finally building the digital single market are examples of areas that both the european commission and individual member states should prioritise. otherwise we will not be able to unlock the full potential of the european single market, which is the opportunity for growth and job creation that europe so badly needs.
in writing. ‒ the annual report analysed is the european parliament's response to the country-specific recommendations published by the european commission in may 2016. the documents of both institutions form part of the so-called european semester, the annual cycle of guidelines on economic and supervisory policy of the european union. in preparing its recommendations, the commission analysed the plans for budgetary, macroeconomic and structural reform in each member state. given the importance of this procedure, i must emphasise that i do not agree with some of the points in the parliament's report, such as the call for the completion of the banking union or the territorial adjustment of the european fund for strategic investments (efsi) projects. i believe that the report should focus more on the importance of member states undertaking major structural reforms, which is why i voted against.
in writing. ‒ i voted in favour of a draft resolution on limiting the intake of trans fats at eu level. trans-fatty acids are unsaturated fats found in food produced from ruminants and in synthetic partially hydrogenated vegetable oils. unfortunately, the public is very exposed to their consumption, often without being aware of it, because the products made using trans fats are now fast food, fast food or snacks (salty and spicy). studies show that eating these fats leads to cardiovascular or coronary heart disease, which kills around 660 000 people in the eu each year. the draft is a very important issue that needs to be resolved as soon as possible, which is why i voted in favour.
in writing. ‒ trans fats are one of the most dangerous food ingredients. they increase the risk of cardiovascular disease. they are commonly added to food to improve its texture and to prolong its shelf life. the world health organization reports that eliminating saturated vegetable fats from the diet has significant health benefits. we should take the example of denmark, austria, latvia and hungary, which already have a ban on trans fats in food, and the united states, where the food and drug administration has ordered food manufacturers to eliminate trans fats from their food products by 2018. this will potentially save tens of thousands of lives a year.
in writing. ‒ the draft resolution sets out parliament's strategic objectives to reduce the consumption of artificial trans fats at eu level. trans-fatty acids are unsaturated fats found in food produced from ruminants and in synthetic partially hydrogenated vegetable oils. consumption of synthetic vegetable oils has been associated with an increased risk of cardiovascular disease. high consumption of trans fats is a risk factor particularly conducive to the development of ischaemic heart disease. products currently made using trans fats are fast food, snacks or salty and spicy snacks, which are therefore classified as highly processed foods. although the majority of citizens in the eu member states consume little trans fat, consumption is still significant in some social groups, contributing to excessively high mortality in these groups. since the adoption of regulation (eu) no 1169/2011, there has been significant evidence of the benefits of limiting artificial trans fats in food. the resolution calls on the commission to propose mandatory limits for artificial trans fats to protect public health. restrictions on trans fats in food have undoubtedly positive health effects and the industry is not suffering any negative consequences. i hereby support the motion for a resolution.
in writing. ‒ trans fats are mainly used in highly processed foods fast food and salty and spicy snacks. consumption of such products increases the risk of cardiovascular disease, including heart failure. mandatory restrictions on trans fats on the internal market would contribute to reducing their consumption. the countries that have done this have shown that it has had a positive impact on the health of their citizens. it is for these reasons that i voted in favour of the resolution.

in writing. the european court of auditors is responsible for auditing the european union's finances. it is an independent external auditor whose task is to examine the legality and regularity of all eu expenditure and revenue and to assess the soundness and regularity of budget management. eto is active throughout the european union. it shall cooperate with the supreme inspection authorities of the member states and the international organisations intosai and eurosai. within these bodies, it participates in the development of international standards for the control of public finances. the eto college shall consist of twenty-eight members, one from each eu member state. they shall be appointed for a term of six years by the council of the european union after consulting the european parliament. the european parliament has the power to give an opinion on candidates for the etu under article 286 (2) of the treaty. the requirements to be met by a candidate for the european court of auditors are set out in detail in article 286 of the treaty on the functioning of the european union. and these criteria alone should decide whether he is appointed by the council to the etu, because they alone form the basis for the european parliament's opinion in a transparent manner. it is therefore deeply concerned that over the past three years in 2013 (1 candidate) and in 2016 (2 candidates) the council has appointed three members of the court with a negative opinion from the european parliament. a negative opinion of the european parliament deprives them of the legitimacy conferred by the treaty.
