on behalf of the vice-president of the commission/high representative of the union for foreign affairs and security policy. – mr president, the european commission very much appreciates the european parliament’s long-standing interest and our cooperation on this important neighbouring country. the high representative’s intervention to you on belarus dates from september last year and we had just witnessed the release of the remaining political prisoners and were hoping to engage in a longer-term strategy focused on building links between the european union and belarus and on supporting reforms for the people of belarus, which are badly needed. one year on, there have been a number of noteworthy developments on the eu-belarusian scene. in recognition of the political prisoners’ release and of a number of positive steps taken by belarus over the last years, the eu lifted most of the restrictive measures against belarus in february of this year. an important factor which contributed to this decision was belarus’ constructive stance on this crisis in and around ukraine which persists today. in the council conclusion on belarus adopted in february, the european union and member states expressed their concern about the human rights situation and particularly also about the continued application of capital punishment. at the same time, we agreed that there was an opportunity for our relationship – for eu-belarus relations – to develop on a more positive agenda and that progress in a variety of fields can better be achieved through enhanced channels of communication. since then, cooperation in areas of common interest has been stepped up. in april the commission adopted a delegated act which made belarus eligible for eib lending. this will bolster support for the belarusian private sector. an agreement was signed between olaf and belarus in july on customs cooperation, in particular in fighting the illicit trade in cigarettes, and the sectoral dialogue on customs and related topics is still foreseen to be launched by the end of the year. a trade dialogue was launched this month, on 13 october, between the european commission dg for trade and belarus in view of improving trade, discussing belarus’ access to the wto and addressing existing barriers in international trade. a mobility partnership was signed also this month, also on 13 october, in view on enhancing cooperation on migration, asylum and border management. this will contribute in tackling the migration challenges, protection of refugees, prevention and combating trafficking in human beings. the european union stepped up its financial support for 2016 to eur 29 million – more than a doubling of the budget initially planned for 2016. assistance is focused on regional and private sector development, support for migration and asylum management, and support for students. we are also intensifying our cooperation in the area of energy. as part of a re-engagement with belarus, the commission is considering relaunching the formal eu-belarus energy dialogue in the near future. nuclear safety issues have always been an overall eu concern, especially when new facilities are being constructed on the border with the eu, and are a key component of the exchanges on energy with belarus. the council’s conclusions adopted on 15 february 2016 reiterate the importance of ensuring nuclear safety beyond the borders of the european union, and call on belarus to cooperate constructively with the relevant international authorities in this regard. in this context, the high-level visit of the competent commission services to belarus took place on 19 and 20 september 2016. in addition, we have continued our strong assistance for civil society and for the promotion of people-to-people contacts. civil society organisations received between 2011 and 2015 over eur 50 million in programmes which strengthen their capacity and further a number of social, economic and human rights issues. hundreds of exchanges are on-going in the areas of education, culture, science and technology and generally youth exchanges. on the human rights front, we have witnessed more openness by the belarusian authorities to engage. eu special representative mr lambrinidis visited minsk in march this year, where we had a meeting with president lukashenko and participated in a conference on the death penalty. in june, the belarusians hosted for the first time a european union-belarus human rights dialogue, for a part of which they also invited civil society representatives. at the same time we are fully aware that there have been no concrete or structural changes in belarus democracy and the human rights situation. the application of capital punishment remains an issue which overshadows our relations with the country. this year alone we have learned about one execution, four confirmed death sentences and two new ones. needless to say, this issue remains high on our agenda, and we will continue engaging with belarus on this. both the presidential election of october 2015 and the parliamentary election of last month were criticised by the osce for falling short of democratic standards and for not addressing a number of key osce and council of europe venice commission recommendations. nevertheless we welcome the entry into rapporteur. – madam president, the discharge for the european council is the main issue of the discharge procedure. the difficulties repeatedly encountered in the discharge procedures to that date, which were due to a lack of cooperation from the council, led to a refusal to grant discharge to the secretary-general of the council. parliament, in relation to the financial years 2009, 2010, 2011, 2012 and 2013, postponed its decision on granting the secretary-general of the council discharge in relation to the financial year 2014. the council continues to be silent in relation to the remarks made by parliament in its discharge resolution of 28 april on the trend from previous years of increasing underspending and carryovers of commitments, the high underspending rate and the very high number of appropriations, as well as major transfers within budget lines. these problems could be avoided with better budgetary programming. moreover, the council has still not adopted a code of conduct, which is indispensable to the transparency, accountability and integrity of the institution. whistle-blowing rules should be implemented by the council by introducing them into the code of conduct without further delay. the council definitely should disclose the relevant documents and put in place a clear reporting system that will enable the public to follow the legislative procedures in an open and transparent manner. the council definitely has to increase transparency and integrity with regard to the negotiations. lack of transparency with regard to the legislative process of negotiations, member states’ positions and meetings with the council, trilogues and conciliation meetings above all undermines the right of citizens of the union to information and transparency and it is becoming a cause of concern reflecting, as it does, a certain democratic deficit within the union institutions. the council should join the european union transparency register to ensure transparency and accountability of the institution. moreover, the council should provide information on its process of administrative modernisation. has the council already introduced the process of organisation aimed at using modern management methods to be efficient? we call for the information on the process and we would like to see the anticipated impact on the council’s budget. we also call on the council to develop detailed anti-corruption guidelines and independent policies within its structures.
rapporteur. – madam president, thank you for the very comprehensive debate. the issue of the council of the european union and the european council is the most urgent to be dealt with. the council ought to be transparent and fully accountable to union citizens for the funds entrusted to it by taking part fully and in good faith in the annual discharge procedure, just as other union institutions do. article 15 tfeu stipulates that each institution, body, office or agency is to ensure that its proceedings are transparent. in this regard, the effective supervision of the union’s budget implementation requires cooperation between parliament and the council through a working arrangement. here we have to clearly say that only three out of some 20 questions submitted to the council by the members of the committee on budgetary control in relation to financial year 2014 within the discharge exercise, which means that there is still no proper cooperation and no correct dialogue. the expenditure of the council must be scrutinised in the same way as the other institutions until the fundamental elements of such scrutiny have been laid down in its discharge resolutions of the past years. we, the members of the european parliament, are using here our competences laid down by the treaties. parliament’s prerogative to grant discharge is introduced by articles 316, 317 and 319 of the treaty, in line with current interpretation and practice, namely to grant discharge of each budget heading dually in order to maintain transparency and democratic compatibility towards union taxpayers. also, under rule 94 of parliament’s rules of procedure, the provisions governing the procedure for granting discharge to the commission in respect of the implementation of the budget shall likewise apply to the procedure for granting discharge to persons responsible for the implementation of the budgets of other institutions and bodies of the european union, such as the council as regards its activity as executive. this is nothing new. finally, we have to strongly say that the lack of cooperation between the european council and the council with the discharge authority constitutes a serious failure to comply with the obligation laid down by the treaties, and we believe that the relevant stakeholders need to take the necessary steps to address this issue without further delay. it is also a negative sign to the citizens of the union. it is a big problem and a big challenge for us too.
on behalf of the s&d group. volunteering is a noble activity, but how often it is not fully appreciated! so let me start by thanking all the volunteers for their work, their time, their effort and their energy. volunteering, as a process of self-realisation and learning, benefits both the volunteers themselves and the society as a whole. it is also a major factor in fostering social capital and promoting social and economic cohesion. in the context of international exchange, volunteering has a huge potential for integration. and if it takes place in the european union, it helps to create a european identity. but this potential of cross-border volunteering is not being fully exploited. according to 2014 data, it is estimated that around 92-94 million people were involved in volunteering activities, and only 7 000 in cross-border activities. legal, administrative, social and economic barriers, as well as a lack of appropriate information, prevent the full development of cross-border volunteering. this untapped potential is estimated at around eur 65 million per year. it is therefore necessary to develop a legal framework that defines the status of volunteering, but also the rights and obligations of volunteers. the european charter of the rights and duties of volunteers was rightly mentioned by the president, mrs silvia costa. we have to answer the question why, for example, voluntary residence should not be a legal basis for residence in a country. for people from poorer backgrounds, from disadvantaged backgrounds, for people with disabilities, the huge problem is, for example, the incomplete health benefits, and also often the loss of social benefits, including unemployment benefits. another issue to be addressed is the valuation of skills and competences acquired through volunteering - as the commissioner rightly pointed out. but it is important that this recognition is promoted in the labour market, especially in the recruitment process. to this end, it is essential to work with employers to ensure that they appreciate the importance of volunteering. the recognition of volunteers' time as a qualified contribution (participation) in the case of eu grants should be implemented and promoted as soon as possible, as the commission itself has recently said. the question for the commissioner is: at what stage are the work on this? finally, the local level of volunteering is needed to be strengthened in order to share experiences, but there is a need for high quality information on the possibilities of participating in the programme. in the context of the work on the revision of the erasmus+ programme, it is important to underline - in writing. ‒ the coup attempt in turkey on 15 july 2016 left hundreds dead and over 2,000 injured. a few days later, the turkish authorities declared a state of emergency, which now gives the authorities almost unlimited control over the population. in the aftermath of the coup, the turkish authorities closed the offices of more than 100 newspapers, magazines, publishing houses and distribution companies. at the same time, more than 100 journalists and media workers were detained and 330 lost their jobs. the european parliament resolution strongly condemned the coup in turkey, stressed the importance of protecting democracy and called on the turkish authorities to release journalists and media workers and to reopen closed offices. a free and pluralistic press is an essential element of any democracy, as are due process, the presumption of innocence and judicial independence. the european union and its institutions must therefore make a clear appeal to the turkish authorities to return to the democratic rule of law.

in writing. ‒ the security situation in the european union's neighbourhood has deteriorated significantly in the last few years and has become more volatile, dangerous and unpredictable, with the result that member states have to deal with a range of threats from state and non-state actors. the 1968 treaty on the non-proliferation of nuclear weapons recognises five nuclear-weapon states, while the three states that de facto possess nuclear weapons have developed nuclear capabilities outside the framework of the treaty (india, pakistan and israel). north korea is considered to be a nuclear weapons state. unfortunately, in recent years both russia and south korea have taken numerous actions that are contrary to the provisions of the npt, reinforcing the sense of threat among the international community as a whole and leading to further proliferation of nuclear weapons by state and non-state actors. the european union and its member states should now take decisive and unambiguous steps towards global arms control, with a clear recognition of a world free of nuclear weapons as a realistic long-term objective.
madam president! ladies and gentlemen! this year marks the 20th anniversary of the european voluntary service. many of the people who have been involved in this project since the beginning already have children of an age that qualifies them for the initiative. it would be very interesting to see how many of these children, who have been taught by their parents' experience, have chosen to participate in european voluntary service. unfortunately, we are not able to do this because, as silvia costa points out, the european commission collects little data on this initiative. we have no information on the contribution of european volunteering to national and european gdp or to social cohesion. so we don't know what the effects of this initiative are. it certainly needs to be changed as soon as possible. consideration should also be given to extending the categories of persons eligible for european voluntary service. the increase in the average life expectancy of people in their 60s means that there is a large group of people over 60 who have the time and the desire to be socially active. it is worth taking advantage of this and creating opportunities for them to work, whether it is through european voluntary service or a completely new programme. for these reasons, i voted in favour of the project.

in writing. ‒ in 2016, the european voluntary service is celebrating its 20th anniversary. over two decades, we've been able to support over 100,000 volunteers. on the one hand, it is a joy to see so many people willingly give of their time for others, without any financial gain in view. on the other hand, we can say that this is a drop in the bucket and that better promotion and material support for the programme is needed. volunteering helps to acquire skills and competences, and is an expression of solidarity and responsibility, which contribute to strengthening active citizenship and personal development. it has a huge added value and a positive impact on intercultural relations. however, volunteering requires appropriate organisational and legal structures that clearly define the rights and obligations of volunteers. in addition, member states should promote european voluntary service more actively in their education systems and, by simplifying the current application system, provide young people with quick and easy access to the programme.
in writing. ‒ professional mobility and continuous upskilling are a huge opportunity for young people and young workers. european voluntary service helps people aged 17-30 to travel abroad, enabling them to take part in volunteering projects lasting from 2 weeks to 12 months. the opportunities offered by european voluntary service are being used by people in erasmus+ programme countries as well as in neighbouring partner countries. individual projects also aim to promote social integration, solidarity and dialogue between different cultures. it is estimated that european voluntary service will support up to 100 000 volunteers between 2014 and 2020. this project deserves support, which is why i voted for it.
madam president! i must admit that i cannot give a clear assessment of the implementation of the eu youth strategy in the years 2013-2015. on the one hand, youth unemployment has declined and fewer people are leaving school early, but on the other hand, it is difficult to be satisfied with the fact that eight million young people are still out of work and a large proportion of those who are working are part-time or below their qualifications. one area where we have not been able to improve is in the digital skills of young people. i am therefore glad that the rapporteur has emphasised this in her report. last week events were held across the union to promote coding skills among young people. this is a very valuable initiative and will certainly have a significant impact in the next few years. in one respect, however, it was symptomatic. as the organizers note, the girls were only marginally involved. this shows the problem we have to face as a whole union. the situation of young people in the labour market cannot be improved if a large proportion of them are excluded from the fastest growing sector of the economy. for these reasons, i voted for the bill.
in writing. ‒ i voted against the evaluation report on the eu youth strategy 2013-2015 because i believe that youth policy should be a responsibility of the member states. the eu's role in this area should be limited to providing guidance and supporting the actions taken by the member states. the report raises concerns about the violation of the principle of subsidiarity. the rapporteur thus seeks to give the eu greater competence in this area, suggesting that intergovernmental cooperation is insufficient. i therefore voted against.
in writing. ‒ i voted in favour of the report on the eu youth strategy 2013-2015. as the rapporteur rightly pointed out in her report, there is a great divide between the different groups of young people in europe. the differences are national, regional and environmental. therefore, any strategy developed at eu level must be holistic and respond to all challenges. of course, the problem of unemployment remains one of the most pressing, but we are already seeing that both the general improvement in the economic situation and the initiatives implemented to promote the employment of young people are beginning to bear fruit. but the decline in unemployment is not enough. if we want to achieve the triple a social standard in the european union, as president juncker has promised, we must also ensure the quality of this employment. unfortunately, statistics confirm that young people are more likely to be in precarious employment and work below their qualifications. the european cooperation framework must take this into account. this also requires the proper use of the european social fund and other financial instruments, and their appropriate synergy.
in writing. ‒ i support the evaluation report on the eu youth strategy 2013-2015, in which initiatives on education and youth labour market entry play an important role. the european parliament once again stresses the importance of vocational training, the practicality and usefulness of education, and the need for the business and social partners to work together to create an education framework that will help young people in their adult lives. at the same time, the report makes no reference to the emerging trend in academia that criticises the current state of education, including the tendency to extend the learning cycle not to prepare for the more innovative and demanding challenges of the future, but to escape unemployment and lack of prospects. universities as repositories for the unemployed and the undecided are a waste of time, money and opportunity on the part of both students and faculty. education is an important factor shaping the future, but it's not going to make up for the shortcomings in other areas, and it's time for politicians to stop presenting education as the panacea for all the ills they encounter in their work. the most important things that young people need to get well into adulthood are training in creativity, critical thinking, openness and willingness to collaborate. the report also stresses the need to involve young people in decision-making and to take responsibility for their social life.
in writing. ‒ the economic crisis in europe has left millions of eu citizens with financial problems, no prospects or without jobs and livelihoods. one of the groups that suffered the most were young europeans. in november 2015, the average youth unemployment rate (in the 15-29 age group) in europe was 20% and in some member states it exceeded 40%. moreover, there are 13.7 million young people in europe who are not in employment, education or training. young people are still faced with the impossibility of finding full-time or long-term employment and with the wrong qualifications that do not correspond to the demands of the labour market. despite much progress in youth employment and integration into the labour market, further action is needed to reduce unemployment, improve the quality of life and prospects of young people, ensure equal opportunities for them, raise their civic awareness and prevent radicalisation. more systematic cooperation is therefore needed at eu and member state level in a wide range of policy areas such as employment, vocational education and training, social policy, youth policy, culture, sport and health. it is also important to ensure adequate financial resources for the implementation of youth programmes.
in writing. ‒ youth policy is a matter for the member states. this is clearly stated in article 6 of the treaty on the functioning of the european union, which states that the union has competence in this area only to support, coordinate and supplement the actions of the member states. such division of competences imposes an obligation on the union to confine itself to actions that are justified, necessary and proportionate. this is the perspective to be taken of the eu youth strategy 2013-2015. i have many reservations about her. the report evaluated the strategy but did not present the level of results achieved. the rapporteur calls for the continuation of the youth employment initiative, even though it is not delivering the expected results in practice. the report also points out that existing intergovernmental cooperation in the youth field is insufficient. in view of the principle of subsidiarity, this wording is unclear as to its implications. i am also concerned by the numerous references in the report to migrants and their integration and to lgbt communities. for these reasons, i voted against the resolution.
in writing. ‒ i support the recommendations proposed in the report to ensure that the eu youth strategy is as effective as possible. youth policy is of course a matter for the member states, but the european union still has an important role to play in coordinating and providing assistance and support through the so-called open method of coordination. i find particularly alarming the continued high rate of youth unemployment and the high proportion of young people not in education, employment or training. therefore, i consider that identifying the causes of youth unemployment and the measures to address them is crucial to achieving the objectives of the next edition of the eu youth strategy (2016-2018). in this context, i stress the importance of investing in education, traineeships, work placements and skills training that reflect labour market opportunities, needs and developments, and the importance of facilitating labour market entry through measures that ensure better coordination of education programmes, employment policies and labour market demand. as in other cases, i would also like to recall that in order to achieve the expected effectiveness of the strategy, it is necessary to promote and coordinate actions properly not only at eu level but also at national, regional and local level. like the rapporteur, i am particularly concerned here with the potential of new technologies to engage young people and to increase their capacity to participate in society.
in writing. ‒ i voted in favour of the report on how the cap can improve job creation in rural areas. in my view, the report tackles a very important subject, namely the rural economy, with the greatest emphasis on employment in this area. i also supported the report because it aims to simplify the cap for individual farmers, to provide better access to services in rural areas and to encourage more research and innovation in the sector. that's why i voted yes.

madam president, president draghi, commissioner, dear colleagues, i think that this report is very rich in content, contrary to what some colleagues underlined. i also think that its main message, at least from my point of view, is that we probably are at a turning point. timid recovery fails to gather momentum. it is true that the political events of the past months have not helped to foster confidence and stability. it is true that monetary policy has done a lot to preserve and enhance this fragile growth, but it seems that unconventional monetary policy is reaching its limits, and the ecb has in fact been in charge of coping with most parts of the post-crisis adjustment. as president draghi stressed earlier this year, half of the growth we have witnessed is due to the exceptional monetary policy that has been put in place. but this alone cannot solve the problem of imbalances; mr. chairman, please! i voted against this report for two main reasons. first of all, money laundering is a vague and propaganda-based term. money that is dirty in one country is not dirty in another country. there is no objective measure of which country has the correct interpretation, and it's very similar with tax laws. it is therefore natural that citizens and entrepreneurs alike move their businesses to places where taxes are lower, because businesses are run to generate income and tax is a cost to entrepreneurs. so countries are competing with each other on taxation, and they should be competing to see which tax system is more efficient for the economy. this should not be unified, but entrepreneurs should be allowed to transfer their activities from disadvantaged to advantageous systems.
in writing. ‒ i abstained from the vote on the access of tax authorities to information on anti-money laundering. the regulation aims to ensure that tax authorities have consistent access to information on anti-money laundering. currently, access to such information varies across the eu. the amendments would therefore provide tax authorities with access to customer information as part of the fourth anti-money laundering directive. the grounds for abstaining shall be the observations appearing in the arrangements with the council of the european union.
in writing. the leaked panama papers, which leaked from mosack fonseca's panama office, revealed how lawyers employed by the firm helped their international clients launder money and evade taxes. as a result of this and other tax affairs, the european commission has embarked on an ambitious programme to combat tax evasion. the european parliament adopted new legislation at its november plenary session to combat such practices more effectively. the new rules will give tax authorities the ability to access information on companies and impose data exchange obligations on them. combating tax evasion is a key objective in achieving a more efficient and fairer tax system in the eu. in this context, it is necessary to increase tax transparency and strengthen cooperation between tax authorities in the eu. access to information for tax authorities on anti-money laundering matters varies considerably between member states. even when such access is provided, authorities often face numerous obstacles that limit the effectiveness of their actions. the new rules are of particular importance in the context of better detection of money laundering, corruption, terrorist financing and other criminal activities.
in writing. ‒ the council regulation aims to provide tax authorities with consistent access to anti-money laundering information to enable them to fulfil their responsibilities in monitoring the proper application of the administrative cooperation directive by financial institutions, e.g. trusts. currently, access to anti-money laundering information varies across the eu. the amendment would therefore provide tax authorities with access to the mechanisms, procedures, documents and information concerning beneficial ownership and their underlying customer due diligence procedures as part of the fourth anti-money laundering directive. i have no objection to the commission's amendments to the directive on administrative cooperation. however, parliament's consultations included elements of automatic exchange of information on anti-money laundering, which was not the aim of the commission's original proposal or the council's compromise and was not taken into account. i therefore abstained.
in writing. ‒ recent media reports on the so-called 'panama papers' have drawn attention to the very serious problem of money laundering and tax havens. this and other similar scandals have made the european union and its member states aware of the need to cooperate more closely in the fight against tax fraud. the amendments to directive 2011/16/eu regarding access to information by tax authorities in relation to the prevention of money laundering can allow the european union to make significant progress in the fight against tax avoidance and tax evasion. member states cannot turn a blind eye to tax fraud, thereby allowing vast sums of money to flow unchecked. therefore, tax authorities need to have access to information on the extent of illicit money flows. the exchange of information between union and national authorities is essential to achieve this objective. at the same time, the right to privacy of union citizens must be safeguarded.
in writing. ‒ unfortunately, i am not convinced that the proposed rules will help to guarantee a uniform anti-money laundering approach in each member state, given the diversity of economies and the procedures used. parliament's consultations included elements which were not the aim of the commission's original proposal or of the compromise prepared by the council. that's why i voted against the bill.
in writing. ‒ i abstained in the vote on the report because there are a number of issues in the report which need to be discussed and clarified. the commission's proposal for a regulation on the introduction of a european credit rating agency is a good example of the need to ensure that the european credit rating agency is able to compete with the national credit rating agencies. what i welcome about the report is that it is a balanced and reasonable approach to the ecb's policy. i think the report contains too many doubts and inaccuracies.
in writing. ‒ the report discusses the ecb's policy in a reasonable way. however, given the report's promotion of a highly expansionary ecb policy (asset purchase programme, targeted longer-term refinancing operations), my serious doubts about the positive effects of mario draghi's statement and the more critical approach to the issue of further enlargement of the banking union than expressed in the report, i decided to abstain.
in writing. ‒ the european central bank plays a very important role in the eu, which is becoming even more important in times of crisis. europe is currently facing a number of challenges, including high unemployment in the euro area, market imbalances, the impact of the russian embargo, low economic growth, low levels of investment, insufficient domestic demand and fragmentation of the financial market. the ecb can help to combat these adverse effects by introducing financial instruments and targeted products. in addition, every effort should be made to ensure the proper functioning of the single monetary and fiscal policy and to ensure stable conditions favourable to investment. it is also very important to monitor and control the effectiveness of the actions undertaken in order to better select solutions and to carry out reliable evaluations of the use of funds. moreover, when taking decisions with pan-european financial implications, it is also necessary to take into account their potential impact on retail clients and the stability of pension systems. the ecb also has to deal with the impact of its current interest rate policy on local and regional banks and savings banks, and the issue of risks in the insurance and pension sectors. for this reason too, detailed monitoring and forecasting and impact assessment are essential.
in writing. ‒ effective development pathways and concrete actions are needed to unlock the full potential of the single market and facilitate innovation for the benefit of end-users. the green paper, while respecting the principle of proportionality, focuses mainly on financial services for citizens in need of cross-border services. the main objective is to ensure that the retail financial services market functions for the benefit of all. action to remove barriers and restrictions should be ensured. i also believe that cooperation between member states within the eu is an important issue, with due regard to the principle of subsidiarity, in supporting retail financial services firms that want to make better use of cross-border business opportunities. i therefore voted in favour of the green paper on retail financial services, as i share the rapporteur's view that the eu retail financial services market is still relatively underdeveloped.
in writing. ‒ the report focuses on a wide range of issues related to financial services in general and, more specifically, on the opportunities for streamlining the sector to the benefit of consumers and smes by ensuring a healthy competitive environment. the main points were the need to improve information on key financial products, the positive effects of digitalisation, the need to simplify rules while avoiding duplication of effort, the importance of financial education, the need to improve competition and the need to further support the financial dispute resolution network. that is why i supported the report.
in writing. ‒ the eu retail financial services market remains underdeveloped and highly fragmented. we still have 28 different, not very competitive, domestic markets. effective action is therefore needed to unlock the full potential of the european single market and to facilitate innovation for the benefit of end-users. the european commission's green paper is a step in the right direction. action needs to be taken as soon as possible to remove the existing barriers that limit the innovation of businesses and the functioning of the european economy as a whole. this is particularly important in the context of the rapidly expanding digitalisation of the world. there is now a real opportunity to connect financial operators operating in different parts of europe with consumers across the whole of europe. further development of the retail financial services market at union level within an appropriate legal framework ensuring the necessary consumer protection would not only facilitate intensive and fruitful cross-border activities but could also create a wider field for healthy competition at national level. i hope that the commission will take legislative action on retail financial services in the near future.
in writing. ‒ this report is a response to the european commission's green paper on retail financial services and aims to initiate a debate on the possible opening of the european market for financial services, in particular retail services, i.e. savings accounts, mortgages, pension insurance, etc. currently, the national financial services markets in the eu remain highly fragmented, for a variety of reasons. the report aims primarily to analyse the possibilities for the creation of a european financial services market. i voted to pass this document.
a year and a half ago, the european council took a very important decision on our common defence - a concrete decision to destroy the infrastructure of illegal immigration trafficking before it is used. in the last year and a half, not a single boat has been destroyed. instead, we hear, basically, all the time, the call for illegal immigration, because that's the only way to interpret the promise of opening legal pathways for immigration, which is illegal today. you can always argue about the right to bear arms, about the creation of new institutions of arms, about boundaries, when it's needed and when it's not. but one thing is certain: you can't give guns to people who, even if they're unarmed, are a danger to the community.
in writing. ‒ i abstained from the vote on the initiative to create a european defence union because i am convinced that defence policy must remain in the hands of sovereign states. the growing security threat facing europe has motivated some to raise the issue of building stronger cooperation between states in the field of security. some even argue that this cooperation should take the form of a formal defence union. taking matters to formal action in this area is a violation of the basic principle of a democratic and sovereign state. the security issue requires cooperation, which is why i believe that we should coordinate our actions within nato. the proposal to create an eu army will weaken nato and have a negative impact on relations with international defence partners.
in writing. ‒ the european defence union is an innovative solution to the important and growing problem of the european union's defence capability. this is a first practical but important step in increasingly complex circumstances and in the face of increasingly dangerous signals and behaviour emanating from eastern europe. in addition, the behavior of the new washington administration is not clear. the proposal that each country should meet its obligation to spend 2% of gdp on defence should be highlighted. poland shall comply with this commitment. the additional resources for the creation of a european defence union should be provided for in the new multiannual financial framework, but not only in terms of cohesion policy. the budgetary effort of each country should be taken into account. the development of the csdp must be supported and further steps encouraged to enhance the eu's defence capabilities in full respect of the treaties, international law and human rights.
in writing. ‒ the growing and unprecedented security threats facing europe have led to increasing calls in some quarters for closer defence cooperation between eu member states, and some to suggest that this should take the form of a formal defence union. i believe that defence cooperation and defence capability development cooperation in the eu should remain voluntary and not lead to duplication of nato defence planning. this is particularly the case for defence planning, the sustainable development of defence industrial cooperation and defence capacity building in all member states. that's why i abstained.
in writing. ‒ the current situation in europe, its immediate neighbourhood and rapidly progressing globalisation require a change of approach in many areas, including external and internal security. this applies both to the common foreign and security policy and to the protection of the external borders. the proper functioning of the eu internal market and the responsible conduct of the member states obliged to implement the common rules are of great importance for the proper functioning and achievement of the tasks of the csdp. it should be stressed that the defence market in europe is very heterogeneous and fragmented, and most contracts are still awarded at national level. in this context, small and medium-sized enterprises have much to gain and could benefit from a more transparent and open market, allowing them to participate in clearly defined tenders also in member states other than those in which they are established. better cooperation in the fight against terrorism and information sharing are also important. given the differences in defence capabilities, eu countries should all the more seek to work towards agreeing a common approach in the context of hybrid threats, trafficking in human beings, intelligence, cybersecurity and customs controls. security is not only a condition for the inviolability of borders, but also for the proper functioning of an integrated europe.
in writing. ‒ in recent years, the level of security in the european union's neighbourhood has deteriorated significantly. in the face of so many threats, no nation or organization can safeguard its citizens on its own. it is therefore high time that the community started to build its own defence system. the outcome of the us presidential elections and the call for greater involvement of the other member states in nato have made the need to build european defence capability even more urgent. building a defence union requires better coordination of national military capabilities, increased defence spending or the commitment of the eu budget to joint armed forces or defence research and development. the report rightly noted that the next post-2020 financial framework should provide financial support for the establishment of a european defence union. closer european cooperation in defence would contribute to enhancing the efficiency, unity and effectiveness, as well as the eu's assets and capabilities, and would have a potential positive impact on defence research and the union industry. the establishment of permanent structured cooperation within the union would undoubtedly give an impetus to the search for new possibilities for joint procurement, maintenance and maintenance of armed forces between member states.
in writing. ‒ the idea of creating a european defence union should be discussed and reflected upon. i have repeatedly argued that the european defence union should be rid of prejudices, but it should address a number of key issues, such as strengthening the industrial base, improving the mobility system for military personnel, equipment, etc. it is good that these issues are addressed in the text of the resolution. unfortunately, on the other hand, the proposal may contain unnecessary postulates which would lead to the eec indirectly taking over nato's competences. the european defence union should be built on the military or intelligence bases of the member states, so that the sovereignty of the member states is guaranteed. that's why i abstained on this resolution.
in writing. ‒ in the face of today's challenges, it is not enough to simply say that europe should do better in defence and security cooperation europe must do it! the geopolitical situation forces the european union countries to bear the burden of responsibility for their own security, rather than relying solely on the assistance of allied powers. we have to become it ourselves. we're the economic leader, but we need military power to follow suit. the report by mr paet contains many good ideas on how to deepen defence cooperation in europe within the european union. the lisbon treaty provides a number of solutions in this area, such as the possibility of joint armaments planning or permanent structured cooperation (pesco). the report also calls for better use of existing structures such as the eu battle groups and the european defence agency. these are initiatives worth supporting. the eu must not be afraid to take responsibility for security and defence capabilities. the low level and unsatisfactory performance of defence spending in europe indicate the need for change and a more collective approach to these important issues. opinion polls show clearly that citizens want closer cooperation on defence and security in europe. this report is a signal that we want to go in that direction.
in writing. ‒ i support the report on the european defence union. this is because the european union needs to respond more decisively to emerging threats, such as terrorism, cyberattacks and energy security. this would require not only better coordination but also the establishment of a joint operational command to make more efficient use of the military resources held by individual member states. the eu budget allocation for defence research is also desirable. unfortunately, this is not possible under the current legal model. this is one of the reasons why europe's military technology is increasingly outpacing countries like the united states and russia, which are spending billions of dollars to gain technological advantage. the proposed changes are in the right direction and i therefore support this report.
in writing. ‒ i abstained on a report on the question of unlocking the potential of passenger water transport. i think it is important to improve the common rules on the safety of passenger ships in eu waters. in the context of the current situation of uncontrolled flows of illegal migrants by sea to europe, there is a need to improve the safety of ship crews and passengers. i also see the need to further improve systems in the operation of large agglomerations to improve the quality of services and the comfort of people travelling by public transport. however, the proposed rules encroach on competences which should be the responsibility of the member states, and i therefore abstained.
in writing. ‒ i support proposals to simplify and streamline the common rules on passenger ship safety in eu waters to improve safety and competitiveness, and to clarify, simplify and update the rules to take account of legal and technical developments. however, in view of the call for decarbonisation and the promotion of non-fossil fuels, i abstained.
in writing. ‒ despite the negative effects of the financial crisis, the ferry and liner industry has consolidated and increased significantly in recent years. the sector currently employs some 160 000 people and offers important connections in coastal, inland and urban areas and is particularly important for peripheral regions. at the same time, water transport is widely recognised as one of the most sustainable modes of passenger transport. attention should be paid to the potential efficiency gains from the strengthening of passenger water transport and the possibility of introducing integrated ticketing to increase coordination between different modes of transport. our aim should be to create a single area for passenger water transport, which would make it possible to reduce the administrative burden on cross-border passenger transport.
in writing. ‒ the draft resolution is positive and important, but several important issues have been omitted, including the need to simplify current regulations and to put the emphasis on the safety of inland vessel crew and passengers, which is particularly important in the context of the immigration crisis. the inclusion of passenger water transport in the framework of systems that take into account the use of two or more modes of transport could be a major opportunity, which may be particularly important in large agglomerations. the absence of these demands has decided that i shall abstain from voting on the adoption of this resolution.
in writing. ‒ water transport is not only cheap and fast, but also an environmentally friendly means of transport. its importance for the creation of a single european transport network is of the utmost importance. unfortunately, in many member states there are significant disparities in the level of infrastructure development, the number of connections available and the diversity of the offer. in poland, inland transport has been neglected for many years, also in terms of passenger transport, despite its great potential in our geographical conditions. this is not just about transport, but also about the opportunity to create many jobs in the shipyards and in the modernisation of the infrastructure. the importance of this means of transport for the development of tourism is also not overestimated, as in many regions of poland the use of passenger water transport is already being taken into account. for the kujawy-pomorskie region, this is a key issue and an opportunity for development by creating new communication opportunities for investors. the strategic location of my region makes it an important water transport hub not only for poland but for the whole of central and eastern europe. however, a huge financial effort is needed to thoroughly modernise existing infrastructure. such an effort is impossible without the support of the european union. the report we are voting on today is an important step towards restoring the rightful place of passenger water transport on the road map of poland.
in writing. ‒ i voted in favour of the report on improving the effectiveness of development cooperation. the aim of improving development aid to member states is of paramount importance. i believe that action should be taken to improve the quality of the delivery of development aid, which tackles the problems of countries linked to poverty and existing inequalities. in the context of the implementation of the development strategy, cooperation between the private and public sectors is important, contributing to sustainable and inclusive development. the implementation of the strategy beyond the objectives should also take into account the fact that development challenges have changed with the emergence of new global challenges such as migration, food security, peace and stabilisation and climate change. i believe that action for the development of the member states is a priority for the eu and that is why i voted in favour of the report.

in writing. ‒ the european union has been committed to improving aid and development effectiveness for many years. this december marks the fifth anniversary of the adoption of the partnership for effective cooperation with pusan. after five years, it is therefore important to take stock of the implementation of the global commitments. it is also a good opportunity to explore how increasing aid and development effectiveness could contribute to the un sustainable development goals and the addis ababa action plan on aid financing. as the world's largest donor, the union has a particular responsibility to improve development efficiency and accountability worldwide. at the same time, we must promote integrated governance based on the rule of law and respect for human rights in developing countries. we should seek to develop new initiatives to develop trilateral cooperation projects involving new donors and middle-income countries. the union, as well as its member states, must be more proactive and systematic in involving national parliaments, local authorities, civil society and private actors in programming.

matter of the utmost importance that parliament expresses its stance on an issue so pertinent and timely. allow me first to strike a very personal note, because this issue is also important for me personally. my whole public life – a large part of it under communist rule and afterwards – has been dedicated to countering the narrative exerted first by the soviet union and then by the russian important for me to monitor the elections in lebanon in 2005 after the assassination of rafic hariri and to see the influence of stratcom at that time. we have, of course, now seen many transformations of the strategic communications and propaganda in these countries. the assignment from the enlarged bureau of the committee on foreign affairs (afet) was very clear. i was given the in writing. a major barrier to growth in many member states is the fact that a large proportion of the population does not have the necessary skills for the labour market. the problem is not just early school leavers but the increasing prevalence of secondary illiteracy. many experts point to the disturbing loss of the ability to read with understanding, to write more elaborate sentences, or to perform simple mathematical calculations. i therefore wholeheartedly support the european commission's initiative to establish a skills guarantee. experts agree that the traditional model of education, as we know it from our own experience or that of our children, is not fully responsive to the challenges of the 21st century. no country has yet created a perfect education system from which all can benefit. to make full use of existing policies, instruments and funds, we should learn from each other and build on ideas that have worked very well in many member states. when creating the skills guarantee, does the european commission intend to focus on sharing good practice and encouraging countries to implement ideas that have already been proven to work?
in writing. the two main challenges facing the skills guarantee are to fill the skills gaps among eu citizens and to better match them to the labour market. in this context, i stress the enormous role of modern education systems, which should focus on the development of core competences and a broader range of skills needed in the labour market now and in the future, including digital, transversal, technical and social skills. i also ask the commission to support member states in modernising their education programmes so that they can more effectively identify, activate and develop the skills and qualifications of europeans. finally, i would stress that skills can translate into better economic and social outcomes if they are clear to all and effectively used across the union. in this context, we must ensure their quality, transparency and recognition in other member states. i also stress the importance of recognising and validating competences and qualifications acquired through non-formal education, which is particularly important for those with lower qualifications, the unemployed, those at risk of unemployment and those who need to change their career path.

in writing. ‒ i voted against the adoption of the calendar of the 2018 monthly sessions of parliament, due to a different position on the question of the change in the duration of the sessions. the calendar presented suggests extending the duration of the plenary sessions in strasbourg. i do not see the need to change this in the light of the current working system of parliament and the organisation of working time. i believe that these changes will not increase efficiency, but may only delay the decision-making process.
in writing. ‒ i voted against the resolution to refer the ceta agreement to the court of justice of the eu for review of its compatibility with the eu treaties. the opinion presented is too liberal in its interpretation of the provisions of the contract. legal experts who have worked on the interpretation of the provisions believe that ceta does not affect the legal framework, the eu's competences or the fundamental rights of the treaty. the european parliament's legal teams that examined the compatibility issue did not find any contradiction between the investment chapter of ceta and the eu treaties. in the light of the foregoing, i do not consider that there is a need to re-examine the case.
in writing. ‒ i see the transatlantic economic and trade agreement with canada (ceta) as an additional component of the security architecture and the deepening of transatlantic relations, as evidenced by the strategic partnership agreement signed in parallel. the arbitration mechanism, which is most often raised as an obstacle, will be subject to separate ratification in the polish sejm. the agreement respects the existing restrictions in polish and eu law on agricultural trade, such as the non-release of gmos. it also eliminates customs duties and other non-tariff barriers, thus increasing the competitiveness of polish goods. i share the view of my colleagues in the ecr who oppose further attempts to delay the vote on ceta, especially after the unanimous agreement of the 28 member states. the position of the polish government on this matter is also unequivocal.
in writing. ‒ the rationale for the ceta vote: after the us presidential elections, the ttip issue is temporarily out of date. but ceta is a breakthrough that will push the weaker european economies into an unequal competition, which for example for agriculture - i note this as a pole, representing the most agricultural country in europe - will be deadly. we have a duty to defend our agriculture, which is a great social asset for poland and for europe. ceta is also a limitation of the sovereign rights of our countries vis-à-vis our national markets, which are threatened by the consolidation and expansion of the international arbitration mechanism. this is a privileging of non-european companies and as such should have been examined by the court of justice of the eu, which i voted in favour of.
in writing. ‒ left-wing, populist and green parties have made another attempt to delay the entry into force of ceta, the most ambitious free trade agreement ever negotiated by the european union. the resolution proposed by some political groups in the european parliament, requesting an opinion from the court of justice of the eu on the compatibility of ceta with the eu treaties, is in fact another move against international trade, transnational cooperation and the globalisation of prosperity. ceta is the most comprehensive and advanced agreement of its kind ever negotiated by the european union. thanks to the agreement, 98% of all tariff lines will be eliminated. it will also allow almost unlimited access to canadian public procurement at all levels. most importantly, in response to the voices of europeans, a new mechanism for investment protection has been introduced, which ensures that the government has the absolute right to legislate in the name of the public interest. the draft resolution should therefore be regarded as nothing more than a political manifesto and an attempt to undertake diversionary action against international trade. it should be noted that this summer the legal services of the european parliament issued an opinion on the compatibility of ceta with the treaties, indicating that it is fully compatible with eu law and does not affect our legal framework, eu competences or constitutional rights. i therefore voted against the resolution.
in writing. ‒ the inta committee has already asked the european parliament's legal service for an opinion on this issue. the opinion explicitly states that the provisions are compatible with the eu treaties, because: 'given the purpose and content of the investment part of ceta, the planned investment dispute settlement provisions can be considered compatible with the eu treaties'. it is worth adding that the legal services opinion was considered sufficient and opposes further attempts to delay the vote on ceta, especially after the unanimous agreement of the 28 member states. that is why i voted against the opinion, which is designed to delay the decision.
in writing. ‒ the signing by the european union of a comprehensive free trade agreement with canada is a subject of much controversy and concern. the initiators of the action to refer ceta to the court of justice were not, however, concerned with clarifying the objections that were emerging. the proposal which was the subject of this vote was an attempt to exploit public doubts to delay the ratification process of this agreement. this kind of trick should not be used in such a serious debate, which is why i voted against this motion. the legal aspects of this agreement, which may give rise to reservations, have been discussed on many occasions in the european parliament and in the committee on international trade, and many experts believe that it is in line with european law. this does not mean, however, that i am uncritical of this agreement, and particularly of the way in which it was negotiated. the lack of transparency in the negotiation process is a huge failure on the part of the commission, which has resulted in the emergence of sometimes very radical voices of opposition to ceta. however, the ratification process of the agreement has just begun and the member states will have the final say. it is the citizens who, by their ability to influence national authorities, should have the final say on this matter. blaming lawyers is not the right answer to the eu's democratic deficit.
in writing. ‒ i voted against the report on emissions of certain air pollutants. the concerns stem from the fact that the initiative, in its wording, by assuming emission limits, may have negative effects on the polish agricultural, steel, construction and, in particular, thermal energy sectors. the introduction of the amendments will consequently entail high financial costs for the reduction of emissions of sulphur dioxide and ammonia compounds, which are listed in the directives. in order to avoid negative consequences for the country and to protect the polish economy, i voted against.
in writing. ‒ the proposal to revise the national emission ceilings directive (necd) is part of the commission's clean air package and replaces the current regulations laid down in directive 2001/81/ec for sulphur dioxide (so2), nitrogen oxides (nox), non-methane organic compounds (nmvocs) and ammonia (nh3), which are in force until 2020. the new directive was to set new emission reduction levels from 2020 to 2030 for these substances, as well as for dust (pm2.5) and methane (ch4). the commission has already taken a number of measures to ensure that the environmental impact of the use of pesticides is not significantly reduced.
in writing. ‒ the european union attaches great importance to environmental protection and the fight against the effects of climate change. however, these actions must take account of a number of factors and the long-term effects on the various sectors of the economy, of which agriculture is a special case. it is worth remembering that agriculture and forestry are the only sectors of the economy that are significant emitters of greenhouse gases, but they are also sectors that simultaneously counteract global warming by absorbing and storing significant amounts of carbon dioxide in soils and plants. moreover, agriculture and forestry are crucial to ensuring food security in europe and supplying raw materials to many industries. given this specific nature, the environmental functions of agriculture and the already introduced restrictions, it would be problematic for the sector to include methane emission commitments in the nec directive. so it's a good thing that methane was left out of this report. eu member states are very diverse in terms of agricultural production structures, farm sizes and production patterns, and the modernisation of the sector to reduce greenhouse gas emissions and environmental impact should be carried out in a flexible way to avoid economic stagnation and to move the economy towards innovative and sustainable solutions. in any case, synergies between agricultural and energy policies and the environment should be ensured.
in writing. ‒ this report is convenient for many countries, but not for poland, whose economy is 90% coal-based. it's the carbon that causes the most carbon dioxide to rise in the atmosphere. the timing of the report does not allow the polish economy to branch out. i voted against the report.
in writing. ‒ i voted against the finalisation of the basel iii package. i believe that the package will have a negative impact on the banks' customers and i have doubts about the estimated economic benefits of the proposed changes. the application of the regulation in the form of a framework rather than specific provisions does not allow a clear assessment of the effects of the package. the lack of a specific impact assessment, on the other hand, has led to a number of conflicting opinions. as experts point out, the introduction of higher capital requirements, as required by the proposed package, will mean higher costs for banks. and those will be passed on to the customers. too much doubt and a lack of clear assessment of the benefits that the package could bring motivates to continue working and, at the moment, to reject the package.

mr president, first of all let me congratulate our rapporteur mr langen on an excellent report. in the report, we can read that the current vat system across the eu is excessively complicated, with a multitude of vat rates and exemptions that put unnecessary burden on companies involved in cross-border trading. moreover, this complexity opens up ample possibilities for vat fraud and vat avoidance within the single market. according to the commission’s assessment, in 2014 alone the vat gap between expected revenue and revenue actually collected was estimated at about eur 160 billion. these enormous losses suffered by all member states call for swift and ambitious action to address vat fraud. the focus should be on three areas: firstly, we should minimise the amount of goods that benefit from reduced vat rates across the eu. secondly, in the longer run, we should aim at gradually harmonising national vat rates within the single market. thirdly, the eu should take steps to address tax fraud coming from the so-called carousel schemes. one way of solving this last problem is to ask banks to separate the vat obligations from the gross price paid for a given transaction. a payment by a payer for any given invoice should then be immediately split by the bank into vat tax due that would be transferred to the national tax authority, and the remaining amount would be transferred to the seller’s account.
mr president, commissioner, i have to ask you to stop this. i would like to take part in this debate and point out that in my country, poland, the so-called vat gap has in recent years been 30% of revenue, and thus clearly above the eu average. therefore, the new polish government has been taking action since the beginning of this year, changing the law, reforming the tax services, which has already had good results, and vat revenues are almost 10% higher than in the same period last year. the changes to non-vat legislation include, inter alia, restrictions on the quarterly system for the clearance of vat, the extension of the reverse vat system, restrictions on the registration of 'pylons' for vat evasion, an increase in the size of financial penalties and penalties for vat evasion, and the introduction of a central register of receipts and a central register of invoices. it therefore seems to me that the proposals drawn up by the commission to reduce vat evasion should concern only intra-community trade, while the decision on the remainder should be left to the individual member states.

in writing. ‒ i voted in favour of the text of the directive on the activities of institutions for occupational retirement provision and the supervision of such institutions (iorps). the text adopted takes account of the principle of proportionality and stresses that pensions are a competence of the member states. the directive focuses on the rules concerning the cross-border aspect of iorps. the directive covers the protection of iorps' members and beneficiaries, who must be adequately informed of the rules of the pension scheme. the provisions of this directive aim to ensure the protection of future pensioners, members of pension schemes and beneficiaries and to safeguard the role of the member states in the actions taken.
in writing. ‒ the first iorp directive was introduced in 2003 and proposals for the second iorp directive started to appear in 2014. iorps manage private collective pension schemes for employers so that their employees can benefit from an occupational pension that includes employer-paid contributions. iorps are not linked to public pensions, which fall under national competence (first pillar), and to private pensions (third pillar). the report shall cover the governance, risk management, transparency and disclosure of information by the iorp. stresses that pensions are a competence of the member states, puts more emphasis on the rules for cross-border iorps than for national iorps and repeals all delegated acts originally proposed by the commission. it ensures that members (employees) and pensioners are informed of all relevant features of their pension scheme in a form adapted to the needs of the users of the annual pension benefit statement and are consulted when decisions affecting the payment of their pensions are taken. the format of the list is less mandatory than the one originally proposed by the commission. i hereby endorse the report.

in writing. ‒ the coup attempt that took place in turkey on 15 july 2016 resulted in the deaths of hundreds of people. over 2,000 people were injured. a few days later, the turkish authorities declared a state of emergency, which now gives the authorities almost unlimited control over the population. the european parliament, in its previous resolution, strongly condemned the coup in turkey but also stressed the importance of protecting democracy. but in a country that has been friendly to us, that seems to be broken. for these reasons, the european parliament should send a clear signal that the accession negotiations with turkey should be frozen and cannot continue in the current situation. a state which does not respect the principles of democracy and the rule of law, which considers the death penalty, which persecutes hundreds of thousands of citizens, which restricts freedom of speech, which restricts the activities of independent media and independent newspapers cannot be part of the european community. both sides should engage in dialogue to find a peaceful and democratic solution to the tense situation in turkey. it should be borne in mind that the freezing of the negotiation process will have negative consequences for both parties.
in writing. ‒ turkey is in a state of social and political chaos following the alleged coup attempt last july. the aim of the coup was to overthrow president erdoğan, who was accused of an authoritarian style of government and of undermining fundamental rights and freedoms. the european parliament's resolution on turkey of april 2016 expressed deep concern at the regression in the area of democracy and the rule of law and the decline in the overall pace of reforms in the country. since then, the risk of the commission and the member states freezing the accession negotiations with turkey has been growing steadily. i abstained from the vote because of the lack of new information on the relationship between the two entities.
in writing. ‒ i voted against the eu's accession to the istanbul convention on preventing and combating violence against women. this is a very important subject. action must be taken to protect women from violence. i wouldn't want to be seen as a person who condones violence against women. this decision was prompted by concerns about the provisions of the resolution which violate the principle of subsidiarity. these provisions transpose the provisions of the convention into national law and the criminal law system. the protection of women from violence cannot be based on gender ideology but must be based on effective legislation and action. the resolution proposed is ideological in nature. in order to ensure the best possible system of protection of women against violence, work should be undertaken on alternative draft resolutions which have been developed with a view to achieving consensus.
in writing. ‒ i support the resolution on the accession of the european union as a party to the council of europe convention on preventing and combating violence against women and domestic violence. the document, signed by 43 countries and ratified by 15, was hailed as the gold standard for violence-reduction policies at the 2013 un session in new york. the main advantage of this convention, in addition to the provisions on assistance to victims of violence and the recognition and punishment of acts of violence, is the chapter on prevention. he says the key to preventing violence is to promote equality, to spread awareness of women's rights, both among school-age youth and adult women and men. it also includes the dissemination of gender and sex education and correctional workshops for perpetrators of violence to prevent the recurrence of violent behavior. the convention talks about including men in the fight against violence, because their influence on perpetrators of violence is very effective and efficient. i believe that this convention, as a vehicle for an effective, modern approach to violence, should be ratified as soon as possible in all eu countries, and i therefore welcome the decision of the european commission to accede to the eu-wide convention. i am also proud that poland is among the countries that have ratified the convention and whose legislation is almost 100% consistent with the requirements of this important document.
in writing. ‒ i am in favour of a firm fight against violence against women, and poland is one of the countries with the lowest rates of such crimes. at the same time, poland cannot support a resolution calling on the eu to join the istanbul convention and establish its own legal act. every eu country has laws against violence and additional provisions will not change anything. they are, however, a matter for the member states. i do not hereby support the resolution.
in writing. ‒ violence against women is not a private matter. it's a serious crime and it's still a huge problem in europe. too often, unfortunately, violence against women is tolerated, and it is our duty to join forces to fight impunity and protect victims. it is therefore time to build a culture of respect for the dignity of women and girls, to fight stereotypes and to focus on prevention. unfortunately, in the european union, one in three women has experienced physical or sexual violence in her lifetime. in this context, the decision of the european commission, which proposed in march 2016 that the union as a whole should also accede to the istanbul convention on preventing and combating violence against women, is welcomed. however, it should be noted that some community countries have not yet acceded to the convention. i hope that this situation will change soon.
